If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.

papers.title: On Shepp's property in free probability
papers.abstract: We establish a free analogue of Shepp's theorem for freely independent standard semicircular elements. We show more generally that a family of self-normalized squared quadratic forms is free, and each has a standard Marchenko-Pastur distribution. The free analogue of Shepp's theorem follows by taking the coefficients of quadratic forms to be the three Pauli matrices. We also prove some new free analogues of Lukacs-type independence results. The key part of the proof is a construction of an equivalent and simpler operator model on a corner algebra compressed by a free projection.

papers.title: $99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point
papers.abstract: When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.

papers.title: Near Optimal Pure Stepsize Adaptation Acceleration for Gradient Descent on Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: Existing accelerated first-order methods for nonconvex optimization typically rely on momentum or extrapolation, requiring auxiliary vectors beyond the current iterate and gradient. On the other hand, memory-free stepsize scheduling alone can accelerate certain convex problems, while no guarantee exists for nonconvex problems. This paper closes this gap by proposing Nonconvex Adaptively Clipped Chebyshev (NACC) gradient descent method, which achieves near optimal acceleration while keeping the vanilla gradient descent update. NACC combines an adaptive selection of reversed fractal Chebyshev stepsizes with an epoch-wise clipping mechanism to control the aggressiveness of stepsizes. For nonconvex problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients and Hessians, we establish a near-optimal $\widetilde O(ε^{-7/4})$ complexity. If the problem is convex in addition, then, without modification, NACC automatically achieves an $\widetilde O(ε^{-3/4})$ accelerated complexity. Importantly, NACC guarantees the standard quadratic sufficient descent at every iteration, even when the stepsizes are substantially larger than the conventional choice. These monotonicity properties further facilitate practical implementations that adaptively adjust the estimated gradient and Hessian Lipschitz constants, demonstrating significant advantages in numerical tests against the existing nonconvex acceleration benchmarks.

papers.title: Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO
papers.abstract: We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $α\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,α,θ}$ is bounded from below by $d$.

papers.title: Counting solutions to sparse systems of congruences
papers.abstract: We obtain new bounds and asymptotic formulas for the number of solutions to sparse systems of $n$ diagonal congruences modulo an integer $q$ in $s$ variables. In a large range of parameters, our results improve and generalise those of A. A. Karatsuba (1976). In particular, our lower bound on $s$, which guarantees the solvability of such systems, depends only on $n$, rather than on specific degrees as in the work of A. A. Karatsuba (1976).

papers.title: Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
papers.abstract: Reconstructing the continuous time dynamics of cell state evolution from sparse snapshot observations can be formulated as an unbalanced optimal transport problem. To study such dynamics at a coarse grained cell type level, unbalanced optimal transport must be extended to discrete state spaces. Inspired by discrete flow matching, we extended the dynamic Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) problem to discrete spaces, and derived a closed form for its solution. For particularly large state spaces or more general models, we proposed an unbalanced discrete flow matching as a numerical approximation method, which provides a Markovian reconstruction of the optimal WFR flow. Our discrete WFR framework also stays stable across different coarse grain resolution. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and applications to real biological data supported the plausibility of the reconstructed dynamics.

papers.title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Turán-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
papers.abstract: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $χ(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024), P1.25] established the corresponding result for the adjacency spectral radius. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the same graph uniquely maximizes the $p$-spectral radius in this class. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.

papers.title: A Sweedler dual seen as a terminal object in a category of bialgebras
papers.abstract: We study the Sweedler dual of the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{K}[X]$ equipped with the multiplicative coproduct $δ(X) = X \otimes X$, and show that the resulting bialgebra $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ is the terminal object in the category of pairs $(B, λ)$, where $B$ is a bialgebra and $λ$ is a character of $B$. This generalizes a result of Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile on combinatorial Hopf algebras in the graded and connected setting. We describe the subcoalgebras and subbialgebras of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$, which lead to the introduction of the spectrum of a bialgebra. We also study the particular cases double bialgebras (bialgebras equipped with two compatible coproducts), firstly examining their connection to unital near-semirings or near-rings. Introducing a subbialgebra of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ obtained from the intersection with another Sweedler dual, we prove it is the terminal object in the category of double bialgebras. As a consequence, we show that the spectrum of any double Hopf algebra is a subgroup of the group of roots of unity. This imply that not any bialgebra can become double. We finally apply this framework to a bialgebra of graphs with a coproduct given by contraction and deletion of edges, relating its invariants to Bergman colorations of edges arising from graphical matroids.

papers.title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
papers.abstract: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Random dyadic shift scattering: scale-uniform deformation stability and phase-aligned Hilbert multipliers
papers.abstract:
Petermichl's theorem represents the Hilbert transform by averaging a single dyadic shift over dilations and random dyadic lattices. We study how the deformation stability of the lattice-averaged shift, and of a parameter-free feature map $Φ$ built from it in the spirit of Mallat's wavelet scattering, depends on the number $J+1$ of scales. For the Haar generator as well as compactly supported $C^1$ orthonormal wavelets, the covariance error under a deformation $f\mapsto f(\cdot-τ(\cdot))$ is $O((J+1)
orm{τ'}_\infty
orm f)$ without a $
ormτ_\infty$ term, because lattice averaging absorbs the translation part of $τ$ exactly. The deformation defect splits into a first-order Calderón commutator, bounded uniformly in $J$ by the $T(1)$ theorem, and a second-order remainder. On a single lattice, affine warps and $C^{1,δ}$ generators give a lower bound $c\,σ_\eps\sqrt{J+1}-C\eps$ for the defect, with an explicit constant $σ_\eps\ge0$ computed to be positive for sym4 and db4 at three values of $\eps$. Averaging over lattices turns the defect into a Fourier-multiplier quadratic form, yielding $J$-uniform bounds both for affine warps, with a logarithmic loss in the Haar case, and for $C^2$ warps with $C^{1,δ}$ generators, and hence a scale-uniform Mallat-type stability estimate for $Φ$. With the standard child pair, the Hilbert component of the averaged shift nearly cancels for smooth Daubechies-type generators; re-indexing the children by integers restores this component. For Haar and general warps, numerical computations agree with a conjectured $J$-uniform bound.

papers.title: Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension
papers.abstract: Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required. In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.

papers.title: Certifying a Sufficient Gaussian Dependence Regime for Learned Weighted FDR Control
papers.abstract: Learning hypothesis weights from informative auxiliary data can improve the power of multiple testing. Even when the weights are learned independently of the tests, the validity of weighted Benjamini-Hochberg depends on their joint distribution. We use reference observations to certify a sufficient dependence condition for one-sided Gaussian tests. An intersection-union test of uncertain correlation signs determines whether to apply weighted Benjamini-Hochberg or a prespecified fallback at an adjusted level. Under conditional separation of certification and testing, the procedure controls the false discovery rate (FDR) for every Gaussian correlation matrix satisfying the stated sampling assumptions and weight constraints. We establish a boundary obstruction to uniform certification and matching minimax sample-size bounds for worst-case pair sets and the all-pairs problem. In the parameter ranges of the matching bounds, the minimax sample size grows logarithmically with the number of checked pairs and quadratically with the inverse of their positive margin. For homogeneous Gaussian observations with known marginal variances, residual contrasts from the testing subjects provide an independent source of certification scores. Simulations with up to 4,950 checked pairs, comparisons under a common subject budget, and Gaussian designs based on correlations estimated from the Healthy Brain Network illustrate the trade-off between certification and detection power.

papers.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite bubbles
papers.abstract: Let $k\geq 6$, $λ\in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $k$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with $\mathrm{Ric}_h > λ$. In this paper, we construct, for each given $ε>0$, a sequence of $(k+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(X\times\mathbb{S}^2 ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_ε,d_ε) $ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} > λ$, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_ε) \leq ε$, and $X_ε$ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. In particular, the sequence of Riemannian manifolds we construct have uniformly bounded topology, which improves the earlier examples of Hupp-Naber-Wang and Zhou.

papers.title: Parallel sums of nilpotent elements: exact realization and structured eigenvalue splitting
papers.abstract: We prove that, over every infinite field and for $m\ge2$, the parallel sums $N(N+C)^{-1}C$ of nilpotent $m\times m$ inputs with invertible sum are exactly the matrices of nullity at least two. Every positive split of the target nullity between the input kernels is realizable. Over $\mathbb{C}$, we determine the paired derivative image and characterize universal full matrix cancellation at nonzero residues. For analytic input paths, nilpotence is required only at the base. An adjugate identity forces the last two characteristic coefficients to be $O(\varepsilon^2)$, yielding sharp bounds $O(|\varepsilon|^{2/3})$ at nonzero three-dimensional nilpotent residues and $O(|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)})$ at nilpotent residues for $m\ge4$. At every base with residue of type $[m-1,1]$, $m\ge4$, we prove a generic splitting law, also with fixed input sum. For $m\ge5$, it has $m-2$ roots on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)}$ and two on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/2}$, separating the largest-root and spectral-gap scales. A separate sharpness family keeps both inputs nilpotent and two roots zero. At the nonzero nilpotent three-dimensional boundary, a finite coefficient criterion computes the splitting orders for each exceptional affine fixed-sum direction. For each such path, the punctured spectral gap is at least $c|\varepsilon|^3$ near zero for some $c>0$, and the exponent is optimal over this class. Over a nonzero unital ring with $2$ invertible, we construct two $3\times3$ matrix inputs, each of nilpotency index exactly three, with invertible sum. In the complex unital Banach case, the residue has spectrum ${0}\cup\tfrac12σ(Q)$ for every coefficient $Q$. With the common core allowed to vary, a complex matrix is a finite-Drazin Hua output if and only if its nullity is not one.

papers.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.

papers.title: Dirichlet eigenvalues of Laplacian with potential on general graphs and Weyl limits in integer lattice spaces $Z^d$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first establish the existence of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian with a vertex weight on an infinite, connected and locally finite graph, via building compact embeddings of suitable spaces, when the weight decays faster at infinity than the optimal Hardy weight. In the particular integer lattice space $Z^d$, we apply a segmentation technique to estimate the mean Riesz potential over the entire space, thereby deriving estimates for the eigenvalue counting function and establishing the Weyl limit of the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Nested Spherical Designs of Optimal Order
papers.abstract: Zheng and Zhuang [22] showed that a spherical $t_1$-design $Y$ with $|Y|=M\sim t_1^d$ points on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$ can be extended to a spherical $t$-design by adding points, with a total of order $t^{2d+1}$, and asked whether the optimal order $t^d$ is attainable. We keep their construction and improve the estimate of the pairing of the given points against polynomials of unit $L^1$-gradient norm. We prove that, if the given spherical $t_1$-design is upper regular at scale $t_1$ (in particular if it is well-separated; such a design exists by Bondarenko, Radchenko and Viazovska [6]), then for $d\ge2$, every $N\ge C(d,K)\,t^d$ suffices to admit a point set $X$ with $|X|=N$, for all $t_1<t$, such that the multiset union $X\uplus Y$ is a spherical $t$-design; in particular $|X\uplus Y|\le C(d,K)\,t^d$. The proof combines the design property, which removes the low frequencies exactly, with an $L^1$ Jackson-type estimate and a sampling inequality applied on dyadic frequency blocks. Upper regularity turns out to be automatic for nested spherical designs of optimal order; that is, every spherical $t_1$-design with $M\le C_M t_1^d$ points extends to a spherical $t$-design with $N+M\le C(d)\,C_M\,t^d$ (with $C_M\ge1$), uniformly in $t_1<t$, without any separation hypothesis. Some control of local multiplicity is necessary for an extension of optimal order. We also show that the estimate of the pairing functional cannot be improved within this method; that is, for every point set of at most $c\,t^d$ points it is at least of order $t^{d-1}$, and for upper regular designs it is of exactly this order. Finally, we treat finite chains of nested spherical designs, and on the circle we remove a logarithmic factor from the general estimate.

papers.title: Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
papers.abstract: Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification. A sparse-regression surrogate of the vector field is reconstructed from the data, and its Jacobian, estimated with a matrix-free Krylov method, is analysed with Computational Singular Perturbation diagnostics. The resulting fast-slow partition guides the learning of explicit SIM algebraic representations through regression, and the reduced model follows by restricting the dynamics to it. For a linear stochastic system, this regression agrees with the Mori-Zwanzig projection at leading order in the timescale ratio. We demonstrate the validity of the framework on an illustrative linear system, the Michaelis-Menten model, a biofilm growth model, and a five-dimensional target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model. The method accurately identifies fast variables, reconstructs slow invariant manifolds, and generates accurate reduced models. Furthermore, we map the performance boundaries of the framework under sparse sampling and measurement noise, showing robust recovery for low-dimensional systems and highlighting data-requirement limits in higher dimensions. These results demonstrate that interpretable multiscale reduction can be achieved directly from time-series data, without requiring explicit prior knowledge of the underlying fast/slow timescale separation.

papers.title: On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)
papers.abstract: We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bièvre and Torrésani.

papers.title: Fairness-Regularized Principal Component Analysis
papers.abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) optimizes aggregate reconstruction accuracy but may represent heterogeneous groups unevenly. We study fairness-regularized PCA, which balances aggregate reconstruction risk against worst-group reconstruction regret, and establish its population and statistical properties. First, we characterize the reconstruction-fairness trade-off and show that, under a nondegeneracy condition, a small fairness penalty reduces worst-group regret to first order while increasing aggregate reconstruction risk only to second order. This reveals a vanishing initial marginal cost of improving fairness. We also identify conditions under which the regularization path remains locally constant. A minimax spectral characterization shows that, under an optimal effective eigengap condition, the convex relaxation is exact and Fair PCA is equivalent to ordinary PCA with endogenously adjusted group weights. Second, we develop a statistical theory for estimating fairness-regularized principal subspaces. A uniform eigengap over the set of possibly nonunique dual optimizers implies polyhedral identification and quadratic growth, yielding first-order perturbation bounds and convergence rates that accommodate growing dimensions, ranks, and numbers of groups. Third, we establish uniform recovery of the reconstruction-fairness path and theoretical guarantees for data-adaptive penalty selection. Simulations and an NHANES accelerometry application demonstrate substantial improvements in worst-group representation quality with minimal loss of aggregate reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
papers.abstract: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the Büchi language forgets. Machines sharing their Büchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its Büchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and Büchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.

papers.title: Decomposition algorithms for rational curves on real classical groups
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to an algorithmic investigation of the decomposition problem for rational curves on real classical groups. The main contributions are: (1) We present two Maple-implemented algorithms for decomposing rational curves on real classical groups. The first algorithm decomposes a curve with multiple poles into a unique product of curves with single poles. For rational curves on (indefinite) orthogonal groups, the second algorithm further decomposes single-pole curves into products of low-degree curves. The former only involves linear equations, whereas the latter requires solving both linear and quadratic equations. (2) We compare the decomposition of the same curve with respect to different ambient groups. Through this comparison, we provide an interpretation of the "multiplication trick" for motion polynomials within our framework. Moreover, we demonstrate that our second algorithm aligns with this trick. (3) We prove that the solvability of linear equations in the second algorithm is preserved under the extension of the ambient group. For illustration, we provide comprehensive computational examples.

papers.title: Size-preserving Cromwell equivalence for unknotted grid diagrams
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that every grid diagram representing the unknot is equivalent, via Cromwell moves which preserve the grid number, to a grid diagram with no crossings, sharpening a monotonic-simplification result of Dynnikov. Moreover, we enumerate the equivalence classes of grid diagrams for the unknot, considered up to size-preserving Cromwell moves. As an application, we generate all grid diagrams for the unknot through grid number $8$ and identify the first examples of weakly Cromwell hard grid diagrams for the unknot.

papers.title: Global solutions of the planar plasma equation with infinite $p$-mass
papers.abstract: We study entire solutions of $-Δu=u_+^p$ in the plane for $p>1$. A solution which is nondecreasing in one direction is invariant in that direction, and for each nonconstant solution in this class the plasma region $\{x:u(x)>0\}$ is a strip, the transverse profile has affine tails, and the Morse index is infinite. The stable solutions are the nonpositive constants, and the nonconstant solutions with finite Morse index are precisely the translated and scaled radial profiles of finite $p$-mass, each of which has Morse index one. We also construct a continuous branch of solutions which are periodic in one variable, depend on both variables and have infinite Morse index.

papers.title: Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis
papers.abstract: Under multivariate normality, we establish exact Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis. A polar decomposition of the centered Gaussian data matrix shows that each of these statistics is independent of the sample covariance matrix. This independence allows the moments of each statistic to be expressed as ratios of expectations involving polynomial numerators and powers of the determinant of the sample covariance matrix. The identities hold in arbitrary dimension $p$. To illustrate their use, we give exact expressions for the variance of Mardia's sample skewness and the third central moment of Mardia's sample kurtosis for $p=2$ and $p=3$. As an application of the exact variance formulas, we construct a moment-matched chi-square approximation to the null distribution of Mardia's sample skewness and compare its performance with Mardia's classical and mean-corrected approximations.

papers.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
papers.abstract: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution. We describe how task directions enter the effective signal channel through spectral activation or transport. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the transferred signal to decrease squared population risk and derive classification error bounds under margin assumptions. These results yield sufficient conditions for the same training trajectory to generalize under one evaluation distribution while failing under another. We show that differences in spectral learning rates can produce arbitrarily long delays between low training loss and low population risk. By relating classification accuracy to the distribution of margin crossing times, we construct a family of gradient flows in which the generalization delay tends to infinity, while both the duration of the transition from zero to full accuracy and the corresponding variation of population risk tend to zero. These phenomena occur without feature evolution during training. Finally, we prove that the occurrence and timing of generalization cannot generally be inferred from training dynamics alone, but depend on the geometry of evaluation transfer and its relation to the target.

papers.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
papers.abstract: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, González's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\leρ(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $ρ(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partialΔ^3,\dots,\partialΔ^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partialΔ^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex Möbius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partialΔ^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.

papers.title: BGPNP: A Non-Euclidean Gradient Projection Newton Pursuit Method for Sparsity-Constrained Optimization
papers.abstract: A non-Euclidean gradient projection Newton pursuit method is proposed for solving sparsity constrained optimization problem via the Bregman distance. The method is also denoted as BGPNP. The method firstly constructs a gradient projection step based on the Bregman distance to ensure that the iterates satisfy the sparsity constraint. Then, when the support set becomes stable or the gradient norm is sufficiently small, a Newton pursuit step is introduced to improve local convergence efficiency. The BGPNP is proved to possess a sufficient descent property and the non-increasing monotonicity of the objective function values. The full convergence and linear convergence rate of the BGPNP are established under appropriate conditions, which do not involve the symmetry coefficient of Bregman distance and the $θ$-uniform condition. Moreover, the locally quadratical convergence rate of the BGPNP is also obtained. This method provides an effective algorithmic framework for sparse optimization in non-Euclidean setting. Numerical experiments on sparsity-constrained compressed sensing problems validate the competitive performance of BGPNP compared with existing leading solvers.

papers.title: The sharp logarithmic loss in vanishing order for real planar Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: We determine, up to constants, the largest possible order of vanishing of real solutions of $Δu=Vu$ in dimension two in terms of the size of the real potential~$V$. For each sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a real potential $V\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ with $\|V\|_\infty$ comparable to $k^2/\log k$ and a smooth real solution $u$ on $\R^2$ that vanishes to order $k$ at the origin, satisfies $\sup_{B_{1/2}}|u|=\|u\|_\infty=1$, and equals a positive constant outside~$B_{7/8}$. Consequently, on every smooth connected closed Riemannian surface, the largest order of vanishing at a prescribed point for real potentials of norm at most $M$ is comparable to $\sqrt{M\log M}$ for large~$M$, uniformly in the point. This gives a negative answer, in dimension two, to the square-root questions of Kukavica and Kenig. With the same building block, we also construct a nonzero real solution on $\R^2$ with $\|V\|_\infty\le1$ and $|u(x)|\le\exp(-c|x|\sqrt{\log|x|})$ for large~$|x|$, so that the Landis conjecture fails in its exponential form in the plane even for real potentials. Both constructions match the estimates of Logunov, Malinnikova, Nadirashvili, and Nazarov, which are therefore sharp.

papers.title: Critical exponent for Nakao's problem in three space dimensions
papers.abstract: We study a system consisting of a semilinear damped wave equation coupled to a semilinear wave equation in three space dimensions. We determine the sharp condition on the exponents of nonlinear terms that separates global existence for sufficiently small initial data from finite-time blow-up even for arbitrarily small data satisfying suitable positivity assumptions. To prove global existence, we combine a weighted pointwise estimate for the damped wave equation, which we established in earlier work, with a new one for the wave equation. The new pointwise estimate for the wave equation uses a combination of a parabolic weight and a light-cone weight. For the proof of blow-up, pointwise lower bounds are compared with integral upper bounds obtained by test functions. In the main estimates, explicit physical-space representations reveal how forcing near the wave cone influences the damped component on parabolic spatial scales and, in turn, the wave component inside the cone.

papers.title: Existence of single-resonance parametric bound states in the continuum: System of Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is an eigenmode of a linear wave system with its eigen-frequency embedded in the radiation continuum of scattering states. At the frequency of a BIC, scattering problems with given incident waves from infinity lose uniqueness. Due to their close connection with strong resonance effects, BICs have found many useful applications in classical and quantum wave systems. Existence theories of BICs have been established for some cases involving the so-called symmetry-protected BICs, Friedrich-Wintgen BICs, and Fabry-Perot BICs. The single-resonance parametric BICs (srp-BICs) are another important class of BICs. Such a BIC emerges from a single resonant state through tuning a real parameter. Using a simple system of two one-dimensional Schrödinger equations, we demonstrate the formation of srp-BICs and establish a rigorous existence theory.

papers.title: A sparse bilinear form with mean oscillations
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish an oscillatory sparse domination for the bilinear forms associated with Calderón-Zygmund operators. We further characterize this oscillatory sparse domination in terms of either the boundedness of $T1$ or local endpoint Orlicz norm estimates. Our method also applies to recover Lerner's Sobolev-type inequality in \cite{L2026}.

papers.title: Variance Reduction Note 6: The Convergence of SAGA
papers.abstract: SAGA corrects a sampled component gradient with a table of previously computed gradients. Updating one entry at a time gives an unbiased gradient estimate at the cost of one new component gradient per iteration. This sixth note on variance reduction proves a linear convergence guarantee for a smooth finite sum with convex components and a strongly convex average. A two-component quadratic shows how the spread of the stored evaluation points determines the variance, even at the minimizer. We track the iterate and the table jointly to obtain a last-iterate bound, then relate its dependence on the sample size to the rate at which individual entries are replaced. For generalized linear losses the same gradient table can be represented by one scalar per observation and a running mean.

papers.title: Murmurations in Short Intervals for Elliptic Curves Ordered by Height
papers.abstract: Murmurations are the phenomenon, first observed by He, Lee, Oliver, and Pozdnyakov (2025), that the average value of $ε(E) a_p(E)$, the $p$-th $L$-function coefficient weighted by the root number, over elliptic curves of conductor in some range $N(E) \in [N_1, N_2]$ seem to approximate a continuous, oscillating function. While murmurations have been proven for other families of $L$-functions (notably by Zubrilina (2025) for weight $k$ modular forms), the only unconditional murmuration formula for elliptic curves is a partial result by Sawin and Sutherland (2025) ordering by naive height instead of conductor. In this setting, murmurations appear by first averaging $ε(E) a_p(E)$ for a single curve over $p \in (C_1, C_2)$ and then average over elliptic curves of bounded height. However, Sawin and Sutherland's results average $ε(E) a_n(E)$ over all of $\mathbb{N}$ instead of a small interval $(C_1, C_2).$ In this work, we prove how small the interval $(C_1, C_2)$ can be taken while preserving the conclusion of Sawin and Sutherland's first murmuration formula (Proposition 7).

papers.title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
papers.abstract: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, we compute the section indices and abelianizations at every sufficiently large level and obtain an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. We also give a branching criterion for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic and formulate three conjectures about the discrete action, the constants, and the case of bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices.

papers.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
papers.abstract: Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds. By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles. Our conjecture includes a correspondence for Higgs bundles twisted by sufficiently ample line bundles on curves. We discuss examples and construct Hecke actions on limit categories and, under certain conditions, on quasi-BPS categories. For symplectic surfaces, these actions are expected to provide a categorical lift of the corresponding Hecke operators on BPS cohomology constructed by Davison--Hennecart--Kinjo--Schiffmann--Vasserot.

papers.title: A Non-Commutative Binomial Theorem, Extensions, and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a matrix trace inequality analogous to the binomial theorem for reals: for Hermitian matrices $A$ and $B$, and a nonnegative even integer $k$ (and any nonnegative integer $k$ when $A, B$ are positive semi-definite), \[ \mathrm{tr}\bigl((A + B)^k\bigr) \le \sum_{\ell=0}^k \binom{k}{\ell} \mathrm{tr}\bigl(A^\ell B^{k-\ell}\bigr). \] The above natural inequality implies the classical Golden--Thompson inequality $\mathrm{tr}(e^{A + B}) \le \mathrm{tr}(e^A e^B)$. It also proves an extension, which can be used to show other new inequalities as well as give short proofs of inequalities such as the Schatten-$p$ two-point inequality for $p \ge 3$ and Hanner's inequality for $p \ge 3$. The main proof was discovered by Gemini Carbon within an agentic system.

papers.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
papers.abstract: In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks. One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks. We establish several fundamental properties of limit categories for symmetric stacks, including compact generation, the existence of semiorthogonal decompositions, functoriality, and a Kunneth formula. In a companion paper, we apply the results of this paper to formulate a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for moduli stacks of sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anticanonical divisors.

papers.title: Universal Stabilization with Six Records
papers.abstract: This letter shows that a single feedback controller needs only six retained observation records to handle the largest universally stabilizable uncertainty range for the scalar discrete-time benchmark model of Xie and Guo, when uncertainty is measured by the radius of a generalized Lipschitz ball. Existing constructions can require arbitrarily many records along bounded trajectories. Our controller retains at most six genuine state-response pairs and five auxiliary real scalars. Each update requires a uniformly bounded number of elementary operations. No knowledge of the plant, its generalized Lipschitz constants, or the disturbance bound is required.

papers.title: An answer to "Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries" by X. Wang and C. Yang
papers.abstract: We give a variant of the recent proof concerning hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundary.

papers.title: A Nonlocal Allen--Cahn Model for Volume-Constrained Wetting and Its Multi-Structure-Preserving Discretization
papers.abstract: At finite interface thickness, small droplets can shrink or disappear during wetting relaxation even when the phase-field mass is conserved. We develop a nonlocal Allen--Cahn model that couples a nonlinear diffuse-volume constraint to dynamic wall relaxation through Onsager's principle. The constraint gradient vanishes at the pure-phase values and does zero work in the energy balance, preserving the original bulk and wall dissipation structure. We construct a Compatible Variational Chain-Rule (CVC) scheme using the same discrete derivative of the volume density in the correction and in the volume increment. The scheme exactly conserves the nonlinear diffuse volume and reproduces the bulk--wall dissipation identity for the original discrete energy. Under a coercivity condition, the energy also yields a mesh-dependent maximum-norm bound. Numerical tests show second-order convergence in space and time. In flat-wall tests, the proposed model improves small-droplet retention and geometric-volume preservation and reproduces equilibrium cap shapes and contact angles. Additional tests illustrate wetting on chemically heterogeneous and rough substrates.

papers.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
papers.abstract: Ternary binding systems occur in signaling, scaffold-mediated assembly, and targeted protein degradation. A mediator brings two partners into a productive ternary complex, but excess mediator can hold them in separate binary complexes. Consequently, ternary complex formation can increase and then decrease as the mediator dose increases, producing the hook effect. Deterministic dose-response curves describe the average behavior but do not indicate whether individual small compartments reliably form the complex. A minimal reversible binding network was studied using deterministic equations, exact stochastic simulations, and a simple catalytic extension. The deterministic model recovered the hook-shaped response. In stochastic simulations, small volumes often failed to accumulate the required number of complexes, even where the deterministic prediction was favorable. At low mediator doses, failure reflected a shortage of mediator molecules; at high doses, material accumulated in free or binary-bound forms. Larger volumes increased the range of mediator doses supporting reliable formation, while stricter copy-number thresholds narrowed that range. Faster ternary-complex completion or slower breakup improved reliability. In the catalytic model, product formation also depended on how early productive complexes formed. These results show why a favorable average binding response does not necessarily ensure reliable assembly in small reaction volumes.

papers.title: Learning to Infer: Statistical Inference through Meta Learning
papers.abstract: We study meta learning for statistical inference, in which neural networks learn inference rules from simulated tasks and apply them to new datasets without parameter updates, providing a form of in-context learning. We draw on statistical decision theory to design training objectives whose population minimizers are Bayes rules and exploit their connections to classical inference procedures to establish frequentist guarantees for the learned rules. The structure of classical inference procedures also motivates the design of our neural network architecture, called Residual Recurrent Deep Sets (RRDS), which repeatedly aggregates information across observations in a permutation-invariant manner and refines its internal state through residual updates. Under suitable regularity and training conditions, we establish asymptotic efficiency in parameter estimation, consistency in model selection, and variable selection guarantees in high-dimensional regression models. The RRDS architecture allows us to avoid the curse of sample size that arises in generic neural network approximation when the network takes the entire dataset as input. For fixed-dimensional models, the network size and the number of meta training tasks need only grow polynomially in the sample size; under additional analyticity conditions, these requirements improve to polylogarithmic growth in network size and nearly linear growth in the number of training tasks. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample advantages of the learned inference rules over classical methods.

papers.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme II: multi-frequency radiation transport
papers.abstract: Conventional discrete ordinate methods are widely used for thermal radiative transfer, but their fixed number of angular degrees of freedom (DoFs) incurs unnecessary computational cost near equilibrium. We therefore develop a nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme (NCUGKS) for multi-frequency radiation transport. The scheme preserves the mul tiscale capability of UGKS through interface evolution that couples transport and collision. Radiation intensity is expanded in an orthonormal basis of the discrete angular space. The expansion coefficients serve as angular DoFs, with their number adapted independently to local nonequilibrium in each cell, frequency group, and quadrant. At each time step, the coefficients to be evolved are selected using the exponentially decayed contribution from the previous step and the requirements of interface transport. The selected coefficients are advanced by the finite volume scheme and corrected to match the macroscopic radiation energy before higher-degree coefficients are discarded according to the prescribed relative tail tolerance. Therefore, in the optically thick limit, the resulting representation retains only one angular DoF per quadrant. Numerical tests spanning different optical regimes show close agreement with reference solutions, validating its accuracy. Furthermore, in terms of memory and computational efficiency, the proposed method reduces memory by factors from 21.7 to 154.0 and achieves speedups from 24.87 to 257.9 compared with the original discrete ordinate UGKS. NCUGKS thus provides the ability to accurately simulate multiscale ra diative transfer with reduced memory and computational costs. The proposed approach also offers a framework for adapting angular degrees of freedom in other discrete ordinate methods.

papers.title: CAMPS: Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers
papers.abstract: Mixed-precision solvers usually assign a fixed precision to each algorithmic component. This makes it hard to reuse a lower-precision solver at different depths inside a higher-precision solver. We introduce CAMPS (Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers), a framework that uses iterative refinement to connect solvers across precisions. An adapter computes residuals and updates in the precision of its parent and passes each correction solve to a child solver in a lower precision. The child can be a direct solver, an iterative solver, or another adapter. The adapter checks every correction and keeps it if the residual does not increase. We prove three results. Adapters can be placed at any compatible set of precision boundaries in a solver tree without breaking the solver interface. Every output that the root solver reports as successful satisfies a backward-error bound set by the stopping tolerance and the root precision. Convergence follows from one sufficient condition per boundary, computed from the leaves of the tree to its root. We test five configurations on dense and sparse systems in 64-bit, 32-bit, and 16-bit floating-point arithmetic (FP64, FP32, and FP16). On dense well-conditioned systems, CAMPS is up to 9.6x faster than an FP64 direct solver for a single solve that includes the factorization. On sparse nonsymmetric systems, a three-precision hierarchy is the fastest method we tested. Compared with our implementation of the nested solver F3R, CAMPS is as fast and uses about 3.4x less peak memory. CAMPS does not always win. Plain conjugate gradient is faster on sparse symmetric positive definite systems. On very ill-conditioned systems, FP32 corrections fail, and the adapter detects the failure and switches to an FP64 fallback.

papers.title: Low treebandwidth colorings, $p$-centred colorings and generalized coloring numbers
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $p$, let $χ^{tb}_p(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a vertex coloring such that every subgraph induced by $i$ color classes has treebandwidth at most $i-1$, for $1\le i\le p$. We establish quantitative relationships between these coloring parameters and generalized coloring numbers. If $\operatorname{wcol}_{2p}(G)\le m$, then $G$ admits a $p$-centred coloring with at most $[(p+1)m]^m$ colors; in particular, $χ^{tb}_p(G)\le[(p+1)m]^m$. Conversely, if $χ^{tb}_{k+1}(G)\le m$, then $\col_k(G) \le 1+4k^4\binom{m}{k+1}^{2}.$ Consequently, a graph class has bounded expansion if and only if its low treebandwidth coloring numbers are uniformly bounded for every fixed parameter. This gives a characterization of bounded expansion in terms of colorings defined by bounded ancestor distances in rooted forest layouts.

papers.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
papers.abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact Kähler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.

papers.title: The finiteness of $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, motivated by J.-P. Demailly's finiteness argument, we establish a criterion for a closed linear operator between Hilbert spaces to have closed range of finite codimension. We then apply this criterion to give affirmative answers to two questions of T. Ohsawa on the finiteness of $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups in a unified manner. To this end, we adapt Demailly's compactness argument to a family of complete approximating metrics, thereby establishing the finite dimensionality of the $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups with respect to a possibly incomplete metric. Furthermore, we extend the answers to the setting of singular metrics with quasi-plurisubharmonic local weights.

papers.title: Topological Clique Exclusion in Positively Curved Graphs
papers.abstract: We study locally finite graphs of positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and minimum degree at least $t-1$ under two exclusions: a topological $K_t$, denoted $TK_t$, and its locally topological version $TK^{(\leq2)}_t$, in which every replacement path has length at most two. The ordinary exclusion gives an $O(t^{7})$ maximum-degree bound by combining the classical density theorem for topological cliques with a curvature-driven rainbow-clique argument. For $K_t$-minor-free graphs, a Hall-matching refinement improves the maximum-degree bound to $O(t^3(\log t)^{3/2})$ and, for connected graphs, the order bound to $O(t^{19}(\log t)^9)$. For the weaker local exclusion, a codegree graph and Ramsey's theorem give the bound $\exp(O(t\log t))$. We also prove an exponential maximum-degree bound when the full 1-subdivision $K_t^{(2)}$ is forbidden as a subgraph, assuming minimum degree at least $t$.

papers.title: Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
papers.abstract: In this paper two long standing open questions are addressed for the first time. Those questions are about Lipschitz stability estimates and uniqueness theorems for two Coefficient Inverse Problems (CIPs) for 3-Dimensional wave-like Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with formally determined input data. We assume that a certain associated PDE is written in finite differences with respect to time t. The unknown coefficients depend on all three spatial variables. The key novelty here is that the input data for these CIPs are generated by only a single location of the point source at the moment of time {t = 0}. In the first CIP (CIP1) the unknown coefficient is the potential of a wave-like PDE. The second CIP (CIP2) is concerned with a far more challenging case when the unknown coefficient is involved in the principal part of the hyperbolic operator. In addition to Lipschitz stability and uniqueness results, numerical methods are developed for both CIPs. Their convergence analysis establishes the global convergence property of both numerical techniques. The latter is unlike the local convergence of conventional numerical procedures for CIPs. The method for CIP1 is tested computationally. Its extensive numerical testing for complicated media structures consistently demonstrates a very accurate performance of this method for noisy input data. The authors declare that artificial intelligence was not used for any part of this work.

papers.title: The maximum number of triangles in a graph without pentagons
papers.abstract: The generalized Turán number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. Inspired by a conjecture of Erdős on the function $\ex(n,C_5,K_3)$, Bollobás and Gy\H ori proposed the problem of $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)$. In this paper, we prove that $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)=(1/(3\sqrt3)+o(1))n^{3/2}$, finally solved this problem. As applications, we determine the asymptotic value of $\ex(n,\{\text{ind-}C_4,C_{5}\})$ which answers a question of Ergemlidze, Győri and Methuku, and the asymptotic value of 3-uniform hypergraph without Berge short cycle which solve a conjecture of Győri and Salia.

papers.title: A fast tangential rational Krylov subspace method with randomized sketching for large Lyapunov matrix equations
papers.abstract: We propose a tangential rational Krylov subspace method augmented with randomized sketching for solving continuous-time Lyapunov equations $AX + XA^T + BB^T = 0$, where $A$ is large and sparse and $B$ has a rank much higher than one. Numerical solutions require high-dimensional rational Krylov subspaces (e.g., of dimensions up to $\sim 1000$), leading to substantial computational cost and long runtime. Building on the adaptive strategies of [SIAM\,J.\,Matrix\,Anal.\,Appl., 35\,(2014), pp.\,476--498], which expand the subspace using the most relevant directions, we introduce several enhancements: selective orthogonalization of basis vectors and fast residual-norm estimation enabled by randomized sketching, and the option to use either adaptive distinct poles or a small set of repeated poles. We derive a new computable error bound for the approximate solutions and show that sketching does not degrade the convergence rate relative to the standard (non-sketched) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved robustness and efficiency, with reduced runtimes and often higher accuracy than the standard tangential method.

papers.title: A Stackelberg strategy for the semi-linear heat equation with boundary controls
papers.abstract: This work continues the results presented in \cite{calsavara2022new} where a hierarchical control problem is solved. Our first goal is the case of both controls acting on the boundary. The follower control solves a null controllability problem, and the leader minimizes a $L^2$ cost functional. Additionally, we solve the case where one control acts on the boundary and the other on an open subset of the domain. More precisely, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a leader-follower couple and give some techniques to solve the problem.

papers.title: Generalized oriented chromatic numbers and directed generalized coloring numbers of graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $q$, we bound the $q$-transitive oriented chromatic number $χ_o^q(G)$ in terms of the directed weak coloring number $\overrightarrow{wcol}_{2q}(G)$. For orientations with no directed cycle of length at most $2q$, we compare $q$-transitive oriented colorings with $\vec P_{2q}$-preserving oriented colorings. We also show that the directed strong coloring number at radius $2k-1$ bounds the density of every depth-$(k-1)$ shallow topological minor of $G$. These results characterize bounded expansion in terms of directed coloring numbers, oriented colorings, and homomorphisms of acyclic orientations.

papers.title: Anderson-Accelerated Landweber Iteration with Regularization Guarantees for Nonlinear Ill-Posed Problems
papers.abstract: Anderson acceleration (AA) can markedly reduce iteration counts for fixed-point solvers, but its unrestricted signed history extrapolation need not preserve the stability required for iterative regularization of ill-posed problems. We introduce a regularization-guaranteed Anderson-accelerated Landweber method (\RG) in which finite-memory AA generates a proposal while the committed iterate is a controlled perturbation of a certified Landweber anchor. Under a local tangential cone condition and a scale-normalized localization condition, we prove strong convergence of the exact-data trajectory to a solution, stability at every fixed iteration, finite discrepancy stopping, and strong convergence of the discrepancy-stopped noisy reconstructions to the same exact-data limit; local uniqueness is needed only if that selected limit is to be identified with a prescribed solution $x^\dagger$. Under the additional benchmark source condition $x^\dagger-x_0=F'(x^\dagger)^*λ^\dagger$ and a standard range-invariance condition, we obtain the discrepancy-principle rate $\norm{x_{k_δ}^δ-x^\dagger}=O(δ^{1/2})$. The rate proof controls data-dependent Anderson coefficients through fixed memory, a fixed-reference ridge in the small AA least-squares problem, and an outer correction budget with an $O(k^{-1})$ tail. The numerical examples verify the efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
papers.abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

papers.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal. We show that $S$ is not aspherical. As a corollary the universal cover of $S$ is not the bidisk $\mathbf{H}\times\mathbf{H}$.

papers.title: Symmetric identities and determinants for matrices composed of Legendre symbols
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a series of identities and evaluate the determinants for a class of matrices composed of Legendre symbols given by Sun [10, Conjecture 3.2 (i)]. Together with [6] which proved Conjecture 3.2 (ii) in [10], these results provide a more general approach for a complete proof of Conjecture 3.2 in [10].

papers.title: Graded Monoidal Categories and Internalization
papers.abstract: In stable homotopy theory, there are a variety of ways to construct a point-set level smash product of spectra, each with its own advantages and limitations. These constructions often involve internalizing some graded external product. In this paper, we aim to formalize this process through a general categorical framework, providing a common language for these constructions. We propose a general theory for internalizing a graded monoidal product, investigate its 2-categorical properties, and use this framework to recover both Day convolution and the smash product of $S$-modules.

papers.title: On the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point for the Yamabe equation in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point of solutions to the Yamabe equation in every dimension $n\ge 25$. On every closed, connected, smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $M$ of positive Yamabe type and at any prescribed point $p\in M$, we construct a smooth metric $ \widehat g$ and a sequence of smooth positive solutions to the Yamabe equation blowing up at $p$, such that the first nonzero covariant derivative of the Weyl tensor at $p$ has any prescribed order $l$ satisfying $l\ge 6$ when $25\le n\le 29$, $l \ge 4$ when $30\le n\le 51$, and $l\ge 2$ when $n\ge 52$. Moreover, $|\nabla_{ \widehat g}^{l}W_{ \widehat g}|>0$ everywhere on $M$. Earlier constructions realize every strictly higher order as the first nonzero order, while the known Weyl vanishing results exclude every lower first nonzero order. Thus the endpoint cases $l=6,4,2$ were the only ones left open, and are settled here. In particular, the order-two examples show that the compactness criterion $|W|+|\nabla W|>0$ is sharp. At the endpoints, the construction arranges global and localized metric perturbations to interact at leading order in a limiting functional. For $l=2,4$, anisotropic polynomial ansatzes involving two orthogonal algebraic Weyl tensors remove a distinguished translation degeneracy and produce $C^1$-stable saddle points. For $l=6$, a different polynomial ansatz produces a nondegenerate local minimum. Higher prescribed orders are obtained by separating the perturbation that determines the limiting functional from the one that prescribes the Weyl derivative.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Multiplayer Differential Games
papers.abstract: Computing per-player feedback strategies in $N$-player adversarial differential games is challenging as the associated coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system is high-dimensional and generally lacks classical solutions. We address this by approximating viscosity solutions using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with a vanishing-viscosity annealing schedule. Theoretically, we establish an explicit $\varepsilon$-Nash guarantee by bounding per-player regret via computable residuals and prove our method reaches this stopping criterion in finite time. For two-player zero-sum games, we further establish a computable bound on the approximation error of the value function. Numerical experiments on pursuit-evasion scenarios illustrate the tightness of these computed bounds and the framework's scalability to high-dimensional environments.

papers.title: On the rigidity of generalized cylinders
papers.abstract: We prove pointed Gromov--Hausdorff rigidity of cylinders $N\times\mathbb R^d$ whenever $N$ is a compact Einstein manifold rigid as a Ricci shrinker.

papers.title: Simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this paper we provide a partial classification (necessary conditions) for all possible simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be such an abelian variety, i.e. $A$ is simple over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and splits as $A \sim B^s$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ for some simple abelian variety $B$. Assume that $d$ is a minimal extension degree over which $A$ splits and $B$ has a minimal field of definition (up to isogeny) $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}\subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$. For dimension $2$, Howe and Zhu showed that the only possible degrees $d$ are $2$, $3$, $4$, and $6$. Moreover, for each such degree $d$, they provided explicit formulae expressing the isogeny invariant, namely the characteristic polynomial of the Frobenius endomorphism $χ_{A,q}$, in terms of the coeffients of $χ_{B,q}$. We extend this result to ordinary abelian varieties of higher dimension. For dimensions $3$--$10$, we provide complete lists of such varieties as components of the Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ together with all possible triples $(d, e, s)$ and restrictions on characteristic polynomial $χ_{A,q}$ of the form $χ_{A, q} \mid χ_{V, q}$. Here, $V$ is a component of Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ containing $A$ as an isogeny factor and having explicit expression of the characteristic polynomial $χ_{V,q}$ in terms of coefficients of $χ_{B,q^e}$. For higher dimensions, we propose an algorithm for enumeration of all possible cases for a given dimension of $A$. We also provide an implementation of this algorithm.

papers.title: Extension complexity is not additive under Cartesian products
papers.abstract: We prove that the linear extension complexity of a Cartesian product of polytopes can be strictly smaller than the sum of the extension complexities of its factors. This disproves Conjecture 1.2 of Grande, Padrol and Sanyal. We construct a rational 24-dimensional polytope $P$ with 50 facets and 150 vertices such that $P$ has extension complexity 40 and $P \times P$ has extension complexity exactly 79. We also prove that the saving can be arbitrarily large, even in a Cartesian square: for every $t$ there is a rational polytope $R_t$ whose square needs at least $t$ fewer inequalities than two separate copies of $R_t$. For two different factors, we construct a family whose product saves at least $\lceil 5n/27 \rceil$ inequalities while the two separate complexities sum to $O(n)$, so that the saving is a constant fraction of the total. The proofs rest on a transfer theorem: wedging over the omitted facets of a polytope turns a gap between the nonnegative ranks of partial slack matrices into a gap between extension complexities. The unbounded squares come from intersecting families of sets on successively larger alphabets. In the square the two copies of each coordinate share generators, while a counting lemma determines the exact cost of a single factor.

papers.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{α,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_α^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $α$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^α$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $Λ_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_α^\infty\to\mathcal B^{α+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<α\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{α,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.

papers.title: Reeb stability for singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We prove a global Reeb stability theorem for singular Riemannian foliations on compact connected manifolds using the semi-local model developed by Alexandrino et al. We show that all leaves are compact if and only if the foliation is infinitesimally closed, and there exists a compact leaf with a linear holonomy groupoid which is proper at that leaf. These conditions are also equivalent to the existence of a smooth map to a Euclidean space whose fibers are exactly the leaves. The proof combines a local criterion for strong stability with compact transverse leaves, Molino's structural theory, and polynomial descriptions of local leaf spaces. Around a closed leaf, we show that the linear holonomy groupoid realizes the original foliation precisely when the infinitesimal foliation is homogeneous. When the infinitesimal foliation is closed, properness of this groupoid yields an associated-bundle model whose compact structure group is its isotropy group. We also characterize the existence, near a compact leaf, of a Hausdorff model Lie groupoid which is proper at that leaf. As an application, we obtain stability results for maps whose connected fiber components form singular Riemannian foliations. We compare linear holonomy with Fernandes's reduced Lie algebroid holonomy and with formal outer holonomy. Finally, we prove that, for every infinitesimally closed singular Riemannian foliation, the compactly supported tangent vector fields form a locally finitely generated involutive module inducing the original leaf partition.

papers.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.

papers.title: A Robust Approach for Regression Analysis of Panel Count Data with Time-varying Covariates
papers.abstract: The validity of statistical inference for panel count data with time-varying covariates depends on the correct specification of within-subject correlation structures; misspecification often leads to questionable inference. To alleviate, robust inference has been proposed for mean models, which implicitly assume monotone mean functions. When covariate values fluctuate with time, however, the assumed monotonicity becomes unrealistic. In this research, we propose a robust inference based on rate models that are free of such constraints. Since the asymptotic variance has no closed form under the rate model, we further develop computationally efficient robust variance estimators using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, thus sidestepping the need for computationally intensive numerical methods, which could undermine the robustness. Rigorous theoretical development is provided in support of parameter estimation and inference. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method. We present a real clinical application to illustrate the use of the proposed method.

papers.title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.

papers.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
papers.abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and étale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.

papers.title: Cohomology growth for pseudoeffective line bundles on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a pseudoeffective line bundle with a singular metric $h$ satisfying $Θ_h(L)\geq0$ on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$. Let $\mathcal{I}(h^k)$ denote the multiplier ideal sheaf of $h^k$. For every holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and $0\le q\le n$, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim}_{\mathbb{C}}H^q\!\left(X,E\otimes L^k\otimes\mathcal{I}(h^k)\right)=O(k^{n-q}),$$ which gives an affirmative answer to Matsumura's growth problem. As an application, we resolve the cohomology growth problem for nef line bundles raised by Demailly.

papers.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Solving the capacitated vehicle routing problem with polygonal neighborhoods using a metaheuristic enhanced with block coordinate descent
papers.abstract: We study a capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) in which customers are represented by planar regions, called customer neighborhoods, rather than fixed points. Visiting a customer consists of selecting a point within its neighborhood. Therefore, besides determining the sequence of customers visited by each vehicle, one must also determine the corresponding visit points. To better reflect practical applications, customer neighborhoods are allowed to be simple polygons, either convex or non-convex, and distances are measured using the Euclidean norm. Applications include aerial reconnaissance, wireless sensor data collection and inspection, and two-stage delivery systems. We propose a general variable neighborhood search framework in which each neighbor is represented by a collection of routes. Constructing a route involves two stages, defining a customer sequence and then determining the associated visit points. The latter task is solved by a block coordinate descent (BCD) procedure, the central methodological contribution of this work, which computes high-quality visit points at a cost low enough to be used repeatedly inside the search. In extensive experiments on newly generated and adapted benchmark instances, within the time limits considered, the proposed framework matches all solutions proven optimal by CPLEX and matches or improves the best solutions found by CPLEX in the remaining instances. For the instances adapted from the CVRP literature, it also improves, in every instance, a CVRP-based upper bound given by the solution of the original CVRP instance reported in the literature, which is feasible for the problem with neighborhoods.

papers.title: Co-amenability and local reflexivity of $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset B$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras. We prove that local reflexivity passes from $A$ to $B$ if the inclusion $A^{**}\subset B^{**}$ is co-amenable.
