It follows that local reflexivity is preserved by minimal tensor products with exact $C^*$-algebras, by inductive limits over directed sets, and by reduced crossed products by discrete amenable groups. We also prove that reduced free products with respect to states with faithful GNS representations preserve local reflexivity and that every locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra embeds into a simple locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra. These results answer Questions~(b), (c), (d), (f) and~(h) in Kirchberg's 2011 list.

papers.title: Reflections in graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce and study an operation on graphs, called edge reflection, modeled on the effect of a reflection on the inversion graph of a permutation. The edge reflection length of a graph counts the fewest edge reflections needed to reduce it to the edgeless graph. Emptying a graph one edge at a time, or one vertex at a time, gives two upper bounds on this length, and each holds with equality precisely when the graph is a forest. For the edge bound we say more: the cyclomatic number of the graph bounds, above and below, the difference between the graph's size and its edge reflection length. Returning to permutations, we show that the edge reflection length of an inversion graph is at most the reflection length of any permutation realizing it, with equality whenever each connected component of the inversion graph has cyclomatic number at most one.

papers.title: PACL: Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting framework for bound-preserving compact single-step DG methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: We develop a Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting (PACL) framework for compact single-step discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws. The key idea is to establish admissibility of weighted averages over overlapping cell patches after a complete high-order time step. Continuous patch weights cancel interior numerical flux contributions, yielding admissibility estimates for weighted patch averages under suitable time-step conditions. A conservative patch correction uses these averages as reference states to obtain admissible physical cell averages, and a subsequent cellwise scaling enforces whole-cell or nodal admissibility in the original DG space. The framework requires neither a strong-stability-preserving decomposition nor auxiliary first-order discretizations, and all limiting is performed at the end of each time step. For scalar conservation laws, we prove a patchwise weak maximum principle for compact Runge--Kutta DG (cRKDG), ADER-DG with converged or fixed-Picard predictors, and Lax--Wendroff DG. We also prove that, under the stated local mesh and scaling assumptions, a single application of the scalar limiter preserves approximation order at active bounds, including flat extrema. For the compressible Euler equations, we establish patch admissibility for cRKDG and fixed-Picard ADER-DG under time-step conditions that maintain positive predictor density while allowing nonpositive predictor pressure. The analysis covers both exact spatial integration and compatible quadrature. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and bound preservation, including problems with near-vacuum states and strong shocks.

papers.title: Spectral bounds of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems: monotonicity, domain limits, and applications
papers.abstract: We study the spectral bound of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems on bounded domains. The spectral bound is continuous under uniform coefficient and suitable nested domain perturbations, and strictly monotone with respect to the coefficients and the domain if either corresponding operator admits a principal eigenvalue. Further results include small-domain limits, large-domain limits for even convolution kernels under suitable coefficient assumptions, and criteria for a unique critical domain size. Applications yield a unique extinction-persistence threshold in the interval length for a heterogeneous epidemic model and a sharp spreading-vanishing threshold for a scalar free-boundary problem. These thresholds remain valid when the spectral bound vanishes on an interval, with the critical habitat length given by its right endpoint.

papers.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.

papers.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
papers.abstract: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points. We prove that the sign of each passive eigenvalue equals the sign of the extinct species' density in the enlarged community, that every partial community containing $X_1$ is a saddle with one unstable direction for each extinct consumer, and that the coexistence state is the only stable fixed point. A WKB treatment of the master equation gives a $2N$-dimensional Hamiltonian whose fluctuational fixed points are obtained in closed form. The resulting extinction network has $3^{N-1}$ fluctuation-driven transitions, and its coarse-grained dynamics yield an exact recursion for every mean extinction time. We analyse the three-species omnivory module in full, including a minimal set of existence conditions, global stability of coexistence, numerical instanton actions for all nine transitions and the most probable extinction route, which we confirm with stochastic simulations. Finally, we show how deleting a single trophic link reshapes the extinction network.

papers.title: Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
papers.abstract: We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. For three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. Below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. At and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. We also quantify the cost of control. The minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted Fourier norm of its periodised defect. For a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of Fourier degree at most $N$ grows linearly in $N$, i.e. Liouville ratios produce superpolynomial growth along subsequences. We derive constructive approximation estimates and sharp worst-case cost--accuracy rates on Sobolev classes of defects. For an arbitrary number of sources, the long-time classification and the quantitative estimates are governed by simultaneous Diophantine approximation of the source positions.

papers.title: An iterative procedure for statistical calibration
papers.abstract: We study the iterative proportional fitting procedure (IPFP) under multiple pushforward constraints, motivated by model calibration. The goal is to find a distribution on model parameters whose pushforward by models matches data distributions. The classic convergence result of IPFP under marginal constraints establish convergence of IPFP under suitable regularity conditions and develop a variant of sequential importance sampling to approximate the iterative procedure. We also propose a related procedure for constructing a high probability parameter region. Simulation studies illustrate the performance of these methods. Finally, we apply IPFP to COVID19 ensemble forecasting. Variation of Covid strains across regions can lead to variation in surge rates and thus affect forecasting accuracy. To capture the variation, we estimate a probability distribution of epidemiological model parameters using early stage surge data from an ensemble of regions. We then propagate the distribution through the model to forecast both the ensemble's overall trend and its variability.

papers.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
papers.abstract: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

papers.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_θ$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<θ<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.

papers.title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
papers.abstract: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast iteration to control a certain fluid-scaled relative entropy error that arises in the ODE approximation. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm and compare it with the existing risk-sensitive Q-learning algorithms.

papers.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the Néron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.

papers.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $α\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(α)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(α)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.

papers.title: Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
papers.abstract: After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

papers.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
papers.abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical pair with $X$ of Fano type, $-(K_X+B)$ nef and coefficients of $B$ in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all $ε$-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of $ε$. We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral $\Q$-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.

papers.title: Hadwigerś Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $λ\in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (λK + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
papers.abstract: We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees. For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings. Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $ν$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

papers.title: The polygonal Weinstock inequality and quantitative stability
papers.abstract: For every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes the perimeter-normalized first positive Steklov eigenvalue $J(P) = |\partial P|σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity. More generally, if $P$ has $p$ strictly convex vertices and $q$ reflex vertices after merging consecutive collinear sides, then $J(P) \le J(R_{p+\min(q,2)})$, with equality if and only if $q = 0$ and $P$ is similar to $R_p$. Among polygons with at most $N$ sides, restricting to those that are nonconvex or have fewer than $N$ genuine sides lowers the supremum of $J$ by $12πζ(3)N^{-4} + O(N^{-5})$ as $N \to \infty$, with a positive gap for every $N \ge 4$. For convex $p$-gons, the spectral deficit $J(R_p) - J(P)$ controls the normalized squared deviations of support heights, midpoint offsets, and side lengths with weights $1$, $p^{-2}$, and $p^{-3}$, as well as $p^{-3}$ times the sum of squared exterior-angle deviations from $2π/p$; the length weight $p^{-3}$ is sharp. For triangles, the deficit is instead comparable to the square root of the relative area deficit at fixed perimeter, or equivalently to $1 - r$, where $r$ is the singular-value ratio of an affine map from an equilateral triangle. Independently of the number of reflex vertices, a boundary phase identity in arc-length balanced disk coordinates yields the sharp fourth-order bound $2π/J(P) - 1 \ge 2ζ(3)p^{-3} + 8ζ(4)p^{-4} + O(p^{-5})$. For fixed $p$, a degree-$p$ Blaschke transport links this identity to $H^{1/p}$ coercivity for the regularized square root of the conformal derivative, perimeter-concentration rigidity at equally spaced convex prevertices, and quadratic Hausdorff stability for $p \ge 4$.

papers.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
papers.abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

papers.title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
papers.abstract: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

papers.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
papers.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

papers.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
papers.abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $ζ_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.

papers.title: The cost functional for hyperbolic systems of conservation laws
papers.abstract: For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. This extends the analysis of arXiv:2611.30663 from scalar conservation laws to $n \times n$ systems.

papers.title: A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
papers.abstract: We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.

papers.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
papers.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. To solve the resulting large-scale linear systems, we introduce an incomplete LU (ILU)-preconditioned sketched GMRES (sGMRES) method as the solver. As far as we know, this work is the first to apply the randomized sGMRES to the practical simulations in the engineering. By reducing the cost of the global orthogonalization, ILU-sGMRES achieves greater computational efficiency than ILU-GMRES while maintaining the accuracy, particularly at relatively large values of the restart. Specifically, numerical tests demonstrate that ILU-sGMRES can reduce the end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 25.38\% on a single machine and up to 11.71\% in a three-node benchmark compared with the conventional ILU-GMRES, while maintaining a maximum relative difference across plasma fields of only 0.194\%. Numerical experiments compare the performance of different numerical schemes and solvers, demonstrating the robustness of ILU-sGMRES in the real simulation.

papers.title: Sampling with graph wavelet kernels: optimality and adaptivity to regularity and geometry
papers.abstract: We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. These samplers satisfy the same variance reduction for linear statistics of $s$-Hölder observables and yield conditionally unbiased estimators of empirical averages with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$, using at most $2n$ function evaluations. In both settings, the rates are governed by the intrinsic dimension $m$ and the regularity $s$ of the observable.

papers.title: A note on approximate projection onto the semidefinite complementarity set
papers.abstract: The proximal slack update in an augmented Lagrangian method for semidefinite complementarity constraints requires a joint matrix projection. Given real symmetric matrices $A$ and $B$, we seek the nearest pair $(X,Z)$ with $X$ positive semidefinite, $Z$ negative semidefinite, and $XZ=0$. Hou, Peng and Ding obtain a squared-loss factor of $2$ by fitting the pair in an eigenbasis of $A+B$. To improve this bound, we replace the orthogonal projector onto the subspace allowed for $X$ by a symmetric matrix $T$ with eigenvalues in $[0,1]$. From an optimal solution of the resulting semidefinite program, we form candidate subspaces by starting at the zero subspace and adding the eigenspaces of $T$ in decreasing order of eigenvalue. For each candidate, we compress $A$ to that subspace and $B$ to its orthogonal complement. We keep the positive eigenvalues of the first compression and the negative eigenvalues of the second. The best pair has squared loss at most $1.189$ times the minimum for arbitrary inputs and at most $1.15487$ times the minimum when $A$ is positive semidefinite and $B$ is negative semidefinite. For arbitrary inputs the factor improves to $1.18$ if $T$ has at most two distinct eigenvalues in $(0,1)$. The threshold-rounding proofs average over a uniform spectral threshold and use computer-assisted bounds for the resulting scalar inequalities.

papers.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
papers.abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

papers.title: Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
papers.abstract: The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: A unipotent witness: vanishing orders of word maps on SU(2) and lengths in the lower central series
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$, $k\ge2$ and $1\ne w\inγ_k(F_n)$, the $k$-th term of the lower central series of the free group of rank $n$. We prove that a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$ has at least $2k$ cyclic syllables, so $w$ has word length at least $2k$; the previous linear bound, due to Malestein and Putman, is $k$. For $1\ne w\in[F_n,F_n]$ we also prove that the word map of $w$ on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ vanishes at the identity to order at most $T/2$, where $T$ is the number of cyclic syllables of a cyclically reduced conjugate of $w$, with equality for $[x_1,x_2]$ and for words with six and eight syllables. Both proofs evaluate $w$ at unipotent matrices $I+tN_i$, with $N_i$ nilpotent of rank one, and compare the degree of the trace of the resulting matrix $M(t)\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z}[t])$ with the order of vanishing of $M(t)-I$ at $t=0$.

papers.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous étale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, where $Ω_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $Ω_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{ét}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.

papers.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
papers.abstract: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fifteen-node quotient. Applying a rational Kuga-Satake criterion, we establish abelianity of Chow motives for explicit infinite arithmetic subfamilies of all three Garbagnati-Sarti lattice types, including their Picard-rank specializations. Finally, we prove a square-Franchetta theorem for the ten-dimensional family of double-cubic K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
papers.abstract: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN drives the pre-polish trajectory-minimum raw QPU sample violation to $0.108 \pm 0.017$ at 4,560 qubits (83.3% exact feasibility after a deterministic 1-bit polish with best-incumbent tracking, reaching 47.3% of the continuous linear-programming relaxation bound), reduces high-constraint error by 6.1- to 20.1-fold over K-scaled first-order updates, attains 5.35-fold deeper feasible energies than linear programming with the identical 1-bit polish within a 4.10-s compute-only budget at 256 spins, and achieves 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the workflow is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

papers.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
papers.abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

papers.title: Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
papers.abstract: We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of Àlvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $λ_{p,q}(\kk[Δ])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.

papers.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
papers.abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}, \] which is tight up to the constant in the exponent, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.

papers.title: A Generalized Lefschetz Degree with applications to Fixed Point Theory
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a class of spaces, named Lefschetz admissible, where the identity maps on compacts can be approximated by certain maps with values in Lefschetz spaces in a suitable sense. For maps defined on these spaces, we introduce a generalized Lefschetz degree obtained as the set of accumulation points of usual Lefschetz degrees for the approximant maps in a certain compactification. We show that when the degree is nonempty, fixed point results hold. We consider both the situation of spaces embedded in topological vector spaces (TVSs) as global and as neighborhood retracts. As two consequences, we obtain a generalization of a fixed point result due to Browder, and a no-retraction criterion for compact subsets of locally convex TVSs.

papers.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvořák, Masařík, Musílek and Pangrác and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvořák, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $ε$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.

papers.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let \(1<p\le2\). We prove that the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant has supremum \(p\), already over finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. This settles the sharpness question of Areshidze~\cite{aresh}, who improved the bound \(π/\sqrt{2}\) of Ivanisvili et al.~\cite{ivv} to \(p\). We also study orthogonal families in a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] If \(p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] Uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(s\) for every \(1\le s<p\), with a quadratic bound in the restricted type constant at \(s=2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} We also record the subcritical type implication for Pythagorean orthogonality and the sharp factor \(p\) for Roberts orthogonality. {For the exponents in (a), as the modulus of roundness \(ν_X(p)\) approaches \(2\), the ratio of the Enflo to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant tends uniformly to \(1\) over real Banach spaces of Rademacher type \(p\). The same limit holds for the ratio of the two constants restricted by mutual Birkhoff--James orthogonality.}

papers.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
papers.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

papers.title: Local energy decay for small radial solutions of the two-dimensional Hamiltonian $abcd$ Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: We consider the $abcd$ Boussinesq system in two space dimensions, a four-parameter family of models for the two-way propagation of small-amplitude long surface waves, in the generic regime $a,c<0$, $b,d>0$. We first revisit the local well-posedness theory in Sobolev spaces in dimensions $2\le n\le4$ and show that for the Hamiltonian case $b=d$ the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed for small data in the energy space $\mathbb{H}^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Then we consider the asymptotic behavior of these global solutions in the $n=2$ case. Under the condition $-a,-c>b/9$, we prove that every small solution with radial symmetry exhibits local energy decay. As a consequence, there are no small radial time-periodic (in particular, stationary) solutions. Decay also holds, along sequences of times, on balls whose radius grows almost linearly in time. The proof is based on new virial identities adapted to the radial structure of the system. In the proof we introduce two correction functionals such that the resulting quadratic form is coercive precisely when $-a,-c>b/9$, a threshold which is sharp for the functional. To our knowledge this is the first result describing the long-time dynamics of $abcd$ systems in dimension two.

papers.title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
papers.abstract: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.

papers.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
papers.abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

papers.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
papers.abstract: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics. Accurate simulations require coupling conditions that preserve underlying symmetries of the microscale equation. Failing to preserve such symmetries may result in an unphysical macroscale simulation that does not satisfy required conservation laws. Here we develop equation-free modelling that preserves self-adjoint symmetry for microscale models defined by a compact self-adjoint operator on a bounded domain with fixed boundary conditions. This new design for equation-free modelling greatly increases the range of systems for which equation-free modelling is applicable.

papers.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$, answering the question of \cite{CLMP}. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: A nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring with finitely based matrix semirings
papers.abstract: We establish that the matrix semiring $\mathbf{M}_n(SR_6)$ over the six-element nonfinitely based additively idempotent semiring $SR_6$ is finitely based for every $n \geq 2$. This provides the first known example of an additively idempotent semiring $S$ that is nonfinitely based, while the matrix semirings $\mathbf{M}_n(S)$ are finitely based. Moreover, we show that the interval $[\mathsf{V}(SR_6), \mathsf{V}(\mathbf{M}_2(SR_6))]$ in the lattice of additively idempotent semiring varieties has the cardinality of the continuum.

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $α$-bundles and $β$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.

papers.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, in the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS)[13], which combines architectural layout, people movement and airborne viral transmission, aerosol concentrations are assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation. Also, particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we extend VIRIS to the VIRIS-3D-L framework to investigate how these two assumptions affect the predicted infection risk. In VIRIS-3D-L, we solve the reaction-diffusion equation in three dimensions (3D), and aerosol deposition is represented by local surface removal through a Robin boundary condition. We compare VIRIS with VIRIS-3D-L across three indoor settings of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. For the courtroom, care home, and supermarket, respectively, at the end of the simulation, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts average infection risks across individuals of 44%, 78%, and 25%, while VIRIS-3D-L predicts risks of 51%, 85%, and 28%. Thus, VIRIS significantly underestimates infection risk in all three settings. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show agreement with a documented courtroom outbreak that was used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between eight minutes and just under 1.5 hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk in indoor spaces without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Stabilization of zero forcing numbers of finite quotients of periodic graphs
papers.abstract: We give a method for determining the zero forcing number of a graph by passing to an infinite cover. When the quotient map is a covering map, forcing commutes with taking preimages. If, in addition, the closure of every small set in the cover touches none of its translates, then no small set is a zero forcing set of the quotient. For covers that are periodic, this condition reduces to a property of the cover alone, and it gives an explicit threshold beyond which the zero forcing number of the quotient equals that of the cover. We apply the method to the generalized Petersen graphs: $Z(P(n,k))=2k+2$ for all $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We also show that the circulant $C_n(1,a)$ has zero forcing number $2a$ for all $n\ge 2a^2-a+1$.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every noncommutative polynomial in independent GUE matrices, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges almost surely to the Brown measure of the same polynomial in free semicircular variables. This is the Gaussian case of a conjecture of Belinschi, Śniady and Speicher. We also prove that the spectrum converges almost surely in Hausdorff distance to the spectrum of the limiting operator, so that the spectral radius converges as well; deviations have probability smaller than every inverse power of the matrix size. For this we show that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables is its whole spectrum, a statement about operators that involves no random matrices. We also give an algorithm, with a convergence guarantee, that computes the limiting Brown measure from matrices whose size depends only on the polynomial. A holomorphic rotation introduces an independent Ginibre component and yields the almost-sure limit without a least-singular-value bound for the original GUE polynomial. We also give a second-moment criterion for weak convergence of Brown measures. On free probability side, we use the Dyson equation of a linear pencil to show that harmonicity of its logarithmic potential forces invertibility.

papers.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a non-zero reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal{H}$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then $\mathcal{H}$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick (CNP) space. This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Cesàro means. As applications, we prove a commutant lifting theorem for concave cyclic analytic operators, and several results about shift-invariant subspaces in de~Branges--Rovnyak spaces.

papers.title: Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
papers.abstract: The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.

papers.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
papers.abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.

papers.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
papers.abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.

papers.title: The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential
papers.abstract: Freezing the coefficients of a banded locally Toeplitz matrix gives a family of Toeplitz eigenvalue measures. Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

papers.title: On bordism classes of symmetric products of surfaces
papers.abstract: We explicitly determine the complex bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a complex curve of genus $g$. In particular, we provide an explicit formula expressing this class as an integral linear combination of bordism classes of products of complex projective spaces. Similarly, we determine the unoriented bordism class of the $n$-th symmetric product of a non-orientable surface of genus $g$ (i.e., $\#_{i=1}^{g+1}\mathbb R P^2$). It turns out that these classes are also expressed as a $\mathbb Z_2$-linear combination of bordism classes of products of even-dimensional real projective spaces. We also give an affirmative answer to a non-orientable version of the Blagojević--Grujić--Živaljević conjecture stating that the topological type of any symmetric product of a noncompact surface of finite type determines the topological type of the surface itself.

papers.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
papers.abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

papers.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $Π$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $Π$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

papers.title: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.

papers.title: Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
papers.abstract: We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and nonnegative, space-time separable boundary data supported in the unit ball and in $[0,1]$, respectively. A separation point is a pair $(x',t)$, with $x'$ outside the spatial support, arbitrarily near which a velocity component takes both signs. The main ingredient is an explicit representation of the velocity and pressure via confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, if the temporal boundary data are regular and unimodal, log-concavity yields a unique separation time for the $i$th tangential component at every boundary point with $|x_i|>1$, and exactly two for the normal component at distant points, one before and one after the boundary data vanish. The later one, a simple zero of the second normal derivative of the normal component at the boundary, is unique even without unimodality. We obtain monotonicity and asymptotics of separation times and vanishing rates of normal derivatives. For tangential boundary data with $n\geq3$, under the same assumptions, a separation time for the velocity component in their direction exists at $x'$ with $|x'|>1$ precisely when the corresponding Riesz transform of the spatial boundary data has a positive derivative in that direction at $x'$, and log-concavity makes it unique. For the remaining components, we prove existence and uniqueness of separation points on distant lines parallel to the axes, with asymptotics in terms of spatial moments and support geometry. For radial spatial boundary data, we determine the signs and zero sets of tangential pressure derivatives.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.

papers.title: Cycles and Symmetries of Non-Transitive Dice with Minimal and Uniform Winning Advantages
papers.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We investigate properties of the directed graphs arising from minimal and uniform winning advantages, including embeddings, isolated vertices and an involutive antiautomorphism. For every \(n\geq9\), we construct a non-transitive triple admitting no pairwise ties with uniform and minimal winning advantage. Moreover, for every \(n\geq7\), we construct a non-transitive triple which is invariant under the involutive antiautomorphism. We consider a two-player game utilizing these constructions and investigate the winning probabilities as \(n\) increases. We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\geq3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage, and identify the two unique such cycles. Finally, we present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is also the largest such \(n\).

papers.title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner.
