papers.abstract: We present a Lanczos tau method for the approximation and optimization of the $H^2$-norm of time-delay systems described by delay differential algebraic equations of index one. The soundness of this approach is proven under the assumption of a finite strong $H^2$-norm. Furthermore, we prove convergence if the rational approximation of the exponential underlying the discretization is well-behaved and the discretization is stability preserving. Numerical results suggest that, for multiple delays, the method converges at cubic rate in the discretization degree for systems of retarded type and linearly for those of neutral type. In the single delay case, we note geometric convergence of the $H^2$-norm for systems of both retarded and neutral type when a symmetric basis is chosen. Explicit formulas are derived for the gradient of the approximation with respect to system parameters and delays. These allow us to compute the entire gradient using only about double the computational time of approximating the $H^2$-norm alone. We illustrate how these can be used to synthesize robust feedback controllers and stable approximate models. The article is concluded by a discussion of how the presented results extend and improve for approximations based on splines. We note acceleration of the convergence rate by a little over a full order for such a choice. Finally, we prove that a Lanczos tau method using a spline based on Legendre orthogonal polynomials preserves stability and guarantees convergence of the $H^2$-norm.

papers.title: Teichmüller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere
papers.abstract: The Teichmüller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere is a simply connected complex Banach manifold. Its complex structure follows from Lieb isomorphism. In this paper, we show the conformal naturality of Lieb isomorphism. We then study Douady-Earle section for these Teichmüller spaces. In particular, we study the real-analyticity of Douady-Earle section for classical Teichmüller spaces. We give two explicit examples of maximal holomorphic motions over simply connected complex Banach manifolds. As an application of the real-analyticity of the Douady-Earle section for the classical Teichmüller spaces of Riemann surfaces, we prove a new result showing that a family of Jordan curves varies real-analytically over a simply connected complex Banach manifold and as quasiconformal images of the one at the basepoint, provided that a finite number of marked points on the Jordan curves vary holomorphically over the same parameter space.

papers.title: An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting
papers.abstract: We collect open problems in permutation patterns on four themes: rank-unimodality in the permutation pattern poset and log-convexity of principal classes, Wilf-equivalence and shape-Wilf-equivalence, the enumeration of derangements in permutation classes, and sorting by stacks in series, generalized stacks, and restricted containers (C-machines).

papers.title: Borel exceptional values in several complex variables and their applications to shared values of shifts and difference operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate shared value problems for shifts and higher-order difference operators of meromorphic and entire functions in several complex variables. Using Nevanlinna theory in $\mathbb{C}^n$, we obtain new uniqueness theorems when functions share values counting or ignoring multiplicities, extending several classical one-variable results to higher dimensions. A key contribution of this work appears in Section 2, where we establish fundamental results on Borel exceptional values in several complex variables. These propositions provide the main tools for proving our principal theorems. As applications, we derive conditions ensuring that a transcendental entire function satisfies $Δ_c^{k} \equiv d\hspace{.05cc} f$ and we study meromorphic solutions of certain partial differential-difference equations, obtaining growth estimates and structural descriptions of entire solutions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of such shared value problems for higher-order difference operators in several complex variables.

papers.title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization for Bearing-Only Localization in GPS Denied Environments
papers.abstract: Accurate localization of maritime targets by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging in GPS-denied environments. UAVs equipped with gimballed electro-optical sensors are typically used to localize targets; however, reliance on these sensors increases mechanical complexity, cost, and susceptibility to single-point failures, limiting scalability and robustness in multi-UAV operations. This work presents a new trajectory optimization framework that enables cooperative target localization using UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras operating in coordination with a surface vessel. This estimation-aware optimization generates dynamically feasible trajectories that explicitly account for mission constraints, platform dynamics, and out-of-frame events. Estimation-aware trajectories outperform heuristic paths by reducing localization error by more than a factor of two, motivating their use in cooperative operations. Results further demonstrate that coordinated UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras achieve localization accuracy that meets or exceeds that of single gimballed systems, while substantially lowering system complexity and cost, enabling scalability, and enhancing mission resilience.

papers.title: Construction of two-bubble solutions for the energy-critical Hartree equation
papers.abstract: We construct a pure two-bubble solution for the focusing, energy-critical Hartree equation in space dimension $N \geq 7$. The constructed solution is spherically symmetric, global in (at least) the negative time direction and asymptotically behaves as a superposition of two ground states (or bubbles) both centered at the origin, with the ratio of their length scales converging to $0$ and the phases of the two bubbles form the right angle. The main arguments are the modulation analysis, the bootstrap argument and the topological argument. The main novelty with respect to existing constructions of pure two-bubble solutions is the nonlocal interaction, which is more complex to analyze.

papers.title: The Fisher score on the closed simplex
papers.abstract: We extend classical analytic tools for finite-state statistical models to allow zero probabilities. Using methods from algebraic statistics and information geometry, we develop a framework in which a smooth statistical model can hit the boundary of the simplex, for example, in contingency tables with non-structural zeros. The central object of our approach is the vector bundle whose fibers are the $p$-contrasts associated to each probability distribution $p$. In this framework, the Fisher score, and other key statistical concepts such as the entropy of one-dimensional statistical models, admit an algebraic representation also on the boundary of the simplex.

papers.title: Symmetry of some noncommutative sphere algebras
papers.abstract: Two known $q$-deformed (or `quantum') $7$-spheres, both denoted $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ in the literature, may be distinguished by the presence or absence of symmetry under $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$. The quaternionic version of $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ has been shown by Brain and Landi to support such a symmetry. Here we show that this is not the case for the older $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ introduced by Vaksman and Soibelman: and as a consequence, these quantum $7$-spheres are not isomorphic.

papers.title: Flow reversal for the Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
papers.abstract: We study the nonstationary Stokes system in the half-space with zero initial data and a localized inflow through the boundary whose time profile behaves like $(1-t)^a$, $-1<a\leq1$, before it is switched off at $t=1$. By careful pointwise estimates of the representation formula of the solution to the Stokes system in the half-space, we show that the flow far from the inflow region reverses its direction. For $t>1$, the tangential velocity component pointing away from the source is negative near the wall and positive above it, and the normal velocity changes sign at a height comparable to the distance $|x'|$ from the source. The way the inflow is switched off determines when the reversal starts: if the inflow amplitude tends to zero ($0<a\leq1$), the reversal is already present shortly before $t=1$, whereas if the amplitude diverges ($-1<a<0$), the tangential component pointing away from the source does not change sign shortly before $t=1$, and neither does the normal component under a mild monotonicity condition on the profile. For $-1<a\leq-\frac12$ the reverse-flow region first appears next to the wall at $t=1$, which yields separation points.

papers.title: An asymptotically tight upper bound for the domination number of the $2$-token graph of path graphs
papers.abstract: In this note, we show that the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the path graph of order $n\geq 2$ is equal to $\frac{n^2}{10}+Θ(n)$.

papers.title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics
papers.abstract: The capabilities of generative AI in mathematics education are rapidly evolving, posing significant challenges for research to keep pace. Research syntheses remain scarce and risk being outdated by the time of publication. We present a Living Meta-Analysis (LIMA) on the effects of generative AI-based interventions on mathematics learning. We update the literature base every two months and apply a cumulative Bayesian multilevel meta-regression model. This paper reports results from the sixth version, including 37 studies, five of which were added since the fifth version. Results indicate a robust overall positive effect (g = 0.52, 95% CrI [0.32, 0.72]) and no evidence in favor of publication bias. Moderator analyses provided strong evidence for including integration mode, intervention dose, and grouping. Estimated effects were larger when generative AI supplemented teacher instruction, with greater intervention dose, and in group, teacher-led, or tutoring settings. For the remaining moderators, evidence was moderate or inconclusive.

papers.title: Conics and rational points of bounded height on cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct auxiliary intersections covering points of bounded height on geometrically integral non-ruled cubic surfaces over a fixed number field, and prove uniform bounds for the contribution of their conic components to rational and integral point counts. In the affine case, when the section at infinity is geometrically integral, the conic contribution admits a bound with a height exponent strictly below one. Under these hypotheses and within the same covering, obtaining a uniform bound for all integral points with any exponent greater than one reduces to controlling components of degree at least three. The proof combines a form of the global determinant method that retains the dependence on the height of Cayley form with uniform estimates for the number of conics of bounded height. The Deligne pairing and the geometry of residual conic pencils yield cubic image curves in fixed coefficient spaces. Uniform point estimates on these curves control the distribution of conic heights, with constants independent of the surface and the pencil.

papers.title: Relaxation to hydrostatic equilibria for two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible viscous flows under a conservative force
papers.abstract: This paper studies the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Navier--Stokes equations governing stratified flows in a bounded domain under a gravitational potential \(f\). Our main results are as follows. First, we provide a rigorous characterization of steady states, proving that under the Dirichlet condition \(\mathbf{u}|_{\partial Ω} = \mathbf{0}\), all admissible equilibria are hydrostatic and satisfy \(\nabla p_s = -ρ_s \nabla f\). Second, through a perturbative analysis around arbitrary hydrostatic profiles, we show that despite possible transient growth induced by the Rayleigh--Taylor mechanism, the system always relaxes to a hydrostatic equilibrium. Third, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial density perturbation for convergence to a linear hydrostatic density profile of the form \(ρ_s = -γf + β\), with \(γ> 0\) and \(β> 0\). Finally, we establish improved regularity estimates for strong solutions corresponding to initial data in the Sobolev space \(H^3(Ω)\).

papers.title: Debiased Inference via Posterior Corrections for High-Dimensional Regression
papers.abstract: There has been significant progress in Bayesian inference based on sparsity-inducing priors, such as spike-and-slab and horseshoe priors, for high-dimensional regression. The resulting posteriors, however, in general do not possess desirable frequentist properties, and the credible sets thus cannot serve as valid confidence sets even asymptotically. We introduce a novel debiasing approach that corrects the bias for the entire (possibly approximate) Bayesian posterior distribution. We establish new Bernstein-von Mises theorems that guarantee the frequentist validity of the debiased law. We demonstrate the practical performance of our proposal through Monte Carlo simulations and two empirical applications in economics.

papers.title: An algorithm to compute upper bounds of dimensions for Siegel Modular Forms of Prime Level and Arbitrary Nebentypus
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithmic method to determine the image of restriction maps for Siegel modular forms with \textit{arbitrary} characters and arbitrary weight. A program has been implemented in the mathematical software \texttt{Java} to compute the Fourier expansion of the image of these restriction maps for Siegel modular forms of genus two. This approach allows us to compute an upper bound for the space of Siegel modular forms with {\it non-trivial} character (which has not been previously known) and arbitrary weights (including low weight $k \leq 4$).

papers.title: The $d$-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the locus $\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}$ of genus $g$ tropical plane curves of gonality $d$ inside the moduli space $\mathbb{M}^{\textrm{nd}}_{g}$ of tropical plane curves of genus $g$. Each such tropical curve arises from a Newton polygon, and we conjecture that the gonality of the tropical curve is equal to an easily computed parameter of this polygon called the expected gonality, closely related to the lattice width of the polygon. Let $\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}$ denote the locus of tropical curves whose associated Newton polygon has expected gonality $d$. We prove that for fixed $d$ and sufficiently large genus $g$, the dimensions of these two loci agree: \[ \\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}\right) =\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}\right). \] Our results provide evidence that, in sufficiently high genus compared to expected gonality, the gonality of a tropical curve is determined by the expected gonality of the Newton polygon from which it arises. We also leverage our results to prove bounds on the dimensions of moduli spaces of non-degenerate algebraic curves.

papers.title: Quantitative BMO-BLO Estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Function
papers.abstract: In this note, we study a quantitative extension of the John-Nirenberg inequality for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function of a $\operatorname{BMO}$ function. More precisely, for every nonconstant locally integrable function $f$ such that $Mf$ is not identically infinite, we prove the inequality \begin{equation*} \left( \frac{1}{w(Q)}\int_Q \left( \frac{Mf(x) - \operatorname{ess\,inf}_{Q} Mf }{M^\# f(x)} \right)^p w(x)\,dx\right)^\frac{1}{p} \le c_n \, [w]_{A_\infty}\, p \end{equation*} for every cube $Q$, every $1\le p<\infty$ and every weight $w\in A_\infty$, where $[w]_{A_\infty}$ denotes the Fujii-Wilson $A_\infty$ constant. This result extends the classical boundedness $\|Mf\|_{\operatorname{BLO}}\le C_n\|f\|_{\operatorname{BMO}}$ proved by Bennett, DeVore, and Sharpley (Ann. of Math. (2) 113 (1981)) and by Bennett (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 85 (1982)). Furthermore, we show that the class $A_\infty$ is both necessary and sufficient for this inequality to hold, providing a new characterization of $A_\infty$ in terms of the action of the maximal operator on bounded oscillation spaces.

papers.title: Structure of Vidinli Algebras: Simple Non-associative Lie- and Jordan-Admissible Algebras
papers.abstract: We extend the three-dimensional Vidinli algebra of Vidinli Hüseyin Tevfik Pasha to a family of unital real algebras \( \Vn \), one in each odd dimension, built from the Euclidean inner product and a symplectic form on \( e_1^\perp \). Our main result is a local-to-global characterization by copies of \( \C \) and \( \V_3 \). A unital real algebra on Euclidean \( \R^{2n+1} \) with unit \( e_1 \) is isometrically isomorphic to \( \Vn \) if and only if every principal \( 2 \)-plane is an isometric copy of \( \C \), every principal \( 3 \)-plane is a subalgebra, and through every direction of \( e_1^\perp \) there passes at least one, and only finitely many, principal \( 3 \)-planes isomorphic to \( \V_3 \). We show that \( \Vn \) is central simple and power-associative with automorphism group \( \U(n) \), that its symmetrization is a Jordan algebra of Clifford type, and that its commutator is the Heisenberg algebra \( \mathfrak{h}_n \).

papers.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
papers.abstract: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $dΦ=θ\wedgeΦ$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $θ$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_θ\colonΓ(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\toΓ(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_θ$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|θ|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenböck formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.

papers.title: Zeroth-order Algorithms for Distributed Online Optimization against Byzantine Edge Attacks
papers.abstract: Byzantine attacks pose a fundamental challenge to distributed optimization, especially when they occur on communication edges, where truthful and corrupted messages coexist and attacked links are difficult to identify. While most existing studies focus on time-invariant objectives, many practical systems operate in dynamic environments and require distributed online optimization under such attacks. A central question is whether sublinear dynamic regret, a benchmark performance in online optimization, can still be achieved under Byzantine edge attacks. This paper answers this question affirmatively. We directly study distributed online optimization with time-varying directed networks, where the identities of adversarial edges are unknown to the agents and may change over time, and only zeroth-order feedback is available. Two resilient algorithms are proposed based on randomized and deterministic zeroth-order schemes. The former is more query-efficient and requires weaker smoothness conditions, while the latter provides deterministic guarantees and better performance in simulations. Both algorithms achieve consensus and, under suitable minimizer-path variation and algorithmic parameter conditions, achieve sublinear dynamic regret with respect to the original unweighted sum of local losses, without imposing stochastic assumptions for losses. Numerical results validate the theoretical findings. Overall, the results show that reliable distributed online optimization remains possible even under complex Byzantine edge attacks and limited feedback.

papers.title: Rigidity and flexibility results for groups with a common cocompact envelope
papers.abstract: A locally compact group $G$ is a cocompact envelope of a group $Γ$ if $G$ contains a copy of $Γ$ as a discrete and cocompact subgroup. We study the problem that takes two finitely generated groups $Γ,Λ$ having a common cocompact envelope, and asks what properties must be shared between $Γ$ and $Λ$. We first consider the setting where the common cocompact envelope is totally disconnected. In that situation we show that if $Γ$ admits a finitely generated nilpotent normal subgroup $A$, then virtually $Λ$ admits a normal subgroup $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are virtually isomorphic. We establish both rigidity and flexibility results when $Γ$ belongs to the class of solvable groups of finite rank. On the rigidity perspective, we show that if $Γ$ is solvable of finite rank, and the locally finite radical of $Λ$ is finite, then $Λ$ must be virtually solvable of finite rank. On the flexibility perspective, we exhibit groups $Γ,Λ$ with a common cocompact envelope such that $Γ$ is solvable of finite rank, while $Λ$ is not virtually solvable. In particular the class of solvable groups of finite rank is not QI-rigid. We also exhibit flexibility behaviours among finitely presented groups, and more generally among groups with type $F_n$ for arbitrary $n \geq 1$.

papers.title: On Casagrande-Druel Fano varieties with Lefschetz defect 2
papers.abstract: The larger the Lefschetz defect delta(X) of a smooth complex Fano variety X, the more information we can deduce about the geometry of X. The structure of varieties with delta(X) greater than 2 is known. In this paper, we study the case delta(X)=2. In particular, we focus on Fano varieties with delta(X)=2 arising from the so called Casagrande-Druel construction, which we refer to as Construction A. We show that among the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 classified by Mori and Mukai, 15 arise from such construction. Moreover, we construct all Fano 4-folds with Picard number greater than 3 and delta(X)=2 admitting such a structure, obtaining 145 distinct families in total. This completes the classification of all Casagrande-Druel Fano 4-folds with delta(X)=2. To broaden the scope, we also study a generalized version of Construction A, which we call Construction B, and we show that 18 out of the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 arise from it.

papers.title: Mixed tori in contact surgery diagrams
papers.abstract: We develop a diagrammatic framework for applying the symplectic JSJ decomposition to exact/weak symplectic fillings of 3-dimensional contact manifolds. Namely, we apply the symplectic JSJ decomposition to a contact surgery diagram for some $(Y,ζ)$, producing a finite collection of contact manifolds, also described diagrammatically, whose exact/weak symplectic fillings determine those of $(Y,ζ)$. We apply this technique to recover known symplectic filling classifications for certain lens spaces and torus bundles, and also to provide an algorithm for classifying the exact/weak symplectic fillings of a large class of plumbed 3-manifolds.

papers.title: Fixed Points and Envelope Dynamics on Credal Hyperspaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and consider the hyperspace $\mathscr C_X$ of nonempty weakly closed convex sets of Borel probability measures on $X$, called credal sets. These sets represent uncertainty about which probability law governs the phenomenon of interest. We equip $\mathscr C_X$ with the Hausdorff metric induced by a metric for weak convergence. Credal order intervals $[\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}] = \{ \mathcal{P}\in\mathscr C_X: \mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{B} \}$ are complete lattices, and every inclusion-monotone, Hausdorff-continuous self map of such an interval has least and greatest fixed points obtained as limits of iteration from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. For families of inclusion-monotone updates that may vary with time, we construct lower and upper envelope maps that bound every admissible trajectory. When these envelope maps are Hausdorff-continuous, the distance of every trajectory from a limiting credal interval vanishes uniformly over all switching sequences and initial credal sets. Coalescence of the limiting interval endpoints yields convergence to a common credal limit. We then construct the credal evolution induced by a time consistent Nisio semigroup. Uniform $W_1$ contraction of the underlying Markov semigroups induces Hausdorff-Wasserstein contraction of the credal evolution, yielding a unique common invariant credal set, exponential convergence from every initial credal set, and a support functional equal to the robust ergodic limit. We also derive perturbation bounds from finite time Nisio discrepancies and one step kernel set discrepancies, and characterize the countable sequences of support coordinates that represent credal sets, providing an explicit reconstruction formula.

papers.title: Lifting Cocycles: From Heuristic to Theory
papers.abstract: The circular coordinates algorithm, a widely used tool in topological data analysis, relies on a lifting step to convert cocycles from a prime field to integer coefficients. We provide a rigorous analysis of this procedure, establishing a criterion for its success. We give an algebraic method for reducing the winding number under explicit torsion hypotheses. The torsion and coprimality hypotheses required by the winding number reduction are automatic in degree 1, because H^1(X; Z) is torsion-free. We extend these principles to homology, deriving analogous coefficientwise lifting criteria for cycles.

papers.title: Algebraic cycles on some Fano varieties. Part I: Quartic double fivefolds
papers.abstract: We study algebraic cycles on quartic double fivefolds, which are Fano fivefolds whose middle cohomology is numerically similar to that of a Calabi-Yau threefold, continuing the work of Skauli on lines, $1$-cycles and the coniveau filtration on double covers of projective space. By means of cubic surfaces which are totally ramified along the branch locus, we prove the integral Hodge conjecture for all of them. We also show that the comparison maps between their Chow groups and étale Chow groups are isomorphisms except possibly in codimension three, where we describe the kernel and the cokernel in terms of Bloch-Ogus cohomology and, via a Sarkisov link, of the unramified cohomology of a cubic surface over the function field of $\mathbb{P}^3$.

papers.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
papers.abstract: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.

papers.title: Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of quadrics via Ehrhart theory
papers.abstract: We show that the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of the d-dimensional non-degenerate quadric hypersurface of characteristic p > 2 is a rational function of p composed from the Ehrhart polynomials of integer polytopes. In consequence, we prove that the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of quadrics of fixed characteristic is a decreasing function of characteristic (previously showed by Meng) and dimension, and give a combinatorial explanation of the Gessel-Monsky formula for the limit Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity of quadrics.

papers.title: The Uniform Functional Interpretation with Informative Types
papers.abstract: We discuss a new approach to functional interpretations based on uniform quantification and relativization. The uniform quantification in the background permits a more penetrating analysis of principles related to collection and contra-collection. Relativization comes from a computationally informative notion of being an element of a given type. The approach is flexible. When the information takes the shape of bounds, we can recapture a form of the combination of Gödel's functional {\em dialectica} interpretation with majorizability. When the information is "canonical" in function types, we obtain new functional interpretations and new models of Gödel's theory T.

papers.title: A Riemannian viewpoint on the Amari-Cencov $α$-connections and Proudman-Johnson equations
papers.abstract:
We give a new geometric interpretation of the Amari-Cencov $α$-connections $
abla^{(α)}$ from information geometry: On the space of densities $\operatorname{Dens}_+(M)$, we show that there exist Riemannian metrics $G^α$, which we call $α$-Fisher-Rao metrics, whose Levi-Civita connections are $
abla^{(α)}$. With the exception of $α=0$ (the Fisher-Rao metric), these metrics are non-invariant to the action of the diffeomorphism group $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$, even though the connections are invariant. This gives a new way of interpreting the geodesics of the $
abla^{(α)}$ as energy-minimizing curves. On the space of probability densities $\operatorname{Prob}(M)$, we show that the same phenomenon holds for $α\in \{-1,0,1\}$ and that the $α$-connections are not metric otherwise. We show that $
abla^{(α)}$-geodesics on this space can be interpreted as radial projections of straight lines on appropriate hyper-surfaces, and use this geometric picture to obtain geodesic convexity for any $α\in \mathbb{R}$. In addition, we prove analogous results for appropriate metrics and connections on $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$, which, for the case $M=\mathbb{R}$, imply that the generalized Proudman-Johnson equations on the real line are the Euler-Arnold equations of non-right invariant metrics. Finally, in the finite-dimensional case, we show that $
abla^{(α)}$ can be metric or non-metric depending on the considered statistical model.

papers.title: Derivative Estimation from Coarse, Irregular, Noisy Samples: An MLE-Spline Approach
papers.abstract: We address numerical differentiation under coarse, non-uniform sampling and Gaussian noise. A maximum-likelihood estimator with $L_2$-norm constraint on a higher-order derivative is obtained, yielding spline-based solution. We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.

papers.title: Mirror descent for constrained stochastic control problems
papers.abstract: Mirror descent is a well established tool for solving convex optimization problems with convex constraints. This article introduces continuous-time mirror descent dynamics for approximating optimal Markov controls for stochastic control problems with the action space being bounded and convex. We show that if the Hamiltonian is uniformly convex in its action variable then mirror descent converges linearly while if it is uniformly strongly convex relative to an appropriate Bregman divergence, then the mirror flow converges exponentially. The two fundamental difficulties that must be overcome to prove such results are: first, the inherent lack of convexity of the map from Markov controls to the corresponding value function. Second, maintaining sufficient regularity of the value function and the Markov controls along the mirror descent updates. The first issue is handled using the performance difference lemma, while the second using careful Sobolev space estimates for the solutions of the associated linear PDEs. Finally, we complement the theoretical analysis with numerical experiments. We provide a model-based algorithm which uses finite difference discretization and discrete mirror descent updates. Empirical results confirm the theoretically predicted convergence rates. We also provide a model-free algorithm which uses martingale differences to learn the advantage rate function and applies this in the mirror descent updates of the policy.

papers.title: On the applicability of the maximality principle in optimal stopping: an example involving a diffusion and its running maximum
papers.abstract: The maximality principle has proved to be a valuable tool for identifying the optimal stopping boundaries in optimal stopping problems involving one-dimensional time-homogeneous diffusions and their running maximum processes. The principle characterises the optimal stopping boundary as the maximal solution to a first-order nonlinear ODE that remains strictly below the diagonal in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or a "zero-level curve". In this paper, we construct a suitably tailored optimal stopping problem to which the maximality principle is not applicable.

papers.title: Iterated harmonic envelopes for multidimensional optimal stopping
papers.abstract: Motivated by the contrast between the classical least-concave-majorant representation of Dynkin and Yushkevich in one dimension and the substantially more complicated potential-theoretic structure of optimal stopping in higher dimensions, we identify a fundamental barrier: a localisation obstruction caused by the geometry of Brownian paths in dimensions $d\ge2$. We overcome it with an iterative construction based on harmonic-function envelopes, each an infimum of harmonic replacements on subdomains of the current non-contact set, with the previous envelope as boundary data. From a continuous gain function $g$, this produces a decreasing sequence of upper bounds $w_n$ converging uniformly to the value function $V$ of optimal stopping. The process may be Brownian motion or, more generally, any diffusion with a short list of properties, including polarity of points. For Brownian motion, every iterate inherits the modulus of continuity of the data. Exponential discounting may be included, and the state space may be a bounded regular domain with absorption at the boundary, or the whole space under a condition at infinity. Equivalently, the iterates converge to the solution of the associated obstacle problem. At each iteration an explicit stopping rule gives a lower bound for $V$. Both bounds are computed from the construction alone, without knowledge of $V$, and their gap falls below any given threshold after finitely many iterations. The first exit time from the limit non-contact set is optimal.

papers.title: Stability Regularized Cross-Validation
papers.abstract: We study hyperparameter selection via cross-validation, motivated by settings in which the selected $k$-fold cross-validation error underestimates the selected model's test error. We propose a nested $k$-fold cross-validation scheme that minimizes a weighted sum of the standard cross-validation error and empirical hypothesis stability, with the stability weight selected by an outer cross-validation loop. We derive a generalization bound that controls test error using the cross-validation error and empirical hypothesis stability, together with correction terms common to every candidate. In a stylized ridge regression setting, we then show that whether the stability weight improves expected test-set performance depends on the signal-to-noise ratio, with the greatest improvement when the signal-to-noise ratio is small. On $13$ real-world regression datasets, the procedure reduces the average out-of-sample MSE relative to $k$-fold cross-validation by $5.6\%$ for sparse regression and by $6.8\%$ for CART. A side benefit of an outer cross-validation loop is that the selected error estimates are better calibrated than those from ordinary $k$-fold cross-validation: the error estimate moves from 12.3\% below the selected test-set MSE to 5.8\% above it for sparse regression and from 10.3\% below to 0.2\% above it for CART.

papers.title: On the Hermitian K-theory of Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We compute the $\mathbb{G}W$-spectrum (Karoubi--Grothendieck--Witt spectrum) of Grassmannians over divisorial schemes defined over fields of characteristic zero, and, as a corollary, determine their stabilized $\mathbb{L}$-theory spectrum. As part of our computation, we establish split fibration sequences in $\mathbb{K}$-theory, $\mathbb{G}W$-theory and $\mathbb{L}$-theory.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
papers.abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.

papers.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $ψ$-Fueter operator
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $ψ$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.

papers.title: Ergodic theorems for set maps under weak forms of additivity
papers.abstract: We investigate various relaxations of additivity for set maps into Banach spaces in the context of representations of amenable groups. Specifically, we establish conditions under which asymptotically additive and almost additive set maps are equivalent. For Banach lattices, we further show that these notions are related to a third weak form of additivity adapted to the order structure of the space. By utilizing these equivalences and reducing non-additive settings to the additive one by finding suitable additive realizations, we derive new non-additive ergodic theorems for amenable group representations into Banach spaces and streamline proofs of existing results in certain cases.

papers.title: L^p-boundedness of the Bochner-Riesz operator
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new approach to the Bochner-Riesz summability. As a result, we show that the Bochner-Riesz operator $\mathbf{S}^δ, 0<\Reδ<{1\over 2}$ is bounded on $\mathbf{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for ${n-1\over 2n}\leq {1\over p}\leq{n+1\over 2n}$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Properties of the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Markov-Switching Observation-Driven Models
papers.abstract: A Markov-switching observation-driven model is a stochastic process $((S_t,Y_t))_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ where $(S_t)_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is an unobserved Markov chain with finite state space and $(Y_t)_{t \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is an observed stochastic process such that the conditional distribution of $Y_t$ given $(Y_τ)_{τ\leq t-1}$ and $(S_τ)_{τ\leq t}$ depends only on $(Y_τ)_{τ\leq t-1}$, through time-varying parameters, and $S_t$. In this paper, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the maximum likelihood estimator for such a model. As a special case, we also give conditions under which the maximum likelihood estimator for the widely applied Markov-switching generalised autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity model introduced by Haas, Mittnik, and Paolella (2004b) is consistent and asymptotically normal.

papers.title: Sharper $L^1$ convergence rates to the Barenblatt profile for the compressible Euler equations with time-dependent damping
papers.abstract: We study the large-time behavior of weak entropy solutions with bounded density and velocity to the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with time-dependent damping and vacuum. Assuming that the spatial primitive of the initial density perturbation belongs to $L^2(\mathbf{R})$, we establish convergence rates to the Barenblatt solution with the same finite mass in $L^1$ for all $γ>1$ and $0\leν<1$, and in $L^γ$ for $γ\ge2$, where $γ$ is the adiabatic exponent and $ν$ is the damping exponent. On the common parameter ranges, the leading $L^1$ decay exponent exceeds the exponents in the earlier estimates compared below, with equality only at $(γ,ν)=(2,0)$. The proof combines a structural inequality for the higher-order entropy remainder, valid for every $γ>1$, with estimates for the relative pressure and time-weighted entropy inequalities. The resulting decay exponent has an explicit formula in each damping regime.

papers.title: Properties of f correlated fuzzy numbers
papers.abstract: This paper investigates structural invariance and algebraic classification properties within the theory of interactive fuzzy numbers, focusing on $f$-correlated and more specifically, linearly correlated fuzzy numbers. Starting from the foundations of joint possibility distributions and the generalized extension principle, we analyze how continuous, strictly monotonic correlation functions $f$ act on $α$-level sets and membership representations. We prove that $f$-correlation preserves the class $\mathcal{F}_C(\mathbb{R})$ of fuzzy numbers with continuous endpoints and transforms any $L$-$R$ fuzzy number into a generalized $L_f$-$R_f$ (or $R_f$-$L_f$) fuzzy number, with explicit formulas for the induced shape functions. Specializing to hyperbolic correlation ($f(x) = q/x + r$) illustrates how nonlinear interactivity preserves generalized $L$-$R$ regularity while deforming piecewise-linear triangular and trapezoidal flanks into rational curves. In contrast, when $f(x) = qx + r$ is affine, the reference shape functions $(L, R)$ are preserved up to orientation reversal, yielding complete set-theoretic characterizations of the $A$-linearly correlated spaces $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{F}(A)}$ for symmetric Gaussian, trapezoidal, and triangular generators, as well as necessary and sufficient shape-ratio conditions for linear correlation in the asymmetric setting.

papers.title: Finite-Dimensional Protori Are Adelic Tori
papers.abstract: We show that every finite-dimensional compact connected abelian group is topologically isomorphic to an adelic torus $(\mathbb{A}^n/C)/Λ$ for the adeles $\mathbb{A}$, a torsion-free profinite group $C$, and a discrete cocompact $Λ\cong \mathbb{Q}^n$. A Lie theory is developed yielding a proper short exact sequence $0 \to \mathbb{Q}^n \to \mathcal{L}(G) \xrightarrow{\exp} G \to 0$ for each adelic torus $G$, where $\exp$ denotes the adelic exponential and $\mathcal{L}(G)$ the adelic Lie algebra of $G$. The adelic structure theory of the category $\mathbf{AT}$ of adelic tori under continuous quasi-homomorphism enables us to establish that the nonarchimedean dimension of an arbitrary number field $K$ with $[K : \mathbb{Q}] = n$ is $1$, while the archimedean dimension is $n$.

papers.title: From Numbers to Container Strings
papers.abstract: We examine two ways of coding sequences in arithmetical theories. We investigate under what conditions they work. To be more precise, we study the creation of objects of a data-type that we call container strings, roughly sequences where the components are ordered but where we do not have an explicitly given projection function and length function. The first coding idea is Smullyan coding and the second one is Markov coding. This second idea is based on the representation of binary strings in the special linear monoid of the non-negative part of discretely ordered commutative rings. We employ Markov coding to obtain an alternative proof that the weak theory ${\sf PA}^-$ is sequential. We prove a correspondence result for a principle for container strings to Euclidean Division under the Markov translation.

papers.title: Stochastic flows for SDEs with critically low regularity growing drifts in Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini spaces
papers.abstract: We study stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with critically low regularity drifts in a Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini class. Under suitable slowly varying and Hölder--Dini-type assumptions on the modulus of continuity, we prove that SDEs with linearly growing drifts in the critical class $L^p\big([0,T];{\mathcal C}^{\frac{2}{p}-1,ρ}_{l,d}(\mathbb{R}^n;\mathbb{R}^n)\big)$, $p\in(1,2]$, generate a unique stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. The proof relies on a maximal regularity theory for parabolic equations in non-divergence form with Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini coefficients, which enables us to apply the Itô--Tanaka trick and reduce the original SDE to one with Lipschitz coefficients.

papers.title: Heights of Drinfeld modular polynomials and Hecke images
papers.abstract: We obtain explicit upper and lower bounds on the size of the coefficients of the Drinfeld modular polynomials $Φ_N$ for any monic $N\in\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. These polynomials vanish at pairs of $j$-invariants of Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-modules of rank 2 linked by cyclic isogenies of degree $N$. The main term in both bounds is asymptotically optimal as $\mathrm{deg}(N)$ tends to infinity. We also obtain precise estimates on the Weil height and Taguchi height of Hecke images of Drinfeld modules of rank 2.

papers.title: On the Hodge theory of toroidal embeddings and corresponding vanishings
papers.abstract: We prove $E_1$-degeneration of the logarithmic Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence for proper toroidal triples. For a compatible Weil divisor, we realize the associated twisted logarithmic de Rham complex as the filtered de Rham complex of an object in the bounded derived category of mixed Hodge modules. We use this realization to prove a vanishing theorem of Kawamata--Viehweg type for toroidal triples. We also prove relative Bott vanishing in the toric case. On the local toric charts of a toroidal triple $(X,!B,*C)$, we characterize when the canonical exchange morphism between the two ordered extensions of the constant sheaf on $X\setminus(B+C)$ is an isomorphism, when each order recovers the logarithmic de Rham complex, and when this complex is perverse.

papers.title: Conjugate points on Lie groups with left-invariant metrics
papers.abstract: We prove sufficient conditions for the existence of conjugate points along geodesics of a left-invariant metric on a Lie group, using a reformulation of the index form in terms of the adjoint action. In the compact semisimple case, with an arbitrary left-invariant metric, we show that all geodesics must have a conjugate point, and we give upper and lower bounds on conjugate times. In particular this applies to the left-invariant metrics on $SU(n)$ and $SO(n)$ which are of importance in fluid dynamics and rigid body motion, and yields estimates for the diameter and injectivity radius. We also establish criteria in the noncompact case: we show that every closed nonhomogeneous geodesic has a conjugate point, and determine explicit conditions for them in the three-dimensional unimodular case. For homogeneous geodesics, we relate conjugate points to Lagrangian stability, and Eulerian stability of the corresponding steady velocity. Finally, we obtain as by-products criteria for conjugate points in general homogeneous spaces, by lifting the problem to the total Lie group of the quotient and using a result of O'Neill. Through several examples, we show that our theorems apply when well-known criteria relying on positive Ricci curvature or other curvature bounds fail, and in some cases even when Ricci curvature is negative along a certain geodesic.

papers.title: Tightness for branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment
papers.abstract: We consider the maximum $M_t$ of branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment on $\mathbb{Z}$. In this model the branching rate while at some location $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ is randomized in an i.i.d. manner. We prove that there is a centering $\widetilde{m}_t$ depending only on the environment such that $(M_t-\widetilde{m}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is tight in an annealed sense.

papers.title: A very short proof of Sidorenko's inequality for counts of homomorphism between graphs
papers.abstract: A fundamental extremality result due to Sidorenko (Discrete Math. 131.1-3, 1994) states that among all connected graphs G on k vertices, the k-vertex star maximises the number of graph homomorphisms of G into any graph H. We provide a new short proof of this result using only a simple recursive counting argument for trees and Hölder's inequality.

papers.title: On Frobenius-Schur exponent bounds
papers.abstract: We study bounds on the Frobenius--Schur exponent of spherical fusion categories in terms of their global dimension, generalizing bounds from the representation theory of finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebras. Our main result is that if the Frobenius--Schur exponent of a modular fusion category is a power of a prime $p$, then it is bounded by the norm of its global dimension when $p$ is odd, and by four times the norm of its global dimension when $p=2$; these bounds are optimal. Moreover, it is bounded by a constant multiple of the geometric mean of the Galois conjugates of its global dimension, which is much smaller when the global dimension is irrational, and a bound of this type is proven for each prime power dividing the Frobenius--Schur exponent of an arbitrary modular or spherical fusion category. Under pseudounitarity, we describe all modular and spherical fusion categories whose Frobenius--Schur exponent is a prime power and at least the norm (respectively, the square of the norm) of their global dimension, using a classification of modular fusion categories of Frobenius--Perron dimension $p^n$ for $n\leq5$.

papers.title: Neur2BiLO: Neural Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization deals with nested problems in which a leader takes the first decision to minimize their objective function while accounting for a follower's best-response reaction. Constrained bilevel problems with integer variables are particularly notorious for their hardness. While exact solvers have been proposed for mixed-integer linear bilevel optimization, they tend to scale poorly with problem size and are hard to generalize to the non-linear case. On the other hand, problem-specific algorithms (exact and heuristic) are limited in scope. Under a data-driven setting in which similar instances of a bilevel problem are solved routinely, our proposed framework, Neur2BiLO, embeds a neural network approximation of the leader's or follower's value function, trained via supervised regression, into an easy-to-solve mixed-integer program. Neur2BiLO serves as a heuristic that produces high-quality solutions extremely fast for four applications with linear and non-linear objectives and pure and mixed-integer variables.

papers.title: Likelihood Geometry of Reflexive Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study the problem of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for statistical models defined by reflexive polytopes. Our focus is on the maximum likelihood degree of these models as an algebraic measure of complexity of the corresponding optimization problem. We compute the ML degrees of all 4319 classes of three-dimensional reflexive polytopes, and observe some surprising behavior in terms of the presence of gaps between ML degrees and degrees of the associated toric varieties. We interpret these drops in the context of discriminants and prove formulas for the ML degree for families of reflexive polytopes, including the hypercube and its dual, the cross polytope, in arbitrary dimension. In particular, we determine a family of embeddings for the $d$-cube that implies ML degree one. Finally, we discuss generalized constructions of families of reflexive polytopes in terms of their ML degrees.

papers.title: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $δ$, the two main ones allow to: - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq δ- 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field; - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq δ-1$ and satisfying a norm condition. We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.

papers.title: Płonka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{Płonka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for Płonka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Properties of Multi-Treatment Covariate Adaptive Randomization Procedures for Balancing Observed and Unobserved Covariates
papers.abstract: Applications of CAR for balancing continuous covariates remain comparatively rare, especially in multi-treatment clinical trials, and the theoretical properties of multi-treatment CAR have remained largely elusive for decades. In this paper, we consider a general framework of CAR procedures for multi-treatment clinal trials which can balance general covariate features, such as quadratic and interaction terms which can be discrete, continuous, and mixing. We show that under widely satisfied conditions the proposed procedures have superior balancing properties; in particular, the convergence rate of imbalance vectors can attain the best rate $O_P(1)$ for discrete covariates, continuous covariates, or combinations of both discrete and continuous covariates, and at the same time, the convergence rate of the imbalance of unobserved covariates is $O_P(\sqrt n)$, where $n$ is the sample size. The general framework unifies many existing methods and related theories, introduces a much broader class of new and useful CAR procedures, and provides new insights and a complete picture of the properties of CAR procedures. The favorable balancing properties lead to the precision of the treatment effect test in the presence of a heteroscedastic linear model with dependent covariate features. As an application, the properties of the test of treatment effect with unobserved covariates are studied under the CAR procedures, and consistent tests are proposed so that the test has an asymptotic precise type I error even if the working model is wrong and covariates are unobserved in the analysis.

papers.title: Solvable subgroup theorem, length function and topological entropy
papers.abstract: We prove a general solvable subgroup theorem in terms of length functions. As applications, we obtain a solvable subgroup theorem in dynamical systems: any solvable group of finite Hirsch length acting on a smooth manifold with uniformly positive topological entropies must be virtually $\mathbb{Z}^{n}.$ Some applications to group actions on cubical complexes and injective spaces, interval exchange transformations, and RFRS groups are also discussed.

papers.title: Inference for Non-Stationary Heavy Tailed Time Series
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of inference for linear autoregressive heavy tailed non-stationary time series. Using the framework of time-varying infinite order moving average processes we show that there exists a suitable local approximation to a non-stationary heavy tailed process by a stationary process with heavy tails. This enables us to introduce a local approximation-based estimator which estimates consistently time-varying parameters of the model at hand. In addition, we study a robust self-weighting approach that enables proving the asymptotic normality of the estimator without necessarily assuming finite variance for the underlying process. A multiplier bootstrap methodology is suggested for obtaining a consistent estimator of the variance for this new estimator. Empirical evidence favoring this approach is provided.

papers.title: The Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: The Weyl symbolic calculus of operators leads to the construction, if one takes for symbol a certain distribution decomposing over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, of an operator with the following property: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the validity of a collection of estimates involving this operator. Pseudodifferential arithmetic, a novel chapter of pseudodifferential operator theory, makes it possible to make the operator under study fully explicit. This leads to a proof of the conjecture.

papers.title: A note on mean field games of controls with state constraints: existence of mild solutions
papers.abstract: We show the existence of mild solutions for a first-order mean field game of controls under the state constraint that trajectories be confined in a closed and bounded set in euclidean space. This extends the results of Cannarsa and Capuani to the case of a mean field game of controls. Our controls are velocities and we find that the existence of an equilibrium is complicated by the requirement that they should have enough regularity. We solve this by imposing a small Lipschitz constant on the dependence of the Lagrangian on the joint measure of states and controls.

papers.title: Playing through a noisy channel (and knowing it)
papers.abstract: We study combinatorial games played through a noisy channel, where the move chosen by a player may differ from the move that is effectively executed. The key feature of this setting is that any received legal move is accepted as the move played, regardless of the player's original intention, while illegal moves trigger retransmission. Both players know the error mechanism and strategically choose their transmitted moves to maximize their winning probabilities. This interaction between strategic choice and imperfect execution gives rise to a rich class of games whose behavior can differ substantially from that of the underlying combinatorial game. We develop a general framework based on move error functions and establish structural results concerning winning probabilities, optimal moves, and conditions for fair chance games. We then investigate in detail one-pile Nim with independent binary transmission errors. Despite its apparent simplicity, this example exhibits unexpectedly intricate behavior. We determine optimal strategies and winning probabilities in the low-error regime and uncover a substantially richer structure in the high-error regime, including changes in optimal play and nontrivial limiting behavior.

papers.title: Strict lax algebra bundles and coherent descent
papers.abstract: Fix coprime integers $k\geq1$ and $l\geq2$, and put $D=M_k\otimes M_{l^\infty}$. Let ${\mathcal C}_{k,l}$ be the topological category with objects $M_{kl^n}$, $n\geq0$, and unital $*$-embeddings as morphisms. Adjoining $D$ as an object and applying topological Quillen Theorem~A gives a weak equivalence $|N{\mathcal C}_{k,l}|\simeq B{\rm Aut}(D)$. On finite CW complexes this space classifies normalized strict lax algebra bundles modulo morphisms, refinement, and concordance. The proof realizes strict diagrams as nested matrix subalgebras of locally trivial $D$-bundles. We show that an $M_k$-bundle embeds in a trivial $M_{kl^N}$-bundle for some $N$ if and only if its stabilization by $M_{l^\infty}$ is trivial. The same classifying space describes Segal-space cover diagrams on finite CW complexes up to paths, specified refinements, and concordance, as well as Čech descent after groupoid completion. A triangulated cylinder realizes equality of completed classes by a concordance of cover diagrams. We compute the homotopy groups of the classifying space and, for $k>1$, exhibit a class outside the image of every allowed finite rank.

papers.title: New approaches to finite generation of cohomology rings
papers.abstract: In support variety theory, representations of a finite dimensional (Hopf) algebra $A$ can be studied geometrically by associating any representation of $A$ to an algebraic variety using the cohomology ring of $A$. An essential assumption in this theory is the finite generation condition for the cohomology ring of $A$ and that for the corresponding modules. In this paper, we introduce various approaches to study the finite generation condition. First, for any finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A$, we show that the finite generation condition on $A$-modules can be replaced by a condition on any affine commutative $A$-module algebra $R$ under the assumption that $R$ is integral over its invariant subring $R^A$. Next, we use a spectral sequence argument to show that a finite generation condition holds for certain filtered, smash and crossed product algebras in positive characteristic if the related spectral sequences collapse. Finally, if $A$ is defined over a number field over the rationals, we construct another finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A'$ over a finite field, where $A$ can be viewed as a deformation of $A'$, and prove that if the finite generation condition holds for $A'$, then the same condition holds for $A$.

papers.title: Self-similar co-ascent processes and Palm calculus
papers.abstract: We study certain renormalised first passage bridges of self-similar processes, generalising the "Brownian co-ascent process" discussed by Panzo (Sém. Prob. L, 2019) and introduced by Rosenbaum and Yor (Sém. Prob. XLVI, 2014). We provide a characterisation of co-ascent processes via Palm measures, namely that the co-ascent of a self-similar process is the process under the Palm distribution associated with its record measure. We use this representation to derive a distributional identity for alpha-stable Lévy-subordinators with alpha in (0,1).

papers.title: 1-Laplacian type problems with strongly singular nonlinearities and gradient terms
papers.abstract: We show optimal existence, nonexistence and regularity results for nonnegative solutions to Dirichlet problems as $$ \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_1 u = g(u)|D u|+h(u)f & \text{in}\;Ω,\\ u=0 & \text{on}\;\partialΩ, \end{cases} $$ where $Ω$ is an open bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $f\geq 0$ belongs to $L^N(Ω)$, and $g$ and $h$ are continuous functions that may blow up at zero. As a noteworthy fact we show how a non-trivial interaction mechanism between the two nonlinearities $g$ and $h$ produces remarkable regularizing effects on the solutions. The sharpness of our main results is discussed through the use of appropriate explicit examples.

papers.title: Cartesian product of $ψ$-badly approximable sets
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the Cartesian products of sets in $\mathbb R^{d}$ that are $ψ$-approximable but not $cψ$-approximable for arbitrarily small $c>0$, often denoted $\mathbf{Bad}_{d}(ψ)$. Setting $d=\sum_{i=1}^{N}d_i\in\mathbb N$ and $ψ_i(q)=q^{-τ_i}$ with $τ_i\geq 1/d_i$, $i=1,\ldots,N$, we calculate \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}\prod_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf{Bad}_{d_i}(ψ_i) =\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{\frac{d_i+1}{τ_i+1}+(d-d_i)\right\}=d- \max_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{ d_i-\frac{d_i+1}{τ_i+1} \right\}, \] for $\dim_{\mathrm H}$ denoting the Hausdorff dimension. The lower bound is obtained by combining the delayed-pruning construction of Koivusalo-Levesley-Ward-Zhang (IMRN, 2024) with the product Cantor-set method of Wang-Wu (TAMS, 2024).

papers.title: Link invariants from charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators
papers.abstract: Turaev's enhanced Yang--Baxter operators produce invariants of oriented links from solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation. If the enhancing endomorphism is diagonal with generic eigenvalues, Turaev's compatibility condition forces the Yang--Baxter operator $R$ to be charge-conserving, that is, to send each $e_i\otimes e_j$ into the span of $e_i\otimes e_j$ and $e_j\otimes e_i$. Charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators were classified by Martin and Rowell. Building on their classification, we determine all enhancements of charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators with diagonal enhancing endomorphism, and we identify the resulting link invariants. The link invariant associated with such an enhancement is a sum over the colourings of the components of the link by the connected components of $R$, in which each monochromatic sublink contributes a specialization of the HOMFLY--PT polynomial and different colours interact only through linking numbers. Every such state sum arises in this way.

papers.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
papers.abstract: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimesΛ_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenböck formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors of the spinor valued forms, and derive vanishing theorems, heat trace invariants and index formulas. Finally, in four dimensions we use these Weitzenböck formulas to construct non-negative functionals whose absolute minima define two generalizations of the Seiberg--Witten monopole equations to right spinor valued $p$-forms, one based on the Dirac operator and one on the twisted de Rham Laplacian, and discuss the resulting integrability conditions.

papers.title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
papers.abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchmarks. Compared to standard PINNs and Physics-Informed DeepONets and their lifted versions, FokasNets achieve significant improvements in solution accuracy in the interior and boundaries, both for single PDEs and particularly for solution operators, where the improvement reaches multiple orders of magnitude and fixed threshold errors are reached faster during training.

papers.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
papers.abstract: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$. When $Y$ is dismantlable, we show that the boundary isomorphism assumption can be weakened to a bijection between the vertex sets of both boundaries with an additional technical condition on boundary edges.

papers.title: Controllability of the Cahn Hilliard System at Finitely Many Observation Points
papers.abstract: We study approximate controllability of the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) system with prescribed targets at finitely many points in the spatial domain. Our aim is to design a L^2 control such that given a finite set of observation points and target values, the solution reaches arbitrarily close to the prescribed targets at these points. First we study the associated linearised system using variational methods and then extend the results to the semi-linear CH system using fixed-point arguments. Further, we investigate approximate controllability in more general setting where we allow the control to be measure valued (in specific, Dirac delta type controls). This formulation is more challenging to obtain requisite regularity due to the simultaneous presence of pointwise observations and pointwise controls. Hence we restrict ourselves to the study of linearised CH system and devise a control which exhibits approximate controllability. We achieve this by approximating measure valued control with L^2 controls and showing appropriate convergence.

papers.title: Stochastic Optimization for Switch-System Identification under Errors-in-Variables
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the identification of switched dynamical systems under errors-in-variables, where both input and output measurements are corrupted by noise, and the number of operating modes and subsystem orders are unknown. We propose a unified identification framework that simultaneously estimates the subsystem parameters, latent switching sequence, and model structure. The proposed formulation combines a variance-normalized data-fitting criterion with temporally regularized soft mode assignments and sparsity-inducing penalties for selecting the active modes and relevant input-output lags. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we develop an alternating algorithm that incorporates convex mode-assignment updates and proximal stochastic variance-reduced gradient optimization for parameter estimation. While the existing approaches in the literature require exhaustive searches over candidate structures, the proposed method performs structure selection within a single model. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate recovery of the underlying system structure and favorable computational efficiency compared with a generalized total least squares and dynamic programming approach, particularly as the number of candidate structures increases.

papers.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
papers.abstract: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erdős--Rényi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $Θ(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit the minimum degree of~$G(n,W)$, giving simplified proofs of results of Hladký and Viswanathan~\cite{HV} and establishing the limiting distribution of $δ(G(n,W))$ under a second-order decorrelation condition.

papers.title: Inverses of split graphs via Ferrers diagrams and degree sequences
papers.abstract: A graph is a split graph if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and a stable set and is a partitioned split graph if the partition is also specified. The inverse of a partitioned split graph is formed by removing all edges within the clique and adding all edges between vertices in the stable set, while preserving the edges between the two parts. In this paper we compare two forms of the degree sequence of a graph: the conventional form and the block representation. We show the effect on the block representation of taking complements of graphs and inverses of split graphs, the latter of which is complicated by the fact that some split graphs have two different inverses. When there are two distinct inverses, we show how the degree sequences of these inverses are related to each other in both the conventional and block representations. We also demonstrate geometric interpretations of these results using Ferrers diagrams.

papers.title: Improving the efficiency of the ratio-of-uniforms method
papers.abstract: In 1977, Kinderman and Monahan showed that under certain conditions, a random variable can be expressed as the ratio $V/U$, where $(U,V)$ is uniformly distributed over a bounded region $S\subset{\mathds R}^2$. Thus, by generating values of $(U,V)$ and computing the indicated ratio, samples from the random variable can be obtained. This procedure is now known as the ratio-of-uniforms method and relies heavily on our ability to produce uniform samples from $S$, for which an acceptance-rejection method is customarily used. In this paper, we propose three sampling schemes based on the polar representation of $S$. The first uses a covering consisting of triangles, the second uses a covering based on circular sectors, while the third employs rectangular coverings of an associated angular density. Numerical examples illustrate that these schemes can achieve acceptance rates close to $100\%$.

papers.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
papers.abstract: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $λ^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = λ$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $λ$.

papers.title: Adaptive Blockwise Tensor Trains for Stochastic Finite-Volume Methods with Uncertain Geometry
papers.abstract: Stochastic finite-volume (SFV) methods extend conservative, shock-capturing discretizations to hyperbolic systems with uncertain inputs by partitioning the parameter domain into finite-volume cells. However, their memory and computational cost grow exponentially with the number of uncertain parameters. Tensor-train (TT) formats can remove this exponential dependence, provided the ranks of the discrete solution remain small throughout the simulation. This requirement is frequently violated when the uncertainty is geometric. Mapping each realization onto a common reference domain introduces parameter-dependent metric factors, so that shocks and contacts propagate at different reference speeds and come to occupy different cells across realizations. The resulting rank growth is spatially localized - a structure that neither a single global TT nor a separate TT for each physical cell is able to exploit. We propose an adaptive blockwise TT representation in which the SFV solution is partitioned along its physical mode into contiguous blocks, each stored as an independent TT for every conserved variable. Blocks are split near discontinuities and in regions of large variance or rank, and merged where the solution is smooth. The mesh itself is never changed; only the grouping of cells into trains adapts.
