The developed framework is applied to three representative inverse problems -- simple source inversion, inverse obstacle scattering, and inverse heat conduction. All three examples substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed methods and, at the same time, demonstrate their broad applicability.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Peskine-Szpiro's conjectures on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to the remaining homological conjectures of Peskine-Szpiro concerning modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. Specifically, we show that the dimension inequality, the strong intersection conjecture, and the grade conjecture are all false in general.

papers.title: Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions:\ Thermodynamic Formalism, Livšic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion
papers.abstract: We study the transfer of Gibbs estimates between a compact dynamical system and a factor with uniformly contracting fibers. A cohomological identity relates the orbit sums; the remaining issue is the comparison of Bowen-ball masses. Subexponential comparison errors give directional weak Gibbs transfer, while bounded errors preserve strong estimates. We also establish a blockwise sequential version along prescribed Gibbs-time sequences, with errors measured against the full block length. Geometric and conditional-mass hypotheses provide practical criteria for these comparisons. A stationary renewal model shows that the distinction between bounded and subexponential comparison is essential. Its invariant lift to a contracting Cantor-fiber extension is not supported on a measurable graph, and the optimal uniform forward logarithmic error is $\log n+O(1)$. This remains true under fixed changes of the base radius. The reverse comparison, along a specified section, has bounded error. We also give an example in which pointwise subexponential bounds cannot be made uniform. For context, projection gives an affine bijection of invariant probability measures and preserves entropy. When the potentials are cohomologous, invariant averages and pressure agree, as do minimizing measures and equilibrium states in the finite-pressure regime. For Hölder potentials, a continuous section yields a stable-direction reduction, with Hölder regularity under additional assumptions. Subactions and Livšic solutions can then be lifted whenever the corresponding quotient hypotheses hold.

papers.title: Rigid motion invariant valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that any measurable, translation and $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-invariant valuation on polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a linear combination of the intrinsic volumes, which extends Hadwiger's classical characterization of rigid motion invariant continuous valuations on convex bodies. This result is based on a novel regularity result for translation invariant, measurable, $1$-homogeneous, and simple valuations. As a consequence, we obtain a similar characterization of the Steiner point map on polytopes.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of generalized modified splitting methods using multi-index series
papers.abstract: We consider splitting methods for partial differential equations involving unbounded operators. For non-time-reversible dynamics, such as dissipative systems, negative splitting coefficients are generally not admissible because they require stepping backward in time, leading to an order barrier when all coefficients are required to be positive. We introduce generalized modified splitting methods that overcome this algebraic order barrier while retaining nonnegative splitting coefficients. To analyze their convergence, we develop a decorated multi-index series formalism and establish a substitution law that provides a systematic framework for deriving order conditions. This law also yields an order-raising procedure based on canceling the leading error through a modification of a single stage. We also derive an explicit composition law for extended multi-index series allowing the composition of methods with independently scaled time steps common in composition and processed methods. We illustrate the construction with two sixth-order methods that use different sets of commutator corrections. Python scripts automate the computation and verification of order conditions and the construction of the methods. Finally, we discuss connections with word series, Lie-Butcher series, and multi-index Butcher series.

papers.title: Origametry and antagonistic heptagon graphs: the braced {35,1} and the complete {21,2}
papers.abstract: We study two planar unit-distance graphs (UDGs) that both look like heptagons but have opposite rigidity yet kindred arithmetic: the braced heptagon {35,1} (19 vertices, 35 edges) and the complete heptagon {21,2} (21 vertices, 42 edges). Neither is straightedge-and-compass constructible -- already the regular 7-gon is not, by Gauss-Wantzel -- so the natural setting is origametry: the construction of each realization by Huzita-Hatori folds, with the quadratic fold O5 (straightedge-and-compass strength) versus the cubic Beloch fold O6. The complete heptagon is over-braced and globally rigid, with a unique realization whose 42 edges are certified unit exactly, with coordinates in Q(cos pi/42), of degree 12 (minimal over all placements), containing the cubic Q(cos 2pi/7): every vertex is an origami number. It is Haugland's H21, whose two heptagram layers are the seed of the 449-vertex 5-chromatic graph of Heule and Przybocki. The braced heptagon is isostatic (minimally rigid) with thousands of non-congruent realizations and a large generic realization count N = 3869504 = 2^6 * 103 * 587; yet we prove that its unit realization is again origami-constructible. In Pegg's explicit construction the pinning angle is a root of an irreducible degree-12 palindromic polynomial whose Chebyshev reduction, an irreducible sextic, factors into quadratics over the heptagon cubic Q(cos 2pi/7); hence the coordinate field is a {2,3}-tower of degree 3*2^k, reached by one trisection followed by quadratics. The primes 103 and 587 belong to the generic complex count, not to the folded coordinates. We solve the governing cubic by folding (Lill's method and the Beloch fold), place both graphs inside Alperin's field of origami numbers, and read the fold-branch signs of the construction as mountain-valley assignments with an empirical Maekawa-type balance. All claims are checked in exact arithmetic.

papers.title: Local and global invertibility of pluriharmonic mappings
papers.abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional Kneser theorem for pluriharmonic maps on bounded Stein domains whose closures are topological manifolds with boundary. A homeomorphism on the boundary and containment in the target domain imply a homeomorphism of the closures and a real-analytic diffeomorphism of the interiors. We classify pluriharmonic homeomorphisms between round shells in $\C^n$ for $n\ge2$. Such maps exist exactly when the two inner-to-outer radius ratios agree, and each is the restriction of a centered real similarity. We also prove the local Lewy theorem in every complex dimension: local injectivity is equivalent to a nonvanishing real Jacobian. For smooth boundary data, a formula counts the critical points of each real scalar projection with their holomorphic multiplicities. The boundary criterion gives removability for maps on punctured domains. For bounded pluriharmonic maps of controlled distortion, we obtain Lipschitz estimates on bounded $C^2$ domains in complex dimension at least two. For quasiconformal pluriharmonic homeomorphisms, we derive bi-Lipschitz bounds for convex targets and for pairs of domains with Dini-smooth boundaries under the corresponding source regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Peripheral Traps and Lower Bounds on Mixing Times for Random Walks on Sparse Heavy-Tailed Random Intersection Graphs
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes mixing time lower bounds for random walks on sparse, heavy-tailed Random Intersection Graphs. In sparse feature regimes, heavy-tailed feature distributions lead to the formation of peripheral trap -- chains of overlapping low-weight feature cliques attached to high-weight hub nodes within the graph's giant component. By modeling escape trajectories from these traps as continuous limit hitting times for reflected Brownian motion, the analysis demonstrates that random walks experience logarithmic squared delays. Consequently, the mixing time is bounded below by $Ω(\log^2 n)$, and the local total variation distance exhibits non-concentrated decay, formally preventing a sharp cutoff phenomenon.

papers.title: An Orlicz variational formula for David-type Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: We develop a Banach-space variational theory for degenerate Beltrami equations of David type. For coefficients supported in a bounded domain $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathbb{C}$, the pointwise change of variables $ν=2μ/(1-|μ|^2)$ identifies the David coefficients with the exponential Orlicz space $L^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ for $Φ(s)=e^s-s-1$. On the open subset of parameters with a sufficiently large exponential moment, the principal solution map is locally real $C^{1,1}$ into $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{C})$, with Fréchet derivative solving the linearized Beltrami equation. On the Orlicz heart $E^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ it is real $C^\infty$, yet fails to be real analytic at zero: along any direction $h$, its Taylor series at zero has radius of convergence $1/\|h\|_\infty$ in $W^{1,2}(B)$ for every disk $B\supset\overline{\mathcal{U}}$. Finally, for $\mathcal{U}=\mathbb{D}$, the exterior Schwarzian map from $E^Φ_{\mathbb{D}}(\mathbb{C})$ to the little logarithmic Bers space is continuous, but fails to be Fréchet differentiable at zero; moreover, its zero fiber is not a $C^1$ embedded Banach submanifold near zero, obstructing any local $C^1$ split submersion structure on the resulting quotient.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of the tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices with diagonals 1, 0, 0, 1
papers.abstract: We perform a thorough analysis of the eigenvalues of tetradiagonal Toeplitz matrices of large order $n$ generated by the Laurent polynomial $a(t)=t^2+t^{-1}$. The spectra of these matrices are invariant under $2π/3$-rotation. They are contained in three segments of the complex plane and asymptotically fill these segments as $n$ tends to infinity. We apply Widom's formula for the determinants and transform the characteristic equation into a convenient form that can be solved by the fixed point iteration method. The main results are asymptotic formulas for the eigenvalues, both close to the origin and far from the origin. The main results are verified by numerical tests for moderate values of $n$.

papers.title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret under Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.abstract: We study online convex optimization on a compact convex domain of diameter $D$ in which the learner observes, at each round, one stochastic subgradient and no loss values. The observations are conditionally unbiased, and the noise has an unconditional $p$-th moment at most $σ^p$ for an unknown $p\in(1,2]$; for $p<2$ its variance may be infinite. For a comparator sequence of path length $P_T$ we write $Λ_T=1+P_T/D$, and we show that the minimax expected dynamic regret is, up to numerical constants, \[ \min\Bigl\{GD\sqrt{TΛ_T}+σDT^{1/p}Λ_T^{(p-1)/p},\ GDT\Bigr\}, \] where $G$ bounds the subgradients. The lower bound holds on every compact convex domain of positive diameter. An algorithm that combines AdaGrad learners restarted at different frequencies through exponential weights with a data-dependent learning rate attains this rate for each fixed $p>1$, without knowing $G$, $σ$, $p$, or $P_T$: the constant of the first term is numerical, the constant of the second is $O(1+\log(p/(p-1)))$, and no logarithmic factor of $T$ appears. The analysis bounds the gradient energy separately on each restart block, which gives the exponent $(p-1)/p$ of $Λ_T$ in the noise term; a bound over the whole horizon gives the exponent $1/2$. Running the algorithm on epochs of doubling length removes the need to know $T$ at the cost of a factor $2+\sqrt2$. The appendices give a high-probability version and a synthetic study.

papers.title: Convergence of entropy-conservative summation-by-parts discretizations to smooth solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: Although entropy-based summation-by-parts (SBP) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws are widely used for their robustness and stability properties, there are very few results on their convergence. We extend a recent convergence analysis of Worku, Del Rey Fernández, and Zingg (2026, DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2603.18369) in two ways. First, instead of allowing only hyperbolic conservation laws whose fluxes are homogeneous and have globally bounded second derivatives (a restriction essentially to linear or quadratic fluxes), we consider general hyperbolic systems with strictly convex entropy and source terms depending on time and space. Second, instead of requiring a special class of SBP operators, we consider a general framework of diagonal-norm SBP operators on curved meshes, including finite differences, continuous and discontinuous Galerkin methods. Since the error analysis is based on a discrete relative entropy, it is restricted to smooth solutions. To enable a unified treatment of conservation laws, we restrict the analysis to periodic boundary conditions. Numerical results demonstrate that the predicted convergence rates are sharp in general, but can be improved for special cases such as discontinuous Galerkin methods with even polynomial degree and multi-block finite difference methods. An optimal analysis is expected to require more sophisticated arguments specialized to the class of methods instead of the general framework of SBP operators used in this work.

papers.title: Analytical Evaluation of Signature 2 Ramanujan-Type Series via Elementary Transformations and Companion Harmonic Expansions
papers.abstract: We provide an explicit analytical evaluation of the known rational Ramanujan-type series for $1/π$ of signature $2$. Focusing on the singular moduli $k_r$ for $r \in \{2, 3, 4, 7\}$, we show that these invariants and their underlying elliptic identities follow from elementary transformations of complete elliptic integrals of the first and second kind. Using this framework, we derive two companion families of rational harmonic Ramanujan-type series for the reciprocal of $π$ involving higher-degree polynomials

papers.title: Edge State Propagation Near Multiple and Singular Interfaces
papers.abstract: We study the semiclassical propagation of edge-states for a two-dimensional Dirac operator with a spatially varying mass. The zero set of the mass models the interface between topological phases and is allowed either to consist of two disjoint smooth curves or to possess an isolated singular point. For disjoint interfaces, we prove that a wave packet initially localized on one component remains confined near this interface over long semiclassical time scales and we quantify the influence of the distance between the two components on the accuracy of the approximation. For singular interfaces, we determine the regime in which the wave-packet approximation remains valid as the packet approaches the singularity and identify the scaling at which our estimates lose their uniformity.

papers.title: Pathwise Uniqueness for Cyclically Catalytic Branching Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study pathwise uniqueness for cyclic catalytic stochastic differential equations whose state-dependent square-root diffusion coefficients are non-Lipschitz and degenerate on the boundary. The approach is the direct construction of a strong solution using a Malliavin compactness criterion. The key is the development of a new family of boundary-sensitive weighted Malliavin estimates for the tangent processes of the smooth approximations. Pathwise uniqueness then follows from the dual Yamada-Watanabe argument together with the weak uniqueness available in the literature.

papers.title: A Markov duration model with power-law decay via level-slope matching
papers.abstract: We develop a two-dimensional Markov duration model with power-law rate decay and a flexible residual distribution. The two state variables specify the excitation level and decay scale of a single power-law rate curve, and each update matches the level and slope jumps of a power-law Hawkes intensity. Under a sufficient stability condition, a finite residual mean, and a positive continuous residual density, the state at event times is positive Harris recurrent and converges geometrically in total variation to a unique invariant distribution. With unit exponential residuals, the sufficient region contains every parameter value for which the matched Hawkes process is subcritical. We apply the model to E-mini S\&P 500 futures and NVDA midquote durations at several price-change thresholds. Flexible residual laws improve likelihood-based fit, and power-law decay lowers one-step negative log predictive scores relative to exponential decay. An autoregressive conditional duration model generally leaves less residual autocorrelation, while forecast rankings vary with the price threshold and evaluation criterion.

papers.title: A Syntactic Approach to Ulmer's Bialgebras
papers.abstract: Ulmer proposed to view a bialgebraic structure on an object $x$ as a structure map $f\colon Fx\to Gx$ satisfying an equation $α_{(x,f)} = β_{(x,f)}$ of natural transformations. This perspective is powerful enough to account for many algebraic and coalgebraic structures, such as varieties of universal algebra, categories of algebras over a PROP, an operad or a monad. We develop Ulmer's bialgebras within a $2$-categorical setting with PIE limits, where structure maps are abstracted by inserters and their equations by equifiers. A syntax of signatures, theories and models is then used to produce these bialgebraic structures. The syntax of the commutative diagrams defining Hopf algebras can be used, as is, to define the $0$-cell of Hopf algebras within any symmetric pseudomonoid in a $2$-category with PIE limits. In this setting, we show that lax morphisms of models induce morphisms between the objects of algebras, extending the classical result lifting a lax monoidal functor to a functor between the categories of internal monoids. Since the construction of the object of bialgebras is expressed entirely in terms of PIE limits, we show that Kan extensions, accessibility, local presentability, orthogonal factorization systems, regularity, and Barr-exactness lift along the construction under suitable assumptions. A bi-dense class of objects allows us to transfer monadicity and local presentability results to formal settings. Finally, we construct a bi-dense class of $\V$-categories with at most three objects, where $\V$ is any monoidal category with an absorbing initial object.

papers.title: Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests
papers.abstract: Let $F_q$ be the rooted forest sampled by Wilson's algorithm for a finite reversible Markov chain killed at rate $q$. We express the probability that $k$ prescribed vertices are roots as a product. For the $i$th factor, start an evolving set from the singleton consisting of the $i$th vertex, in the domain obtained by removing the preceding $i-1$ vertices. The factor is the probability that the set contains its starting vertex at an independent exponential time of rate $q$. These factors are the successive Schur-complement pivots of the determinantal root kernel. The construction couples the walk up to its exit from a domain with the evolving set biased by its mass. For the ordinary evolving set, the expected mass at that time divided by the initial mass is the probability that the walk has not yet left the domain. We use the probability that a second walk hits the first Wilson branch to bound the probability that two vertices belong to the same component. For a symmetric transition kernel, the expected size of the component of any vertex is at most $(1+1/q)^2$. Under a Gaussian heat-kernel upper bound with exponent $ν>4$, we also obtain spatial decay on the scale $q^{-1/2}$, up to a finite-volume correction.

papers.title: Graph-Induced Rotational Twisted States in Systems of Identical Oscillators
papers.abstract: In this article, we study a new class of collective motion for identical coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators on graphs. This model was previously known to converge to the synchronized state for a certain class of initial data. Here, we show that when the interaction matrix is circulant, there exists another class of attractors, in which the particles are uniformly distributed on a circle, reminiscent of the \textit{twisted states} known for the Kuramoto model, but which rotate around the origin. However, contrary to the classical Kuramoto case, here the rotation is caused by the asymmetry of the graph structure, and not by the natural frequencies. We identify conditions for the existence and local stability of the \textit{rotational twisted states}, both in the Stuart-Landau model and in the Kuramoto model. We also provide sufficient conditions for the existence and stability of the synchronized state, which can co-exist with the rotational twisted state in a certain parameter region. We provide a generalization of the class of interaction matrices able to generate rotational twisted states via leader-follower interaction matrices. We show that heterogeneous rotational twisted states can also exist for a system of heterogeneous oscillators, attracted to different individual target amplitudes. This study is accompanied by numerical simulations that illustrate the possible behaviors of the system, which also include metastable dynamics and a chimera state.

papers.title: Higher-power inverse functional identities and Frobenius collision obstructions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring, let $n\geq 2$, and let $f,g:D\to D$ be additive maps satisfying $f(x)x^{-1}+x^n g(x^{-1})=0$ for every nonzero $x\in D$. We establish general vanishing criteria, give an explicit classification over finite fields, and determine the additive-polynomial solutions over infinite fields of positive characteristic. If $\mathbb{F}_q\subseteq Z(D)$, every additive map $D\to D$ admits a canonical decomposition into $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$-weight components, and the identity pairs precisely the weights $r,s$ satisfying $r+s\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Consequently, for $q=p^m$, the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the solution space is the number of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $0\leq i,j<m$ satisfying $p^i+p^j\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Over an infinite field of characteristic $p>0$, the additive-polynomial solutions are exactly the sums of paired Frobenius terms with $p^i+p^j=n+1$. This classification concerns additive-polynomial maps and does not assert a classification of arbitrary additive maps. Prime-field dilation gives complete vanishing in characteristic zero and, in characteristic $p>0$, whenever $p-1$ does not divide $n-1$. In characteristic two, we prove complete vanishing for $n=2$ on every noncommutative division ring. More generally, when $[D:Z(D)]=\infty$, every solution vanishes if the center is infinite. If the center is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, the same conclusion holds for $2\leq n\leq q-1$. The remaining cases are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Homological Topological Quantum Field Theories
papers.abstract: We develop a new framework for quantum invariants of $3$-manifolds by extending to cobordisms a homological construction of mapping class group representations. More specifically, we construct a $(2+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theory (TQFT) that assigns to each surface the twisted homology of its unordered configuration space. The construction requires a choice of local systems on configuration spaces together with additional data. We formulate sufficient conditions on these data that guarantee the TQFT axioms, and we show that there are at least two useful examples satisfying them. One of them yields a homological construction of the projective Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, while the other recovers the Frohman--Nicas--Donaldson TQFT. In contrast to the classical algebraic constructions of quantum invariants, our approach is purely topological and relies on multi-trajectory spaces of cobordisms.

papers.title: On $F$-thresholds of differential power filtrations
papers.abstract: We study the $F$-threshold of differential power filtrations of monomial ideals. We give the existence of this number and show that it is upper bounded by the maximum height of the minimal primes of the underlying monomial ideal. As an application of our results, we show that the dimension of the polynomial ring and the $F$-threshold of the differential power filtration of the monomial maximal ideal are the same.

papers.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
papers.abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.

papers.title: $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a graph with $m>0$ edges and $n$ non-isolated vertices. For every $ρ$-locally dense graphon $W$, we prove that $\|W_F\|_q\geρ^m$ whenever $q\ge\binom n2/m$, where $W_F$ is the product of $W$ over the edges of $F$. The KNRS conjecture asks for this bound at $q=1$. More generally, averaging over the automorphisms of an edge-transitive KNRS supergraph $J$ yields the sufficient exponent $e(J)/m$; for $ρ>0$ and $q>e(J)/m$, equality holds only for constant graphons. The proof averages over vertex relabellings via Hölder's inequality, in the spirit of Conlon and Lee. We also prove that replacing every edge of a Sidorenko-good graph by a fixed theta pattern preserves goodness for all branch lengths, and that applying the same substitution to a KNRS graph yields a regular-KNRS graph. For non-uniform substitutions, we establish goodness under the branch-count conditions of Im, Li, and Liu and determine when equality forces the kernel to be constant. Passing to the one-subdivision recovers their theorem for even branch lengths.

papers.title: Stochastic Operator Algebras: Intrinsic Cumulant Geometry
papers.abstract: If an orthogonal projection splits a random vector into independent parts, every mixed cumulant across the cut vanishes. For a family of cuts we identify the subspaces on which higher cumulants can survive. A distance bound on vectors characterizes when square-integrable defects at the individual cuts admit a simultaneous correction by a Hilbert tensor. The criterion is the same in every integer degree $r\ge3$ and can be tested on Hilbert-space-valued random variables. For laws fixed by random recombination, uniform cutting supplies the moment asked for by Courtade. The minimum dimension of a nonzero finite-dimensional common reducing subspace determines the optimal fourth-moment ratio. A separate application to polynomial optimization characterizes the $r^{-2}$ push-forward rate on a convex body by the boundary area of sublevel sets at regular minima.

papers.title: A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where $u$ carries a weak signal while $\log u$ diverges and the entropy density $u\log u$ falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density $u$, the log-density $\log u$, the entropy density $u\log u$, and the score $\nabla\log u$, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to $1024$ where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.

papers.title: Local solutions to hyperbolic systems with fractional dissipation
papers.abstract: We study the local Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^α$ with arbitrary $α\in(0,1)$ in the framework of Sobolev spaces. The analysis is motivated by the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest order nonlocal terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem to provide local existence for large initial data. The resulting theory identifies the obstacles to deduce local uniqueness in the presence of commutators.

papers.title: On triviality and scalar curvature estimation of gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons
papers.abstract: In this study we have explored gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons on both compact and complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. We have established several sufficient conditions for the triviality of such solitons with respect to integral inequalities involving the scalar curvature and the soliton function. In this regard, we have acquired scalar curvature estimation under certain $L^1$ and $L^2$ integrability conditions, and defined signal of the function $h$. Our results extend and refine former works on almost and $h$-almost Yamabe solitons, and characterize the geometric structures of generalized Yamabe solitons.

papers.title: Computing canonical labellings of finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: We define a canonical labelling function on the class of finite solvable groups so that two such groups $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic if and only if can$(G)=$can$(H)$. Specifically, can$(G)$ is a group presentation that describes a group isomorphic to $G$, and our description explains how to construct an isomorphism $G\to$can$(G)$. Our approach is motivated by O'Brien's (1993) canonical presentations for finite $p$-groups and utilises ideas from group cohomology first described by Robinson (1982) and automorphism group algorithms developed by Smith (1994), Holt (2001), and others. We also discuss a proof-of-concept implementation for the computer algebra system GAP and comment on the major bottlenecks and open research questions.

papers.title: Polynomial valuations on plane polygons
papers.abstract: Scissors congruence problems involving translations have prompted the study of translation invariant simple valuations. We review this classical theory from a naive and consistent viewpoint: starting from a description of all simple valuations on polygons, we characterize the effect of translation invariance. A description of all polynomial simple valuations is obtained as a bi-product of the adopted approach and as a direct generalization of the translation invariant theory; it appears to be new.

papers.title: Optimized high-order IMEX-RK schemes for degenerate diffusion-reaction problems with application to travelling waves phenomena
papers.abstract: We study a class of IMplicit-EXplicit Runge--Kutta (IMEX-RK) schemes for the numerical approximation of reaction and diffusion-reaction problems arising in a variety of biological and physical applications. Such models may admit travelling wave solutions, with the Fisher--Kolmogorov equation representing a prototypical example. Motivated by this feature, the proposed time integration schemes are designed to accurately capture sharp propagating fronts. We also investigate a less standard use of IMEX-RK methods that circumvents a splitting of reaction terms into linear and nonlinear components, while still requiring the solution of linear systems at each stage. This semi-implicit formulation, referred to as SI-IMEX-RK, enables a targeted treatment of stiffness by isolating its relevant contributions. The time discretization is coupled with a high-order polygonal discontinuous Galerkin method for space discretization, resulting in a flexible and robust framework for the treatment of multiscale dynamics in complex geometries. A comprehensive validation strategy is presented to assess the accuracy and stability properties of the proposed schemes across a hierarchy of increasingly challenging test problems.

papers.title: On a local variant of the 12th Delfino problem -- the $Π$-side
papers.abstract: Assume that \(M_n\), the canonical inner model with \(n\) Woodin cardinals, exists, where \(1\leq n<ω\). We force a cardinal-preserving extension of \(M_n\) in which CH holds and the reals have a lightface \(Δ^1_{n+3}\) wellorder. In this extension \(\bfΣ^1_{n+3}\)-separation holds and rules out every good \(\bfΔ^1_{n+3}\) wellorder of the reals. Every boldface \(\bfΣ^1_{n+2}\) set of reals is Lebesgue measurable and has the Baire property, and \(\bfΠ^1_{n+1}\)-determinacy fails. Thus the regularity and wellorder at the levels suggested by \(M_{n+1}\) can already be obtained by forcing over \(M_n\). For odd \(n\), \(\bfΔ^1_{n+1}\)-determinacy also fails. Hence for odd \(n\geq3\) we answer the adjacent-level Friedman--Schindler question negatively, while for even \(n\geq2\) we answer its \(Π\)-determinacy variant negatively. We prove in \(\ZFC\) that for every \(k\geq2\), a \(\bfΔ^1_k\) wellorder of the reals precludes \(\bfΠ^1_k\)-reduction. Hence \(\bfΠ^1_{n+3}\)-reduction and \(\bfΠ^1_{n+3}\)-uniformization fail in our extension.

papers.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.

papers.title: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux differentiability space : over 46 years of open problem solved
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, an iterative and rigid theory of weak\(^{*}\) slices in a non-metric setting, demonstrating that dual convex sets admit localization, diameter control and fine structural analysis under the pure weak\(^{*}\) topology. It fundamentally reshapes the classical perspective on the geometric features of the weak\(^{*}\) topology and thereby pioneers a new direction in non-metric weak\(^{*}\) slice geometry. Using a novel technique built upon intricate manipulation of weak\(^{*}\) slices and a carefully engineered iterative selection scheme, we prove that if $M$ is a closed subspace of a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space $X$, then $M$ itself is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. As a corollary, we obtain that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, then $M$ is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. This settles definitively an open problem posed 46 years ago by D.G. Larman and R.R. Phelps (J. London Math. Soc., 20 (1979), 115-127).

papers.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
papers.abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

papers.title: Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
papers.abstract: By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.

papers.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.

papers.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, stable log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out consecutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

papers.title: Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resistance forms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study discrete approximations of semi-Dirichlet forms obtained by adding non-symmetric drift terms, expressed in terms of mutual energy measures, to resistance forms whose associated resistance metric spaces are compact. The main novelty is that the drift terms need not to be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Under suitable smallness assumptions, we prove generalized Mosco convergence of the approximating forms and derive weak convergence of the associated Feller processes. We also demonstrate the applicability of our main theorem to post-critically finite self-similar fractals and describe the resulting perturbation of the approximating jump chains in the case of the Sierpiński gasket.

papers.title: Logarithmic oscillatory multipliers and log-subdyadic square functions
papers.abstract: We develop square-function estimates for Fourier multipliers whose local oscillation scale is \[ ρ(R)=\frac{R}{(\log R)^{γ-1}}, \qquad γ>1. \] This scale lies strictly between the dyadic scale and every fixed power-subdyadic scale at high frequency. For high-frequency symbols satisfying a localized Sobolev condition on balls of radius comparable to $ρ(R)$, we prove a pointwise square-function estimate and a weighted $L^2$ multiplier inequality. After adjoining a smooth compactly supported low-frequency part, we derive unweighted $L^p$ bounds. The weighted estimate is governed by a logarithmic geometric maximal operator which is strongly bounded above the critical $L^r$ threshold, satisfies weak type at the critical equality, and fails even weak type below it. As a model application, consider \[ L(ξ)=\frac12\log(e^2+|ξ|^2), \qquad m_{γ,β}(ξ)=L(ξ)^{-β}e^{iL(ξ)^γ}. \] For $p=2$, the associated multiplier is bounded on $L^2$ for every $β\geq0$. For $1<p<\infty$, $p\neq2$, it is bounded on $L^p$ under the sufficient condition \[ β> d(γ-1)\left|\frac12-\frac1p\right|. \] At the critical equality we obtain the corresponding Lorentz endpoint estimates.

papers.title: A quasi-orthogonal method based on the inverse operator for Schrödinger eigenvalue problems
papers.abstract: The simultaneous computation of many Schrödinger eigenpairs requires mutually orthogonal eigenfunctions. We propose a quasi-orthogonal evolution model based on the inverse operator and a two-stage time discretization for nonorthogonal initial data. The continuous trajectory and discrete iterates remain full rank and approach orthogonality without any orthogonalization. The discretization preserves the current Gram matrix in the first stage and reduces the orthogonality error in the second. We establish well-posedness, energy decay, asymptotic orthogonality, and exponential convergence to the target eigenfunctions up to fixed orthogonal transformations. Numerical experiments for two Schr{ö}dinger eigenvalue problems validate the decay of the energy, gradient norm, and relative iterate error, while the iterates become numerically orthogonal. Further experiments show that the discrete time steps remain effective under mesh refinement, that convergence rates depend on the spectral gap, and that dynamically adjusting the solve accuracy can accelerate the computation.

papers.title: Incremental SVD for Large-Scale Dynamic Matrices: Accuracy, Subspace Stability, Refresh Strategies, and Financial Factor-Based Risk Models
papers.abstract: Return panels, covariances, and large feature matrices evolve one observation or entry at a time, yet downstream models require an up-to-date low-rank factorization $A_t \approx U_t Σ_t V_t^\top$ on every tick - a regime where a full singular value decomposition (SVD) is prohibitive and existing alternatives sacrifice singular vectors, singular values, or long-horizon stability. We present a metric-driven study of Brand-style incremental SVD, built around a unified engine that handles row appends, column appends, rank-1 entry updates, and metrics tracking. For rank-1 entry updates, we derive an explicit projection-based rule $U'Σ'(V')^\top = P_U(\widehat{A} + δ\,e_ie_j^\top)P_V$ that keeps rank fixed while discarding only the out-of-subspace remainder quantifiably, turning Brand's rank-suppression heuristic into an operational scheme. Each update discards a part whose norm is available at negligible cost; the error at the last refresh plus the sum of these norms since then is an a posteriori error bound $β_t$. We then treat refresh scheduling as a first-class design axis, comparing periodic refresh with a bound-triggered rule that refreshes once $β_t/\|A_t\|_F$ exceeds a tolerance. The engine tracks error ratios, principal angles, explained variance, and per-update runtime on long synthetic streams and a factor model of exchange-traded funds for covariance and portfolio-risk estimation. With a sensible rank and refresh cadence, incremental SVD matches full-SVD accuracy within a few percent at a fraction of the cost. The bound-triggered rule keeps the relative error below any tolerance above its rank-$k$ optimum, with accuracy close to periodic refresh at a matched number of full SVDs.

papers.title: A Mathematical Characterization of Neural Activation Induced by Temporal Interference Stimulation
papers.abstract: Temporal Interference Stimulation (TIS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique in which two high-frequency sinusoidal currents with slightly different frequencies generate a low-frequency envelope that can activate deep neural structures. This study investigates the conditions under which TIS elicits action potentials in a single neuron modeled by the FitzHugh-Nagumo system. This research integrates phase-plane analysis and geometric singular perturbation to develop a mathematical framework for analyzing TIS. By combining a mathematical analysis of differential equations with computer simulations, the study elucidates how the amplitudes and beat frequency jointly determine whether the neuron remains quiescent, exhibits only transient responses, or undergoes persistent (tonic) firing.

papers.title: The clumsy coupon collector's problem
papers.abstract: We consider a generalisation of the classical coupon collector's problem, in which at each time step a collector either receives a new copy of a randomly chosen coupon, or loses all their previously collected copies of that coupon. We consider the amount of time it takes this clumsy coupon collector to obtain the full set of $m$ coupons. We establish limit theorems as $m\to\infty$ for the clumsy coupon collection time, and describe the large $m$ asymptotics of its mean and variance. We identify three regimes, depending on how the probability of a clumsy update, $p$, scales with $m$. If $p=o(1/m)$, we obtain a Gumbel limit theorem, as is the case for the classical coupon collector. If $p=ω(1/m)$, we instead show weak convergence to an exponential random variable. In the critical case, $p\sim c/m$, we give a full characterisation of the limiting distribution in terms of a birth-and-death process. We also describe the asymptotics of the mean and variance in these three regimes.

papers.title: Robust stochastic first order methods in heavy-tailed noise via medoid mini-batch gradient sampling
papers.abstract: We consider a first order stochastic optimization framework where, at each iteration, $K$ independent identically distributed (i.i.d.) data point samples are drawn, based on which stochastic gradients can be queried. We allow gradient noise to be heavy-tailed, with possibly infinite variances. For the considered heavy-tailed setting, many algorithmic variants have recently been proposed based on gradient clipping or other nonlinear operators (e.g., normalization) applied over noisy gradients. In this paper, we take an alternative approach and propose a novel gradient estimator. The core idea of proposed estimator is to split the $K$-sized data batch into $M$ distinct data chunks, form for each chunk the stochastic gradient, and select the stochastic gradient of the chunk that is medoid of gradients of all data-chunks. For a broad class of symmetric heavy-tailed gradient noise distributions, we show that the proposed estimator has a finite second moment even when the underlying gradient noise has an infinite second moment. For nonconvex objectives, this yields convergence to a neighborhood of zero in expected squared gradient norm at a rate of $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$. We explicitly characterize the size of this neighborhood in terms of the noise and algorithm parameters. When the time horizon $T$ is known in advance, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. A diminishing step size achieves the same rate up to a logarithmic factor. Incorporating clipping or a more general nonlinear transformation yields high-probability convergence guarantees with the same rate up to logarithmic factors. Experimental results indicate that R-SGD-Mini and its clipped or nonlinear variant consistently perform favorably compared to SGD, clipped SGD, Nonlinear SGD and Median-of-Means based methods.

papers.title: The Threshold Breakdown Point
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel approach to finite sample robustness that avoids the pessimism of traditional breakdown analyses. We define the threshold breakdown point, the smallest contamination fraction needed to induce a prescribed deviation, and the finite sample $m$-sensitivity, the worst-case deviation that an estimator can incur after $m$ observations are contaminated. We derive these measures for commonly used $M$-estimators, their standard errors and related test statistics. This allows us to extend the decision breakdown point of Zhang (1996) to obtain general breakdown characterizations for hypothesis testing, and show how these notions connect to finite sample counterparts of the power and level breakdown functions of He, Simpson and Portnoy (1990). We complement our work with an inferential framework for the threshold breakdown and $m$-sensitivity that yields consistency and asymptotic normality results, as well as a valid multiplier bootstrap for uncertainty quantification. We illustrate the practical utility of our methods in various numerical examples and an application to a two sample testing problem for a blood pressure dataset.

papers.title: Sharp regularity for degenerate fully nonlinear equations with oblique boundary conditions and Hamiltonian terms
papers.abstract: We prove optimal boundary $C^{1,α}$ regularity for viscosity solutions of degenerate fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with oblique boundary conditions and Hamiltonian terms of the form \[ \begin{cases} |Du|^γF(D^2 u) + \varrho(x)|Du|^σ = f(x) & \text{in } Ω,\\ β(x)\cdot Du+ζ(x)u = g(x) & \text{on } \partial Ω, \end{cases} \] where $γ>0$ and $0<σ\le 1+γ$. We develop a compactness framework for affine translations, linking the size of the translation to the Hamiltonian structure. This is combined with a boundary improvement-of-flatness argument adapted to oblique boundary data, yielding the optimal boundary regularity.

papers.title: Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI
papers.abstract: We study the ferromagnetic random field Ising model (RFIM) on a graph $G=(V,E)$ having maximal degree $Δ$, where the external field at each vertex is an i.i.d. random variable. When the random field distribution is sufficiently anti-concentrated, we prove that with high probability over the quenched randomness of the external field, the Glauber dynamics of this RFIM mixes in polynomial time as a consequence of a Poincaré inequality. This model is relevant to the Griffiths phase where the correlations decay exponentially fast in expectation over the quenched random field, but contraction does not hold point-wise due to the existence of weak fields that lead to low-temperature behavior. Previously, fast mixing of Glauber dynamics under large disorder was only proven on the integer lattice, and for RFIM on general graphs, only a sampling algorithm based on self-avoiding walks was known. Under a further technical condition that the random fields are bounded, we prove a modified log-Sobolev inequality for the Glauber dynamics. When the random field is weaker but still satisfies weak spatial mixing (exponential decay of correlations from boundary to bulk) in expectation, and the graph has $α$-stretched-exponential growth for some $α<1$, we prove a weak Poincaré inequality. If weak spatial mixing holds uniformly along a given sequence of growing induced subgraphs, we further obtain a polynomial-time sampling algorithm based on Glauber dynamics with warm starts. These results extend the corresponding weak Poincaré and sampling results from the integer lattice to graphs with $α$-stretched-exponential growth.

papers.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
papers.abstract: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.

papers.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
papers.abstract: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-τ(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $τ(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $Δ(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $Δ(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $Δ(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.

papers.title: Families of Eliahou semigroups linked to Farey intervals
papers.abstract: We describe new classes of numerical semigroups with a Farey interval as a crucial parameter. We compute their Eliahou number and show many cases in which it is negative, encompassing families described by Delgado, Eliahou and Fromentin, and Bras-Amorós. We show that all these semigroups satisfy Wilf's conjecture. This work is based on an experimental search that found all Eliahou-negative semigroups with conductor up to 200 (and conjecturally up to 400) thanks to a new way of representing the semigroup and pruning off unwanted branches. This proves that Wilf's conjecture holds for conductor up to 200.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs
papers.abstract: We study backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) in infinite horizon and {design} efficient numerical schemes for solving them. We establish a probabilistic representation of the solution of the BSDE using Malliavin derivative and prove results for contraction of a Picard scheme. We develop three numerical schemes, of which the first two are based on a fixed point argument using contraction, imposing additional assumptions compared to what is needed for existence and uniqueness of the solution. The first scheme is a space grid based approximation where we establish tight numerical error bounds using a growth truncation argument; it performs well in low dimensions but computational times increase exponentially with dimension. The second scheme uses neural network approximations for which we have proved a convergence result. Using neural networks alleviates the curse of dimensionality, giving good accuracy in very high dimensions. The third scheme also uses neural networks but does not directly rely on a contraction scheme, showcasing good performance even for larger z-Lipschitz dependence outside the empirical domain of contraction.

papers.title: Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model
papers.abstract: We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ is $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\}) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where the conductances $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\})$ are independent, uniformly elliptic and have a common mean. Below the critical exponent $(d+2)$ the walk converges to a stable process; above it, to Brownian motion with diffusive $\sqrt{t}$ scaling. At criticality the second moment of the jump kernel diverges logarithmically. We establish quantitative homogenization of the associated heat equation at the rate $1/\sqrt{|\ln \varepsilon|}$. As a consequence, we deduce annealed convergence of the random walk to Brownian motion under the anomalous $\sqrt{t \log t}$ scaling. Unlike in standard homogenization, the effective diffusivity is determined by the mean conductance alone, with no corrector contribution at leading order.

papers.title: An Implicit Compact-Kernel Material Point Method for Computational Solid Mechanics
papers.abstract: The numerical performance of the material point method (MPM) is strongly governed by the particle-grid kernel, which controls the trade-off among smoothness, locality, numerical diffusion, contact accuracy, and computational cost. Although wide-support smooth kernels can effectively suppress cell-crossing instability, they often introduce increased numerical diffusion, artificial contact gaps, and higher transfer cost. In contrast, the suitability of compact-kernel designs for implicit computational solid mechanics remains unclear. In this work, we develop an implicit formulation of the Compact-Kernel Material Point Method (CK-MPM) building on the framework of Liu et al. [2025], and assess its performance through benchmark problems in linear and nonlinear solid mechanics. Numerical assessment comprises cantilever bending, Hertzian contact, narrow-clearance free fall, and colliding hyperelastic rings, supplemented by a transfer-only diffusion test and spatial and temporal refinement studies. Implicit CK-MPM mitigates the cell-crossing stress noise and numerical energy loss observed in linear MPM, while retaining bending and energy responses comparable to those of quadratic B-spline MPM. Meanwhile, its more localized transfers improve contact-pressure accuracy and reduce the artificial contact gaps and early-contact artifacts associated with the wider-support quadratic kernel. These results demonstrate that the developed implicit formulation retains CK-MPM's favorable balance between smoothness and transfer locality in static and dynamic solid-mechanics analysis.

papers.title: Birational $\mathbb P^2$-bundle structures and toric 2-Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general birational program toward the classification of toric 2-Fano manifolds through the investigation of the minimal projective bundle dimension \(m(X) \in \{1,\dots,\dim(X)\}\) introduced in our previous work. This invariant captures the minimal degree of a dominating family of rational curves on \(X\) and admits a natural combinatorial interpretation in terms of centered primitive collections. We establish a general obstruction to being 2-Fano in terms of the existence of projective bundle structures and prove a birational reduction theorem for toric Fano manifolds with \(m(X)=2\). This allows us to show that the only toric 2-Fano manifold \(X\) with \(m(X) = 2\) is \(X\cong \mathbb{P}^2\). We also investigate how this strategy might extend to \(m\ge3\).

papers.title: Ultracontact algebras and stack systems
papers.abstract: We study the class of structures that, in a way, generalize various approaches to the contact relation on Boolean algebras.

papers.title: Infinitely many associated primes of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings
papers.abstract: We construct examples of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings with infinitely many associated primes and infinite Bass numbers.

papers.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.title: A High-Order Fast Direct Solver for Surface PDEs on Triangles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a triangular formulation of the hierarchical Poincaré--Steklov (HPS) method for elliptic partial differential equations on surfaces. It admits high-order discretizations on unstructured triangular meshes of complex geometries, with spectral collocation in the orthogonal Dubiner basis on each element. As in quadrilateral HPS, local solution operators and Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps are built and merged hierarchically, yielding a fast direct solver with $\mathcal O(N \log N)$ complexity for repeated solves on meshes with $N$ elements. Since the precomputed operators are reused for every elliptic solve, the solver also accelerates high-order implicit time-stepping schemes on surfaces. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order convergence under mesh refinement and spectral accuracy under polynomial refinement for static and time-dependent test problems.

papers.title: Soft projections for robust data-driven control
papers.abstract: We consider data-based predictive control based on behavioral systems theory. In the linear setting this means that a system is described as a subspace of trajectories, and predictive control can be formulated using a projection onto the intersection of this behavior and a constraint set. Instead of learning the model, or subspace, we focus on determining this projection from data. Motivated by the use of regularization in data-enabled predictive control (DeePC), we introduce the use of soft projections, which approximate the true projector onto the behavior from noisy data. In the simplest case, these are equivalent to known regularized DeePC schemes, but they exhibit a number of benefits. First, we provide a bound on the approximation error consisting of a bias and a variance term that can be traded-off by the regularization weight. The derived bound is independent of the true system order, highlighting the benefit of soft projections compared to low-dimensional subspace estimates. Moreover, soft projections allow for intuitive generalizations, one of which we show has superior performance on a case study. Finally, we provide update formulas for soft projectors enabling the efficient adaptation of the proposed data-driven control methods in the case of streaming data.

papers.title: List Estimation
papers.abstract: Classical estimation outputs a single point estimate of an unknown $d$-dimensional vector from an observation. In this paper, we study \emph{$k$-list estimation}, in which a single observation is used to produce a list of $k$ candidate estimates and performance is measured by the expected squared distance from the true vector to the closest candidate. We compare this centralized setting with a symmetric decentralized MMSE benchmark in which $k$ agents observe conditionally i.i.d.\ measurements and each agent outputs its own MMSE estimate. On the centralized side, we show that optimal $k$-list estimation is equivalent to fixed-rate $k$-point vector quantization of the posterior distribution and, under standard regularity conditions, admits an exact high-rate asymptotic expansion with explicit constants and decay rate $k^{-2/d}$. On the decentralized side, we derive lower bounds in terms of the small-ball behavior of the single-agent MMSE error; in particular, when the conditional error density is bounded near the origin, the benchmark distortion cannot decay faster than order $k^{-2/d}$. We further show that if the error density vanishes at the origin in a power-law fashion, then the decentralized benchmark is provably unable to match the centralized $k^{-2/d}$ exponent, whereas the centralized estimator retains the $k^{-2/d}$ scaling. Gaussian specializations yield explicit formulas and numerical experiments corroborate the predicted asymptotic behavior. Overall, the results show that, in the scaling with $k$, one observation combined with $k$ carefully chosen candidates can be asymptotically as effective as---and in some regimes strictly better than---this MMSE-based decentralized benchmark with $k$ \rev{conditionally independent} observations.

papers.title: Repair-Based Duality for Distributionally Robust Optimization via Conditional-Moment Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) models often admit dual representations that replace optimization over probability distributions with more tractable formulations, but estab- lishing primal-dual equality can be challenging when ambiguity sets involve conditional moment restrictions, noncompact uncertainty spaces, or unbounded losses. We study these questions through the conditional-moment optimal transport (CM-OT) framework, which encompasses transport-, divergence-, and jointly perturbed DRO models. Our main contribution is a repair- based sufficient condition for primal-dual equality. The approach constructs feasible couplings from nearly feasible ones by mixing with suitable reference couplings, while a local conditional uniform integrability condition on positive-loss tails ensures that the resulting repairs do not incur a nonvanishing loss in objective value. This establishes the closedness of the associated perturbation value function without relying on compactness or conventional interiority condi- tions. We further distinguish primal-dual equality from the additional steps required to obtain pointwise dual representations, providing conditions under which essentially bounded measurable conditional-moment multipliers can be replaced, at the level of optimal values, by bounded continuous multipliers and under which optimization and integration can be interchanged. Finally, we apply the framework to a class of DRO models combining divergence-based ambiguity with distributional calibration, including contextual resource-allocation and reliability applications.

papers.title: Uniform Maximum Projection Designs for Computer Experiments
papers.abstract: Space-filling experimental designs are widely used in engineering computer experiments, where only a limited number of expensive model evaluations can be afforded. Distance-based designs such as Maximin or Minimax ensure global space-filling, while Latin hypercube sampling enforces uniform one-dimensional projections, yet neither guarantees uniformity in lowdimensional subspaces. Maximum Projection (MaxPro) designs were introduced to improve uniformity in low-dimensional subspaces, yet their original formulation relies on the Euclidean distance and may induce systematic density distortions in bounded domains. We demonstrate that the standard MaxPro criterion leads to statistically non-uniform sampling, resulting in undersampling of corner regions and biased Monte Carlo estimates. To remedy this issue, we introduce a periodic variant of the criterion, termed Uniform Maximum Projection (uMaxPro), in which the Euclidean metric is replaced by a periodic distance based on the minimum image convention. The proposed uMaxPro designs preserve the projection-aware structure of MaxPro while achieving statistical uniformity of the design-generation mechanism. Numerical experiments show unbiased Monte Carlo integration with reduced variance, excellent subspace projection performance, and competitive discrepancy properties. The methodology is further validated on benchmark engineering problems, including a meso-scale finite element model of concrete, demonstrating improved accuracy in surrogate modeling and probabilistic estimation. The resulting criterion provides a simple and computationally efficient modification of MaxPro that enhances its robustness for nonadaptive computer experiments. The construction algorithm, open-source implementation, and reproducible optimized designs are provided to facilitate practical adoption of the method.

papers.title: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: Hausdorff dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
papers.abstract: We study the classical limiting laws of $\varphi(n)/n$ and $σ(n)/n$ over integers and shifted primes $p-1$. Let $μ_G$ denote the shifted-prime totient law and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. The law $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero, while every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-measure has packing dimension one. All four ratio laws and their logarithmic images have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions satisfying $0.550<\underline{d}_1\le\overline{d}_1<0.571$. The law $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both $μ_G$ and $μ_f$ have quantitative Fourier decay. For $μ_f$, we obtain sharp concentration asymptotics and localize maximizing intervals. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a random Euler product with an independent uniform phase. For a uniform square matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the probability of a primitive-root determinant tends, as the matrix size grows, to $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Over primes, $c(p)$ has limiting law $μ_G$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ over primes $p\le x$ converge to their common progression law with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. We also obtain transport estimates in growing progressions. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for every $A>0$, disproving the Erdős--Kátai singularity conjecture for $A>2$. Applications include extremal determinant bounds and certified prime selection without complete factorization of $p-1$. These results are unconditional; further quantitative refinements assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions.

papers.title: A Direct Approach to Rough Differential Equations Driven by Controlled Rough Paths
papers.abstract: We study rough differential equations driven by controlled rough paths. Given a rough path $\mathbf X$ and an $\mathbf X$-controlled rough path $\mathbf Z$, we develop a direct controlled rough paths approach to the rough differential equation $dY_t=F(Y_t)\,d\mathbf Z_t$. More specifically, we establish rough integral estimates and the universal limit theorem directly in the space of $\X$-controlled rough paths.

papers.title: Extension of results on generalized Pólya's urns for polynomially self-repelling walks
papers.abstract: This is a technical note which extends the results of Kosygina, Mountford and Peterson (Ann. Probab., 51(5):1684-1728, 2023, Section 4) about generalized Pólya's urns from a specific weight function $w(n) = (n+1)^{-α}$ to a general family of weight functions satisfying $(w(n))^{-1}=n^α\left(1+2Bn^{-1}+O\left(n^{-2}\right)\right)$ as $n \to \infty$. The latter was considered by Tóth (Ann. Probab., 24(3):1324-1367, 1996) as a part of his study of polynomially self-repelling walks. This extension is used in the study of scaling limits of these walks and related processes; see arXiv:2610.28935 and arXiv:2610.38591.

papers.title: Direct Scattering of the Focusing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation with Step-like Oscillatory Initial Data
papers.abstract: In this manuscript we set up the direct and inverse scattering problems for step-like traveling wave solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Specifically, we consider the initial data $u_0(x)=u_e^\ell(x)$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_e^r(x)$ for $x>0$, where $u_e^\ell(x)$ and $u_e^r(x)$ are elliptic traveling wave solutions of NLS. More generally, we consider initial data satisfying $u_0(x)\to u_e^\ell(x)$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u_0(x)\to u_e^r(x)$ as $x\to+\infty$. Under the assumption that $u_0-u_e^\ell \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^-)$ and $u_0-u_e^r \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^+)$, we formulate the direct scattering problem and establish analytic properties of the scattering data. We then formulate the inverse problem as a Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its solvability, thus proving the existence of the nonlinear Schrödinger solution with the above step-like initial data. Finally, we observe that our Riemann--Hilbert formulation is a special case of the one arising for full soliton-gas initial data.

papers.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Shallow Water Moment Equations
papers.abstract: The Shallow Water Moment Equations (SWME) are an extension of the Shallow Water Equations (SWE) for improved modelling of free-surface flows. In contrast to the SWE, the SWME incorporate vertical velocity profile information. The SWME framework approximates vertical velocity profiles using a polynomial expansion with Legendre polynomials and polynomial coefficients, also called moment variables. The SWME have an increased number of variables that must always be incorporated, even when the flow approaches a viscous slip equilibrium state that could be characterised by vanishing moment variables. To reduce the complexity of the SWME in cases proximate to this equilibrium, we conduct an asymptotic analysis of the SWME. This yields the closed form Reduced Shallow Water Moment Equations (RSWME) for deviations from the equilibrium. The RSWME have fewer variables, compared to the SWME. The hyperbolicity of the RSWME is analysed. Numerical tests include a wave with a sharp height gradient, a smoother height gradient and a square root velocity profile. The numerical tests demonstrate that the RSWME reduce computational cost up to 77% compared to the SWME and improves accuracy up to 88% over the SWE.

papers.title: Learned Finite Element-based Regularization of the Inverse Problem in Electrocardiographic Imaging
