The constants are independent of the mesh aspect ratios and of the number of atoms, and inexact flux equilibration and errors in the elementwise residual means are included. We also give a quantile-based budget for the delay residual and a weighted finite-horizon bound beyond the mass-subcritical regime. Under an elliptic equilibration hypothesis, we prove a two-sided estimate for a combined error norm that includes the time derivative. On right-triangular meshes satisfying the maximum-angle condition, however, the lowest-order Raviart--Thomas estimator can exceed the combined graph error by a factor at least proportional to the aspect ratio. Numerical experiments on anisotropic meshes, including a law beyond the mass-subcritical regime, illustrate the behaviour of the residual indicators and the limitations of efficiency.

papers.title: Regular models for F-coherent rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring of characteristic $p>0$ with perfection $R^\infty$. We study whether coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R^\infty\cong S^\infty$ for some regular Noetherian local ring $S$. For a normal Noetherian local domain, coherence of $R^\infty$ forces $R$ to be $p$-almost factorial, equivalently $R^\infty$ is a GCD domain; a finite regular extension $R\subseteq S$ with $S^q\subseteq R$ gives the uniform bound $q Cl(R)=0$. In the non-Noetherian direction, we construct, for every prime $p$ and every $d\geq2$, a perfect coherent local valuation domain of dimension $d$ that is not the perfection of any Noetherian ring. In the positive direction, we characterize coherence for affine semigroup local rings. Finally, we give an F-coherent ring without regular model.

papers.title: Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
papers.abstract: The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
papers.abstract: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincaré inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Operators: Strict Monotonicity and Asymptotic Behavior
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the properties of the generalized principal eigenvalue for a coupled local/nonlocal operator. First, we establish sufficient conditions to guarantee strict monotonicity properties, obtaining weaker hypotheses than those currently available in the literature for nonlocal operators. Next, we establish several results concerning the asymptotic behavior of this generalized eigenvalue, along with the convergence of the corresponding eigenfunctions. These results are very useful for the study of nonlinear problems. Our findings reveal novel phenomena that are not present in purely local or purely nonlocal cases. The main mathematical difficulty lies in the fact that the generalized eigenvalue does not always admit an eigenfunction, in addition to the inherent technicalities of the considered coupling.

papers.title: Statistics of Fundamental Fourier Coefficients of Cusp Forms
papers.abstract: We study sign changes of Fourier coefficients of elliptic and Siegel modular forms in considerable generality. For any $N \geq 1$ and an arbitrary non-zero elliptic cusp form $f\in S_κ(Γ_1(N))$ ($κ\in \frac{1}{2} \mathbb{Z}$) with real Fourier coefficients, we show that a positive proportion of its non-zero Fourier coefficients change sign if $κ\geq 1$ is integral. If $κ\geq 1/2$ is half-integral, we get an almost optimal result. As applications, we establish quantitative sign-change results for `fundamental' Fourier coefficients of Siegel cusp forms of arbitrary degree $n$. These improve the previous best known results on the number of non-zero fundamental Fourier coefficients, even in degree $n=1$.

papers.title: On the Unique Identification of Finitely Many Radial Heat Sources
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate an inverse source problem for the heat equation in $\R^d$ ($d\geq1$), in which the source is a finite positive linear combination of translates of a known real-valued radial Schwartz profile with nonzero total mass. Both the locations and strengths of the sources are to be identified from the observations of time traces at finitely many spatial points over an arbitrary nonempty open positive-time interval. For $d\geq2$, we prove that the sharp universal measurement threshold is $dN+1$: every set of $dN+1$ measurement points in affine general position uniquely identifies every source configuration with at most $N$ locations. For $d=1$, we prove that two distinct measurement points uniquely identify every finite source configuration, independently of the number of sources, and that this count is sharp. The analysis relies on an equivalence between equality of heat traces and equality of weighted distance measures, and then employs perpendicular-bisector hyperplanes to resolve geometric ambiguities. We also establish identification guarantees using $d+1$ measurement points: clustered designs under a reference-distance separation condition, adaptive designs for arbitrary configurations, and any fixed affinely independent design for almost every location configuration, uniformly over all positive strengths.

papers.title: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
papers.abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

papers.title: Equivalence of Cohen generics is hyperfinite
papers.abstract: It is shown that the equivalence relation on Cohen generic reals over a countable model of set theory, where two are equivalent if they produce the same generic extension, is hyperfinite, answering a question of the author. The proof uses asymptotic separation and is a digestion of an argument originally produced by GPT-6.

papers.title: On $k$-very ample line bundles on blowups of surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article we study the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow ups of some smooth surfaces. We begin by investigating the $k$-very ampleness of line bundles on general blow-ups of smooth surfaces with Picard number $1$, extending the previously known cases of uniform line bundles to arbitrary line bundles, under certain restrictions. We then show that for blowups of smooth surfaces with trivial canonical divisor, $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles implies the $k$-very ampleness of arbitrary line bundles. In view of the above, we study $k$-very ampleness of uniform line bundles on blow ups of certain $K3$-surfaces $(K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X)$. Finally, we provide a result concerning the $k$ very ampleness of certain uniform line bundles on the general blow up of product of curves $(K_X \not\cong \mathcal{O}_X)$.

papers.title: Microlocal and global smoothing effect of variable coefficient ZK-type operators
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the smoothing effect of a class of Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equations, which generalize the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to higher dimensions. Specifically, we consider linear evolution equations generated by ZK-type operators with variable coefficients, and we study both their microlocal and global smoothing effects under suitable conditions on the coefficients of the operator. Our analysis requires a detailed study of the geometric properties of the Hamiltonian flow associated with the operator under consideration. These properties allow us to prove a dispersive and a strong smoothing effect associated with the Cauchy problem in question: under suitable moment conditions on the initial datum, the solution becomes smooth in space for positive times in a finite time interval.

papers.title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
papers.abstract: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.

papers.title: Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors
papers.abstract: We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $θ$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(θ/2)\leq p\leq\cos(θ/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion left multiplication through Euclidean projection onto the zero-divisor cone.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity and zero divisors in random graphical groups
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for hyperbolicity of random groups presented by labelled graphs. On $n$ vertices, we prescribe the proportions of the possible sets of outgoing labels. For each generator, we choose a uniform matching between its occurrences and those of its inverse, independently across generators. We condition the graph to have girth at least $\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$ for sufficiently small $c>0$, and take the labels of closed paths as relators. The distribution of outgoing labels determines a matrix of turn weights. Suppose that each letter occurs as often as its inverse and with positive frequency, every vertex has degree at least three, and the entrywise square of the turn matrix has spectral radius less than one. We prove that, with probability tending to one as $n$ grows, the resulting group is torsion-free and non-elementary hyperbolic and admits a finite two-dimensional classifying space. On the same event, every path from a prescribed root to a different vertex has nontrivial label in the group. The proof uses the spectral radius bound to control repeated path labels in diagrams and a local-to-global argument to obtain a linear isoperimetric inequality. Applied to OpenAI's characteristic-two zero-divisor construction, the criterion recovers the hyperbolicity result of Mghirbi and Douglas.

papers.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
papers.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

papers.title: Robust Mixture Regressions and EM Algorithms via the Log-Truncated Likelihood
papers.abstract: Finite mixture regression is sensitive to gross residual outliers when component errors are modeled by Gaussian likelihoods. We propose a log-truncated likelihood for mixture regression. The likelihood is obtained by integrating a logarithmically growing Catoni-type score and exponentiating the negative integrated score, producing a proper location-scale density with a reusable normalizing constant and EM-compatible responsibilities. Although the induced density itself is lighter than exponential and has all moments, its likelihood score grows only logarithmically; this distinction yields a smooth residual-robust estimator that can be stably fitted when the data are generated from Laplace, Pareto, or even infinite-variance heavy-tailed error mechanisms. We derive deterministic tail envelopes, the location-scale decomposition of the normalizing constant, a rejection sampler, a lower-bounded mixing-weight update, a unique componentwise scale update, and a constrained generalized EM algorithm. The theory gives monotonicity of the observed likelihood and a local population-to-sample perturbation guarantee under standard compactness, contraction, and numerical-accuracy conditions. Simulations and applications to insurance claim severity and crypto return innovations show that the method is a competitive smooth likelihood-based alternative to Gaussian and pseudo-robust EM procedures, especially in residual-outlier regimes, while also clarifying its limitations under high leverage and extremely adversarial contamination.

papers.title: Structure Preservation of $2$-Wasserstein Barycenters on the Real Line with Applications to Log-Concave Distributions
papers.abstract: We study to what extent the $p$-Wasserstein barycenter ($p$-WB) of arbitrary, not only finite, collections of distributions preserves their structure, focusing on shape constraints on the densities, such as monotonicity, unimodality, or log-concavity. This preservation is a generalized convexity property in Wasserstein space, which we call $p$-WB convexity. We investigate $p$-WB convexity of the families of $φ$-unimodal distributions: an absolutely continuous distribution $μ$ is $φ$-unimodal if composition with $φ$ turns a density into a concave function on the interior of the convex support of $μ$. This notion generalizes log-concavity and $s$-concave densities. We find a quantile representation of $φ$-unimodality and then use a novel closed-form expression of the quantile density function of the $2$-WB to decide on $2$-WB convexity. In higher dimensions or for $p\neq2$, we give counterexamples ruling out the $p$-WB convexity of $φ$-unimodal distributions. On $\mathbb{R}$ and for $p=2$, we characterize which $φ$ generate $2$-WB convex families. The family of log-concave distributions is $2$-WB convex, as is the family of distributions with $s$-concave densities if and only if $s\geq-2$. General unimodality, corresponding to $s=-\infty$, is not preserved.

papers.title: Logarithmic stability from finite-time boundary measurements in an infinite slab
papers.abstract: We prove logarithmic stability for an inverse convection--diffusion problem in an infinite slab from finite-time partial boundary measurements. The data consist of boundary fluxes generated by a fixed temporal profile and varying spatial Dirichlet inputs. For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfers the partial data to a full boundary map on an interior domain, where magnetic stability estimates apply. We also prove conditional stability for boundary-touching supports and uniqueness from one encoded input with unknown initial state. A tracer-transport application identifies an incompressible velocity and a reaction-loss coefficient.

papers.title: Quantum Variance of Holomorphic Modular Forms and Benjamini-Schramm Convergence
papers.abstract: We study quantum variance for holomorphic modular forms of fixed weight on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the sense of Benjamini-Schramm. We first show that quantum ergodicity need not hold for an arbitrary choice of orthonormal basis, even for sequences with a uniform lower bound on the injectivity radius and a uniform spectral gap. The counterexample is constructed using a tower of coverings and arises from the identity contribution in the automorphic kernel. We then show that this obstruction is exceptional from the point of view of the choice of basis. For a Haar random orthonormal basis of holomorphic modular forms, the quantum variance converges to zero with probability tending to one uniformly over all observables with bounded supremum norm. The proof combines estimates for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a projected multiplication operator with the Haar expectation of the quantum variance, concentration of measure on the special unitary group and a finite-dimensional approximation of the space of observables.

papers.title: Revisiting the role of reorthogonalisation in LSQR
papers.abstract: In this paper, we revisit the role of reorthogonalisation in the LSQR method for large-scale overdetermined linear least-squares problems. Motivated primarily by practical applications where matrix--vector products dominate the computational cost and only a limited number of iterations can be afforded because of time and/or memory restrictions, we investigate when reorthogonalisation can significantly accelerate convergence. Through synthetic test problems with controlled singular value distributions and experiments on practical sparse problems, we demonstrate that reorthogonalisation is particularly beneficial when the least-squares matrix has large outlying singular values. In such cases, loss of orthogonality can severely delay convergence. We explore the effectiveness of full (one-sided) reorthogonalisation when using LSQR, and present alternative reorthogonalisation strategies that can provide substantial acceleration compared to no reorthogonalisation and significant storage savings compared to full reorthogonalisation. The possibility of using low precision arithmetic for the reorthogonalisation is also investigated. We present bounds that demonstrate the quality of the solution depends on the level of orthogonality maintained by the selected reorthogonalisation strategy. Our results suggest that reorthogonalisation should be regarded as a practical tool for modern least-squares applications that can be employed instead of, or in addition to, preconditioning.

papers.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
papers.abstract: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $δ$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\logδ|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $δ$-neighborhood of an $ε$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim ε^{-1}|\logδ|^{-1}$, for $δ$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $ε$.

papers.title: The Hamilton cycle space in the Erdős--Rényi random graph process
papers.abstract: Let $G(n,m)$ denote the graph at step $m$ of the Erdős--Rényi random graph process on $n$ vertices. The process starts with the edgeless graph and adds one edge at each step, chosen uniformly at random from the missing edges. Let $τ_3$ be the first step at which the minimum degree of $G(n,m)$ reaches three. We answer a question of Christoph, Nenadov and Petrova [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 176 (2026) 254--267] by proving that, as $n$ tends to infinity through odd integers, with high probability the Hamilton cycles of $G(n,m)$ span its cycle space over $\Ftwo$ simultaneously for all $m\geτ_3$. On the same event, $G(n,m)$ is Hamilton-connected for every $m\geτ_3$.

papers.title: A uniform Picard-rank bound for Calabi Yau threefolds with finitely many flop chambers
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective strict Calabi Yau threefold of sufficiently large Picard number either has infinitely many marked flop chambers or admits a fibration on a smooth flop model.

papers.title: Global Stability Analysis of an Excitable Infinite-Dimensional System
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of excitable control of infinite-dimensional linear systems, we investigate the global stability properties of a closed-loop system consisting of a stable linear infinite-dimensional plant and a non-monotone controller. The controller has piecewise-linear dynamics that resemble the FitzHugh-Nagumo model of neural behaviour. As our main result, we derive a checkable condition for the global exponential stability of the closed-loop system using the circle criterion. Finally we illustrate the stability result for a one-dimensional heat equation.

papers.title: Fundamental gaps of the restricted fractional Laplacian on thin planar convex domains
papers.abstract: We study the fundamental gap $Γ_s(Ω)=λ_{2,s}(Ω)-λ_{1,s}(Ω)$ of the restricted Dirichlet fractional Laplacian for $0 < s < 1$. Building on the thin-rectangle estimates of Dyda and Kulczycki, we establish compact Mosco convergence of shifted quadratic forms and convergence of their eigenvalues on collapsing convex strips. This yields the next-order expansion, with exact coefficients, of each fixed eigenvalue of a thin rectangle. Let $G_s(θ)$ be the infimum of $D^{2s}Γ_s(Ω)$ over bounded open convex planar domains with $|Ω|/D^2=θ$, where $D$ denotes the diameter of $Ω$. As $θ\downarrow0$, we obtain $G_s(θ)\simκ_s\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}θ$ for $0 < s < 1/2$, $G_{1/2}(θ)\sim3π^2γθ\log(1/θ)$, and $G_s(θ)\sim3π^2β_sθ^{2-2s}$ for $1/2 < s < 1$. The constants $κ_s$, $γ$, and $β_s$ are determined by the transverse interval ground state. On $I=(-1/2,1/2)$, let $\mathfrak{g}_t$ be the infimum of the fundamental gap of the restricted Dirichlet operator $(-Δ)^t+V$ over convex $V\in C(\overline{I})$. For every $0 < t < 1$, this infimum is positive and is attained by a finite convex potential on $I$. Thin rectangles attain the optimal leading coefficient for $1/2\le s < 1$. For $0 < s < 1/2$, they do so exactly when the zero potential attains $\mathfrak{g}_{s+1/2}$. Finally, after diameter normalization, rescaling by $θ^{-1}$ in a minimum-width direction, and suitable rotations and translations, the closures of asymptotically minimizing domains converge to $[-1/2,1/2]\times[0,1]$ in Hausdorff distance.

papers.title: What Environment Invariance Identifies: Minimal Invariant Sets in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.abstract: Invariant causal prediction identifies the direct causes of a target $Y$ by searching for covariate sets whose conditional law of $Y$ is stable across environments. We state that criterion at the level of operators, calling a set $S$ invariant when the conditional mean embeddings of $Y$ given $X_S$ agree across environments, and characterise the resulting family exactly: under two conditions on the environments, which we state separately because they fail independently, the invariant sets are precisely those containing $PA(Y)$ and no descendant of $Y$. Two consequences follow. Invariance does not identify $PA(Y)$ uniquely, since every descendant-free superset is invariant as well; and $PA(Y)$ is the unique minimal invariant set. In finite samples, recovery requires the non-invariant sets to be separated from invariance by a margin, and the sample size splits into a screening term logarithmic in the ambient dimension and a term inherited from conditional mean embedding estimation, which is the binding one. The characterisation yields two selection rules with different failure modes, of which the conservative one controls false positives. Controlled experiments verify each population prediction directly, including the failure of uniqueness. They also show that invariance testing is a practical bottleneck: two natural designs are severely miscalibrated, while the selected test reduces but does not eliminate Type I error inflation.

papers.title: On the quaternionic Goldberg conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove a quaternionic Kähler analogue of the Goldberg conjecture, namely: Let $(M^8,g,Ω)$ denote a compact $8$-manifold endowed with an $\mathrm{Sp}(2)\mathrm{Sp}(1)$-structure defined by a closed $4$-form $Ω$. If the metric $g$ is Einstein with non-negative scalar curvature then it is quaternionic Kähler i.e. $Ω$ is parallel. In fact we prove a slightly stronger result allowing for the scalar curvature to be negative under a suitable pinching condition by the square norm of the intrinsic torsion.

papers.title: Scaling-invariant conditions for two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with either far-field vacuum or non-vacuum. Under suitable smallness conditions on explicitly constructed scaling-invariant initial quantities, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions involving initial vacuum states and large oscillations. The two far-field regimes present distinct analytical difficulties and require different approaches to the {\it a priori} estimates. Although the two smallness criteria have different forms, they arise from the same intrinsic scaling of the equations. Our results provide a unified scaling-invariant framework for the global well-posedness of strong solutions in both far-field regimes.

papers.title: Geometry of ground states in the long-range Ising model
papers.abstract: We study the ground states of the ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with long-range interactions and prescribed exterior data. We first show that the half-space configuration is a ground state, by means of a discrete calibration (which is the lattice counterpart of the calibrations of Cabré and Pagliari for nonlocal minimal surfaces). In dimension $d\ge2$ and for positive kernels, the half-space configuration is the unique minimizer in every finite domain, and it is "stable" with respect to perturbations of the exterior datum whose energy is below half of a positive excitation gap. This rigidity has no counterpart in the continuum. For general exterior data and positive kernels, we show that along a monotone family the minimizer is unique except for finitely many data. This can be considered a "generic uniqueness result" that provides the discrete counterpart of a recent work of Dipierro, Fernández-Real and Valdinoci in the continuum. We then introduce a pointwise notion, called perception, which is the lattice counterpart of the instability and stickiness phenomena for nonlocal minimal surfaces discovered by Dipierro, Savin and Valdinoci. We give a local criterion for the half-space configuration to be perceptive at a given site. Finally, we consider a box with exterior datum $+1$ above and below a slab and $-1$ on its sides. For fractional kernels with small exponent, the minimizer is $+1$ in the whole box, and its positive phase is connected. For short-range kernels, instead, the negative phase may enter the box, and the positive phase may be disconnected. Moreover, if the datum is $-1$ around the box and $+1$ only at distance two from it, the configuration identically $-1$ is perceptive at every boundary site of the box for fractional kernels with small exponent.

papers.title: Wirsing type approximation over totally real and totally $p$-adic extensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Wirsing-type bounds for approximation of real and $p$-adic transcendental numbers by totally real and totally $p$-adic algebraic numbers, respectively. More precisely, for every $n\ge 1$, we show that every transcendental $ξ\in\mathbb{Q}_p$ admits infinitely many totally $p$-adic algebraic approximants $α$ of degree at most $n$ satisfying $0<|ξ-α|_p\ll H(α)^{-1-\lceil n/2\rceil}$. We improve this bound for even $n\ge 4$. For each $n\geq 2$, we also show that every real number $ξ$ that is not algebraic of degree at most $n$ admits totally real approximants of degree at most $n$ with a bound stronger than Wirsing's. In both cases, we can also restrict the approximants to be totally $\ell$-adic for every prime $\ell$ in a fixed finite set.

papers.title: A new frequency-time hybrid RPML-BIE solver with few-mode corrections for the wave-equation problems in nonuniform closed waveguides
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to proposing a novel FTH integral equation solver for wave-equation problems in two-dimensional nonuniform closed waveguides with multiple channels. The FTH methodology, which combines the Fourier transform with frequency-domain BIE formulations, has demonstrated its effectiveness in solving time-dependent wave scattering problems. However, when applied to waveguide problems, the modal expansions arising from multiple scattering introduce cut-off frequencies. Such frequencies pose significant challenges, requiring both a frequency-robust solver for frequency-domain waveguide problems and an efficient treatment of the solution's non-smooth behavior near the cut-off frequencies for the evaluation of the inverse Fourier transform. The first issue is addressed by developing a new frequency-domain BIE method based on the free-space fundamental solution and regionalized perfectly matched layer truncation, together with a few-mode Dirichlet-to-Robin modification. The method is rigorously proved to achieve uniform exponential convergence, even at frequencies arbitrarily close to the cut-off frequencies. To address the second issue---the recovery of the time-domain solution via the inverse Fourier transform---a sine-transform based stationary-point Filon--Clenshaw--Curtis quadrature is introduced to accurately handle the non-smoothness and square-root singularities of frequency-domain solutions. Additionally, theoretical result shows that the complex resonances closing to the real axis may significantly effect the convergence of the Fourier transform algorithm and then a novel strategy of complex resonance extraction based on AAA rational approximation and singularity subtraction is utilized to avoid this influence. Numerical experiments for both frequency-domain and time-domain problems illustrate the efficiency and high accuracy of the proposed method.

papers.title: Restrictions of planar doubling measures to piecewise C1 Jordan domains
papers.abstract: We compare the class $\mathscr R(Ω)$ of restrictions of full-support planar doubling measures with the class $\mathcal D(Ω)$ of internal doubling measures on a piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domain. These classes coincide in the absence of zero-interior-angle cusps. At any such cusp, $\mathscr R(Ω)\setminus\mathcal D(Ω)$ is nonempty. For power-comparable widths, $\mathcal D(Ω)\subsetneq\mathscr R(Ω)$; for infinitely flat widths the two classes are disjoint. Under smooth endpoint regularity, finite versus infinite contact order gives these two alternatives. Under only $C^1$ regularity, finite logarithmic order does not determine whether the classes intersect, and examples with nonempty intersection and neither class containing the other also occur. For an individual internal measure, membership in $\mathscr R(Ω)$ is characterized by a potential inequality for its axial projection. We prove this criterion by a positive-kernel construction and Whitney mass replacement, and also obtain sufficient conditions for variable-power widths and an independent finite-system criterion.

papers.title: Finite simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes
papers.abstract: A theorem by Guralnick classifying finite simple groups with subgroups of prime power index implies that $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ is the unique finite non-abelian simple group whose maximal subgroups all have prime power index. Motivated by this result and appealing to Li and Li's classification of primitive permutation groups of degree $p^a q^b$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, we classify all finite non-abelian simple groups whose maximal subgroups have indices divisible by at most two distinct primes, proving that they are precisely $A_5$, $A_6$, $A_7$, $A_8$, ${\rm PSL}(2,7)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,8)$, ${\rm PSL}(2,11)$, ${\rm PSp}(4,3)$, ${\rm PSU}(3,3)$, and ${\rm PSU}(3,4)$.

papers.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.

papers.title: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents
papers.abstract: Scoring rules are used to elicit probabilistic beliefs through payments that depend on reports and realised outcomes. We ask how these rules should be designed to induce truthful reporting and incentivise costly information acquisition when the agent is risk averse. For agents with entropic risk preferences in finite state spaces, we characterise proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation, derive optimal structures for information acquisition under bounded payments, and obtain explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. The risk-neutral limit preserves properness and, in the binary case, optimality, while recovering the optimal betting structure for nonbinary states. For optimal design in the binary model, it suffices to focus on rules whose associated concave function is affine on each side of the prior. The optimal coefficients depend only on the prior and the risk-aversion parameter. The binary optimal rules we construct also admit an exact transformation from a particular risk-neutral optimal rule. In the nonbinary model, optimal design reduces to choosing the best prior bound in a transformed betting mechanism.

papers.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
papers.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

papers.title: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restriction to almost every $\la$ in \cite[Theorem 1.6]{CZZ}, answers a question of Zou \cite{Z}, and disproves the conjecture in \cite[Remark 1.7]{TT1}. The proofs rely on a scale-invariant estimate uniform in $\la$, a Hadamard-type identity for the half-space extremal and a localized Pohozaev identity combined with sharp decay estimates. Notably, no regularity of $\partial\Om$ is required away from $0$.

papers.title: Irreducible shallow tanh neural networks are a manifold
papers.abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been increasingly used as function approximators, motivating the study of the geometry of their function spaces. We study the set of functions represented by shallow neural networks with hyperbolic tangent activation, fixed input and output dimensions, and $n$ hidden neurons. In particular, we prove that the subset represented by irreducible networks in the sense of Sussmann (Neural Networks, 1992), i.e., networks with no redundant neurons, is a smooth embedded submanifold of the Sobolev spaces $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ on bounded sets for any $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\in[1,+\infty]$. The key step is to show that if a sequence of networks converges in $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ to an irreducible network with the same number of hidden neurons, then the parameters of the approximating networks remain bounded. Finally, we show that this manifold has exactly $n+1$ connected components when both the input and output are scalar, and is connected otherwise.

papers.title: On \(q\)-ary Minimal Linear Codes from Hierarchical Posets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study several families of \(q\)-ary linear codes constructed from two-level hierarchical posets over finite fields \(\mathbb{F}_q\), where \(q>2\). By using generating functions and additive characters, we determine their complete weight distributions, dimensions, and minimum distances. This paper focuses on constructing minimal codes that violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition. By analyzing the weight distributions and support sets of the codewords, we show that a large class of the constructed codes are minimal and strictly violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

papers.title: Bilinear sum involving $GL(3)$ Fourier coefficients
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the circle method to establish non-trivial bounds for certain summatory functions and a bilinear sum involving the Fourier coefficients of a general Hecke-Maass cusp form on $SL(3,\mathbb{Z})$.

papers.title: A corank one Lipschitz normally embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with non-trivial link
papers.abstract: We show that the knot-triviality theorem for Lipschitz normally embedded (LNE) corank one surface singularities in $\mathbb{R}^4$ proved by Birbrair, Mendes and Nuño-Ballesteros (2018) does not generalize unrestrictedly. More precisely, we exhibit a polynomial map germ $F:(\mathbb{R}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{R}^4,0)$ of corank one at the origin, with isolated singularity and $2$-jet $(x,0,0,0)$, whose image $X=F(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is LNE at the origin, yet its link is the granny knot $T\#T$, and hence non-trivial. The example is obtained via a general uniform-degree homogenization procedure applied to a known polynomial parametrization of the trefoil knot. We also give a finitely $\mathcal A$-determined polynomial realization with the same LNE and knot properties.

papers.title: Dirichlet does not imply Regularity for general elliptic operators in smooth domains
papers.abstract:
In the upper half-space $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$, $n\geq2$, we show that there exists a real, diagonal, strongly elliptic matrix $A$ of bounded measurable coefficients, smooth in the interior of $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ and continuous on its closure, such that for the elliptic operator $L=-\operatorname{div}A
abla$, the Dirichlet problem with data in $L^p$ is solvable, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, but the Dirichlet-Regularity problem is not solvable for any $p\in(1,\infty)$. The counterexample has the following properties, in particular: 1. $A$ equals the identity matrix at the boundary and their $L^\infty$ distance in $\mathbb R^{n+1}_+$ can be made arbitrarily small. 2. $A$ satisfies that $t|\partial_t A|^2$ is a Carleson measure. 3. $A$ fails to satisfy the Dahlberg-Kenig-Pipher condition only slightly, in the sense that for every $q>2$, $t^q|
abla A|^q rac{dxdt}{t}$ is a vanishing Carleson measure, but $t|
abla A|^2$ is not a Carleson measure. The counterexample resolves a long-standing question of C. Kenig.

papers.title: Towards a unified treatment of structured deformations theories
papers.abstract: Relying on the theory of $\mathcal B$ gradients, with $\mathcal B$ a $\mathbb C$-elliptic homogeneous linear partial differential operator of order $k$, with constant coefficients, we propose a method which allows to treat in a unified way the theories of structured deformations. Introducing the space of structured $\mathcal B$-deformations, $SD_{\mathcal B}$, we establish an integral-representation result for the associated energies, involving both bulk and surface contributions. Our approach relies on a direct application of the global method for relaxation, suitably adapted to the space of functions of $\mathcal B$-bounded variation.

papers.title: Density of states for random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder
papers.abstract: We study the density of states of random Schrödinger operators with linearly correlated heavy-tailed disorder. Using an integration-by-parts supersymmetric representation, we prove smoothness of the density of states and Wegner estimates in the strong-disorder regime. We are particularly interested in mixed-sign correlation kernels, which serve as a toy model for the hyperbolic structures arising in the analysis of averaged squared Green's functions. Our approach applies to a broad class of correlation kernels and disorder distributions, including $α$-stable laws.

Among others, most of the far-famed operators derived from functionals with linear growth, as for instance the $1$-Laplacian and the minimal surface operator are included in our model. Under suitable assumptions on the data we prove existence and regularity results for problem \eqref{P1abs} which recover the sharp thresholds known in the model cases.

papers.title: Solvability of one-dimensional sub-quadratic BSDEs with unbounded stochastic coefficients
papers.abstract: This study is devoted to solvability of the unbounded solutions of a class of one-dimensional sub-quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) with unbounded stochastic coefficients and general time horizons. In a general sub-exponential moment integrability space linked with the stochastic coefficients, we first establish existence of an unbounded solution of the preceding BSDE when the generator $g$ has a one-sided linear growth in the state variable $y$ and a sub-quadratic growth in the state variable $z$, and then prove a comparison theorem of the unbounded solutions of such two BSDEs when either of generators satisfies an extended convexity/concavity condition in $(y,z)$ with unbounded stochastic coefficients, yielding naturally the uniqueness of the solution. Particularly, the unbounded stochastic coefficient before the state variable $y$ is supposed to take values in $\R$ such that the required integrability condition of the terminal value may be weaker than that under the usual situations. These findings incorporate and generalize some corresponding known results.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=ψ(|D|/N)$ with $ψ\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_ψ\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $α$ with $\operatorname{Re}α>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $β$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,β}^αx$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $πx/Γ(1+α)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

papers.title: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
papers.abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.

papers.title: Algorithms and topological invariants for dynamic systems. IV. Topological Equivalence of Functions and Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: This is the fourth part of a series on algorithms and topological invariants for dynamical systems. We study the topological equivalence of smooth functions and of Hamiltonian flows on surfaces, and the discrete invariants, Reeb graphs and cell decompositions, that classify them. We recall the notions of topological equivalence and structural stability, introduce two equivalences of functions (with and without the order of the critical values) and show that simple Morse functions on closed orientable surfaces are classified by their Reeb graphs with vertex odering, while simple Hamiltonian flows are classified by Reeb graphs with marked edges. For the disc and for the sphere we obtain a recursive description and a generating function for the numbers of such trees, and compute the numbers of topologically non-equivalent simple Morse functions and Hamiltonian flows with a given number of saddles. We also describe functions with isolated, possibly degenerate, critical points by cell decompositions, and give an algorithm and computational results for functions with three critical points. In the first part (arXiv:2501.15657) we discussed the basic concepts of differential topology. In the second part (arXiv:2502.00506) we discussed the discrete topological structures used in the topological theory of dynamical systems. In the third part (arXiv:2502.09958) we constructed algorithms that recognize $2$- and $3$-manifolds in simplicial complexes and regular CW-complexes and determine the topological type of a $2$-manifold (connectivity, orientability, genus, number of boundary components).

papers.title: Functionals commuting with reparametrizations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties. The proof involves the study of polyharmonic functions on the positive discrete orthant $\mathbb Z^n_{>0}$, and a relation with the co-invariant algebra of type $A$. We also provide a generalization connected to colored permutations, and discuss the analogue problems where $E=\mathbb C[T]_0/(T^\ell)$ for some $\ell >0$, and where $E$ consists of infinitely differentiable functions. Finding a complete description of algebraic solutions in these settings is still open.

papers.title: Generic Strong Regularity and the Branson--Gover Conjecture
papers.abstract: On each closed smooth manifold of even dimension $2N\ge 4$, we prove that the Branson--Gover detour operators are strongly regular in every degree $k-1$, $1\le k<N$, on a $C^\infty$-open dense set of Riemannian metrics. Consequently, every de Rham cohomology class of positive degree below the middle dimension has a unique conformal harmonic representative for these metrics. On a connected manifold, the critical scalar GJMS operator has only constants in its kernel on an open dense set of conformal structures modulo diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, as conjectured by Canzani, Gover, Jakobson, and Ponge. The proof computes the principal symbol of a reduced metric Hessian that accounts for the motion of the kernel through a Green operator.

papers.title: Fast Gradient-Based Framework for Spatial and Length Optimization of Geothermal Borehole Fields
papers.abstract: Common analytical design tools for Borehole Heat Exchanger (BHE) fields size the total drilling length for a given layout but do not optimize the positions of the boreholes. We introduce a framework (OptiGeoS) for the simultaneous, gradient-based optimization of the borehole length and the continuous borehole positions under groundwater advection. It couples the Moving Finite Line Source model with local BHE equations and evaluates the temporal convolutions by Fast Fourier Transforms. The gradients with respect to the length and the positions are computed analytically. A flow-dependent Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation confines each borehole to its own cell, which enforces the spatial separation and provides advection-informed layouts. Under purely conductive conditions, the fluid temperature extremes of the forward model for a single borehole lie between those of EED and GHEtool, which differ by $0.32\,\mathrm{K}$. For a field of 120 boreholes, the hourly outlet temperature agrees with that of EED with an RMSE of $0.28\,\mathrm{K}$, while the peak temperatures deviate by up to $2\,\mathrm{K}$. For 25 boreholes simulated hourly over 20 years, one forward simulation takes less than $0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ and a full optimization about $8\,\mathrm{min}$ on a laptop CPU. In a case study with groundwater advection, the optimized layout requires $16.2\,\%$ less borehole length than a fixed grid. It reduces the length increase caused by the advected thermal plume from $20.9\,\%$ to $1.4\,\%$.

papers.title: Optimal first eigenvalue estimates for positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Let $(M,ω_g)$ be a compact Kähler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature $\geq 2$. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplacian $Δ_d$ satisfies $$λ_1\geq 4, $$ and $λ_1=4$ if and only if $(M,ω_g)$ is holomorphically isometric to $(\mathbb{P}^1,ω_{\mathrm{FS}})$.

papers.title: Weitzenböck curvature estimates in arbitrary degree and sectional-scalar curvature pinching
papers.abstract: For each odd dimension $n\ge7$ we give an explicit constant $B_n<(n-1)/(n+2)$ such that a closed, connected, nonflat Riemannian $n$-manifold with $K_{\min}\ge B_n S_0$ is a rational homology sphere, where $S_0=\operatorname{Scal}/[n(n-1)]$. For example, $B_7=28/43<2/3$. This answers the question of Li, Matinpour, and Petersen about lowering the sectional curvature coefficient in the remaining odd dimensions. The same argument recovers their five-dimensional endpoint $B_5=10/19$. The proof starts with a four-frame inequality for two-forms. Contracting forms and averaging over hyperplanes propagates a Ricci-weighted estimate whose coefficient depends on the parity of the codimension. For an algebraic curvature tensor with nonnegative sectional curvature, we obtain lower bounds for the Weitzenböck curvature endomorphism in every degree. When the dimension and degree are both even, we classify all nonzero equality pairs for the sharp bound by powers of Kähler forms. For three-forms the optimal coefficient in the scalar curvature bound is $1/3$ in dimensions five and six and lies between $4/9$ and $5168/11253$ in dimension seven. On the cone of strongly nonnegative curvature tensors we determine the optimal coefficient in every degree.

papers.title: Asymptotic approximation for a certain class of statistics associated with generalized urn models
papers.abstract: The generalized urn model is defined in terms of a collection of random frequencies, which is treated as a collection of conditionally independent random variables given their sum. We consider a class of random variables that can be represented as series of functions of these frequencies. The general results concern asymptotic normality, estimates of remainder terms, and Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansions for such random variables. We then consider random variables defined in various versions of the generalized urn model. These models include the random allocation of particles of several types into finite or infinite numbers of cells, random sampling without replacement from a finite population, random coverage of a circle, random forests, and random permutations.

papers.title: Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras
papers.abstract: Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant. We establish several inequalities and equalities relating these weighted regularities to the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of derived Hom and derived tensor complexes. These results recover their unweighted counterparts and yield new relations involving the a-invariant for a fixed weight. Some of these results generalize the inequalities of Kirkman-Won-Zhang between weighted CM-regularity and Tor-regularity by allowing the weight to range over the entire plane R^2. We also give conditions under which these inequalities become equalities, thereby answering a question posed by Kirkman-Won-Zhang. We use weighted AS-regularity to study the Artin-Schelter regularity of A. Under mild conditions, we prove that the weighted AS-regularity of A vanishes if and only if A is an N-graded AS-regular algebra. This generalizes an unweighted result of the present authors and a weighted result of Kirkman, Won, and Zhang.

papers.title: One-shot identification of analytic systems
papers.abstract: We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.

papers.title: Cyclic changes of frame for designing non-retracing verification cases for numerical interface tracking
papers.abstract: A forward-backward deformation test supplies an exact final interface, but retracing can allow errors from the two halves to cancel. We construct alternative tests by superposing a cyclic change of frame on the same base deformation. The frame returns to its starting pose, preserving the exact final phase and the deformation history up to rigid placement. A small returning translation can keep trajectories close to the retraced ones. A full rotation about a fixed centre or axis gives closed paths with nonzero winding for material labels that stay off that centre or axis. For incompressible base fields the transformed velocity is divergence-free. We construct discretely solenoidal face fluxes for geometric volume-of-fluid advection by circulating the transformed potential. In three TwoPhaseFlow benchmarks, with a shared time grid for each pair, a full-turn frame increased the final cell-average shape discrepancy in all 30 comparisons, with a median factor of 1.50. The fitted convergence exponent decreased in each of the six benchmark-reconstruction comparisons over the tested grids.

papers.title: Consecutive sums and Reconstructing Problems
papers.abstract: We study several problems concerning consecutive sums of integer sequences and their relationship with Sidon sets. We also provide new lower bounds for an extremal function related to sequences with distinct consecutive sums, and consider reconstruction problems from multisets of consecutive sums.

papers.title: Approximate L_r-factorization of \ell_p-strictly singular operators on L_p
papers.abstract: For \(1<p<2\), we study norm approximation of operators on \(L_p(0,1)\) by operators that factor through \(L_r(0,1)\), where \(p<r<2\). Using a sharp factorization estimate for finite diagonal blocks, we show that the corresponding norm-closed factorization ideals form a strictly decreasing chain as \(r\) increases. We also construct a strictly singular operator \(T_p\) at positive distance from the closed linear span generated by these ideals and all finitely strictly singular operators on \(L_p(0,1)\). In particular, \(T_p\) is \(\ell_p\)-strictly singular, yet its distance from the \(L_r\)-factorization ideals has a positive lower bound independent of \(r\). This answers a question due to Johnson and Schechtman in the negative.

papers.title: Signed Admissible Regions and 2-adic Area Obstructions for Perfect Triangles
papers.abstract: A perfect triangle is a triangle whose sides, medians and area are all integers; whether one exists is an open problem. We study Buchholz's rational parametrization of triangles with two rational medians on the whole $(θ,φ)$-plane, allowing the generated side lengths to be negative. We factor its Heron polynomial $H(θ,φ)$ into ten explicit factors and show that the points whose componentwise absolute values form a triangle are exactly those with $H>0$; the points giving positive side lengths directly form three open quadrilaterals, one of which is the region used by Buchholz and Rathbun. Every triangle with two rational medians arises from sixteen signed parameter points, given by explicit rational functions. Rational area forces $H$ to be a square in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and the valuation and the unit part of $H$ yield parity and modulo-8 conditions in three valuation ranges. Since a triangle is excluded as soon as one of its sixteen parameter points fails a test, these conditions exclude infinite families of signed admissible parameters, including non-integral ones. The conditions are necessary only and do not settle the existence of perfect triangles.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Analysis of Resonances by a Contraction Mapping on Complex Domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a perturbation problem of embedded eigenvalues for an abstract Friedrichs--Lee Hamiltonian and analyze its spectral properties. By deforming the contour and constructing a contraction mapping on complex domains, we prove the existence of resonance poles.

papers.title: Complex Oscillation and Non-Oscillation Results of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate oscillation and non-oscillation results of second order differential equations \begin{equation} f''+(H_1e^z+H_2e^{αz}+q)f=0,\tag{+} \end{equation} where $H_1,H_2\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, $0<α<1$, and $q$ is an entire function of order less than $1$. First, we show that if equation (+) has a zero-free non-trivial entire solution, then either $α=1/2$ or $α=3/4$, which settles the Problem 9 posed in \cite{HITW}. Second, we prove that if either $q$ is transcendental, or $α=(2m-1)/(2m)$ for some integer $m\geq 2$ and $q\equiv 0$, then every non-trivial entire solution $f$ of $(+)$ satisfies $λ(f)=\infty$.

papers.title: Newton iterations and semi-Lagrangian schemes for mean field games of controls
papers.abstract: We study Newton methods for second-order mean field games of controls (MFGC), in which agents interact through local averages of their controls. We prove local quadratic convergence of full Newton iterations, and of Newton iterations on reduced unknowns, near stable classical solutions. Stability holds under weak control interaction and under an infinitesimal monotonicity condition of Lasry--Lions type. We propose a semi-Lagrangian (SL) scheme for second-order MFGC, in which the average-control relation is solved by a convergent Chebyshev iteration, and two matrix-free solvers: a full Newton--SL method with block Gauss--Seidel preconditioning, whose spectrum we characterize in the absence of control coupling, and a reduced Jacobian-free Newton--GMRES method whose density iterates are nonnegative and mass-preserving by construction. We also construct an exact, time-dependent, coupled MFGC solution for use as a benchmark. In the experiments, the reduced solver converges quadratically in its final iterations, also in a strong-alignment test in which full Newton updates lose positivity. On the benchmark, the SL scheme and a finite-difference scheme both converge at first order with errors of comparable size, and our SL implementation is faster.

papers.title: Quantum walks and conformal mappings
papers.abstract: We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying integral representations. They are applicable in several other situations as well.

papers.title: Morita equivalence classification for irrational noncommutative solenoids
papers.abstract: Given a prime integer $p$, we define a $p$-angle to be an element of the $p$-solenoid ${\mathcal S}_p$ or equivalently an element of $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{Q}_p$ modulo $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$. Noncommutative $p$-solenoids, or equivalently $p$-rotation algebras, are $C^*$-algebras defined by a $p$-angle in the same way as non-commutative tori or usual rotation algebras are defined by an angle. We give a complete classification, in terms of their $p$-angles and in the irrational case, of these $C^*$-algebras up to strong Morita equivalence, but also the associated groupoids up to Morita equivalence; more precisely, we obtain the following classification result: two irrational $p$-angles define strong Morita equivalent noncommutative solenoids if and only if they define isomorphic dimension groups if and only if they are congruent modulo $GL_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/p])$ if and only if they define Morita equivalent groupoids. This generalises, with a different proof, the classification up to isomorphism, previously obtained by Latrémolière and Packer. We also give a geometrical construction of projective $C^*$-modules in terms of proper $G$-spaces which exhaust the dimension group up to a shift and implement all relevant Morita equivalences by groupoid equivalences.

papers.title: New applications for optimal adaptivity
papers.abstract: We introduce an explicit time-stepping scheme for ODEs, together with a residual-based a posteriori error estimator. Using this estimator, we show a new approach to proving optimality and linear reduction of adaptive algorithms for time-dependent problems that works in $H^1(0, t_{\rm end})$ and $W^{1,\infty}(0,t_{\rm end})$ norms, does not require quasi-orthogonality, and poses no restrictions on the marking parameter $θ$. The key idea is to use the Lipschitz continuity of the semi-discretized operator to obtain a stronger form of estimator reduction. Numerical experiments illustrate the benefits of this explicit scheme coupled with adaptive refinement over uniform time stepping for classical evolution problems, regularized dynamical approximation, and neural ODEs.

papers.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
papers.abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{é}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.

papers.title: No coexistence in the two-type Richardson model when one side is stronger than the other
papers.abstract: We study the two-type Richardson model in two dimensions. We prove that there is no coexistence of the two species when their infection rates are different, establishing a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m and Pemantle from 1997. In our proof we analyze a second order approximation of the infected region and use a Mermin--Wagner style argument to push the strong type out of the weak one.

papers.title: Strongly meet continuous posets
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to introduce and investigate strongly meet continuous posets. It is shown that a poset is strongly meet continuous if and only if the Scott closure of the set of elements way below each element coincides with its principal ideal. Moreover, the Scott topology of every strongly meet continuous poset is shown to have a basis consisting of Scott open filters, and a countable strongly meet continuous dcpo that is not continuous is constructed. For posets with the one step closure property, strongly meet continuity is equivalent to continuity. Further, a poset is continuous if and only if it is strongly meet continuous and its Scott space is core compact. As a consequence, every core compact strongly meet continuous dcpo has a sober Scott space.

papers.title: Dimension-uniform Connectivity Laws and Hitting Times for Spherical Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G_d(n,p)$ be the graph formed by joining pairs of $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ within a radius chosen to give edge probability $p$. For each fixed integer $K\ge0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, we prove that at $np=\log n+K\log\log n+t$, the probabilities of $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity both converge to $\exp(-e^{-t}/K!)$ uniformly over all $d=d(n)\ge3$. This is the same limit as in the Erdős--Rényi graph. Moreover, as the radius increases on a single sample, the first radii for minimum degree at least $K+1$, $(K+1)$-vertex-connectivity, and $(K+1)$-edge-connectivity coincide with probability tending to one uniformly over $d\ge3$. To our knowledge, this is the first critical-window law for connectivity in a random geometric graph that holds uniformly from fixed dimensions to dimensions growing arbitrarily with $n$.

papers.title: Low-Rank Tensor Representations for Efficient Multimarginal Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Multimarginal Optimal Transport (MOT) suffers from exponential computational and memory costs in the number of marginals, as transport plans are represented by high-dimensional tensors. We introduce Low-Rank Multimarginal Optimal Transport (LRMOT), which restricts transport plans to tensors with bounded multilinear rank, providing a compact and structured representation of multimarginal couplings. This structure enables efficient algorithms with a low memory footprint. We establish approximation bounds for the resulting low-rank formulations and demonstrate experimentally that the proposed algorithms substantially reduce computational time while achieving solutions with low transport cost.

papers.title: The limit shape of uniform random antichains in $[0,1]^d$
papers.abstract: For each $d\ge2$, we study $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, conditioned to form an antichain: no point is strictly smaller than another in every coordinate. We prove that the point cloud converges in Hausdorff distance to the closure of the hypersurface \[\mathcal S_d=\left\{\mathbf x\in(0,1)^d: \sum_{i=1}^dΦ^{-1}(\mathbf x_i)=0\right\}\] in probability as $n\to\infty$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The proof also shows that the antichain probability $a_n$ satisfies $\log a_n=-\frac{n}{d-1}\log n+β_d n+o(n)$ for a finite constant $β_d$. We identify the limiting empirical distribution and hence the limiting permuton of uniform random $d$-dimensional permutations avoiding a single pattern of size $2$.

papers.title: Eigendecomposition for instantons via infinity-category
papers.abstract: Suppose $L$ is a framed link in a balanced sutured manifold $(M, γ)$. We construct a link spectral sequence in sutured instanton homology. For properly embedded surfaces in $M$ disjoint from $L$, we refine the spectral sequence to preserve the induced multi-grading. We use $\infty$-categories to encode homotopical information from instanton theory. In particular, we obtain a simultaneous eigendecomposition of homotopy-coherently commutative operators on a chain complex or a hypercube complex. As the algebraic foundation for subsequent work of the second author and collaborators, we construct the mixed hypercube by combining the hypercubes of positive and negative bypass maps. This construction is compatible with the eigendecomposition associated with the surface multi-grading on sutured instanton homology.

papers.title: Normalized solutions of critical biharmonic equations on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the critical biharmonic equation with clamped boundary conditions and prescribed $L^2$ norm on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$. For every sufficiently small mass, the constrained energy admits a local minimizer. We also obtain a second solution for masses in the closure of a measurable set having positive measure in every interval adjacent to zero. This holds on arbitrary smooth bounded domains when $N\ge8$ and, when $N=5,6,7$, under a condition involving the first clamped eigenvalue and a cutoff quotient. Explicit sufficient conditions are given and verified on balls. The proof combines a quantitative monotonicity argument with a norm estimate excluding loss of compactness.

papers.title: The Hlawka-Schatten inequality: an exposition of recent progress
papers.abstract: We give an expository account of recent progress on a question of Audenaert and Kittaneh concerning a Hlawka-type inequality for Schatten norms of matrices. We review the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality and explain the motivation behind understanding the so-called Hlawka-Schatten inequality. We present an elementary $2 \times 2$ construction showing that no finite constant satisfies the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for the trace norm, and explain Esa's proof that a dimension-independent constant exists for every $1 < p < \infty$. We also discuss the Hlawka-Schatten inequality for diagonal matrices and subsequent developments thereof on Prove2Me. Our aim is to make the mathematical ideas behind these AI-assisted results accessible, and to clarify their relationship with the available Lean formalizations.

papers.title: A preconditioned Reconstructed Discontinuous Approximation for Darcy flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an efficient numerical method for Darcy flow based on the reconstructed discontinuous approximation (RDA). The key contribution is a mesh-robust piecewise-constant preconditioner for arbitrarily high-order RDA discretizations of Darcy flow. The method discretizes the Darcy equations by a stabilized discontinuous Galerkin scheme in coupled velocity-pressure form, with RDA spaces for both velocity and pressure. Function spaces of this type can achieve arbitrarily high-order approximation accuracy while retaining only one degree of freedom per element. We establish an optimal-order error estimate in the energy norm and a suboptimal error estimate in the L2 norm. Benefiting from the property that the number of degrees of freedom of the RDA space is independent of the approximation order, we can construct a simple and efficient preconditioner based on piecewise constant functions for algebraic systems arising from arbitrarily high-order discretizations. We further prove a mesh-independent spectral equivalence between the preconditioner and the original algebraic system, so that the convergence of the GMRES residual does not slow down under mesh refinement. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed preconditioning method.

papers.title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras
papers.abstract: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$.
