Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.

papers.title: Alpha-points of a putative binary $q$-analog of the Fano plane
papers.abstract: A point $P$ of a putative $q$-analog $\mathcal{D}$ of the Fano plane is an $α$-point if the derived design of $\mathcal{D}$ in $P$ is a Desarguesian line spread. Kiermaier showed that for $q$ prime or even every hyperplane contains a point which is not an $α$-point. For $q=2$ we study the $45$ blocks of $\mathcal{D}$ inside a hyperplane $H$. Call a $5$-subspace of $H$ a $β$-flat if all its blocks pass through one point, its focal point. We show that at least $41$ points of $H$ are not focal points of $β$-flats. Consequently $\mathcal{D}$ has at least $85$ non-$α$-points, at most $42$ $α$-points, and at most $22$ $α$-points in every hyperplane.

papers.title: The sharp mass threshold for the three-dimensional Riesz liquid-drop model near the Coulomb exponent
papers.abstract: We determine the exact mass threshold of the three-dimensional liquid-drop model with repulsive kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ in a two-sided neighborhood of the Coulomb exponent $s=1$. The infimum is attained precisely for $0<m\le\mstar$, with balls as the unique minimizers up to translation and null sets. Here $\mstar$ is the mass at which one ball and two equal balls at infinite separation have the same energy. We compute the first-order variation of this threshold at $s=1$. For $s>1$, a diameter bound proportional to the mass supplies a lower bound on the averaged planar slicing integral and yields a uniform mass bound. The resulting compactness and a uniform quadratic energy gap for finite-perimeter sets close in measure to a ball allow us to transfer the Coulomb classification to nearby exponents. At $m=\mstar$, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence asymptotic in measure to single balls or pairs of equal balls with diverging separation, with both alternatives realized by minimizing sequences. For $\mstar<m\le3\mstar/2$, only the separated pair occurs and the infimum is twice the energy of a half-mass ball. We also obtain the first-order change in interaction energy with respect to the exponent along subsequences of near-minimizers as $s\to1$ and $m\to m_*(1)$.

papers.title: Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points
papers.abstract: A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber. The convergence is uniform over compact sets disjoint from the tropical hypersurface, independently of the arguments of the point coordinates. When the chamber is nonempty and its index is an interior lattice point, the limit is the classical linking number of the oriented chamber boundary with the limiting logarithmic point. A plane cubic illustrates both this interpretation and its failure on a tropical wall.

papers.title: The $H^p$-Corona theorem on bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
papers.abstract: For $0<p\le2$, we solve the $H^p$-Corona problem on bounded pseudoconvex domains $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$ with $C^2$ boundary, obtaining the bound $C_Ωδ^{-q-1}|\logδ|$, where $q=\min\{n,m-1\}$ and $m$ is the number of generators. The range of $p$ is sharp even on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain admitting a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function and having only one weakly pseudoconvex boundary point.

papers.title: Free-boundary minimal varifolds I: zero boundary mass
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a $k$-varifold in a compact Riemannian manifold $M^n$ with smooth nonempty boundary, where $2 \le k < n$. Assume that $V$ is stationary with free boundary and almost minimizing modulo two in every sufficiently small relative annulus about each point of $M$. We prove that $V$ is integral and that the trace of the boundary second fundamental form on $T_x V$ vanishes at $\|V\|$-almost every boundary point. On all of $M$, the first variation is $δV = ν\,σ$, where $ν$ is the outward unit normal and $σ$ is a nonnegative measure on $\partial M$ singular with respect to $\|V\|$. A strict sign for the trace on all tangent $k$-planes at each boundary point forces zero boundary mass. For hypersurfaces in ambient dimensions three through seven, strict mean convexity gives smoothness and proper embeddedness. In every bounded smooth Euclidean domain $Ω$, we obtain $\|V\|(Ω) \ge c_{Ω,k}\|V\|(\overlineΩ)$ with $c_{Ω,k} > 0$. For smooth connected free-boundary minimal submanifolds in $\overlineΩ$, assuming a volume bound and a common annular almost minimizing condition at a fixed scale, then their first Dirichlet eigenvalues uniformly bounded above.

papers.title: Local limit theorem for the Kemperman's oscillating walk
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the local probabilities of the so-called oscillating walk on the latttice Z; this class of discrete time Markov chains was introduced by Kemperman. Our main result is a local counterpart of the convergence of a properly rescaled oscillating walk towards the corresponding skew Brownian motion. In particular, we show that the approximation of local probabilities by the density of the limiting distribution may fail in the points which are not far from zero.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.

papers.title: Scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map and applications to Kähler reduction
papers.abstract: Suppose that a compact and connected Lie group acts holomorphically on a Hodge manifold, and that the action linearises to the associated Hermitian ample line bundle. Assume that zero is a singular value of the associated moment map. The spaces of global holomorphic sections of powers of the line bundle decompose over the finite dimensional irreducible representations of the group. The main goal of this paper is to study the scaling limits for equivariant Szegő kernels near a singular point of the moment map. As an application, we discuss the quantization of the singular reduced space: the behaviour of invariant sections along the singular strata, the failure of the asymptotic unitarity of the Guillemin--Sternberg map near the singular strata, and the number of invariant sections concentrated near a singular orbit.

papers.title: Optimal quantitative stability near the Coulomb fission threshold
papers.abstract: We study the optimal quadratic stability constant for the three-dimensional Coulomb liquid-drop energy at fixed volume, measured by the squared Fraenkel asymmetry. Let $M$ be the critical mass at which the energy of one ball equals the limiting energy of two infinitely separated balls of equal volume. We prove that, as $m$ approaches $M$ from below, the optimal constant satisfies $Λ(m)=(36π)^{1/3}(2^{1/3}-1)(1-m/M)+o(1-m/M)$. We further show that every almost optimal sequence with masses $m_n\to M$ from below is asymptotic in measure to a union of two equal-volume balls whose centers diverge. We also identify the corresponding perimeter and Coulomb-energy limits and give a necessary and sufficient criterion for almost optimality after rescaling to mass $M$. The proof combines a strict binding inequality for mass partitions, a local spectral gap at the critical ball, and a BV truncation argument for critical minimizing sequences. All results hold for arbitrary finite-perimeter competitors, without connectedness or boundary regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Sharp global well-posedness for the defocusing nonlinear wave equation outside a ball with radial data
papers.abstract: Let $Ω=\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\overline{B(0,1)}$ and $3<p<5$. We prove sharp global well-posedness of the defocusing Dirichlet boundary value problem of nonlinear wave equation with radial data in the critical space $\dot H^{s_c}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)\times \dot H^{s_c-1}_{D,\mathrm{rad}}(Ω)$, where $s_c=\frac32-\frac{2}{p-1}$, thereby improve the result in \cite{XuYangYou2025}. The proof combines the distorted Fourier transform in \cite{LiSZ:NLS,XuYang2024} with the energy--Morawetz estimate by Dodson in \cite{DodsonCubic2018,Dodson2018}.

papers.title: Endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules in special characteristic
papers.abstract: We classify the division algebras that occur as endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank in special characteristic which cannot be defined over a finite field. The classification is in terms of the center of the algebra and its local invariants. Together with the known results in generic characteristic and over finite fields, this gives a complete description of the endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank.

papers.title: Degree 2 foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with only saddle-node and nilpotent singularities
papers.abstract: We classify all foliations of degree $2$ on $\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ having only saddle-node or nilpotent singularities up to projective equivalence. To do so, we use the bijection between such foliations and their polar configurations stated by Campillo and Olivares~\cite{CO}. We also show that three families of the found foliations admit no algebraic invariant curve.

papers.title: Periodic orbit asymptotics and dynamical zeta functions for smooth surface diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a closed surface $M$, and let $H$ be a closed homoclinic class with topological entropy $h=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f|H)>0$ and homoclinic period $\ell$. We prove that \[ \forall\,0<χ<h,\qquad \lim_{\ell\mid n,\;n\to\infty} \frac{\#\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)}{e^{nh}}=\ell, \] where $\mathrm{Per}_χ(n,H)$ denotes the saddle points in $H$ of least period $n$ whose Lyapunov exponents lie outside $[-χ,χ]$. We also prove exponential remainders for the class and global counting formulas. As a result, for every $0<χ<h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$, the Artin--Mazur zeta function of all $χ$-hyperbolic periodic orbits, including sinks and sources, extends meromorphically beyond its disk of convergence. Its leading poles are determined by the periods of the ergodic maximal measures. This answers the meromorphic continuation question of Buzzi.

papers.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
papers.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.

papers.title: Backward Error and Scaling in Level-Based ILU(k) and IC(k) Preconditioners
papers.abstract: We analyse the effect of rounding errors and diagonal scaling on level-based ILU($k$) and IC($k$) preconditioners. Because the sparsity pattern is fixed in advance, the computed factors are those that the incomplete factorization produces, in exact arithmetic, for a nearby matrix, and the deviation of the preconditioned matrix from the identity is bounded by an incompleteness term plus a rounding term. When no shift or pivot modification is needed, scaling leaves the iterates unchanged in exact arithmetic but can change the quantities in this bound by orders of magnitude. For IC($k$), we bound the change in the preconditioned eigenvalues caused by rounding by a multiple of the Skeel condition number of the incomplete factor, which does not depend on the scaling, and we show that after Jacobi scaling the entries of the factor are bounded, so that in half precision a breakdown can be detected before any overflow. Experiments in double, single and half precision illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Principal spectral theory of time-periodic nonlocal advective cooperative systems and its applications
papers.abstract: We develop a new spectral theory for time-periodic nonlocal cooperative systems with advection on bounded intervals, allowing asymmetric dispersal kernels. By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincaré map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. For spatially homogeneous coefficients, we establish the limit of the principal eigenvalue as the interval expands to $\mathbb R$ and identify it as the minimum of the principal Floquet exponents of the associated exponentially weighted periodic systems. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solutions either converge to a unique positive time-periodic solution or vanish as time tends to infinity. We also prove convergence of positive periodic solutions as the interval expands. For the Cauchy problem on the whole real line, we characterize the leftward and rightward spreading speeds, which may differ for asymmetric dispersal kernels, and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for accelerated spreading in either direction. In particular, under irreducible coupling, accelerated spreading in one component induces accelerated spreading in all components in the same direction.

papers.title: Sierpiński Gaskets Julia set and Postcritically finite fractals
papers.abstract: Devaney's work on the Julia sets of the McMullen family, established these rational maps as central objects in holomorphic dynamics. For Misiurewicz parameters, that is when the orbits of the critical points are all strictly preperiodic to a repelling cycle, the topological point of view taken by Kameyama links the dynamics of such rational maps to that on the attractors of invertible self-similar iterated function system. Eroğlu, Rohde, and Solomyak showed that in favorable cases the topological conjugacy is in fact quasisymmetric. We survey the machinery underlying these results and propose directions for further research.

papers.title: How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges
papers.abstract: After causal discovery, a confidence interval for a total effect valid uniformly over the model class must pay for structural uncertainty. We measure this price by the worst-case ratio of expected length to that of the efficient interval knowing the graph, for linear Gaussian models with a known superset of the adjacencies and k-triangle faithfulness. The global price is of order sqrt(n) once one edge can be malignant, so we study it locally, near a generic distribution with one edge absent. Our main result classifies this weak edge by Meek closures. It is benign if deleting it leaves the effect identifiable in the resulting MPDAG and Markov equivalent explanations agree; the local price is then bounded, and otherwise, for small k, of order sqrt(n). At benign edges the price is of order R+K, with R a ratio of efficient lengths and K a cross-model constant. It equals one, so that honesty is free, exactly when K = 0, generically decided by a d-separation. For two Markov classes it is determined within a factor 3.40, and its upper bound is approached without knowing the base point or the weak edge. A further graphical condition gives the rate uniformly in a second edge's margin.

papers.title: Existence and multiplicity of radial solutions for higher order logarithmic and infinite mass Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the Schrödinger equation $-Δu+V(x)u=g(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge3$, where $V$ is radial and $g(t)/t\to-\infty$ as $t\to0$. In this infinite-mass case the energy functional is not finite on $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$. First let $g(t)=t|\log|t||^{α-1}\log|t|$ with $α>1$. We only assume that $V$ is continuous and bounded from below. So $V$ may change sign, and it need not be coercive or have a limit at infinity. We obtain a nontrivial radial solution and a sequence of radial solutions whose energies tend to infinity. To do this, we add the term $λ|u|^{p-2}u$ with $1<p<2$, find critical points of the perturbed functional by minimax methods, and let $λ\to0$. The infinite-mass structure gives the compactness in this limit. Next let $g$ be odd, with a power bound near zero and at most critical growth at infinity. Let $V$ be bounded, with a smallness condition on $(x\cdot\nabla V)_+$. We combine the Pohozaev identity with an augmented symmetric minimax method and obtain infinitely many pairs of radial solutions. A negative critical power term is allowed.

papers.title: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers via Oriented Palette Constructions
papers.abstract: Given a family $\mathcal F$ of $k$-graphs, the Ramsey number $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(k)}$ yields either a red copy of some $F\in\mathcal F$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(k)}$. In particular, if $\mathcal F=\{F\}$, we write $r_k(F,n)$. In this paper, we use oriented palette constructions and the hypergraph container method to obtain a lower bound on $r_k(\mathcal F,n)$ for special families $\mathcal F$. More precisely, we independently label lower-dimensional faces and use the palette to exclude prescribed red configurations, while a container argument controls the size of blue cliques. As a first application of our theorem, we obtain \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)>2^{Ω_k(n\log n)}\). Combined with the upper bound due to Mubayi and Suk, this yields \(r_k(B^{(k)},n)=2^{Θ_k(n\log n)}\), where \(B^{(k)}\) is the half-graph. This answers in the affirmative a question posed by Mubayi and Suk. As a second application of our theorem, we show $r_k(k+1,3;n)=2^{Θ_k(n^{k-2}\log n)}$, which, together with a new stepping-up lemma developed in this paper, further yields $r_k(k+1,t;n)=\twr_{t-1}(Θ_{k,t}(n^{k-t+1}\log n))$ for every fixed $k\ge6$ and $4\le t\le k-2$, where $\twr_1(x)=x$ and $\twr_{j+1}(x)=2^{\twr_j(x)}$. Here $r_k(k+1,t;n)$ denotes the minimum $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-subsets of an $N$-vertex set contains either $k+1$ vertices spanning at least $t$ red edges or a blue clique of order $n$. As a third application of our theorem, we show that $r_k(F_{\ell,k,d},n)>2^{Ω_{k,\ell,d}(n^{k-d-2}\log n)}$ for all fixed integers $k\ge4$, $1\le d\le k-3$, and $\ell\ge2k+1$ with $k\nmid\ell$, where $F_{\ell,k,d}$ is obtained from the $k$-uniform tight cycle of length $\ell$ by deleting $d$ consecutive edges.

papers.title: Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We study the fractional mean curvature flow near shrinking spheres. The first shape eigenvalue changes sign at \(s_*(n)=(\sqrt{n^2+6n+1}-n-1)/2\). Above this threshold, sufficiently small perturbations of a sphere become extinct at one point, and their extinction rescalings converge exponentially to the round shrinker. Below the threshold, the sphere is nonlinearly unstable modulo translations and dilations. We also construct smooth, strictly convex, nonspherical homothetic shrinkers bifurcating from the spherical family near the threshold. In the plane, the noncircular branch bifurcates on the side \(s>s_*(2)\).

papers.title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.

papers.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_λ$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $λ^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: A construction of proper Jordan schemes of rank $5$
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power such that $m=q^2+q+1$ is a prime satisfying $m\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. We construct a proper symmetric Jordan scheme of rank $5$ on $2m$ vertices using a Singer difference set with parameters $(m,q+1,1)$ and the Paley graph on $m$ vertices.

papers.title: $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property
papers.abstract: Let $(E, P)$, $(E', P')$ be elliptic curves over $\mathbb{C}$ with marked $p$-torsion points; a marked isogeny is an isogeny sending $P$ to $P'$. We show the marked isogeny relation is interpretable in $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and has strict infinite chains. It follows that $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property, which confirms a special case of the stable fields conjecture.

papers.title: Asymptotic insolubility of alternating groups
papers.abstract: Let $a,b\in\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)$ with $a\neq 1$, and let $s$ be chosen uniformly in $A_n$. We show that the probability that $\langle a, bs\rangle$ is insoluble tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly in $a$ and $b$. More precisely, this probability is at least $1-O(n^{-1/24})$. The proof combines a bound in terms of the support of $a$ with estimates on permutations lying in transitive subgroups of the symmetric group.

papers.title: Synchronisation under quasi-periodic forcing of circle diffeomorphisms with two attracting and two repelling fixed points
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of circle diffeomorphisms, which have exactly two attracting and two repelling fixed points, under quasi-periodic forcing. For sufficiently small forcing, such a system exhibits uniformly hyperbolic behaviour. The results focus on systems with larger forcing, where every orbit intersects the basins of attraction of both attracting fixed points infinitely often. For such quasi-periodically forced circle diffeomorphisms, we identify a set of parameters of positive measure for which the corresponding skew-product systems admit a unique attracting and a unique repelling invariant graph, which capture the dynamics of Lebesgue almost every point on $\mathbb{T}^2$. Further, we show that both continuous invariant graphs and invariant graphs that are discontinuous on a dense set can occur within the same class of forced circle diffeomorphisms, for different quasi-periodic rotations on the base.

papers.title: Support monotonicity for quadratically regularized optimal transport
papers.abstract: We study the support of the optimizer $π_\varepsilon$ of the quadratically regularized optimal transport problem for quadratic cost and compactly supported marginals. As $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, this support converges to the support of the Monge coupling. We investigate whether the regularized supports are nested as $\varepsilon $ decreases. Under regularity assumptions on the marginal densities, their domains, and the Brenier map, we establish interior support inclusions in every dimension. More precisely, for each compact $K\subset\operatorname{int}X$ and fixed $θ\in(0,1)$, we prove that $\mathrm{spt}π_δ\cap(K\times Y) \subseteq\mathrm{spt}π_\varepsilon\cap(K\times Y)$ whenever $0<δ\leθ\varepsilon $ and $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small. On these points, the rescaled density $\varepsilon dπ_\varepsilon/d(μ\otimesν)$ is bounded below by a positive multiple of $\varepsilon^{2/(d+2)}$. Our analysis combines sharp potential estimates with affine rescaling and a Liouville theorem that identifies the unique limiting density of the rescaled problem.

papers.title: Families of regular non-Berwald Landsberg surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct families of smooth, strongly convex, non-Berwald Landsberg metrics of zero flag curvature on open subsets of the plane. Each metric is regular in every nonzero tangent direction and is nonreversible. The indicatrices are obtained from the inverse differential of a periodically forced oscillator. The construction is indexed by smooth balanced periodic seeds satisfying a simple characteristic condition at a nonzero initial value. It includes single-frequency seeds of every even frequency at least four, mixtures of interacting frequencies, and seed neighborhoods of arbitrarily large finite dimension within the balanced class. A normalized profile of the canonical Cartan invariant distinguishes fixed seed orbits at sufficiently small amplitudes. In particular, the construction yields countably infinitely many pairwise locally nonhomothetic metrics. The analytic problem is to make the actual return map equal to the identity on an open set of nonzero initial values. We show that exact return on a fixed open set forces three balance equations on the seed. Under a positive drift condition a finite formal approximation gives an arbitrarily high prescribed power of a small amplitude in the return error. We normalize the complete two-branch linearized operator and reduce its scalar part to a real transport direction. A local inverse, followed by an exact correction of the full vector remainder, yields estimates with a fixed loss of derivatives. A smoothing iteration then eliminates the actual return error on a fixed open set of positive radius while retaining the seed as the leading nonlinearity.

papers.title: Spacelike Curve Shortening Flow of Entire Graphs in One Spacelike Codimension
papers.abstract: We study curve shortening flow of entire spacelike graphs in the pseudo-Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{2,k}$, $k\geq1$, where the graph directions have mixed spacelike and timelike signature. Consequently, the region of spacelike slopes is nonconvex, making the preservation of spacelikeness more delicate. We identify a natural geometric condition that overcomes this difficulty: the closed convex hull of the initial slopes is compactly contained in the spacelike region. We prove that the convex hull is preserved along the flow, yielding uniform spacelikeness and uniform acausality. For initially $C^{1,α}$ graphs, we establish global existence and uniqueness, without assuming convexity or initial curvature bounds. If the initial perturbation vanishes at spatial infinity, we further prove smooth and uniform convergence to the prescribed affine spacelike line, without rescaling. Finally, we show that every ancient entire graphical flow with globally bounded slopes that remains uniformly spacelike throughout its evolution is a stationary affine line.

papers.title: Remotest Operator Control String-Averaging Methods in Feasibility-Seeking
papers.abstract: The string-averaging (SA) method is a versatile algorithmic scheme for solving feasibility-seeking problems. It partitions the index set of all constraints into subsets of indices, called strings, allowing the user to apply operators successively along each string separately, and thus in parallel. The end-points of all such string operations are convexly combined to create the next iterate. Due to its flexible framework, SA is not restricted solely to this procedure; however, this characteristic applies only to the simultaneous step, while the sequential one is restricted to operator compositions. To permit alternative strategies in the latter, a novel algorithmic structure termed the Skeletal SA is introduced. Although its convergence is not established, it serves as a foundational "parent" structure that unveils unexamined SA algorithmic structures, as well as other known methods, obscured by standard compositions. To demonstrate the benefit of adopting the Skeletal SA framework over the standard SA scheme, we investigate a new approach, where instead of passing sequentially over each string via compositions, we employ a remotest-set-control-like strategy on every string by identifying the index of the operator farthest from the current iterate, and invoking it. This method favorably handles the common fixed point problem (CFPP), which requires finding a point within the intersection of finitely many constraint sets whose intersection is nonempty. Many iterative methods, including SA ones, have been proposed to solve the CFPP due to its importance in many scientific fields. However, remotest operator control SA (ROC-SA) methods have remained unexamined in this context.

papers.title: Bismut formula and applications for conditional McKean-Vlasov SDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability of Lions derivatives under transition-rate perturbations for conditional McKean-Vlasov SDEs driven by fractional Brownian motion with $H>1/2$. For bounded measurable terminal functions, we establish Lions differentiability, a Bismut formula, and a gradient estimate under bounded first-order drift derivatives with suitable Hölder regularity, without imposing additional higher-order regularity assumptions on the drift's Lions derivative. Fractional Volterra estimates accommodate switching-induced discontinuities, while the Bismut weight has a common representation in terms of the switching process for all admissible transition-rate matrices. Combining this representation with likelihood-ratio methods, we prove quantitative stability, Fréchet differentiability, and a quadratic remainder estimate for Lions derivatives under perturbations preserving the positive off-diagonal support. In a nonlinear two-state model, the quadratic remainder estimate holds uniformly over terminal threshold events. We also demonstrate nonzero transition-rate sensitivity of Lions derivatives under fractional noise, whereas the corresponding Brownian model has a rate-independent terminal law.

papers.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen
papers.abstract: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $Δ$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $Δ$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.

papers.title: The first Fučík curve of the $p$-Laplacian on compact quantum graphs: slopes at the diagonal and nonresonance
papers.abstract: We study the Fučík spectrum of the $p$-Laplacian, $1<p<\infty$, on a compact connected quantum graph, with Dirichlet conditions on a possibly empty set $V_D$ of vertices whose removal does not disconnect the graph and Kirchhoff conditions at the others. We construct the first nontrivial curve $\mathfrak C$ of the spectrum by a mountain pass argument and show that it is Lipschitz and strictly decreasing. As the parameter tends to infinity, $\mathfrak C$ tends to the first eigenvalue if $V_D\neq\emptyset$, and otherwise to the smallest first eigenvalue obtained by a Dirichlet condition at a single point. If the second eigenvalue is simple, we compute the two one-sided slopes of $\mathfrak C$ at the diagonal. The curve is differentiable there if and only if the positive and negative parts of the second eigenfunction have the same $L^p$ norm. On three-edge stars these norms differ for suitable edge lengths and every $p$, so the Lipschitz regularity is optimal. For $p=2$ the simplicity assumption can be dropped, and for a simple eigenvalue the corner is the crossing of the two smooth branches of the spectrum through the diagonal point. Finally, we prove a nonresonance result in which, for $V_D=\emptyset$, the ratio $f(x,s)/|s|^{p-2}s$ may be arbitrarily large at $+\infty$, provided it stays below the threshold at $-\infty$.

papers.title: Joint Cohort Laws and Mixed Cumulants with Spectral Asymptotics for Growing Gaps in Finite-Age Branching Processes
papers.abstract: We investigate the joint distribution and temporal dependence of birth cohorts in a discrete-time age-dependent branching model in which an individual may reproduce at several integer ages. Under an independent age-specific reproduction array, we derive a recursive joint probability generating function, an exact history-dependent transition kernel, and a martingale innovation representation. These identities yield explicit covariance formulae and finite coefficient recursions for mixed factorial moments and mixed cumulants. When reproduction is restricted to a finite maximum age $L$, the cohort vector admits a finite-dimensional companion-matrix representation. In the primitive supercritical case, we establish an exact $L^p$ criterion: for every integer $p\geq2$, the Perron martingale and the normalized cohort state converge in $L^p$ if and only if all age-specific offspring distributions have finite $p$th moments. The normalized cohorts consequently share a common limit, which satisfies an age-indexed smoothing-transform equation with an explicit triangular cumulant recursion. Our principal asymptotic result concerns two cohorts whose separation increases with time. Under a simple-real-subdominant-root condition, we obtain a three-regime asymptotic equivalent for the mean-square distance between their mean-normalized sizes. The rate is governed by whether the squared modulus of the dominant non-Perron root is smaller than, equal to, or larger than the Perron root. This result quantifies the approach to the common cohort limit and distinguishes the present cohort-level question from first-order Perron convergence alone.

papers.title: Products of translates: bounds and constructions
papers.abstract: We study products of translates of the form $(A+d)(A+d)$ with $d\in D$, where both $A$ and $D$ are finite subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. We show that $|(A+a)(A+a)|\ge C|A|^{5/3}$ for some $a\in A$, and that $|(A+D)(A+D)|\le |A|^{2-c(α)}$ for some $c(α)>0$ when $|D|=|A|^α$ with $α<1$.

papers.title: Dirichlet heat kernel estimates for Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a $C^{1, η}$ open set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{B}: D\times D\to (0, \infty)$ a symmetric Borel function which blows up at the boundary of $D$. Let $\overline{X}$ be a conservative purely discontinuous Markov process on $\overline{D}$ with jump kernel $\mathcal{B}(x,y)|x-y|^{-d-α}$, $0<α<2$. In a recent paper, we obtained two-sided estimates on the transition density of $\overline{X}$. In this paper, we consider the process $X$ obtained by killing $\overline{X}$ upon approaching the boundary of $D$ or by a critical potential. We obtain sharp two-sided estimates on the transition density of $X$. The estimates capture the interplay between the blow-up rate of $\mathcal{B}$, the geometry of $D$, and killing.

papers.title: A High-Order Geometry-Conforming Selective Discontinuous Galerkin Method and Its Error Analysis for Elliptic Interface Problems on Curved Domains
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a high-order geometry-conforming immersed finite element (GC-IFE) method for elliptic interface problems on curved domains. The method uses a triangular mesh that conforms to the outer boundary but need not fit the internal interface. Using Frenet--Serret coordinates, the method combines GC-IFE spaces on interface elements, geometry-conforming finite element spaces on curved boundary elements, and standard Lagrange spaces elsewhere. The global degrees of freedom of the proposed method are asymptotically the same as that of the standard continuous finite element method on the same mesh. The main analytical contributions are approximation estimates and trace inequalities for triangular GC-IFE functions. These estimates are used to establish stability and an optimal $O(h^m)$ error bound in an energy norm for the proposed method, which is based on a symmetric selective discontinuous Galerkin formulation. An optimal $O(h^{m+1})$ error bound in the $L^2$ norm is also obtained under the standard regularity assumption on the dual problem. Numerical experiments confirm theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate a reduction in global degrees of freedom to a fully discontinuous Galerkin method.

papers.title: Groups with dual classes of subgroups
papers.abstract: We completely characterize insoluble groups whose subgroups are pronormal or pronormalize every subgroup. We also completely describe $p$-groups with this property, and prove many structural results in the soluble case (for example, such groups are always of length at most $3$ and have Sylow towers).

papers.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.

papers.title: Compatible expansions and rigidity in subtraction games with a single pass
papers.abstract: We study normal-play subtraction games with one globally shared pass. An expansion of the subtraction set is pass-equivalent if it leaves the pass-available Sprague--Grundy sequence unchanged. We show that pure periodicity of the ordinary sequence, together with an eventual translation identity for the pass-available sequence, forces every pass-equivalent expansion to preserve the ordinary sequence. For two-element sets $\{x,y\}$, we classify the compatible additional moves: they are exactly $x+1,\ldots,y-1$ when $y\leq 2x$, and there are none when $y>2x$. We extend this result to sets in short intervals. An exact recurrence certificate also exhibits a three-element set for which pass-state rigidity fails.

papers.title: Maximal sections of the cube
papers.abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture on maximal central sections of the cube in every dimension and codimension. The maximizing sections are exactly the products of diagonals of disjoint coordinate blocks whose sizes differ by at most one. This determines the sharp volume in the cases left open by Ball's 1989 bounds. In fixed dimensions, the logarithmic volume deficit controls both the direction and the displacement of an affine section linearly, with optimal exponent. We also obtain the sharp uniform bound on projection densities for independent real random variables with bounded densities.

papers.title: The Riemann Hypothesis for L-Functions of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Frobenius Polynomials and Intersection Cohomology
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$. Using the imported arithmetic relative-image identification, we construct a reflection pairing and derive the completed functional equation with positive root number. We also give a canonical Frobenius-equivariant splitting of the fibrewise compact-support/parabolic sequence by separation of weights and examine the comparison on open coordinate-zero divisors. The statements do not assume global arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or a higher-codimension wild-boundary exchange. An explicit source-and-dependency ledger distinguishes results imported from the companion papers from deductions established here.

papers.title: Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.

papers.title: Reverse Schensted bumping, inverse reduction map and concatenation in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection
papers.abstract: Provided the explicit formula for the inverse reduction map, arXiv:2606.24840, we exhibit for symplectic bumped intervals and for symplectic bumped columns disjoint for the action of the parity involution, the feasibility of the concatenation operation to return a semi-standard tableau in the inverse quantum Littlewood-Richardson bijection

papers.title: Every Finite Incline Is Finitely Based
papers.abstract: We prove that every incline of finite additive height generates a Cross variety. In particular, every finite incline is finitely based. Moreover, we obtain a uniform bound on the number of variables needed to axiomatize subvarieties of decreasing Catalan semiring varieties, and give an effective construction of finite equational bases.

papers.title: Improvements to explicit Burgess-strength bounds for quadratic characters of prime modulus
papers.abstract: For positive integers $M$ and $N$, consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n\in[M,M+N)}χ_p(n)$, where $χ_p$ is the quadratic character modulo $p$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}+\varepsilon}$ for any integer $r\geq 2$ and any real $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Booker, who showed (under size restrictions on $M$, $N$, $p$ and $r$) that $\lvert S(M,N)\rvert \leq α(r)N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}}(β(r)+\log{p})^{1/2r}$, where $α(r)$ and $β(r)$ are given in (Booker, 2006). We show that when $M$ is not too small compared to $N$, we can improve $β(r)$ by a fixed amount. If $M$ is also not too large compared to $N$, we can further improve $β(r)$ by an amount proportional to $\frac{M}{M+N}$.

papers.title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $σ(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $μ(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $μ(p)$ known as the time constant. We compute the near-critical asymptotics of the two quantities in high dimensions, showing that \begin{align*} σ^2(p) \asymp (p-p_c)^2 \qquad \text{ and } \qquad μ(p) \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{p-p_c}} \end{align*} for all $p>p_c$. Our results concerning the diffusivity confirm a conjecture of Biskup (2011). We also compute the asymptotic critical probabilities of slabs in the same regime, showing that $p_c( \mathbb{Z}^{d-1} \times \{0,\ldots,n\}) - p_c(\mathbb{Z}^{d}) \asymp n^{-2}$ as $n\to \infty$.

papers.title: A Constructive Lower Bound for the Growth Constant of Ternary Cap Sets
papers.abstract: Let $r_3(d)$ denote the maximum size of a cap set in $\mathbb{F}_3^d$. We prove that the exponential growth constant $Λ= \lim_{d\to\infty} r_3(d)^{1/d}$ is strictly greater than $2.22920646813$. The main advance comes from combining two-color recursive synchronization with cross-layer joint filling of a seven-dimensional local alphabet that contains collinear triples (lines). By encoding marked positions as $14$-step closed walks on a two-state directed graph, any zero-sum triple with a fixed outermost color is forced to choose the identical closed walk---and hence the identical record---at every recursive layer, at a net cost of $1000$ dimensions per level. Because the open seven-dimensional coordinates are deferred to the outermost layer, all positions of the same type across all layers can be pooled per record and filled jointly via grouped binary-flag nodes. A $2\times 2$ transfer matrix governs the weighted record count, and spectral dominance over two tilted tail matrices converts this count into a capacity lower bound. Feeding each resulting bound back into the filling parameters iteratively amplifies the growth rate, while a companion-path score exclusion test further enlarges the admissible walk family. The final bound is certified by finite enumeration and exact integer comparisons.

papers.title: Square-zero preservers and tracial states on C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We show that a $C^*$-algebra $A$ of dimension at least two has no tracial states if and only if, for every complex normed space $E$, each bounded symmetric bilinear map $V:A\times A\to E$ with $V(x,x)=0$ for every square-zero $x\in A$ factors through the Jordan product, that is, $V(x,y)=S((xy+yx)/2)$ for some bounded linear map $S:A\to E$ and all $x,y\in A$. The factor $S$ is unique and $\|S\|=\|V\|$. Moreover, applying this bilinear result, we show that $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every bounded square-zero-preserving linear surjection $φ:A\to B$ onto a nonzero Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity factors as $φ=WJ$, where $J:A\to B$ is a bounded Jordan homomorphism and $W:B\to B$ is a bounded invertible linear centralizer. Likewise, $A$ has no tracial states if and only if every spectrally bounded linear surjection $φ:A\to B$ onto a nonzero semisimple Banach algebra with a bounded approximate identity admits such a factorization. In both cases, the factors are unique and $J$ induces a bounded Jordan isomorphism $A/\kerφ\to B$. In particular, when $φ$ is unital, the factorization reduces to $φ=J$, which settles Mathieu's square-zero conjecture for nonscalar domains and answers the related question on spectrally bounded surjections.

papers.title: Difference estimates for Chern connections on homolomorphic vector bundles
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the uniqueness issue of Chern connections from the Cheng-Yau type estimate point of view. We establish local difference estimates for Chern connections on holomorphic vector bundles over complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded from below. These local estimates not only enable us to obtain uniqueness results for Hermitian-Einstein connections on complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, but also apply to study the Liouville theorem for complex Monge-Ampère equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ as well as the Chern flatness and Kählerness for Hermitian metrics on complete noncompact Ricci flat Kähler manifolds.

papers.title: Silver rate is sharp for gradient descent
papers.abstract: We determine the minimax convergence rate of gradient descent with predetermined real stepsizes on smooth convex functions up to an absolute constant factor. Let $p=\log_2(1+\sqrt{2})\approx 1.2716$. We prove that for every $L>0$, every integer $n\ge1$ and every stepsize schedule $h\in\mathbb{R}^n$ there exist a convex $L$-smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ in some finite dimension $d$, a minimizer $x_\star$ of $f$ and an initial point $x_0\neq x_\star$ such that the iterate $x_n$ of gradient descent with stepsizes $h$ satisfies $(f(x_n)-f(x_\star))/(L\|x_0-x_\star\|^2)\ge c\,n^{-p}$ with an absolute constant $c>0$. This lower bound matches the $O(n^{-p})$ upper bounds achieved by silver-type stepsize schedules and establishes the optimality of the silver rate up to an absolute constant factor. Previous lower bounds reached the optimal polynomial exponent for both nonnegative and signed schedules but retained subpolynomial losses. We remove these losses for all predetermined real stepsize schedules. The proof combines a quantitative stability estimate for a splitting inequality at the silver proportions with Moreau-envelope constructions that join prescribed gradient descent trajectories and with multiscale averaging over stepsize thresholds.

papers.title: A complete knot invariant from grid diagrams
papers.abstract: Using grid diagrams, we define an infinite graph associated to each knot type. We prove that the isomorphism class of this grid graph is a complete invariant of the knot, up to mirroring. Even more, we prove that algorithmically determinable finite parts of this graph are enough to determine the knot type.

papers.title: GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

papers.title: Coalescence and the Two-Point Covariance in the Directed Landscape
papers.abstract: In the directed landscape with Brownian terminal data, we express the spatial derivative of the two-point height covariance in terms of the probability that two geodesics coalesce before the terminal time and the exit law of a single geodesic. This formula arises as the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling limit of a zero-temperature Brownian last-passage identity from our earlier work on the O'Connell-Yor polymer. To pass the coalescence probabilities to the limit, we show that two paths sharing an optimal exit almost surely lose total weight if they must stay disjoint before reaching it. At stationarity, we determine when two zero-direction semi-infinite geodesics first coalesce. We recover this distribution by differentiating the height-increment variance first in the starting separation, then in the boundary strength. When the terminal reward is zero everywhere, the starting points with the same leftmost optimal exit as the origin form an interval. The probability that this interval extends past given distances on both sides equals the rate at which the height covariance decreases at their sum.

papers.title: Obstructed Harvey--Lawson cones and logarithmic special Lagrangian singularities
papers.abstract: We construct two exact embedded special Lagrangian germs with the same unique multiplicity-one tangent cone, the Harvey--Lawson cone in $\mathbb C^9$. A quadratic obstruction and a corrected cubic obstruction yield the distinct sharp $C^1$ convergence rates $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1}$ and $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$, respectively. These rates distinguish the germs under unitary transformations and dilations. We also prove Jacobi nonintegrability of the Harvey--Lawson cones in $\mathbb C^8$ and $\mathbb C^9$, and realize the sharp rate $\lvert\log r\rvert^{-1/2}$ at the eight-dimensional cone.

papers.title: Growth versus boundedness for viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a forcing term: a Fujita-type dichotomy
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=Δu+|\nabla u|^q+a(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where $q>1$ and the integrable forcing has positive total mass. Unlike classical Fujita problems, regular solutions exist globally, so the relevant dichotomy concerns boundedness versus grow-up. We identify the critical exponent $q_c=N/(N-1)$ for $N\geq 2$, with $q_c=\infty$ for $N=1$. For stationary forcing, every solution grows at least linearly on a fixed ball when $1<q\leq q_c$. In two dimensions, solutions tend to infinity locally uniformly for every $q>1$, with an explicit logarithmic lower bound. For $q=2$, the Cole--Hopf transformation relates the exact growth rate to the spectrum of $-Δ-w$. Conversely, when $N\geq 3$ and $q>q_c$, bounded solutions exist for sufficiently small nonnegative data and forcing. We also establish growth criteria for time-dependent forcing, including decaying profiles.

papers.title: H(n)-Gordian graphs of knotoids and their quotients: Gromov hyperbolicity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $H(n)$-moves on knotoid diagrams and the corresponding $H(n)$-Gordian graphs. We establish that the $H(n)$-Gordian graphs of knotoids are not Gromov hyperbolic. We also consider quotient graphs of the $H(n)$-Gordian graph of knotoids by the following knotoid invariants: the height of a knotoid, the span of the affine index polynomial, the $y$-span and $z$-span of the invariant $H_K(t, y, z)$, and the span of the Jones polynomial. We prove that in all these cases, the quotient graphs are Gromov hyperbolic.

papers.title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. Simulations with up to $10^5$ degrees of freedom confirm both predictions without adjustable parameters. Requiring neither tangent-space evolution nor prior specification of an order parameter for its computation, trajectory arclength provides a simple, quantitative link between microscopic Hamiltonian motion and collective thermodynamic criticality.

papers.title: The response field approach to path integral control
papers.abstract: This paper investigates non-linear path integral control problems within the response field formalism of nonequilibrium field theory. The aim of this work is exploratory, based on the identification of correspondences between backward adjoint processes and the response field of non-equilibrium statistical physics, whose properties have not been set out in an optimal control setting. The response field is found to play an analogous role to the backward adjoint process under the stochastic maximum principle. In particular, the gradient of the optimal cost-to-go at the initial time, which is proportional to the optimal control, is given by the average of the response field at the initial time. In contrast to the case of non-equilibrium dynamics, the response function is found to be acausal in the control setting. The linear-quadratic case of path integral control is studied, confirming it as the free theory, meaning that solving the control problem is equivalent to completing the square and determining the propagator for a two point boundary value problem. The developments presented here are a necessary prelude to applications based on field theoretic approximation, for both path integral control and their dual inference problems.

papers.title: Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing
papers.abstract: The hockey-stick divergence is a fundamental distinguishability measure in quantum information theory. It characterizes quantum differential privacy and determines the optimal error probability of binary quantum hypothesis testing with arbitrary priors. We study how it behaves on tensor-product states. To this end, we consider the noncommutative minimum $m(A,B):=(\mathrm{Tr}[A]+\mathrm{Tr}[B]-\|A-B\|_1)/2$ of positive semidefinite operators, which reduces to $\sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}$ when $A$ and $B$ commute, and we prove that it is super-multiplicative, i.e., $m(A\otimes C,B\otimes D)\ge m(A,B)\,m(C,D)$. As a consequence, we establish a sub-additivity property of the hockey-stick divergence on product states, in which the parameters of the individual systems are multiplied, and no additional prefactor appears. We show that this bound is tight, also for noncommuting states, and that it is strict for faithful states whenever at least two of the divergences are positive. Using this, we obtain sub-additivity of the Datta-Leditzky divergences, a parallel composition theorem for quantum differentially private channels under product neighboring inputs with at most linear degradation of the privacy parameters, and a sharp sub-additivity property of the hypothesis-testing relative entropy normalized by the acceptance probability. Finally, we apply the same tools to symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing. We determine the exact prefactor of the quantum Chernoff bound for every pair of noncommuting states satisfying mild conditions including a nonlattice condition and, under a quantitative version of this condition, the full asymptotic expansion to every fixed order in $1/n$, with explicitly computable coefficients. As a consequence, we determine the sample complexity of symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing up to one sample, as the error probability tends to zero.

papers.title: On the extension of non-faithful and non-normal traces of von Neumann algebras to their affiliated operators
papers.abstract: Let $τ$ be a positive tracial functional on a finite von Neumann algebra ${\mathcal{M}}$, not necessarily normal. For a positive self-adjoint operator $A$ affiliated with ${\mathcal{M}}$ we define ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)=\lim_{h\downarrow0}τ(A(\mathrm{I}+hA)^{-1})\in[0,\infty]$. We show that $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(A)=\sup_Rτ(\min(A,R \mathrm{I}))$. We prove that ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is additive on positive affiliated operators, by a form--resolvent comparison valid for arbitrary positive traces. As a consequence, $τ$ has a positive linear extension to the span $\mathscr D_τ$ of the positive affiliated operators of finite extended trace, and $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(T^*T)$ defines a pre-Hilbert structure for every positive trace. For every trace, $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S+T|)^{2/3}\le τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|S|)^{2/3}+τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)^{2/3}$; hence the operators $T$ with $τ_{\mathrm{Y}}(|T|)<\infty$ form a ${\mathcal{M}}$-bimodule $\mathscr L_Y^1$, on which the linear extension is defined and cyclic. It turns out that $\mathscr L_Y^1=\mathscr D_τ$; $d(S,T)={τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(|S-T|)^{2/3}$ is a translation-invariant pseudometric on $\mathscr L^1_Y$ and is a metric iff $τ$ is faithful. On the approximation side, a Chernoff family in ${\mathcal{M}}$ forces affiliation of its generator. Trace defects of Chernoff families need not converge to ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}(A)$, even for faithful normal traces, while two-sided resolvent comparison suffices. For faithful normal traces, ${τ_{\mathrm{Y}}}$ is the canonical extension and the associated space $\mathscr L_Y^p$ coincide with the classical $L^p({\mathcal{M}},τ)$ as well as their norms ($1\leq p<\infty$).

papers.title: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the list-recoverability of folded Reed--Solomon codes and provides new evidence toward a recent conjecture. Chen--Zhang (STOC 2025) established that for any $\ell,a \ge 2$ and $L = \ell^a - 1$, if a folded Reed--Solomon code of rate $R$ is $(ρ,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, then $ρ\leq \frac{L+1-\ell}{L+1}(1-\frac{aR}{a-1}).$ It is conjectured that this upper bound is tight. We provide two pieces of evidence concerning this conjecture. First, we prove that explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes of rate arbitrarily close to $\tfrac{a-1}{a+\ell-2}$ are $(0,\ell,L)$-list-recoverable, which confirms the conjecture in the special case $ρ=0$ and $\ell=2$. Second, we show that for any $R\in(0,\tfrac{a-1}{a})$, there are rates arbitrarily close to $R$ at which attaining the conjectured bound requires exponentially large alphabets. This mirrors the phenomenon observed by Alrabiah--Guruswami--Li (SODA 2024), where achieving the generalized Singleton bound in the list-decoding setting also necessitates exponential alphabet size.

papers.title: An Exact Vertex Localization of Zykov's Theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a vertex-based localization of the exact form of Zykov's theorem. For a graph $G$ of order $n\geq1$, let $N(G,K_t)$ denote its number of copies of $K_t$, and let $c(v)$ be the order of a largest clique containing $v$. Write $Z_t(n,s)=N(T_s(n),K_t)$, where $T_s(n)$ is the balanced complete $s$-partite graph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every integer $t\geq2$, \[ N(G,K_t)\leq \frac1n\sum_{v\in V(G)}Z_t(n,c(v)). \] Equality holds if and only if $G$ is $K_t$-free or $G\cong T_s(n)$ for some $t\leq s\leq n$. Moreover, the coefficients $Z_t(n,s)$ are pointwise best possible among all bounds of this form. Our result strengthens the previous vertex-localized bound \[ N(G,K_t)\leq n^{t-1} \sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{\binom{c(v)}{t}}{c(v)^t} \] by accounting for the integer part sizes of Turán graphs. The comparison between the two upper bounds is strict precisely when some vertex $v$ satisfies $c(v)\geq t$ and $c(v)\nmid n$. As consequences, we recover the exact Zykov and Turán bounds without divisibility assumptions.

papers.title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
papers.abstract: Being able to find multiple solutions of a semilinear elliptic equation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing. In this paper, fully taking the advantages of randomized neural networks, we propose a new efficient and accurate method for identifying potentially as many solutions as possible. The new method is constructed from three aspects--initialization, optimization, a technique for acceleration and improving accuracy, two of which are innovative developments. Firstly, based on the basis functions of a randomized network and the sampling points, a characteristic matrix is introduced so that its singular value decomposition can be used to determine weakly variant search directions, followed by a newly developed algorithm to generate effective initial candidates. Then the good deflated Gauss-Newton method [see {\em A. Riley, et al., SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47~(5) (2025) A2963-A2987}] using an exponential deflation operator is adapted as the optimization to search for all multiple solutions. Local error estimate of a particular solution under some proper condition is given in terms of the neurons in the hidden layer and the sampling points for this newly designed method. Furthermore, to accelerate the computation and improve the solution accuracy, a new multilevel method based on hierarchical networks is designed. Without using any {\em a priori} information, several numerical tests show together with the multilevel method, the new method can not only accurately find multiple solutions with relative errors reaching $10^{-16}$ only in less than one-tenth computational cost for the best case, but also preserve the inherent symmetries of multiple solutions.

papers.title: Tableau Consequence under Positive Contexts: A Reconstruction of Walukiewicz's Completeness Proof
papers.abstract: We establish a positive-context lifting theorem for tableau consequence in the modal $μ$-calculus: under explicit syntactic hypotheses, $\mathcal T_B\Rightarrow\mathcal T_C$ induces $\mathcal T_{A(B)}\Rightarrow\mathcal T_{A(C)}$. The proof orders instances of the given relation by birth time and assigns overlapping formula occurrences to the oldest supporting instance. A corollary gives bidirectional replacement by automaton normal form inside positive contexts. Together with a separate unfolding consequence lemma and ANF bisimulation, the lifting theorem yields a self-contained reconstruction of Walukiewicz's completeness proof for Kozen's axiomatisation and makes its least-fixpoint step more transparent. We also give a finite parity-game proof of regular-refutation existence and a two-sided transfer from tableau consequence to thin refutations.

papers.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent
papers.abstract: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches between human players and an adaptive bot.

papers.title: Statistically Optimal and Near Linear Time Hypothesis Selection
papers.abstract: In hypothesis selection we are given $n$ distributions $q_1,\dots,q_n$ on a countable domain $\mathcal{X}$ and samples from an unknown distribution $p$. The goal is a distribution $q$ with $\mathrm{TV}(p,q)\leα\min_i\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)+ε$. The factor $α=2$ is optimal for algorithms using a number of samples from $p$ that is independent of $|\mathcal{X}|$, and in general only improper learners achieve it. We give a learner that achieves $α=2$ with $O(\log(n/δ)/ε^2)$ samples of $p$, with probability at least $1-δ$. This matches the sample complexity of Yatracos's factor-$3$ estimator, and it removes the logarithmic factors in the factor-$2$ bound of Bousquet et al. (FOCS 2021). The learner accesses the $q_i$ only through sampling and pointwise comparisons. We measure its running time by its oracle complexity, the number of oracle calls. In expectation it makes $O((nε^{-2}+ε^{-4}\log(1/ε))\log(n/δ))$ oracle calls, independent of $\mathcal{X}$. It runs multiplicative weights over the constraints $\mathrm{TV}(q,q_i)\le\mathrm{TV}(p,q_i)$ and uses at most one sample of $p$ per round.

papers.title: A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^nζ(\{1,3\}^n)=ζ(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.

papers.title: Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values
papers.abstract: We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.

papers.title: Complex structures on products with $S^4$
papers.abstract: The main theorem of the present paper is that $S^4\times P$ admits a complex structure whenever $P$ is the fibre product, over a compact complex manifold, of the unit circle bundles of an even number of holomorphic line bundles. This theorem has lots of significant applications. For example, $S^4\times G$ admits a complex structure for every compact Lie group $G$ of even dimension. The same holds for $S^4\times V_{2s}(C^n)$ and $S^4\times V_{2s}(H^n)$ when $n\geq 2s\geq2$, and for $S^4\times V_{4s}(R^n)$ when $n\ge4s\ge4$. The theorem also gives complex structures on the product of $S^4$ with any even number of odd-dimensional spheres. Moreover, complex structures exist on $S^4$ times some moment-angle manifolds, including certain connected sums of sphere products. The construction uses a holomorphic $(C^*)^2$-action on $S^4 \times T^2$ endowed with the complex structure we constructed in [Gao-Tang-Yan, arXiv:2610.06067v1] and a smooth splitting equivariant under the compact torus.

papers.title: Computable certificates for data-driven dimension reduction on reaction-diffusion lattices
papers.abstract: Data-driven methods recover low-dimensional coordinates from high-dimensional spatiotemporal data. Whether those coordinates track a genuine invariant object or a finite-resolution artifact is not settled. On reaction-diffusion lattices, the spectral-gap condition of inertial-manifold theory reduces to a critical lattice size $n_*$. Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $\varphi\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions to the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane
papers.abstract: We classify the self-similar solutions of the inverse mean curvature flow in the Lorentz--Minkowski plane $\mathbb{R}^{1,1}$. Using hyperbolic numbers, the self-similarity condition becomes a linear ODE system, and all solutions are obtained in closed form with explicit smoothness and completeness criteria. Translating solitons occur in three causal types, and dilation--rotation solitons are governed by the discriminant $Δ=a^2-4(b-1)$, as in the Euclidean case. When $a^2=b^2$ the translation cannot be eliminated, owing to the zero divisors of the hyperbolic numbers, and a genuinely Lorentzian class of mixed solitons arises, whose complete smooth members form a one-parameter family. The planar classification is then extended to translationally invariant solutions in $\mathbb{R}^{n,1}$, and rotationally invariant solutions are reduced to an explicit ODE system.

papers.title: Global existence and large-time behavior of classical axisymmetric solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Saint-Venant equations and related models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes system with density-dependent viscosity in a disk, subject to the no-slip boundary condition. We consider both the symmetric viscous stress and the stress written in terms of the full velocity gradient. In each case the coefficients satisfy the BD relation $μ(ρ)=ρ^α$ and $λ(ρ)=2(α-1)ρ^α$. For every $1/2<α\le1$ and $γ>1$, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for arbitrarily large axisymmetric initial data with strictly positive density and possibly nonzero tangential velocity. Moreover, the density has upper and positive lower bounds independent of time, and the solution converges to the constant equilibrium. The two stresses give the same radial momentum equation, but require different estimates of the tangential velocity. The endpoint $α=1$, $γ=2$ includes the viscous shallow-water equations.

papers.title: Space-Time Covariance with Screening Effects, Markov Property, and Long-Range Dependence
papers.abstract: Constructing space-time covariance models is an essential task to account for spatio-temporal dependence. However, there is a lack of practical guidance for constructing new covariance constructions. This paper focuses on studying the interplay among three statistical properties: screening effect, Markov property, and long-range dependence for constructing desirable parsimonious space-time covariance functions. While these properties imply seemingly conflicting statistical practice, it is shown in this paper that closed-form parsimonious covariance functions that simultaneously possess all these properties could be constructed and may be desirable for understanding space-time dependence. To examine these properties, this paper first shows that the confluent hypergeometric (CH) covariance function has asymptotic screening effect even in long-range dependent regime. Then this paper provides theoretical characterizations on Markov property for the hierarchical mixture construction including a necessary and sufficient condition. To account for more practical structures, this paper constructs a flexible Lagrangian CH model with the time-lag varying smoothness and tail decay parameters via a hierarchical mixture approach. These properties are illustrated via simulation studies. The practical performance under these models is evaluated for the Irish wind data and the sea surface temperature data.

papers.title: Division rings of fractions of LV-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and let $A=L_K(E,ω)$ be an LV-algebra of a row-finite weighted graph. We prove that $A$ embeds in a division ring if and only if $E$ has one vertex and its ordered loop weights satisfy $w_n=n$ and $w_j>j$ for $1\le j<n$. Under these conditions, $A$ has a universal division ring of fractions, which we identify with the free field on $2\sum_{j=1}^n w_j-n^2$ generators over $K$. We construct a free generating set explicitly by factoring the matrix of generators. We classify the resulting division rings over $K$ and bound the stabilization required to recognize invertible matrices. These results include mixed weights, for which the LV-algebra need not be a semifir.

papers.title: Rayleigh's conjecture for clamped plates in dimensions four and five
papers.abstract: In 1877, Lord Rayleigh conjectured that the disk minimizes the fundamental frequency of a clamped plate of prescribed area.
