Consequently, $Λ(M,N)$ depends only on the index for all extremal inclusions of finite index, in particular for all irreducible ones. Extremality cannot be dropped: for $d>4$, Popa's locally trivial inclusions are exactly those whose relative dimension set misses the middle interval. Other non-extremal inclusions can contain the whole middle interval in their relative dimension set, or miss part of it.

papers.title: On the Conditional Consistency of the Bootstrap
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on the conditional consistency of the bootstrap. The target is the conditional law of a statistic given a common shock, and the bootstrap approximates it by the law of a resampled statistic conditional on the shock and the data. We call the bootstrap consistent if these laws are close in the Kolmogorov distance for almost every realization of the shock. The conditioning $σ$-algebras are allowed to be unrelated across sample sizes, and both the comparison law and the dimension of the data may vary with the sample size. We give sufficient conditions for consistency in this sense, show that they yield asymptotically correct conditional coverage for bootstrap quantiles, and provide a finite-sample bound on the coverage error. We also relate the Kolmogorov formulation to the merging of probability measures. The results are specialized to statistics depending smoothly on an estimator or on an estimated nuisance parameter.

papers.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
papers.abstract: Predicting spin polarization and light attenuation in optically pumped atomic devices requires solving the coupled diffusive quantum master equation (DQME)--light system. Its nonlinearity, spatially nonlocal coupling, and physical admissibility constraints make high-fidelity numerical simulation challenging. We develop a structure-preserving high-fidelity solver that combines second-order finite differences for three-dimensional atomic diffusion, explicit pseudo-time marching for atomic populations, and an exponential integrator for light propagation. Under a derived time-step restriction, the solver preserves population normalization and nonnegativity, as well as the positivity and monotonic attenuation of the light intensity. Three complementary test cases based on an analytical reduction, asymptotic limits, and an analytical invariant are constructed to verify the solver. To accelerate repeated parameter queries, we eliminate the light field and construct a reduced-order model (ROM) using proper orthogonal decomposition and Galerkin projection of the resulting integro-differential formulation involving only atomic populations. An exact quadratic expansion of the spin-exchange term and discrete empirical interpolation of the optical-pumping term make the cost of evaluating the reduced operators independent of the full-order dimension. Numerical tests verify the solver and demonstrate ROM accuracy outside the training set. The GPU implementation completes simulations with millions of unknowns in minutes, while single-core ROM evaluations take seconds, achieving respective speedup factors exceeding 150 and 7000 relative to the single-core high-fidelity solver.

papers.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.

papers.title: On the Impact of Alternative Settlement Rules for State-of-Charge-Limited Resources in Electricity Markets
papers.abstract: Standard two-settlement markets compute a participant's total profit as the sum of its day-ahead (DA) profit and its incremental real-time (RT) profit. This rule was designed for conventional generators, which can always deliver their DA schedules in RT because their capacity is the same in both markets. Energy storage resources, in contrast, are limited by their state of charge (SOC), so their ability to honor a DA award depends on the SOC available at the time of RT dispatch. When this SOC is insufficient, the RT market may impose a buy-back or sell-back that can lead to a monetary loss. This paper formalizes this asymmetry between SOC-unlimited and SOC-limited resources and assesses three alternative settlement rules: a zero-profit floor; a max rule, which pays storage the maximum of its RT-only profit and its standard DA plus incremental RT profit; and a variant of the max rule applied only when the standard profit is negative. Through our analysis and a case study based on a realistic version of the California system, we identify when storage is most exposed to losses, assess how the alternative rules let storage deviate from DA awards to provide flexibility, and quantify their impact on revenue adequacy.

papers.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-étale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This settles a case left open by Manin's construction. We also obtain unirationality results for Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees $1$ and $2$, and discuss applications to the Hilbert property, equivariant unirationality, and the real plane Cremona group.

papers.title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback (SOF)? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin independently of the initial condition. Two SOF methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial discrete output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is provided only for SISO systems. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays that may be large, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For practical implementation, we further present an SOF controller with time-varying gains that depends on discrete-time delayed measurements. For unknown constant measurement or input delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation of Gramian-based gains is also suggested. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Diffusion-limited aggregation: Boundary, vacancies and shape exclusion
papers.abstract: For external Diffusion-Limited Aggregation (DLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we prove that the number of boundary edges grows linearly. Consequently, a positive fraction of the aggregate lies outside every compact region rescaled to have volume equal to the number of particles. We also show that the probability that the limiting aggregate covers more than a $1-α$ fraction of a cube decays exponentially in its volume for some $α>0$. For Euclidean DLA in every dimension $d \geq 2$, we show that each particle has approximately two near neighbors on average. We then deduce that a positive fraction of the planar Euclidean DLA particles lie outside any compact region scaled to the optimal sphere packing volume.

papers.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

papers.title: Bias Correction and Inference for Panel Quantile Regression
papers.abstract: We develop a large-$n$, large-$T$ theory for the unsmoothed fixed-effects quantile regression estimator that allows for serially correlated panel data. An exact rank-score identity for the profiled criterion, with a convexity argument, delivers the leading incidental parameter bias of the slope estimator, of order $T^{-1}$, in closed form, paralleling Hahn and Newey (2004) for smooth nonlinear panel models. When $n$ and $T$ grow at the same rate, the estimator is asymptotically normal but in general not centred, and conventional intervals are invalid. In stationary panels whose dependence decays geometrically or polynomially, with $n/T$ bounded, serial correlation changes the structure of this bias: the long-run variance of the quantile score enters it, and feedback from past errors to current regressors adds a term that can bias the estimator even at the median. A split-panel jackknife with contiguous half-panels removes the bias, whereas one with interleaved half-panels does not in general, and a cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered by individual, yields valid inference. Under independence over time, the admissible growth of $n$ relative to $T$, up to $n=o(T^3)$, depends on the regularity of the conditional error densities, and the jackknife is valid throughout this range.

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $σ$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $σ$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,σ)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $σ$-preserving action $α$ satisfies that $\overline{α(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,σ)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $α$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $α:G\curvearrowright (D,σ)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $σ$-preserving action with $\overline{α(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
papers.abstract: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. We then show how to improve the bound to $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-1})$. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.

papers.title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
papers.abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4 and all of their powers. To this end, we show that such hyper-Kähler varieties are homologically motivated by their intermediate Jacobians.

papers.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_χ)$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established. A series of numerical experiments has been performed to confirm the theoretical results of this paper.

papers.title: Some results on representation type and Galois covering with application to the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
papers.abstract: We prove some general results on representation types of special biserial algebras and on Galois coverings of quivers with relations. Moreover, combining these results with the covering theory of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras we determine the representation types of the associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras.

papers.title: Avoiding Distances
papers.abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n \log{n})$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.

papers.title: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $α\in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,α}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_δ$ for the closed $δ$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,α})_δ$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,α}(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_α$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < δ< 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_α)_δ$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_α(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $γ((E_α)_δ)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/δ))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, with constants depending only on $α$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_α)_δ$ is at most $C_αγ((E_α)_δ)^{2α}$ for every $0 < δ< 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $α> 1/2$, and its exponent $2α$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $α$ tends to one.

papers.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. These are double affine versions of the quantum affine wreath algebras of Rosso and Savage. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite cyclic group, we obtain new double affine versions of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the supercentre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.

papers.title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
papers.abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Conditional limit theorems for open intermittent dynamical systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study conditional limit theorems for open intermittent systems endowed with big/small holes. The initial measure for the system can be a broad class of (non)invariant probability, including SRB and Lebesgue measures. Unlike the limit theorems for closed systems, we obtain unexpected new limits for both ``regular" and singular observables.

papers.title: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
papers.abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.

papers.title: Ending currents of hyperbolic group actions
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of ending currents for properly discontinuous isometric actions of hyperbolic groups on Gromov hyperbolic spaces, generalizing Thurston's ending laminations. Several natural generalizations are considered, which agree in the 3-dimensional hyperbolic setting but are otherwise distinct. We illustrate these invariants and their differences by several examples, including closed surface group actions on hyperbolic group extensions arising from Teichmüller theory and a geometrically finite action of a closed surface group on $\mathbb{H}^4$ with a single cusp that corresponds to a non-simple curve on the surface. We also discuss the conditions under which ending currents characterize geometrically finite actions, obtaining several equivalent conditions and some surprises, illustrated by an example of a geometrically infinite action whose ending currents are all supported on a single orbit of peripheral subgroups.

papers.title: Postcritically finite endomorphisms II: algebraic core and Fatou set
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a postcritically finite endomorphism of the complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^N$ of degree at least two. We prove that at every periodic point of $f$, the non-superattracting tangent directions span the tangent space of a periodic projective subvariety which is rationally connected. This phenomenon strongly constrains both the dynamics and the geometry of postcritically finite endomorphisms. In particular, we show that every Fatou component of $f$ is preperiodic and is eventually mapped into the basin of a superattracting cycle.

papers.title: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

papers.title: Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations: Condition Number Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper gives bounds on the spectral condition numbers of Sobolev Gram matrices for deterministic ridge features with Gaussian or tanh-difference activations. In earlier work we showed that the shallow neural network spaces spanned by these features attain optimal Sobolev approximation rates. For either activation $σ$, the construction uses $N_{σ,M}\asymp M^d$ features at resolution $M$ on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$. For each fixed integer $m\ge0$ and all sufficiently large $M$, the raw $H^m(Ω)$ Gram matrix $G$ and its column-normalized counterpart $\widetilde{G}$ are positive definite and satisfy \[ \max\{κ_2(G),κ_2(\widetilde{G})\} \le \exp(CM)\quad (d=2), \] and \[ \max\{κ_2(G),κ_2(\widetilde{G})\} \le \exp(CM\log(M+1))\quad (d\ge3), \] where $C$ is independent of $M$. On the unit ball in every dimension $d\ge3$, matching lower bounds show that the order of the exponent is sharp for both matrices.

papers.title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $Φ(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $Φ$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $Φ$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.

papers.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
papers.abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type. We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: Central algebraic cohomology of Galois gerbes and its abelianization
papers.abstract: We study central algebraic cohomology and its abelianization for Galois gerbes over local fields of characteristic zero and over number fields. The coefficients consist of a connected reductive group and a central subgroup that need not be finite or connected. We construct a canonical abelian group structure on abelian central cohomology. When the gerbe admits a morphism from Kaletha's rigid gerbe, we obtain a fiber product formula for this group in terms of rigid cohomology and homomorphisms from the band to the central subgroup. Over number fields, abelianization and localization at the real places recover the full central cohomology set. We obtain explicit formulas for Kottwitz's local and global gerbes and for Fargues's extended Kottwitz gerbe.

papers.title: When Hedging Changes the Payoff: Option Replication with Price Impact and Execution Costs
papers.abstract: Hedging a derivative by trading the underlying asset changes the payoff that the hedging intended to replicate. We study this phenomenon when trading generates price impact and execution costs. In a binomial model, we characterize replication through a fixed point equation. In continuous time, we derive a nonlinear pricing PDE whose implicit terminal condition captures the nature of the moving target problem of the hedger. For monotone convex Lipschitz payoffs (such as calls and puts) we establish exact replication under midpoint execution costs. Numerical experiments illustrate: (i) how price impact shifts the effective strike, (ii) the nonlinear dependence of the option price on the number of contracts, (iii) how execution costs smooth terminal holdings, (iv) the extent to which the hedger's own trading can bring an otherwise worthless option into the money, and (v) how the spread and the shape of the limit order book in the options market arise from the price impact and the shape of the limit order book of the underlying. In particular, calibrating the one-period binomial model to trade and quote data on near-expiry SPY call options, we find that our model explains 85\% of the observed option bid-ask spread for near-the-money options.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support Kähler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.title: The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex
papers.abstract: A polyhex is a connected set of n cells of the regular hexagonal tiling, joined edge to edge, where each cell has area one. Kurz conjectured an upper bound for the area of the convex hull of a polyhex, after the corresponding problem for squares was solved. We prove that the convex hull of a polyhex with n cells has area at most one sixth of the ceiling of $n^2+14n/3$, and that for every n this value is attained by a path made of three straight runs of nearly equal length. This proves the conjecture of Kurz and improves his bound by 1/6 when n is divisible by 3. The proof bounds the hull of the cell centres and three of its widths with a spanning tree of the polyhex. The upper bound is formalised in the Lean 4 proof assistant with the Mathlib library. We also show that for every n the extremal polyhex is unique up to rotation, reflection and translation, which an exhaustive search had confirmed for at most 12 cells. The proof of uniqueness was generated by Claude at the request of Sascha Kurz, and it is also formalised in Lean.

papers.title: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

papers.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
papers.abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $μ_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $μ_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete Birkhoff series through order $14$ and World Cup series through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$14$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.

papers.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
papers.abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schrödinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.

papers.title: Equilibrium Numbers in Non-Square Bimatrix Games
papers.abstract: Bimatrix games may have an exponential number of mixed Nash equilibria if both dimensions of the game are allowed to grow. Bounds on their maximal number give structural insights that have been used to construct hard-to-solve games. We show new sharp or asymptotically sharp bounds on the (polynomial) number of equilibria for generic games where one dimension of the game is fixed and the number of strategies of the other player grows. These results go beyond the hitherto studied square games. Our methods employ combinatorial properties of polytopes, and recent obstructions that relate to the graph of those polytopes. For $n\ge5$, we construct $3\times n$ games that have all $2n+1$ vertices of the best-response polytope as equilibrium strategies, proved using a simple case of the 4-color theorem for planar graphs. Generic $4\times 5$ games are shown to have at most 17 equilibria, using computer calculations with existing datasets for all combinatorial types of the relevant polytopes. For $d\times n$ games, we construct games where all but a fraction of $O(1/n)$ of the maximum number of vertices are equilibrium strategies.

papers.title: Bulk-edge sticking beyond the Perron mode in Gaussian softmax attention
papers.abstract: We study row-softmax self-attention with independent Gaussian query and key weights in the proportional regime, at fixed inverse temperature. Hayase, Collins, and Karakida proved Gaussian equivalence for the empirical squared singular-value distribution after removal of the Perron direction. A global law alone does not exclude finitely many nonleading outliers. We prove that no such outliers persist: the rescaled squared singular value $\ell s_k(A)^2$ converges in probability to the upper edge of their bulk law for every fixed $k\ge 2$. In fact, this convergence is uniform over any deterministic sublinear number of leading non-Perron indices. The proof uses an exact decomposition of the softmax normalization, conditions on the key matrix, identifies the conditional covariance exactly with a diagonally conjugated inner-product kernel, linearizes that kernel in operator norm, and applies the outside-support local law of Fan, Ma, Paquette, and Wang. A separate stability argument identifies the finite conditional deformed Marchenko-Pastur edge with the limiting bulk edge. We also derive a scalar formula for that edge throughout the proportional regime and recover the explicit square-model formula of Hayase, Collins, and Karakida, including its physical branch.

papers.title: Positive normalized solutions for a singular regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study a singular Dirichlet problem driven by a regularized $p(x)$-Laplacian under a prescribed modular constraint. We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.

papers.title: Affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures
papers.abstract: In 2025, the affine dual curvature measures $\widetilde{C}_m^a(K,\cdot)$ of convex body $K$ were introduced by Cai, Leng, Wu, and Xi, and the even Minkowski problem for the affine dual curvature measures was solved. In this paper, the necessary and sufficient condition of affine dual Minkowski problem for general measures with $m>1$ are proposed.

papers.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{ö}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $κ-1$, with $κ$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
papers.abstract: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.title: The density of long runs of non-$r$-free integers
papers.abstract: Fix $r\ge2$ and let $D_k$ be the natural density of the $n$ such that none of $n+1,\dots,n+k$ is $r$-free. We prove that $\log(1/D_k)=\frac{r-1}{ζ(r)}k\log k+\frac{r}{ζ(r)}k\log\log k-C_rk+o(k)$, where $C_r=\frac{1}{ζ(r)}((r-1)\logζ(r)+r-1+r\log\fracπ{r\sin(π/r)})$; for $r=2$ this is $C_2=\frac{6}{π^2}(1+\log\frac{π^4}{24})=1.4595513\dots$. This determines Mirsky's constant $α(h)$, the density of the $n$ with $s_{n+1}-s_n=h$ in the squarefree numbers, to the same precision. Previously the only known estimate was $\logα(h)\le-\frac54 h\log\log h+O(h)$; ours improves this by a factor of order $\log h/\log\log h$, and is two-sided. The upper bound rests on the observation that the primes $p\le z$ with $\prod_{p\le z}p^r\le\sqrt k$ sieve a window of length $k$ with no freedom of alignment, so that at least $(1/ζ(r)+o(1))k$ positions must be covered by $r$-th powers of distinct primes exceeding $k^{1/r}$. The resulting sum over injections is $m!e_m$ with $m\sim k/ζ(r)$, evaluated by a saddle point. For the lower bound the Chung-Erdos inequality recovers the full contribution of $m!e_m$ rather than merely its largest term, which is what makes the linear coefficient explicit. As a consequence the first-moment threshold for gaps between $r$-free numbers is $\frac{ζ(r)}{r-1}\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}(1-\frac{(1+o(1))\log\log\log x}{(r-1)\log\log x})$; for $r=2$ the constant is $π^2/6$, that of Erdos's 1951 lower bound. We also prove that every covering system of length $k$ has modulus at least $\exp((\frac{r}{ζ(r)}+o(1))k\log k)$, so the Chinese remainder construction yields only $ζ(r)/r$, half of $π^2/6$ when $r=2$. Erdos's bound is thus equivalent to the assertion that the first run of $k$ consecutive non-$r$-free integers occurs at the first-moment threshold, not at the scale set by the minimal modulus of a covering system.

papers.title: A remark on polycyclic groups of birational automorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an algebraic variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of zero characteristic. Suppose that $G$ is a virtually polycyclic subgroup in the group $\mathrm{Bir}(X)$ of birational automorphisms of $X$. We show that the virtual derived length of $G$ does not exceed $2d$. Moreover, if $X$ is a surface, the bound can be improved to $3$, and this value is optimal.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.title: On the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in spaces generated by Rademacher functions and their $p$-adic analogues
papers.abstract: Sufficient conditions for the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in the space spanned by generalized Rademacher functions are proved. It is shown that the sufficient number of nodes for discretization with the minimal number of nodes is equal to $N$ or $N+1$ and depends on the dimension $N$. The conjecture of F.~Dai, A.~Prymak, V.~N.~Temlyakov, and S.~Yu.~Tikhonov on the positivity of weights in the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm with a minimal number of points considered. It was investigated in which cases it holds and in which it fails for the spaces spanned by the $N$ generalized Rademacher functions with base $p$, and how the validity of the conjecture in this case depends on the parameters $p$ and $N$. The connection with generalized Hadamard matrices, the Hadamard's conjecture and Seberry's conjecture is demonstrated.

papers.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.title: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

papers.title: Integrals of some compound processes
papers.abstract: By means of the theory of compound (non-homogeneous) Poisson processes we define a general framework which includes most of the generalizations of the Poisson processes, both in the Skellam sense and in the space-fractional sense. We prove that Bernstein subordination is the only time change that leads to a compound Poisson process. We also consider the case of subordination with inverse Bernstein subordinators. Then, we focus on the integrals of compound processes. We give an explicit representation of the fractional integral of a compound Poisson process, showing that for fixed $t$ it is distributed as a compound Poisson random variable. We then extend this result to more general integral forms. Furthermore, we obtain some limit results, explicit forms of the iterated integrals and their governing equation. Finally, we study the integral of compound renewal processes in the Fourier-Laplace domain.

papers.title: Reference-free logged energy-oracle recovery for neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems: conforming Riesz reconstruction and archive-level selection
papers.abstract: Neural PDE training yields a finite checkpoint archive, yet its logged energy errors are inaccessible without the exact solution, while loss-based selection does not necessarily recover the logged energy oracle. For admissible neural approximations of symmetric coercive variational problems, we introduce a reference-free selection rule based on minimizing a computable conforming Riesz monitor. The exact residual-energy identity and conforming projection make the monitor an unconditional lower bound converging monotonically to each logged energy error under nested conforming refinement; under saturation, hierarchical enrichment yields a computable upper estimate and hence a lower-upper bracket. A key finding is that archive selection is order-sensitive: unresolved checkpoint-dependent components can reverse the oracle-non-oracle ranking at finite resolution, so checkpointwise recovery alone is insufficient. For finite archives, we prove uniform recovery, yielding convergence to the logged-oracle error and, without saturation, logged-oracle selection at sufficiently fine auxiliary resolution. Under saturation, the bracket gives a computable near-oracle bound and certifies unique logged-oracle selection upon interval separation. We also bound logging-resolution loss and certify oracle inclusion over prescribed comparison trajectories. Experiments on diffusion and elasticity, including a non-manufactured perforated plate, demonstrate energy-scale calibration, oracle-level selection, and modest post-processing cost. This work frames neural checkpoint selection as an ordering problem, establishes projection-based reliability guarantees beyond checkpointwise error estimation and loss-error equivalence, and opens directions for variational loss design and more general selection theory.

papers.title: Bayesian Distilled Clustering for High-Dimensional Mixture Models
papers.abstract: Latent subgroup analysis is central to fields such as genomics, precision medicine, and social science, where the goal is to identify heterogeneous populations with distinct covariate structures or response behaviors. Mixture models provide a natural probabilistic framework for this task, representing the data-generating distribution as a weighted combination of subgroup-specific laws with unobserved labels. In high-dimensional regimes, these analyses face significant challenges. Often, only a small subset of covariates drives meaningful subgroup separation; the remaining variables may introduce noise or redundancy. Standard clustering methods typically treat all dimensions as equal, but in high-dimensional spaces, irrelevant coordinates can distort distances and obscure the low-dimensional structures defining latent classes. This paper introduces a Bayesian distilled clustering framework for high-dimensional mixture models. We propose that clustering should occur within a statistically justified subspace rather than the full ambient space. Our method utilizes a Bayesian variable selection model to estimate posterior inclusion probabilities, quantifying the evidence that each covariate contributes to subgroup separation or response behavior. A "distilled" covariate set is then identified by controlling the expected false-discovery proportion. Clustering is performed on this reduced subspace, followed by conditional independence diagnostics to examine subgroup-specific dependencies among selected variables. Critically, this framework is model-based: the distillation step is tied directly to the mixture structure and response model rather than a generic dimension-reduction criterion. This ensures the resulting subspace remains aligned with the scientific objective: identifying latent subgroups that differ in both distributional structure and behavior.

papers.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
papers.abstract: Different optimization algorithms can find very different solutions to the same problem. Gradient descent (GD) exhibits a low-rank bias in overparameterized problems when initialized near zero, while Adam does not. GD is rotationally equivariant: rotating both factors of a factored model $W = UV^\top$ by an orthogonal matrix leaves the loss unchanged, and GD's solution rotates accordingly. In contrast, Adam is not. We show that any algorithm using only the current gradient and respecting rotational symmetry amounts to a left-preconditioner depending only on the gradient's Gram matrix. This gives a norm-based test, which passes for the spectral norm in Muon and fails for Adam's $\ell_\infty$ norm. Empirically, nine optimizers fall into groups consistent with the test on underdetermined matrix sensing. Sharing Adam's second moment across coordinates gradually recovers a low-rank bias, and its solutions approach GD's as the stepsize decreases. On four hyperspectral scenes, Adam's solutions are hundreds to thousands of times further from GD's than two GD runs with different step sizes are from each other. In transformers and LoRA adapters, Adam separates two rotationally equivalent models from the first iteration, and learns higher-rank attention updates. Overall, recovering particular solutions depends on the optimizer's invisible coordinate basis, as well as how fast it grows small singular values relative to large ones.

papers.title: A note on some upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator
papers.abstract: For two square complex matrices $A,B,$ and a real number $q$, the $q$-deformed commutator of $A$ and $B$ is defined as $AB-qBA$. We give some upper bounds on the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator in the case $q\ge0$. All of the inequalities derived in this paper generalize the Böttcher-Wenzel inequality.

papers.title: Proper-Score Observation-Driven Filters: Tracking Efficiency, Estimation, and Continuous-Time Limits
papers.abstract: Observation-driven filters usually update a time-varying parameter with the score of the predictive log density. Replacing the logarithmic score by another proper scoring rule changes both the target the filter tracks and the precision with which it tracks it. These filters form a subclass of the PRADA models of de Punder (2026), and we study their properties at the level of the filtered path. In an in-fill framework, the local tracking error is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process. Optimised over the gain, its invariant variance is the geometric mean of the target's volatility and an effective observation noise determined by the scoring rule. Tracking efficiency is the squared correlation between the scoring-rule driver and the true score at the rule's own target. In scale models it equals the asymptotic relative efficiency of the corresponding static minimum-score estimator. The resulting frontier quantifies the robustness--efficiency trade-off. Under Gaussian innovations, density-power and CRPS volatility filters raise minimal tracking risk by 3% and 11%. Under Student-$t_5$ innovations, the Gaussian log-score filter raises it by 58% in the limit, and by more at daily frequency. We also give primitive conditions for bounded scale-invariant drivers, a matrix version, a population self-tuning result for the gain, minimum-score estimation theory whose invertibility conditions hold at the fitted values, and diffusion limits. An international equity application separates the roles of the predictive density and the scoring rule.

papers.title: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
papers.abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_β$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $β>0$.

papers.title: Nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras, defined as reduced crossed product C*-algebras associated with free odometer actions of nonamenable countable discrete residually finite groups on a Cantor space. These are nonnuclear counterparts to the generalised Bunce-Deddens algebras introduced by Orfanos. For large classes of groups, we show that they share many regularity properties, including real rank zero, stable rank one, strict comparison of positive elements, and admitting a unique tracial state. In many cases, we deduce that they are even selfless and hence pure. Finally, we compute the ordered K-theory and trace pairing of Bunce-Deddens algebras over nonabelian free groups.

papers.title: Smart predict-then-robustly-optimize
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose and study a robust variant of the smart predict-then-optimize approach that accounts for prediction shifts due to disturbance in the covariate feature space. While traditional integrated-learning-and-optimization models assume that side information is perfectly revealed, empirical data-driven features are frequently corrupted or noisy at the time of decision-making, leading to fragile operational policies. To bridge this gap, we integrate principles of robust optimization directly into the predictive-prescriptive pipeline via a smart predict-then-robustly optimize loss and establish a computationally tractable convex surrogate, designed to hedge against worst-case feature perturbations. On the theoretical front, we formalize the structural validity of this surrogate by proving its approximation error probability decays exponentially according to a sub-Gaussian concentration profile. Furthermore, we establish that under mild assumptions, the surrogate is Fisher consistent with high probability. We also prove necessary conditions under which our framework outperforms standard smart predict-then-optimize and maintain its superiority even when the standard method is equipped with regularized upstream predictions. Numerical experiments validate that our robust framework consistently yields significant performance improvements over standard methods, both in out-of-sample terms and in training stability.

papers.title: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
papers.abstract: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Grebík and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(λ)$ tends to zero as the intensity $λ$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(λ)$ tends to one as $λ$ tends to zero, and $p_u(λ)>1/2$ for all $λ>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(λ)\leq 1/2$ for all $λ>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{λ>0}p_u(λ)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Grebík and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $λ\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.

papers.title: Nilpotent quiver varieties with multiplicities and symmetrisable crystals
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Nakajima's nilpotent quiver varieties for quivers with multiplicities, by developing new stability conditions for framed nilpotent quiver representations with multiplicities and exploiting their interplay with Hecke correspondences. Using these new quiver varieties, we extend Saito's geometric construction of Kashiwara crystals of irreducible highest-weight representations of Kac--Moody algebras from the symmetric to the symmetrisable case.

papers.title: Singular limit for nonlocal conservation laws with non-locality in density and velocity
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a generalized nonlocal conservation law intro- duced in [18]. The nonlocal equation incorporates non-locality both in density and velocity. We derive entropy solutions of the underlying Burgers equation as a singular limit. The main ingredient of the proof is a nonlocal Oleinik type estimate, extending the method of [7]. The nonlocal Oleinik estimate provides uniform bounds on the total variation, thereby enabling to pass to the limit in the regularization parameter.

papers.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Lattès family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.

papers.title: A structured quasi-Newton augmented Lagrangian algorithm for nonlinear least squares with linear and nonlinear constraints
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for solving nonlinear least-squares problems subject to a mix of nonlinear constraints, linear equalities, and bounds. The nonlinear constraints are handled through an augmented Lagrangian reformulation of the objective, while the linear constraints are kept explicit. Each outer iteration therefore requires the approximate minimization of the augmented Lagrangian over a polyhedron, which we carry out with a gradient projection technique combined with a trust-region step computation. To capture the second-order information specific to the least-squares structure, we approximate the Hessian of the augmented Lagrangian by a Gauss--Newton term corrected by a structured quasi-Newton update, activated by a hybrid switching rule. The correction is built from a secant equation that we derive for the augmented Lagrangian itself. The outer iteration follows the augmented Lagrangian framework of Conn, Gould, Sartenaer and Toint for linearly constrained subproblems, for which we provide an explicit inner solver: a trust-region method whose Cauchy point is computed along nested faces of the polyhedron, without any projection onto it, and safeguarded by classical active-set devices, namely the release of bounds based on least-squares multiplier estimates and $\varepsilon$-active bounds. We prove that this inner solver satisfies the stopping rule required by the outer analysis, which yields global convergence of the overall method to a first-order critical point, and report numerical experiments. Our method outperforms an augmented Lagrangian solver built on the same outer update rules but without least-squares structure, and is competitive in computation time with a state-of-the-art solver for nonlinear programming.

papers.title: Fixed-parameter tractable computation of Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomials via tensor networks
papers.abstract: We give a thorough analysis of the time complexity of computing Reshetikhin--Tuareg knot polynomials via tensor contractions on the associated tensor networks, showing that the computation is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to a parameter at most linear in the tree-width of the input knot diagram. In particular, this gives a simpler proof to the sub-exponential bound $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$ for the time complexity of computing any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial. We present along with this paper, in SnapPy, the first general-purpose implementation of this algorithm, which computes any Reshetikhin--Turaev knot polynomial given its $R$-matrix and ribbon element. We stress the remarkable efficiency of our implementation by demonstrating that: (1) our implementation is several orders of magnitude faster than existing packages on computing the colored Jones polynomial; (2) our implementation is able to compute the Jones polynomial of (i) census knots with large width and over 200 crossings and (ii) some generic random knots with over 2000 crossings, in several hours using less than 10GB RAM, whereas Regina is not able to compute the Jones polynomial of these knots within a memory constraint of 160GB.

papers.title: The number of composite class sizes in finite groups
papers.abstract: We consider finite groups with at least three conjugacy class sizes that are composite numbers and we prove that, in that situation, the number of prime class sizes is bounded by the number of composite class sizes. The analogous result for (non-)prime-power class sizes is also addressed.

papers.title: Involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction
papers.abstract: We determine all involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction that extend the involution of the original $*$-algebra. We also find all algebra isomorphisms between the resulting Cayley doubles that extend the identity automorphism of the original $*$-algebra, and consequently classify the resulting $*$-algebras up to such $*$-algebra isomorphisms. As applications, we show that Cayley doubles of algebras without zero divisors admit exactly one additional extension of the original involution in the 2-torsion-free case and none otherwise, prove that the classical Cayley-Dickson involution is the unique scalar involution, and obtain a classification of the $*$-algebras arising from $\mathbb{R}$ up to dimension 4.

papers.title: LLM-ACES: Closed-Loop Discovery of Dynamical Systems with LLM-Guided Adaptive Search
papers.abstract: Recovering governing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from data is a central challenge in modeling dynamical systems across scientific domains. Existing approaches cast discovery as a static inference problem over fixed datasets, assuming that the observed trajectories are sufficiently informative. However, dynamical systems evolve over large state spaces, and limited data can make multiple equations observationally indistinguishable, leading to identifiability gaps and the recovery of incorrect governing equations. To address this, we introduce LLM-ACES, or LLM-guided Active Closed-loop Equation Search, a closed-loop framework that jointly optimizes symbolic hypothesis construction and adaptive data acquisition. In LLM-ACES, a large language model (LLM) proposes operator priors that define constrained subspaces of the symbolic search space, within which candidate equations are fit to the observed data. The disagreement among these candidates guides the acquisition of informative trajectories, creating a feedback loop that iteratively refines both the hypothesis space and the discovered dynamics.
