On 122 ODE systems spanning ODEBench and ODEBase, LLM-ACES achieves the lowest median NMSE, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while reaching the highest symbolic accuracy up to 70.8% on ODEBench and 69.5% on ODEBase across different LLM backbones. Our analysis further shows that LLM-ACES is sample-efficient, achieving better performance with less data. Under observation noise and sparse sampling, LLM-ACES keeps the lowest reconstruction error without inflating expression complexity, whereas baselines tend to add spurious terms that fit the data locally but obscure the governing relationships. Code: https://github.com/scientific-discovery/LLM-ACES

papers.title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.

papers.title: Birational Algebraic Topology
papers.abstract: Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_Σ(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $π_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero. Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $π_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.

papers.title: On $H=W$ in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove ``$H=W$" in the context of a Banach function space $X(Ω)$. Let $Ω$ be a subset of ${\mathbb R}^n$ and denote by $W^1_X(Ω)$ the collection of all those $f\in X(Ω)$ whose distributional derivatives $\partial_jf$ are contained in $X(Ω)$. Our main result provides a small collection of ``universal" hypotheses on $X(Ω)$ that ensure $W^1_X(Ω)$ is equal to $H^1_X(Ω)$, the formal closure of ${Lip}(Ω)\cap W^1_X(Ω)$ with respect to the norm \[\|f\|_{W^1_X(Ω)} = \|f\|_{X(Ω)} + \|\nabla f\|_{X(Ω)}.\] The main theorem has two corollaries. The first gives a slightly stronger set of hypotheses for ``$H=W$", and the second gives density of $C^\infty_c({\mathbb R}^n)$ in $W^1_X({\mathbb R}^n)$.

papers.title: Simplicity of q-Gaussian C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We show that q-Gaussian $C^*$-algebras for $q \in (-1, 1)$ have the Dixmier averaging property, and hence are simple with a unique trace. We argue by combining rapid decay and spectral gap estimates for the commutators with the generators, which are obtained from free probability.

papers.title: Geometry of Holomorphic One-forms on Smooth Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $f\colon X\to A$ be a morphism from a smooth projective variety to an abelian variety. We show that if an irreducible component of the exceptional set of a birational map from $X$ to its good minimal model has general type image in $A$, then every 1-form pulled back from $A$ has a zero. For the Albanese map, this yields a sharp dimension bound for spaces of nowhere vanishing holomorphic 1-forms, which refines the Popa-Schnell inequality. Furthermore, we investigate the structure of the spaces of holomorphic 1-forms with zeros, and show that they are linear for large classes of varieties. Also, we construct a delicate example of a smooth projective subvariety of an abelian variety for which the holomorphic 1-forms with positive-dimensional zero loci do not form a linear subset. Finally, we study algebraic surfaces admitting holomorphic 1-forms that have zeros and do not arise from cohomology jump loci.

papers.title: $\boldsymbol{2}$-Neighbor Bootstrap Percolation on Odd Graphs
papers.abstract: The $r$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on a graph $G$ is a vertex-activation process that begins with a set of initially active vertices. In each subsequent round, every inactive vertex having at least $r$ active neighbors becomes active. Denote by $m(G,r)$ the minimum number of initially active vertices required for the activation process to spread to all remaining vertices of $G$. In this article, we consider the odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{O}_k\) and the bipartite odd graph \(\mathbbmsl{B}_k\), and prove that $m(\mathbbmsl{O}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+3k+2)/4\rceil$ and $m(\mathbbmsl{B}_k, 2)=\lceil(k^2+2k+3)/2\rceil$. The first formula confirms the quadratic-growth conjecture proposed in 2021 by Grippo, Pastine, Torres, Valencia-Pabon, and Vera.

papers.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
papers.abstract: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.

papers.title: A high-order IMEX-DG solver for atmospheric dynamics: rotating tests on non-conforming meshes
papers.abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly and advective terms explicitly. The solver is built on the deal.II finite element library, combining matrix-free operator evaluation, adaptive non-conforming mesh capabilities, and distributed-memory parallelism. The inclusion of rotation extends the framework to large-scale atmospheric dynamics, where the Coriolis force plays a central role in geostrophic balance. Its incorporation into a high-order matrix-free DG discretisation is, however, non-trivial, as it requires a careful formulation of the discrete rotational operator. Two alternative treatments of the rotational and gravitational source terms within the solution strategy, based on nonlinear fixed-point iterations, are therefore introduced and compared in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. A discrete analysis of the rotational operator is also carried out in order to derive a formulation suitable for efficient matrix-free implementation. The proposed formulation is verified through convergence studies on rotating inertia-gravity wave benchmarks and further assessed in fully three-dimensional simulations of stratified flow over orography on both uniform and adaptive meshes. The numerical results show that the rotating IMEX-DG framework has the expected accuracy and stability properties while correctly capturing the asymmetry and wave structures induced by rotation in large-scale atmospheric flows.

papers.title: Axioms for validity: from tests, e-values and p-values to decisions
papers.abstract: The emerging literature on hypothesis testing with data-dependent significance levels relies on a particular extension of the Type-I error. Existing arguments for this extension are heuristic. We show it is uniquely characterized by three axioms: law-invariance, agreement with classical testing on constant levels, and the preservation of (in)validity under independent selection of the level. We find that three analogous axioms characterize the e-value as a multi-decision generalization of a test. We also characterize the p-value, reducing the p-vs-e debate to a simple property: should independent selection among evidence variables that are invalid under the same null distribution be able to produce a valid evidence variable? Our main technical contribution is to show how e-values emerge in every decision problem with a notion of validity that satisfies law invariance, the independent selection axiom, and an axiom stating that a procedure that selects an invalid procedure with arbitrarily high probability must itself be invalid. We also extend recent results using e-values to support decision making to arbitrary evidence variables. In an application, we justify expectation-based error rates in multiple testing and recover the 'e-closure principle'.

papers.title: Pseudo-Likelihood Regression for the Marginal Rate of Recurrent Events with a Competing Terminal Event
papers.abstract: Regression modeling of recurrent and terminal events continues to present methodological challenges in survival analysis. Existing approaches either make unverifiable assumptions about the dependence between the two event types, rely on a proportional mean rate assumption, or use ad hoc estimating equations. We propose a semiparametric regression model based on a novel weighted pseudo-likelihood function that directly targets the marginal rate of the recurrent event and extends the Ghosh--Lin model to a large class of transformation models. Our framework accommodates external time-dependent covariate effects on the marginal rate and enables flexible prediction of the marginal mean. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators and propose a robust sandwich estimator for the variance. In simulation studies, we demonstrate a strong performance of the proposed estimator under independent right-censoring. We apply the method to data from the interim analysis of a randomized clinical trial on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease to predict the expected number of severe exacerbations, and illustrate how the choice of regression model affects the estimated covariate effects and predictions.

papers.title: Deformed seminorms, anisotropic sectors and Phragmén Lindelöf principles for $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$\allowbreak difference operators
papers.abstract: We study the deformed derivative of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba on spaces of holomorphic functions, with the induced geometry and growth principles. The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $ρ$ into those on the disc of radius $ρ/β$, $β$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/φ_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carathéodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fréchet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragmén Lindelöf and Lindelöf principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $θ\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.

papers.title: Conformal tubular parameterization and toroidal bending of tube-like surfaces
papers.abstract: Tube-like surfaces are widely encountered in geometry processing, engineering structures, and medical anatomy, yet their intrinsic longitudinal and circumferential information is not well preserved by conventional planar annular or rectangular parameterization domains. In this work, we propose a new conformal parameterization framework for open tube-like surfaces with two boundary components. The proposed method first constructs a fixed-boundary tubular parameterization by cutting the input mesh, computing a disk-to-parallelogram quasi-conformal map, and lifting the result to a cylindrical surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. To reduce residual distortion introduced near the cut seam, we further introduce a localized quasi-conformal correction scheme formulated on an annular domain, which improves conformality while leaving regions away from the seam unchanged. To handle noisy or irregular input boundaries, we also develop a free-boundary variant based on boundary extension and cycle-Laplacian smoothing, allowing the prescribed boundary constraints to be imposed on artificial outer rings rather than directly on the original surface. Finally, as an optional post-processing step, we derive two conformal toroidal bending maps that embed the tubular parameterization into toroidal geometries without altering its conformal structure. Experiments on synthetic tube meshes and real vascular surfaces demonstrate that the proposed framework produces low-distortion parameterizations, effectively mitigates seam-induced artifacts, improves robustness for boundary-noisy inputs, and provides flexible tubular and toroidal target domains for downstream surface processing tasks.

papers.title: A tree-like fractal Dirichlet space lying between strong and weak elliptic Harnack inequalities
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a self-similar fractal configured as an infinitely branched tree and equip it with a regular self-similar Dirichlet form. Fixing a typical metric ball, we compute accurately the effective resistance between an inner point and the boundary of this ball. Based on this result, anomalous behaviour of the mean exit time from such balls is shown -- the ratio between whose supremum and infimum can be arbitrarily large. Under properly selected self-similar measure, we further show the weak elliptic Harnack inequality holds but the strong analogue fails.

papers.title: On Maximal Prime Gaps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that the gap between a prime number $p_n$ and its consecutive prime $p_{n+1}$ is on the order of $\log^2{p_n}$; consequently, we show the existence of a prime in certain types of intervals.

papers.title: Characterization of stability radii for robustly asymptotically stable dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems
papers.abstract: We study linear time-invariant dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic systems. We characterize when the systems are robustly asymptotically stable and derive exact conditions and bounds when this property is lost under structure-preserving perturbations.

papers.title: On the global convergence of gradient flow for wide shallow models beyond homogeneous nonlinearities
papers.abstract: A surprising phenomenon in the training of neural networks is the ability of gradient descent to find global minimizers of the training loss despite its non-convexity. Following earlier work, we investigate this behavior for wide shallow models. Existing global convergence results primarily concern models with positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities, such as ReLU activations, and models with scalar output weights and bounded nonlinearities, such as sigmoid activations. We study a broader class of models, including multi-head attention layers and two-layer fully connected networks with bounded or asymptotically positively one-homogeneous activations and vector output weights. Building upon (Chizat and Bach, 2018), we prove that, in the limit of infinitely many hidden neurons or attention heads, non-minimizers of the training loss are unstable under the mean-field gradient flow dynamics by constructing "escape regions" in the parameter space. Our global convergence statements are conditional in the following sense: if the mean-field gradient flow converges for the Wasserstein 2-distance, then its limit must be a global minimizer. We revisit the bounded nonlinearity, scalar-output setting of (Chizat and Bach, 2018), giving an escape region construction adapted to unbounded nonlinear parameter domains. We also propose new constructions for nonlinearities with at most linear growth under a non-degeneracy assumption and for asymptotically positively one-homogeneous nonlinearities. Finally, we show the well-posedness and stability estimates for the mean-field training dynamics under sub-Gaussian initializations.

papers.title: Structural and Lagrangian properties of analogue ensembles to characterize multifractality of stochastic processes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for the scale-invariance characterization of stochastic processes in reconstructed finite-dimensional spaces. This framework analyses the structural and dynamical properties of the reconstructed space and is based on a Takens embedding reconstruction followed by the definition of ensembles of analogue states. First, we specify a collection of target states densely sampling the full embedding space. For each target state, we search for the ensemble of its k-nearest neighbors, its k-best analogues, and we analyze its volume and dynamics. On the one hand, we study the probability distribution of the volumes and relate its mean and variance to the scale-invariance properties of the stochastic process. On the second hand, we study the Lagrangian properties of the analogues by characterizing how they disperse in time. More particularly, we study the volume occupied by the analogue's successors in function of time and of their initial volume. The main contribution of this paper is to highlight the link between these dynamical properties and the scale-invariance features of the process. We analyze two types of stationary and dissipative 1-dimensional scale-invariant processes: regularized fractional Brownian motion and regularized multifractal random walk. For both processes, the structure and dynamics of the embedding space are determined by their scale-invariant properties.

papers.title: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
papers.abstract: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for the $τ$-Quantile of Heterogeneous Individual-Specific Coefficient
papers.abstract: We study quantiles of heterogeneous coefficients across the $n$ observed units of a panel. Treating the coefficients as deterministic, we estimate each from $T$ observations, then use the estimates and their standard errors to construct a smoothed quantile estimator and estimate its variance. When $T^{1/2}\ll n\ll T^{3/2}$, the estimator is asymptotically normal around a deterministic center. A feasible bias correction relaxes the sample growth restriction to $n/T^{3/2}\to c\in[0,\infty)$, accommodating panels with large $n$. Normal inference extends to the target quantile when the difference between the deterministic center and the target is negligible relative to the standard error. Without this restriction, we establish an impossibility result that the distribution of the studentized error relative to the target cannot be estimated uniformly consistently. For practical inference in this case, we construct a conservative interval whose coverage tends uniformly to one and whose length attains the optimal worst-case rate in probability. We give primitive conditions for smooth GMM. Mortgage data show widespread but uneven declines in delinquency across credit scores.

papers.title: The coordinate ring of the universal centralizer via Demazure operators
papers.abstract: We give a simple description of the coordinate ring of the universal centralizer associated to a simply connected semisimple group. To this end, we prove a general result on Weil restriction of affine schemes $X$ over the Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$ equipped with a compatible action of the Weyl group $W$. Specifically, we show that the coordinate ring of the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ of $W$-fixed points of Weil restriction of $X$ to the categorical quotient $\mathfrak{t}//W$ can be obtained from the coordinate ring of $X$ by applying Demazure operators if and only if the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ is integral.

papers.title: Well-Conditioned Oblivious Perturbations in Linear Space
papers.abstract: Perturbing a deterministic $n$-dimensional matrix with small Gaussian noise is a cornerstone of smoothed analysis of algorithms [Spielman and Teng, JACM 2004], as it reduces the condition number of the input to $O(n)$, and with it the complexity of many matrix algorithms. However, when deployed algorithmically, these perturbations are expensive due to the cost of generating and storing $n^2$ Gaussian random variables. We propose a perturbation that requires generating and storing $O(n)$ random numbers in $O(\log n)$ bits of precision, and reduces the condition number of any deterministic matrix to $O(n)$, matching Gaussian perturbations. Our result takes a step towards derandomizing matrix perturbations in numerical linear algebra, and in particular, implies that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system to within $\varepsilon$ backward error in $O(n^2\log(n)/\varepsilon)$ time using only $O(n\log n)$ random bits. In our construction, we introduce the concept of a pattern matrix, which is a dense deterministic matrix that maps all sparse vectors into dense vectors in a way that goes beyond the classical uncertainty principle of the Fourier transform. We combine this with a sparse perturbation whose entries are dependent and located in a non-uniform fashion. In order to analyze this construction, we develop new techniques for lower bounding the smallest singular value of a random matrix with dependent entries.

papers.title: The Pentagon Graph Operator
papers.abstract: The pentagon graph $C_5(G)$ of a finite simple graph $G$ is the edge-intersection graph of its induced cycles of length five. We prove that the dodecahedral graph is mapped to the icosahedral graph $I$, which is a fixed point of the operator. Our principal result classifies every graph obtained by adjoining one vertex to $I$: it is eventually fixed if the added vertex belongs to no induced pentagon, and it is expanding otherwise. The proof shows that every new pentagon gives rise to a tadpole hat within at most two iterations. More generally, an induced icosahedral core with $h$ tadpole hats gives the lower bound $12+h2^k$ on the orders of the iterates. We also establish a replication principle and construct two vertex-disjoint induced copies of the Shrikhande graph in its pentagon graph, yielding the bound $16\cdot2^k$. The general vanishing--periodic--expanding trichotomy is included as background.

papers.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Time-Invariant Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Learning Cut Distributions with Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: The probabilistic nature of quantum computation can be an asset rather than an obstacle for combinatorial optimization. In this work, we tackle the problem in which the sampled distribution itself is the object being optimized. This perspective is especially natural for fairness, coverage, and robustness objectives, where success is determined by the least-protected components rather than by average or best performance. We develop this idea by learning graph cut distributions. The resulting framework turns Fair Cut Cover into a native quantum distribution-learning problem and uses quantum circuits as trainable generators of cut distributions. We prove that standard QAOA at depth one achieves higher Fair Cut Cover values than optimal Semidefinite programming plus Gaussian hyperplane rounding on complete graphs with at least four vertices. We further establish a separation on a family of high-girth graphs using published QAOA evaluations, compare against a classical column-generation heuristic in numerical experiments, and examine finite-sampling and noise effects in quantum hardware implementations. These results suggest a broader role for this type of quantum algorithms: not merely finding good bitstrings, but learning useful combinatorial distributions for worst- and average-case-aware optimization.

papers.title: Rare Event Analysis via Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Rare events, from biomolecular conformational changes and phase transitions to chemical reactions, are central to many physical systems, yet extremely difficult to study computationally because unbiased simulations seldom produce them. Transition Path Theory provides a rigorous statistical framework for analyzing such events: it characterizes the ensemble of reactive trajectories between two metastable states (reactant and product), and its central object, the committor function (the probability that the system next reaches the product rather than the reactant), encodes essential kinetic and thermodynamic information. We introduce a framework for committor estimation that builds on stochastic optimal control, with a principled formulation that grounds committor learning on capped hitting-time trajectories. In this framework the committor defines a feedback control, proportional to the gradient of its logarithm, that steers trajectories toward the reactive region, enabling sampling of reactive paths. As practical algorithms, we develop two training losses: a heuristic on-policy direct backpropagation loss and a principled off-policy Value Matching loss, for which we establish first-order optimality guarantees. Being off-policy, Value Matching can leverage simulated trajectories from alternative sampling processes and reuse them from a replay buffer, which enables efficient learning. In particular, we derive a reactive current-preserving sampling process that can accelerate exploration. On reversible and non-reversible dynamics, the framework yields more accurate committor estimates, reaction rates, and transition path samples than existing methods.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
papers.abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((Θ,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(μ)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(θ)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.

papers.title: On the Chevalley-Bass number of a field
papers.abstract: We give upper and lower bounds on the Chevalley-Bass number of a field of characteristic zero, whenever this quantity is well-defined. We also describe an algorithm which computes the Chevalley-Bass number of a field, provided its maximal abelian subextension is known. As a primary application, we improve the value of a constant related to exponential Diophantine equations.

papers.title: One-sided certification of surrogate near-minimizers: exact worst-case envelopes under strong convexity and smoothness
papers.abstract: We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $μ$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.

papers.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-Stäckel problem in the non-diagonal case
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--Stäckel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.

papers.title: The Integral Chow Ring of Smooth Non-strict Toric Stacks
papers.abstract: We extend the Stanley--Reisner ring to the non-strict stacky fans introduced by Geraschenko and Satriano. We then prove that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the associated toric stack when the underlying fan is smooth. More generally, we show that this ring is isomorphic to the integral Chow ring of the canonical stack over the associated toric stack for an arbitrary non-strict stacky fan. These generalize earlier results on the integral Chow rings of smooth toric varieties and several classes of toric stacks. We also give an explicit description of the pullback homomorphism induced by a morphism of non-strict stacky fans.

papers.title: A Trust-Region Interior-Point Stochastic Sequential Quadratic Programming Method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a trust-region interior-point stochastic sequential quadratic programming (TR-IP-SSQP) method for solving optimization problems with a stochastic objective and deterministic nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. In this setting, exact evaluations of the objective function and its gradient are unavailable, but their stochastic estimates can be constructed. In particular, at each iteration our method builds stochastic oracles whose estimates of the objective value and gradient satisfy proper adaptive accuracy conditions with a fixed probability. To handle inequality constraints, we adopt an interior-point method (IPM), in which the barrier parameter is taken from a prescribed decreasing sequence and is reduced once a stochastic stationarity test is passed. Under standard assumptions, we show that, almost surely, the KKT residual vanishes along the iterations at which the barrier parameter is reduced, and every limit point of these iterates is a KKT point. We implement the method on a subset of problems from the CUTEst test set, as well as on constrained logistic regression problems, to demonstrate its practical performance.

papers.title: RL unknotter, hard unknots and unknotting number
papers.abstract: We train a reinforcement learning agent to simplify hard unknot diagrams and pair it with a learned crossing selector to search for short unknotting sequences. Four examples found by the agent lead to two infinite families of prime two-bridge and Montesinos knots of unknotting number three whose connected sums with the figure-eight knot also have unknotting number three, and fifteen new unknotting upper bounds were found on the set of prime knots up to 13 crossings.

papers.title: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
papers.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

papers.title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.

papers.title: Pathwise stability of Wasserstein contractive Markov chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: We study pathwise behaviour of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms. For chains satisfying a contraction assumption w.r.t. a Wasserstein distance we establish explicit deterministic rates that hold for single realisations on sets of high probability. Additionally, we show that the median of means estimator further increases the pathwise stability. To prove our main results we employ a well-known martingale decomposition technique based on solutions of Poisson's equation. Finally, we apply our results to concrete MCMC methods including the No-U-Turn-Sampler, the Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm and slice samplers.

papers.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
papers.abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $Γ$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{Γ,λ}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{Γ, λ}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{Γ,λ}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{Γ,λ}$, whereas the converse fails.

papers.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.

papers.title: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.

papers.title: Soliton-type metrics associated with weighted constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics on Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish an existence equivalence between a weighted constant scalar curvature Kähler metric introduced by Lahdili and an associated soliton-type metric introduced in this article on Fano manifolds. We apply it to semisimple principal fibrations with Fano fiber. This yields a family of extremal Kähler metrics, including a constant scalar curvature Kähler metric, on a non-Fano complex four-fold with non-toric Fano fiber. A further application concerns Sasaki metrics on canonical circle bundles over $n$-dimensional Fano manifolds. For a fixed (possibly irregular) Reeb field, we show that there exists a Sasaki Mabuchi soliton if and only if there exists a Sasaki extremal metric whose transverse scalar curvature is strictly less than $n+1$. Finally, we characterize Reeb fields on the standard sphere $S^{2n+1}$ that admit Sasaki Mabuchi solitons.

papers.title: From Inexact Gradients to Byzantine Robustness: Acceleration and Optimization under Similarity
papers.abstract: Distributed learning algorithms are vulnerable to adversarial nodes, a.k.a. Byzantine failures. To solve this issue, robust algorithms have been developed, which typically replace parameter averaging with robust aggregations. While generic conditions on these aggregations exist to guarantee the convergence of (Stochastic) Gradient Descent (SGD), the analyses remain rather ad hoc. This hinders the development of more complex robust algorithms, such as accelerated ones. In this work, we show that Byzantine-robust distributed optimization can, under standard generic assumptions, be cast as a general optimization with inexact gradient oracles, an active field of research. This allows us to obtain state-of-the-art results for Byzantine-robust optimization from general inexact first-order analyses. We first show that inexact GD on top of standard robust aggregation procedures obtains optimal asymptotic error in the Byzantine setting. Going further, we study an algorithm for Optimization under Similarity, in which the server leverages an auxiliary loss function that approximates the global loss. Then, we introduce an Accelerated Extra-gradient method that yields acceleration in both the standard and similarity settings. We first give new general convergence results for these inexact schemes, improving the tolerance level of acceleration to a relative error term by a $κ^{1/2}$ factor over previous analysis, and then instantiate these results in the Byzantine setting through our reduction. Both algorithms drastically reduce the communication complexity, as we show theoretically and empirically.

papers.title: On a definitition of slice regular algebraic varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a complete correspondence between irreducible slice regular algebraic sets and quasi prime radical right ideals in the ring of quaternionic slice regular polynomials. In particular we make use of the definition of quasi prime ideals to give a characterization of irreducibility of slice regular algebraic sets. More precisely, we show that if $I$ is a radical and quasi prime right ideal, then $\mathbb S_{V_c(I)}$, the symmetrization of $V_c(I)$, is an irreducible slice regular algebraic set, where $V_c(I)$ denotes the set of common zeros with commuting components of polynomials in $I$. Combining this fact with the results of one of our previous papers, we obtain that for $I$ radical, $V_c(I)$ is irreducible if and only if $I$ is quasi prime. We also find a complete characterization of quasi prime radical right ideals, proving that either they are completely prime or the radical of the symmetrization $S(J)$ of a completely prime right ideal $J$.

papers.title: Contextual Distributionally Robust Optimization with Causal and Continuous Structure
papers.abstract: WWe propose a framework for contextual distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that considers the causal and continuous structure of the underlying distribution, and we develop interpretable and tractable decision rules. We first introduce the causal Sinkhorn discrepancy (CSD), an entropy-regularized causal Wasserstein distance that encourages continuous transport plans while preserving causal consistency. We then formulate a contextual DRO model with a CSD-based ambiguity set, termed Causal Sinkhorn DRO (Causal-SDRO), and derive its strong dual reformulation, where the worst-case distribution is characterized as a mixture of Gibbs distributions. To obtain an (infinite-dimensional) optimal policy, we propose a soft regression forest (SRF) decision rule: it preserves the interpretability of classical decision trees while being fully parametric, differentiable, and Lipschitz-smooth, enabling intrinsic interpretation from both global and local perspectives. To solve Causal-SDRO with parametric decision rules, we develop an efficient stochastic compositional gradient algorithm that converges to an $\varepsilon$-stationary point with $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ iteration complexity and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-5})$ sample complexity. Finally, numerical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance and interpretability of our method.

papers.title: On subradically sifted sums related to Alladi's higher order duality between prime factors
papers.abstract: In this paper, I utilize a variant of the Selberg--Delange method to find quantitative estimates of the sums \[M_{k,ω}(x,y)=\sum_{\substack{p_{1}(n)> y\\ n\leq x} } μ(n) {ω(n)-1\choose k-1},\] where $y$ can grow with $x$ but we must have $y\leq Y_0\exp(\mathscr{p}\frac{\log x}{(\log\log (x+1))^{1+ε}})$ with $Y_0,\mathscr{p},ε>0$. Moreover, I give preliminary upper bounds for the general range $1.9\leq y\leq x^{\frac{1}{k}}$. In addition, I formalize the notions of subradical and radical dominance and discuss their relevance to the analytic approach to the study of arithmetic functions. Lastly, I give a fascinating formula related to the derivatives of the gamma function and the Hankel contour, which should be relevant for those employing the Selberg--Delange method to obtain higher-order terms.

papers.title: The non-ergodic Host-Kra-Ziegler structure theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions via measurable selections
papers.abstract: We establish a non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem for measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^d$-actions. Our argument reduces the non-ergodic case to the ergodic theorem (for $d\ge 2$ due to Candela and Szegedy) via a measurable selection procedure. We also establish a non-ergodic vertical nilcharacter version of our main result. The non-ergodic version of the Host--Kra--Ziegler structure theorem is a key input in the companion paper by the second author and Fraczyk classifying point processes (i.e. random subsets) of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ whose law is invariant under the group $\mathrm{ASL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$ of affine transformations.

papers.title: Kantorovich Distance via Spanning Trees: Properties and Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study optimal transport between probability measures supported on the same finite metric space, where the ground cost is a distance induced by a weighted connected graph. Building on recent work showing that the resulting Kantorovich distance can be expressed as a minimization problem over the set of spanning trees of this underlying graph, we investigate the implications of this reformulation on the construction of an optimal transport plan and a dual potential based on the solution of such an optimization problem. In this setting, we derive an explicit formula for the Kantorovich potential in terms of the imbalanced cumulative mass (a generalization of the cumulative distribution in R) along an optimal spanning tree solving such a minimization problem, under a weak non-degeneracy condition on the pair of measures that guarantees the uniqueness of a dual potential. Our second contribution establishes the existence of an optimal transport plan that can be computed efficiently by a dynamic programming procedure once an optimal spanning tree is known. Finally, we propose a stochastic algorithm based on simulated annealing on the space of spanning trees to compute such an optimal spanning tree. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed approach for optimal transport on finite metric spaces.

papers.title: Stochastic Deep Learning: A Probabilistic Framework for Modeling Uncertainty in Structured Temporal Data
papers.abstract: I propose a novel framework that integrates stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with deep generative models to improve uncertainty quantification in machine learning applications involving structured and temporal data. This approach, termed Stochastic Latent Differential Inference (SLDI), embeds an Itô SDE in the latent space of a variational autoencoder, allowing for flexible, continuous-time modeling of uncertainty while preserving a principled mathematical foundation. The drift and diffusion terms of the SDE are parameterized by neural networks, enabling data-driven inference and generalizing classical time series models to handle irregular sampling and complex dynamic structure. A central theoretical contribution is the co-parameterization of the adjoint state with a dedicated neural network, forming a coupled forward-backward system that captures not only latent evolution but also gradient dynamics. I introduce a pathwise-regularized adjoint loss and analyze variance-reduced gradient flows through the lens of stochastic calculus, offering new tools for improving training stability in deep latent SDEs. My paper unifies and extends variational inference, continuous-time generative modeling, and control-theoretic optimization, providing a rigorous foundation for future developments in stochastic probabilistic machine learning.

papers.title: State integrals for the quantized $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant
papers.abstract: Previous work of the author and N.\ Reshetikhin defines an invariant $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ(K, ρ, μ)$ of a knot $K$, a representation $ρ\colon π_{1}(S^{3} \setminus K) \to \operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$, and a logarithm $μ$ of a meridian eigenvalue of $ρ$. It can be interpreted as a geometric twist of the Kashaev invariant or as a quantization of the $\operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant and is defined via a discrete state-sum involving quantum dilogarithms. In this paper we show how to express $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ(K, ρ, μ)$ as a sum over contour integrals in a space parametrizing hyperbolic structures on the knot complement. Such state integral presentations are an important step in determining the asymptotics of quantum invariants as predicted by the Volume Conjecture. We discuss this perspective and the remaining obstacles to establishing exponential growth of $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ$.

papers.title: On identity Seidel switches
papers.abstract: An identity Seidel switch of a graph is a vertex subset whose Seidel switch produces an isomorphic graph. We distinguish the elementary abelian group of switching operations from the family of identity switches of a fixed graph, which need not be a group. We obtain an edge-count condition for identity switches and deduce that every vertex-identity switch has degree half the number of remaining vertices. In particular, no graph of order at least two has every vertex as an identity switch. For a two-vertex switching set inducing an edge, we characterize the switches admitting an isomorphism that preserves the endpoint pair, in terms of automorphisms of the remaining induced subgraph. We establish modification results under this additional hypothesis and give explicit constructions of identity switches. Counterexamples show why edge-count conditions and unrestricted modification assertions do not suffice.

papers.title: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Kollár's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.

papers.title: Rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully nonlinear extrinsic geometric flows: Classification and Applications
papers.abstract: We study rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully non-linear extrinsic geometric flows in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ driven by positive $α$-homogeneous curvature functions, building on Rengaswami's classification of bowl-type translators. For positive ends at infinity and every $α>0$, we derive two correction terms beyond the leading order in the nondegenerate case and the growth rate in each degenerate regime. Imposing the translator equation across the neck on a signed extension of the curvature function, we construct catenoidal translators and classify their continuations according to a branch of the rotational level set. These yield complete embedded translators or maximal pieces, for which we determine the regularity at each transition and the shrinking-neck asymptotics; each alternative is realized in a model family of curvature functions. As applications of the tangency principle, we obtain rigidity and nonexistence results governed by the global geometry of the bowl-type solutions. When the bowl is entire, it is unique up to vertical translation among convex translators with a single graphical end asymptotic to it (also under a weighted condition in the strictly convex case), and its existence rules out both convex translating graphs over bounded domains that blow up at the boundary and entire ones growing uniformly faster or slower than the bowl. When the bowl is not entire, it may have finite height for $α>1$; in this setting, any strictly convex translating graph over a ball that is continuous up to the boundary and has vertical tangent planes there is necessarily a bowl of finite height.

papers.title: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
papers.abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

papers.title: On the connectedness of a minimizing cluster's boundary
papers.abstract: We verify that an isoperimetric minimizing cluster on a simply connected homogeneous Riemannian manifold with at most one end always has connected boundary. In particular, the boundary of a single-bubble isoperimetric minimizer on such manifolds must be connected, and hence all isoperimetric sets and their complements must be connected. This is demonstrably false without the simple connectedness assumption or the restriction on the number of ends.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. II
papers.abstract: This paper is the second in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we solve the linear preserver problem for the Cullis' determinant defined on the spaces of matrices of size $n\times k$ with $k \ge 4,\; n \ge k + 2$ and $n + k$ is odd. In comparison with the case when $n + k$ is even, in this case linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant could be singular and are represented as a sum of two linear maps: first is two-sided matrix multiplication and second is any linear map whose image consists of matrices, all rows of which are equal.

papers.title: Regularity of Cohomogeneity two equivariant isotopy minimization problems and minimal hypersurfaces with large first Betti number on spheres
papers.abstract: We prove the regularity of cohomogeneity two equivariant isotopy minimization problems. Based on this, we develop cohomogeneity two equivariant min-max theory for minimal hypersurfaces proposed by Pitts and Rubinstein in 1987. As an application, for $g \ge 1$ and $4 \le n+1 \le 7$, we construct minimal hypersurfaces $Σ_{g}^{n}$ on round spheres $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$ with $(SO(n-1) \times \mathbb{D}_{g+1})$-symmetry. For sufficiently large $g$, $Σ_{g}^{n}$ is a sequence of minimal hypersurfaces with arbitrarily large Betti numbers of topological type $\#^{2g} (S^{1} \times S^{n-1})$ or $\#^{2g+2} (S^{1} \times S^{n-1})$. For $4 \le n+1 \le 6$, $Σ^{n}_{g}$ converges to a union of $\mathbb{S}^{n}$ and a Clifford hypersurface $\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}}\mathbb{S}^{1} \times \sqrt{\frac{n-1}{n}} \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ or $\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\mathbb{S}^{2} \times \sqrt{\frac{n-2}{n}} \mathbb{S}^{n-2}$. In particular, for dimensions $5$ and $6$, $Σ_{g}^{n}$ has a topological type $\#^{2g} (S^{1} \times S^{n-1})$.

papers.title: The 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups
papers.abstract: We determine the 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups over S^4.

papers.title: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

papers.title: Seshadri Regions and the Asymptotic Shape of Multigraded Regularity
papers.abstract: We introduce the Seshadri region of a subvariety, a convex region packaging the classical Seshadri constants with respect to every line bundle simultaneously. We develop the theory of Seshadri regions as a measure of positivity along subvarieties and apply it to determine asymptotic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for ideal powers and symmetric powers on smooth projective toric varieties.

papers.title: Shallow-water convergence of the intermediate long wave equation in $L^2$
papers.abstract: We continue our study on the convergence issue of the intermediate long wave equation (ILW) on both the real line and the circle. In particular, we establish convergence of the scaled ILW dynamics to that of the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) in the shallow-water limit at the $L^2$-level. Together with the recent work by the first three authors and D. Pilod (2024) on the deep-water convergence in $L^2$, this work completes the well-posedness and convergence study of ILW on both geometries within the $L^2$-framework. Our proof equally applies to both geometries and is based on the following two ingredients: the complete integrability of ILW and the normal form method. More precisely, by making use of the Lax pair structure and the perturbation determinant for ILW, recently introduced by Harrop-Griffths, Killip, and Vişan (2026), we first establish weakly uniform (in small depth parameters) equicontinuity in $L^2$ of solutions to the scaled ILW, providing a control on the high frequency part of solutions. Then, we treat the low frequency part by implementing a perturbative argument based on an infinite iteration of normal form reductions for KdV.

papers.title: The Solver's Paradox for SAT
papers.abstract: We show in Rocq that every circuit verifier $v$ determines a formula $ψ_v$ whose satisfiability is $v$'s acceptance of its own diagonal claim: a satisfiability predicate thus behaves like a provability predicate. Every solver represented in the language misclassifies its own diagonal instance, and every verifier misjudges its own diagonal claim. We distinguish our result from (i) the refuters of Chen et al. (2024), which produce from the description of a solver an instance it gets wrong, and (ii) the refuter of Gutfreund et al. (2007) for efficient SAT solvers, which needs a hardness hypothesis and a simulation. Here the refuter is purely syntactic, and it separates evaluation of the language from its own expressions, not SAT from a resource-bounded class. The identity behind the fixed point uses no property of quotation; its reading as self-reference depends on the coding, and an injective recoding flips the branch. A truth table decides $ψ_v$ only from outside the language. Written inside, it is brute force: it settles the claim from above and has a diagonal instance of its own. This yields an unconditional certification hierarchy with tower growth, a quadratic lower bound on every internal evaluator, and an exponential lower bound on brute force.

papers.title: Some error estimates for semidiscrete finite element approximations of stable solutions to mean field game systems
papers.abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for semidiscrete finite element approximations of stable solutions to time-dependent mean field game systems with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Expressing solutions to the MFG system as zeros of a nonlinear abstract mapping, we show that the stability of solutions is equivalent to the invertibility of its differential. This characterization allows us to apply the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem in combination with discrete L^p maximal regularity estimates to prove existence of solutions to the semidiscrete MFG system and to derive the error estimate. Finally, for solutions satisfying sufficient regularity assumptions, we establish quasi-optimal error bounds, meaning the approximation achieves the best possible convergence rate when the solution has sufficient smoothness.

papers.title: On the $h$-polynomials of cyclotomic standard graded commutative algebras
papers.abstract: We call a standard graded commutative $\Bbbk$-algebra \textit{cyclotomic} if its $h$-polynomial has all its roots on the unit circle in the complex plane. Complete intersections provide typical examples of cyclotomic algebras, since the $h$-polynomial of any standard graded complete intersection is a product of polynomials of the form $1 + t + \cdots + t^{m-1}$. We refer to such polynomials as being \textit{of type CI}. A natural question is whether there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra whose $h$-polynomial is not of type CI. In this paper, we give a partial answer to this question. We show that the $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ of a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ is of type CI whenever $h_R(1) \in \{1, 4, 6\}$ or $h_R(1)$ is prime. On the other hand, if $n$ is a composite integer with $n \geq 8$, then there exists a cyclotomic standard graded $\Bbbk$-algebra $R$ whose $h$-polynomial $h_R(t)$ is not of type CI and satisfies $h_R(1) = n$.

papers.title: Fine-grained deterministic hardness of the shortest vector problem
papers.abstract: Let $γ$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ be the decision version of the shortest vector problem in the $\ell_p$-norm with approximation factor $γ$, let $n$ be the lattice rank and $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$. We prove that there is no algorithm that solves $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ uniformly for all $p\in\mathbb{N}$ in time\[ 2^{2^{o(p)}}\cdot 2^{o(n)},\] unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. The proof is based on a deterministic Karp reduction from a constrained variant of the subset-sum problem to $\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ for fixed $p$. While most hardness results for the shortest vector problem in finite norms rely on randomized reductions, our method is entirely deterministic. As a consequence, we also obtain a deterministic Karp reduction from the standard subset-sum problem to $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_{\infty}$.

papers.title: TWIN: Two window inspection for online change point detection
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of sequential change point tests based on two-window inspection (TWIN). TWIN scans for changes by comparing symmetric subsamples of data and combining them in a weighted maximum, similar to Levy's modulus of continuity. The TWIN detector generally admits a Gaussian approximation, which becomes an above-threshold approximation at Levy's critical weight. For this weight, the detector achieves rate-optimal detection delays. We present a version of TWIN for detecting mean changes and establish convergence even for weakly dependent data taking values in a separable Banach space. We also discuss the detection of general distributional changes. Controlling the Levy modulus of continuity of partial sum processes typically requires subgaussian data. However, we show that this requirement can be circumvented by an adaptive version of TWIN that requires only finite moments of low order. The adaptation is based on a data-dependent clock, that can be motivated by the Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz theorem. Simulations and an application to monitoring COVID-19 data illustrate the performance of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Exploring the Scaling Crossover of Generalized Jeffreys-Type Law: Stochastic Modeling, Analysis, and High-Accuracy Numerical Computation
papers.abstract: The generalized Jeffreys-type law is formulated as a multi-term time-fractional Jeffreys-type equation (MT-TFJE), whose dynamics exhibit rich scaling crossover phenomena associated with different diffusion mechanisms. In this work, we provide a microscopic stochastic interpretation of the MT-TFJE through a continuous-time random walk (CTRW) framework with a generalized waiting-time distribution, elucidating the physical mechanisms underlying the scaling crossover. Based on the Laplace-Volterra formulation and spectral analysis, we establish the well-posedness and stability of the MT-TFJE and derive Sobolev regularity estimates under appropriate assumptions on the initial data and source term. We further develop a high-accuracy numerical scheme, termed CIM-CLG, which combines a contour integral method for temporal approximation with the Chebyshev-Legendre Galerkin method for spatial discretization. The proposed method achieves exponential temporal convergence under the stated regularity of the governing equation, together with high-order spatial accuracy. The temporal approximation involves $\mathcal{O}(N)$ independent contour evaluations, where $N$ is the number of contour points, while the FFT-based transforms have a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(M^n\log M)$ for spatial dimensions $n=1,2$, with $M$ denoting the number of modes per spatial dimension. The resulting algorithm is naturally parallelizable. Detailed implementation procedures and rigorous error estimates are presented. Extensive numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate the efficiency, accuracy, and robustness of the proposed method, providing a computationally effective framework for generalized nonlocal diffusion problems.

papers.title: Moments of the zeros of Faber polynomials of the Miller basis
papers.abstract: We study the zeros of modular forms in the Miller basis, a natural basis for the space of modular forms. We show that the zeros of their Faber polynomials have linear moments. By analyzing the moments we can extend the known range of the forms in the Miller basis for which at least one of the zeros is not on the arc - the circular part of the boundary of the fundamental domain. Additionally, for forms in the Miller basis of an index asymptotically linear in the weight such that all zeros are on the arc, we compute the limit distribution of the zeros, which depends on the asymptotic ratio of the index to the weight.

papers.title: A Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation for Automated Aircraft Arrival Routing and Scheduling
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing dynamic arrival routes (DARs) in a terminal maneuvering area (TMA) together with an automated scheduling of all the arrivals within a given time interval. DARs are aircraft arrival routes from all entry points of a TMA, which merge traffic in that time interval towards the runway, and are modeled as energy-efficient continuous-descent operations, such that separation based on wake-turbulence categories is guaranteed within the TMA. We propose a new model based on a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of a previous model for this problem. As in the previous model, we include tree consistency across consecutive planning intervals. However, the reformulation enables us to further improve the model and also consider aircraft that remain in the TMA from the previous period, a feature critical for operational safety. In computational experiments for Stockholm Arlanda airport, the new model consistently outperforms the previous one: we obtain solutions within 5 seconds to 12.65 minutes compared to up tp 40.9 hours with the old model for instances of half hours with high traffic. In addition, we are able to solve instances of a full hour of arriving aircraft with high traffic (33 aircraft) within 22.22 to 58.57 minutes, whereas the old model could not solve these instances at all. While we schedule all aircraft as continuous-descent arrivals, our model can be applied to any type of speed profiles for the arriving aircraft.

papers.title: Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.

papers.title: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.

papers.title: Area Rigidity for the Regular Representation of Surface Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\tildeΣ$ be the universal cover of a closed surface $Σ$ of genus at least $2$. We characterize all equivariantly area-minimizing maps from $\tildeΣ$ to a Hilbert sphere, which are equivariant with respect to an isometric action of $π_1(Σ)$ weakly equivalent to the regular representation. As part of our proof, we classify all totally isotropic minimal surfaces in Hilbert spheres with constant negative Gaussian curvature. This builds on earlier results of E. Calabi, K. Kenmotsu, R. Bryant.

papers.title: Validity and Power of Heavy-Tailed Combination Tests under Asymptotic Dependence
papers.abstract: Heavy-tailed combination tests, such as the Cauchy combination test and harmonic mean p-value method, are widely used for testing global null hypotheses by aggregating dependent p-values. Existing theoretical guarantees, however, are largely restricted to the case of asymptotically independent p-values, leaving the behavior of these tests under broader dependence structures poorly understood. We develop a unified framework based on multivariate regularly varying copulas, a flexible class defined by a mild regularity condition on the joint behavior of p-values near zero, that accommodates a wide range of dependence structures. Within this framework, heavy-tailed combination tests are asymptotically valid when the transformation distribution has tail index $γ\leq 1$, with $γ= 1$ maximizing power while preserving validity. We further show that combination tests with $γ= 1$ achieve strictly greater asymptotic power than Bonferroni's method if and only if the p-values are not asymptotically independent and signals are not extremely sparse, with the power advantage growing as dependence strengthens. Bonferroni emerges as the $γ\to 0$ limit and becomes overly conservative under asymptotic dependence. These results provide theoretical support for using truncated Cauchy or Pareto combination tests, offering a principled approach to enhance power while controlling false positives under complex dependence.

papers.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
papers.abstract: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established. Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

papers.title: Dirac reduction algebra
