papers.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Kollár and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

papers.title: Exponential Convergence of the Lifted Gradient Flow of the Bass Functional
papers.abstract: How quickly can we construct the martingale with prescribed initial and terminal laws that is closest to Brownian motion in the sense of the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem? The construction requires the initial law of an auxiliary Brownian motion. One can take this law to be the distribution of a minimizer of the lifted Bass functional. In dimension one, Backhoff, Pammer and Schachermayer proved, under additional assumptions, that the gradient flow of this functional converges exponentially to a minimizer. We extend this result to arbitrary dimension. Under the assumptions of the paper, the gradient flow starting from a bounded random vector converges exponentially in $L^2$ to the minimizer with the same mean. We prove this by showing that, for a fixed random vector $X$ with the prescribed initial law, the lifted Bass functional is strongly convex on each set of $σ(X)$-measurable vectors with a prescribed mean and a common $L^\infty$ bound.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: Distribution-free predictive inference with instrumental variables
papers.abstract: We study the problem of predictive inference with outcomes missing not at random, when instrumental variables are available. While conformal prediction and weighted conformal prediction provide valid distribution-free inference when outcomes are missing completely at random and missing at random, respectively, inference is generally not possible without additional assumptions when outcomes are missing not at random. In this work, we consider a setting where we remain within the distribution-free framework but instead have access to an instrumental variable (IV). We explore the theoretical possibility of IV predictive inference and establish that it is characterized by a parameter that we refer to as the identification index. We derive an impossibility result for the case where the identification index is not sufficiently large, showing that any distribution-free approach fails to provide informative inference in this case. For the case where the identification index is sufficiently large, we introduce a practical method that achieves informative predictive inference. Our method leverages modern semiparametric efficiency theory which involves deriving the efficient influence function of the identifying functional for sharp IV bounds of the quantiles of the missing outcome, delivering a double robustness property in the coverage guarantee of the proposed framework for IV-based predictive inference. We illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed procedure through simulations and two real-data applications---FES wages and NHANES III self-reported heights.

papers.title: Frangible prime gaps
papers.abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.74161, 2.79201]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

papers.title: An elementary proof of rational injectivity in equivariant KK-theory
papers.abstract: Antonini, Azzali and Skandalis proved that, for every countable discrete group $Γ$, the canonical map $EΓ\to\underline{E}Γ$ induces a split injection in equivariant $KK$-theory with real coefficients. In this paper, we give a more elementary proof of the corresponding rational injectivity result in ordinary equivariant $KK$-theory without using $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.

papers.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(λ,p)=\sup_{\|u\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}\le1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(e^{4πu^2}-1-λ|u|^p\bigr)\,dx, \qquad p\ge2, \] Chen--Jiang--Lu--Zhu gave the first classification of attainment away from the thresholds across the full range of $p$. We prove attainment at both thresholds for $p=2$ and at the unique threshold for each $2<p\le4$. At and above the upper quadratic threshold, $S(λ,2)=4πe^{1-2γ_{\mathrm E}}$, Nguyen's concentration level, where $γ_{\mathrm E}$ is the Euler--Mascheroni constant. At each endpoint, the centred radial extremals form a compact set and their $L^p$ masses determine the slope from within the attainment interval. For fixed $p>4$, we obtain the expansion \[ S(λ,p)=4π+\mathcal C_pλ^{-2/(p-4)} +D_pλ^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(λ^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \qquad λ\to\infty. \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting problem at unit $L^2$ mass, and $D_p$ selects the limiting profiles. For fixed $λ$ above the quartic threshold $λ_*(4)$, we prove \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(λ,p)-4π\bigr) =2\log\frac{λ_{\mathrm{loc}}}λ<0, \] where $λ_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. An exact radial transformation extends these results to every planar norm.

papers.title: Fully First-Order Optimization for Implicit Multilevel Compositions via Recursive Perturbations
papers.abstract: We study multilevel optimization problems in which the outer objective depends on a finite composition of implicit response maps defined by smooth inner functions. This model covers chains of strongly convex minimization responses, strongly convex--strongly concave saddle responses, or a mixture of the two. We propose a fully first-order method that estimates the outer gradient through recursive response perturbations. The main difficulty with approximate responses is that an adjoint error at one level changes the perturbation vector at the preceding level. To control this propagation, we pair the unperturbed and perturbed updates at each level and track their scaled differences jointly with the forward response errors. The resulting tracking bounds are uniform in the perturbation radius $δ$. For the exact composite objective, we establish an $O(K^{-1}+δ^2)$ bound on the average squared gradient norm after $K$ outer iterations. For fixed problem data and finite depth, a suitable choice of $δ$ yields $ε$-stationarity in $O(ε^{-2})$ outer iterations with inner budgets independent of the target accuracy. For strongly convex minimization chains, we also derive condition-number-dependent first-order oracle complexity bounds.

papers.title: Equivalence of Restricted and Full Division
papers.abstract: We prove over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$ that the restricted Euclidean division principle $\mathrm{pa17}^{-}$, which asserts division only for co-prime pairs, is equivalent to the full principle $\mathrm{pa17}$. The proof uses a transformation that preserves the quotient in division with remainder to reduce an arbitrary division problem to one for a co-prime pair. This answers Visser's Open Question 8.29 and shows that the restricted principle has the same strength as full Euclidean division over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$. An appendix further shows that $\mathrm{PA}^{-}_{\mathrm{jer}}+\mathrm{pa17}$ proves both the predecessor principle $\mathrm{pa14}$ and the subtraction principle $\mathrm{pa15}$.

papers.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
papers.abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $α\in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $α\in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.

papers.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
papers.abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.

papers.title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+Δu=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we prove a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that the leading-order relativistic Euler system admits a smooth self-similar imploding profile whose associated normalized coefficients satisfy quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the existence of the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using the finite speed of propagation, we then obtain a threshold $p_0$, independent of the dimension, such that for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, there exist smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data whose solutions blow up in finite time. The proof combines three ingredients: a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, the growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.

papers.title: Doubly commuting invariant and co-invariant subspaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_{i}$ be complex separable Hilbert spaces and $T_{i}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{i})$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. On the Hilbert tensor product $\mathfrak{H}:=\mathcal{H}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{H}_{n}$, consider the operator tuple $(\tilde{T}_{1},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n})$ defined by $T_{i}:=I_{\mathcal{H}_{1}}\otimes \cdots \otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i-1}}\otimes T_{i}\otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{i+1}}\otimes \cdots \otimes I_{\mathcal{H}_{n}}.$ A closed jointly $(\tilde{T}_{1},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n})$-invariant subspace $\mathfrak{M}\subseteq\mathfrak{H}$ is doubly commuting if $(\tilde{T}_{1}\vert{}_{\mathfrak{M}},\dots,\tilde{T}_{n}\vert{}_{\mathfrak{M}})$ is doubly commuting. We prove that if the hereditary polynomials in each $T_{i}$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) are ultraweakly dense in $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_i)$, then $\mathfrak{M}$ is doubly commuting if and only if $\mathfrak{M}=\mathcal{M}_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal{M}_n$, where each $\mathcal{M}_i\subseteq\mathcal{H}_i$ is a closed $T_{i}$-invariant subspace. As applications, this provides a unified framework for characterizing doubly commuting quotient modules of weighted Bergman spaces over $\mathbb{D}^{n}$ and tensor products of complete Nevanlinna-Pick spaces. It also characterizes doubly commuting jointly invariant subspaces for tuples of backward shifts and their adjoints on tensor products of de Branges-Rovnyak spaces $H(b)$ (for both extreme and certain nonextreme $b$), as well as for tuples of coordinate Volterra operators and its adjoints on $L^2((0,1)^n;\mathbb{C})$. In particular cases, we recover known characterizations of doubly commuting quotient modules of $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)$ and doubly commuting submodules of its Jordan blocks. Finally, our framework extends naturally to mixed tensor products combining distinct factor spaces from any of these settings.

papers.title: Nonminimizing Attration of Stochastic Subgradient Methods on Semialgebraic Functions
papers.abstract: We construct a globally Lipschitz, coercive, semialgebraic function in two dimensions for which stochastic subgradient iterates converge to the origin, a Clarke critical point that is neither limiting critical nor a local minimizer. For power-law stepsizes, this attraction holds on open sets of initial points and linear tilts, uniformly over all noise sequences within a prescribed bound. The example shows that subdifferential regularity cannot be removed from the generic guarantee of convergence to local minimizers established by Davis, Drusvyatskiy, and Jiang (2026). For the same tilted objectives and initial points, the unique Clarke subgradient flow converges to a strict local minimizer. Thus, convergence of continuous-time flows to local minimizers cannot by itself justify the corresponding guarantee for discrete subgradient methods, even with diminishing stepsizes.

papers.title: Fourier Restriction Beyond Dimension Data: A Multiscale Moment Criterion
papers.abstract: We establish an exact restriction criterion for weighted Moran measures with uniformly bounded one-level frame bounds: for every $2<s<\infty$, $L^2(μ)\to L^s(\mathbb R)$ extension holds if and only if $\widehatμ\in L^s(\mathbb R)$, equivalently, if and only if $\sum_nG_{s,n}<\infty$, where $G_{s,n}$ sums the $s$th powers of the magnitudes of the $n$th digit mask at its nonzero grid frequencies. The proof combines finite-frame stability and multiscale iteration with disjoint resonant frequency grids. The criterion determines the critical restriction exponent and characterizes its attainment when it lies in $(1,2)$. We construct singular continuous spectral Moran measures with common scales, digit cardinalities, exponential spectrum, maximal mask magnitudes at nonzero grid frequencies, and a global Fourier decay bound sharp along a common resonant sequence, yet different critical restriction exponents. For any prescribed finite positive summability exponent of these maxima, we determine the optimal interval of critical restriction exponents and realize both endpoint attainment and failure at every interior point with the same fixed data. These measures can simultaneously satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm F}^θμ=θ$ for $0\leθ\le1$ and $D_q(μ)=1$ for $1<q\le\infty$, with local dimension one at every support point. Finite-field spectral constructions realize every critical restriction exponent in $[1,2]$ with these dimensional data and exhibit sharp logarithmic endpoint transitions. They also yield singular continuous measures with Fourier dimension zero, restriction for all $1\le p<2$, and stretched-logarithmic Fourier decay with an optimal exponent. Finally, all-scale $L^q$-dimension formulas yield explicit examples where dimensional criteria strictly improve the classical Stein--Tomas--Mockenhaupt range.

papers.title: Non-degeneracy and Fibering with Applications to Diophantine Approximation
papers.abstract: Motivated by applications in Diophantine approximation, we develop a new fibering mechanism for non-degenerate manifolds in $\mathbb{R}^n$, showing that they admit local decompositions into families of non-degenerate curves with uniform quantitative non-degeneracy estimates. Our construction applies to $l$ non-degenerate $C^N$ manifolds under the optimal regularity assumption $N\geq\max\{n,l\}$, requiring no additional smoothness. Furthermore, we show that this uniform quantitative local control can be globalised into a qualitative statement, so that almost every point of a non-degenerate manifold lies on a non-degenerate curve contained in the manifold. The resulting quantitative fibering estimates are also stable under sufficiently small $C^n$ perturbations at each fixed spatial scale. The method provides a framework for extending fibering based results in Diophantine approximation from curves to manifolds. Such applications are considered in the paper.

papers.title: A Single-Loop, Constant-Batch First-Order Penalty Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Recent advances in penalty-based methods for stochastic bilevel optimization (SBO) have eliminated the need for second-order derivative oracles. However, for stochastic nonconvex-strongly convex bilevel problems, existing first-order methods typically rely on nested loops and/or large batch sizes for attaining $O(ε^{-6})$ or $O(ε^{-4})$ sample complexity under standard bounded-variance assumption or mean-square smoothness assumption. Achieving these rates with a single-loop penalty method and a constant batch size remains challenging due to a large penalty value needed for an accurate approximation. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic SIngle-loop COnstant-Batch first-order penalty method (SICO) that combines two complementary ingredients. First, it performs one stochastic-gradient update per-iteration for both the original lower-level and penalized problems, with a projection that controls the separation between their iterates. Second, it applies an exponential moving average to stabilize the upper-level gradient estimator. We show that this combination achieves $ O(ε^{-6}) $ sample complexity using only $O(1)$ stochastic-gradient samples per iteration under unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Under the additional mean-square smoothness assumption on the lower-level stochastic gradients, the same algorithm improves the complexity to $O(ε^{-4})$ also with $O(1)$ batch size. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to match the best-known convergence rate for fully first-order SBO methods using a single loop and a constant batch size. This result addresses an open problem posed in the literature.

papers.title: Montesinos Knots with Delta-Unknotting Number One
papers.abstract: The $Δ$-unknotting number for a knot is defined as the minimum number of $Δ$-moves needed to deform the knot into the trivial knot. In this paper, we discuss Montesinos knots whose $Δ$-unknotting number is equal to one. We propose a conjectural characterization of Montesinos knots with $Δ$-unknotting number one and provide examples admitting distinct $Δ$-moves, each of which deforms the knot into the trivial knot. Furthermore, we present examples illustrating the relationship between the locations of $Δ$-moves and $X$-moves for knots with $u^Δ(K) = 1$, considering separately the cases $u(K) = 1$ and $u(K) = 2$.

papers.title: Asymptotically Hölder gradient regularity for degenerate or singular parabolic normalized $ p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We study bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular parabolic equation \[ u_t-|Du|^γΔ_p^{\mathrm{N}}u=f \qquad \text{in } Q_1, \] where \[ Δ_p^{\mathrm{N}}u := Δu+(p-2) \left\langle D^2u\frac{Du}{|Du|}, \frac{Du}{|Du|} \right\rangle, \qquad -1<γ<\infty,\quad 1<p<\infty, \] and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,α)>0$ such that \[ |p-2|+|γ|\leq\varepsilon \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+α,\frac{1+α}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $ 1 $ as $(p,γ)\to(2,0)$. This extends the result of Andrade and Santos (Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{61}, Paper No. 196, 2022) for $γ=0$ to the joint regime $(p,γ)\to(2,0)$ and answers affirmatively the question raised in Remark~1.1 therein.

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal matching covered graphs
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is {\em matching covered} if each of its edges lies in a perfect matching. A matching covered graph is {\em minimal} if the removal of any edge results in a graph that is no longer matching covered. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 23 (1977) 127--138] proved by ear decompositions that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ edges, and this bound is sharp for all even $|V(G)|\ge6$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (4) (2026) 559--606] determined the extremal graphs achieving this upper bound. In this paper, we prove that every minimal matching covered nonbipartite graph $G$ with at least 6 vertices has at most $(5|V(G)|-10)/2$ edges. Moreover, we show that if $G$ is not bicritical, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-14)/2$ edges and if $G$ is 3-connected and has at least 14 vertices, then $G$ has at most $(5|V(G)|-26)/2$ edges. All three bounds are sharp, and all the corresponding extremal graphs are characterized.

papers.title: Radial Limits and Euler Exponents of a False Theta Series with Character Modulo 8
papers.abstract: Let $T_k=k(k+1)/2$ and let $N_n(q)$ be the series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}(2k+1)^{2n+1}q^{T_k}$ for $k\ge 0$. We study the false theta function $D=N_0$ and the moment quotients $N_n/D$. We prove an exact transformation formula for twists of even order. It expresses each moment as a convergent series of derivatives of the Dawson integral, with the dual twist and its phase determined by a quadratic Gauss sum. The formula gives the finite radial values of the moments at roots of unity as nonzero cyclotomic integers and yields congruences between them. Inside the unit disc we consider the quotient of $D$ by the theta series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}q^{T_k}$. Each nonconstant coefficient of this quotient is minus twice a positive integer that counts divisors and restricted partitions. These counts give a Lyndon-word formula for the exponents in the formal Euler product of $D$. The factorization also identifies the unique real zero in $(-1,1)$. A comparison with a cubic polynomial shows that this simple zero is the only zero in $|q|<1/2$.

papers.title: A Single-Loop Method with Optimal Leading-Order Oracle Complexity for Optimization and Game Stationarity in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a single-loop first-order framework for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization, with matching leading-order upper and lower bounds for optimization and game stationarity in a projected zero-respecting oracle model. We propose a single-loop projected damped extragradient method coupling projected extragradient updates with dual momentum and a moving proximal center. Each iteration uses at most three gradient evaluations, without nested subproblems. For game stationarity, a deterministic best iterate has first-order residual below $\varepsilon$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$, where $L$ is the gradient Lipschitz constant, $D_Y$ bounds the dual feasible-set diameter, and $Δ_φ$ is the initial-point-dependent value-function gap. For optimization stationarity, a uniformly selected iterate has expected squared Moreau-envelope gradient norm at most $\varepsilon^2$ with leading oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$. Matching lower bounds are $Ω(L^{3/2}D_Y^{1/2}Δ_φ\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ for game stationarity and $Ω(L^2D_YΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-3})$ for optimization stationarity over projected zero-respecting first-order methods. Under dual strong concavity, the same framework achieves leading first-order oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκLΔ_φ\varepsilon^{-2})$ under both criteria, where $κ$ is the dual condition number. Matching lower bounds hold for both criteria in the same oracle model. To our knowledge, this is the first work to close the oracle complexity gap for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax optimization under both stationarity criteria by simultaneously improving upper and lower bounds in the projected zero-respecting oracle model.

papers.title: Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes
papers.abstract: Let X be a spectrally negative Lévy process observed up to an inde- pendent exponential time T with parameter γ > 0. We study the joint law of the maximum drawdown and the maximum drawup of X on [0, T ]. The path is decomposed according to the two possible orderings of its in- fimum and supremum. Conditional on the values of these extrema and on their ordering, the resulting pre-, intermediate, and post- components are independent. We identify their laws as Doob h-transforms of killed spec- trally negative Lévy processes and express the corresponding distribution functions explicitly in terms of the γ-scale functions W (γ) and Z(γ) and their derivatives. Combining the conditional laws with the joint densities of the extrema yields integral representations of the joint distribution and moments.

papers.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: Orbits of submaximal dimension for Sylow $p$-subgroups of finite classical orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup in a classical orthogonal group over a finite field with $q$ elements of characteristic $p$ large enough. The coadjoint orbits of the group $U$ play the key role in the description of irreducible complex characters of $U$. In the paper, we provide a classification of such orbits of pre-maximal dimension. As a corollary, we compute the number of all orbits mentioned above. It turned out that each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q - 1$ with integer non-negative coefficients, which agrees with the Isaacs' conjecture.

papers.title: Fujiki Class $\mathcal C$ Varieties and a Kähler Criterion
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that flips and divisorial contractions preserve the Kähler condition (for strongly $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial compact Kähler generalized klt pairs with $B+β_X$ big), and we give a criterion for varieties in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$ to be Kähler. We also prove the existence of small $\mathbb Q$-factorializations for generalized klt pairs and of dlt modifications for generalized pairs.

papers.title: Boundary Layers and Finite-Section Asymptotics for Small Polygons
papers.abstract: In large even polygons of unit diameter, computed angle profiles oscillate near the vertex carrying the pendant diameter. We study the half-line variational problem behind this observation of Bingane and Mossinghoff. Its unique positive equilibrium approaches the regular state with alternating multiplier $(-3+\sqrt5)/2$. We determine the sharp energy errors for two ways of closing a finite section and enclose the limiting cubic coefficient in a rational interval of width below $9.4\times10^{-29}$. An explicit scaling identifies these energies with the cubic coefficients of the finite polygon constructions. Transferring the profile to unrestricted area maximizers is a further, conditional result: under the stated geometric hypothesis, the profile gives the $n^{-3}$ term of their maximal area. The recurrence, its finite-section estimates and the enclosure can be checked independently of that hypothesis.

papers.title: Comeager hereditary families of compact sets are big
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Polish space and let $\mathcal K(X)$ be its Vietoris hyperspace. A family $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K(X)$ is hereditary if it is downward closed under inclusion. Matheron and Zelený asked whether every comeager hereditary family in $\mathcal K(X)$ contains a dense hereditary $G_δ$ subfamily. We give an affirmative answer in ZFC.

papers.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.

papers.title: An asymptotic Liouville-type theorem for systems of Lane-Emden equations on RCD*(-K,N) spaces via gradient estimates
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish elliptic gradient estimates for positive solutions of the Lane-Emden system on metric measure spaces satisfying the synthetic Ricci curvature-dimension condition $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$. Our approach combines the weak differential calculus and the Bochner inequality available in the $\mathrm{RCD}^*(-K,N)$ setting with suitable auxiliary function arguments, extending classical gradient estimate techniques to nonsmooth spaces. The resulting estimate is valid for all exponents $α,β>0$ and all $N\in[1,\infty)$, with no dimensional case distinction and with explicit constants. As an application, we prove a quantitative, asymptotic Liouville-type theorem on $\mathrm{RCD}^*(0,N)$ spaces: for positive solutions that are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, the normalized gradients $|\nabla f|/f$ and $|\nabla h|/h$ are bounded by a quantity that is of order $\max\{α,β\}$ and hence tends to zero as the exponents tend to zero (with comparable size). We also explain why the method gives no rigidity for large exponents, which is consistent with, but does not prove, the existence of nonconstant solutions there. These results generalize corresponding results from the smooth Riemannian setting and contribute to the study of nonlinear elliptic systems on spaces with synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds.

papers.title: Hypothesis Testing with Conditional Queries: Learnability and the Value of Interaction
papers.abstract: Model evaluations may fix all tests before observing any responses or select later tests using earlier responses. We study this choice in a conditional-query model on a finite outcome space $\mathcal{X}$ with $|\mathcal{X}|=N$. We first ask which pairs of distribution classes can be reliably distinguished. We then ask how many additional queries are required to match an adaptive tester when all queried events must be fixed in advance. We show that learnability holds if and only if the two classes have positive separation in their pairwise conditional probabilities. When this separation is zero, the optimal worst-case error is exactly $1/2$ at every finite query budget. For any $T$-query adaptive policy and any $ρ\in (0,1)$, we construct a randomized non-adaptive procedure using $O(N^2(T + \log(1/ρ)))$ pair queries chosen before any response is observed. Its simulated transcript is within $ρ$ in total variation of the adaptive transcript, uniformly over all distributions in the model. We also construct a matching family with constant adaptive query complexity and $Ω_\varepsilon(N^2)$ non-adaptive query complexity. Consequently, the worst-case fixed-error adaptivity gap is $Θ_\varepsilon(N^2)$. Thus interaction can reduce the required number of tests by a quadratic factor, but the apparent exponential branching of an interactive evaluation does not yield an exponential query advantage.

papers.title: Dirichlet symbols and the nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We develop the geometry of conformal mappings through Dirichlet operator symbols and the nonlinear wave equation. These symbols, introduced in the work of Hedenmalm and Shimorin (2020), are holomorphic functions on the bidisk associated with contractions on $L^2(\mathbb{D})$. For Grunsky operators, the nonlinear wave equation and the related Riccati equation induce a hierarchy of of differential relations along the diagonal. We use this jet hierachy to obtain alternative coordinates and a characterization of the manifold $Σ/\mathbb{C}$ of normalized exterior univalent functions modulo translations, without an explicit univalence test. This manifold may be viewed as an extension of the universal Teichmüller space beyond the quasicircle boundary setting. The diagonal jets also give rise to a hierarchy of \emph{diagonal series Schwarzian derivatives}. Already the fourth Schwarzian $S_4(ψ)$ leads to differential equations connected with the Weierstrass elliptic $\wp$ function and Painlevé I, revealing a comparison between the geometry of conformal mappings and that of complex tori. As a quantitative application of the framework, we interpret asymptotic variance through the Littlewood-Paley formula as an asymptotic density of quadratic nonlinearity energy under logarithmic averaging. We introduce Schwarzian asymptotic variance and obtain the lower bound $5.686\ldots$ and the upper bound $12.566\ldots$ for its averaged squared hyperbolically normalized amplitude, in comparison with the classical pointwise bound $36$. Note that the lower bound shows that the Nehari sufficient squared bound $4$ does not hold on average.

papers.title: On the Kähler MMP and the transcendental base-point-free theorem
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the minimal model program for big gklt Kähler pairs, and in particular we prove Tosatti's transcendental base-point-free conjecture.

papers.title: Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: This paper studies real-linear automorphisms of $\mathbb C^2$ through the ranks of their complex-linear and conjugate-linear blocks. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) automorphisms of $\mathbb R^4$, for which both blocks have rank $1$. Such a map is complex-linear on one complex line and conjugate-linear on a complementary complex line. Equivalently, the SPCR automorphisms form the double coset ${\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)\,σ_0\,{\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)$, where $σ_0(z_1,z_2)=(z_1,\bar z_2)$ is a mixed real-linear involution whose fixed locus is a real hypersurface. We show that the SPCR locus is a $12$-dimensional submanifold of $M_2(\mathbb C)^2$ and carries a CR structure of CR dimension $4$ and CR codimension $4$ on an explicit open dense subset. We also construct canonical diagonal and genuinely non-diagonal examples.

papers.title: National-scale scheduling of long-distance electric vehicle charging under plug capacity
papers.abstract: Can today's U.S. public charging network serve long-distance trips by electric vehicles (EVs), and at what cost to travelers? We plan the charging stops of 2.2 million long-distance trips that need en-route charging, from a 1% sample of a one-month simulation, through the contiguous U.S. fast-charging network. Plans value detour, charging, and waiting time. Charging to a fixed battery level makes each trip's problem a shortest path, solved exactly; common modeling shortcuts can reverse the cost comparison. For trips competing for plugs, we compare four coordination methods, from none to reservations by departure time; the best two come within 2.2% and 6.1% of the best known solutions on small cases. First, if every plug serves every EV, existing fast chargers can reach 98.5% of the trips that need to charge, excluding those with an overly long link, with under four stops and about seven minutes of detour. Second, charging speed and electricity price decide the cost comparison: at \$0.15 per kWh, the EV is cheaper only for travelers valuing their charging time below \$11 per hour with 50 kW, or \$111 per hour with 350 kW chargers; at \$0.45 per kWh, it costs more at either speed. Third, without coordination, long queues form at several hundred small stations at 50 kW while nearby larger ones are less busy. If every trip books a plug, almost all waiting disappears on all trips at 350 kW for under a minute of extra detour, and at \$0.15 per kWh the EV trip stays about 21% cheaper.

papers.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
papers.abstract: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

papers.title: Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
papers.abstract: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.

papers.title: Approximate Controllability of the generalized Burgers-Huxley equation in one dimension
papers.abstract: The generalized Burgers-Huxley (GBH) equation is a prototype model that describes the interplay among reaction, convection, and diffusion. In this article, we explore the controllability of this model by means of an interior control supported in an arbitrary non-empty open subset of the domain. We establish that the GBH equation is not globally approximately controllable in a given time. However, it is possible to steer the system from any steady state to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of another steady state in some suitable time by means of a localized interior control, provided that both steady states lie in the same connected component of the set of steady states.

papers.title: Coupling and Maximal Inequalities for Graph-Dependent Empirical Processes
papers.abstract: We develop maximal inequalities for empirical processes indexed by graph-dependent observations. Our bounds separate the complexity of the indexing class from two features specific to graph dependence: the geometry of the underlying graph and the cost of coupling graph-separated blocks to independent copies. The coupling construction combines a novel graph-adapted dependence coefficient with a coloring of a block partition. As an application, we derive Glivenko--Cantelli results and characterize the associated effective sample size. A central implication is that graph-dependent empirical processes need not exhibit a generic root-$n$ rate: convergence is jointly determined by function-class complexity, graph geometry, and the decay of dependence with graph distance. We specialize the results to graphs with polynomial and exponential growth and to directed dyadic graphs. Finally, we apply the results to network autoregressive models, nonlinear local-propagation models, and treatment-interference settings.

papers.title: Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative trace-norm propagation of chaos for finite-dimensional quantum mean-field systems governed by Belavkin equations under continuous diffusive measurements. Our results concern random reduced states conditioned on the observation records of the entire particle system, rather than states averaged over these records. We allow arbitrary one-particle density matrices, general measurement operators, and both perfect and inefficient detection. Two regimes of initial data are considered. For initial states approaching a tensor product in trace norm, without requiring permutation invariance, we establish explicit convergence rates, improved from an inverse fourth-root to an inverse square-root rate when the one-particle initial state is faithful. More importantly, for permutation-invariant initial states, convergence of the two-particle marginal to a product suffices for propagation of chaos, even when the full initial state remains far from a tensor product. Quantitative convergence rates are obtained in this setting, including a sharper estimate under faithfulness. Our proofs combine purification, fully observed dilation, and uniform stability of linear Zakai equations with a relative-entropy method for the joint observation law and conditional quantum state. The latter controls the interacting dynamics through entropy-production estimates and extends to arbitrary-rank initial states by regularizing only the reference dynamics. These results provide a rigorous foundation for low-dimensional approximations of continuously monitored interacting quantum systems, including those with initially correlated states.

papers.title: Finite-core Volterra reductions for the Riemann phase kernel
papers.abstract: We derive exact same-sign formulas for a Riemann theta phase kernel and give a Volterra representation with its boundary and integrated tail terms. The formulas apply to finite theta cores, and the boundary-plus-tail identity also holds for the full theta series. We give an outward-rounded fourteen-node counterexample to nonnegativity of the exact endpoint-B form on the active closed-trace core in the original application. Continuity of the defining kernel transfers the negative value to a smooth witness supported outside the trace interval. As a result, the original energy is unbounded below on every nonempty affine trace fiber that retains this vertical direction. We specify a coercive modification and its changed Euler equation. Positivity of the original full-coordinate Weyl kernel and the zeta-facing application remain unresolved.

papers.title: Convergence of Scalar Curvature of Long Time Kähler-Ricci Flow on Kähler Manifold
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the long time Kähler-Ricci flow on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$ with semi-ample canonical bundle. We establish a uniform $μ$-entropy estimate and a uniform Sobolev inequality along the normalized Kähler-Ricci flow. As a consequence, we prove that the scalar curvature of the Kähler metrics along the normalized Kähler-Ricci flow converges uniformly on $X$ to the negative Kodaira dimension $-κ$ of $X$. In the noncollapsing case $κ=n$ we also obtain the rate of convergence $-Ce^{-t}\leq R(t)+n\leq C(1+t)^{-1}$ and $\fint_X|R(t)+n|ω(t)^n\leq Ce^{-t}$.

papers.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.

papers.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
papers.abstract: Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $δ$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties. The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and André.

papers.title: Proper edge coloring with rainbow diamonds
papers.abstract: Motivated by the B-coloring defined by Gyárfás and Sárközy, we introduce a new edge coloring called \emph{D-coloring}. For a graph $G$, a D-coloring of $G$ is a proper edge coloring such that every diamond subgraph is rainbow. The \emph{D-chromatic index} of $G$, denoted by $χ'_D(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a D-coloring of $G$. Denote by $Δ$ the maximum degree of $G$. We propose a Brooks-type conjecture stating that $χ'_D(G)\le \frac{1}{2}Δ^2+\frac{1}{2}Δ$ and verify this conjecture for $Δ\le 5$. We also prove a general upper bound $χ'_D(G)\le \frac{9}{16}Δ^2+\frac{1}{2}Δ$.

papers.title: Existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle, helping to establish the universality of the C-type route to chaos in families of non-invertible maps of the plane. Families of two-dimensional non-invertible maps, with at least two parameters and critical points of fold type, exhibit a distinct type of critical scaling, the C-type. An accumulation of parameter values leads to an infinite collection of coexisting attracting cycles of periods $4^n$ or $2\cdot 4^n$. Asymptotically, period quadrupling is accompanied by parameter-space scaling and state-space scaling governed by particular universal constants. Kuznetsov et. al. explained this phenomenon in terms of a stationary orbit of period two of the renormalisation group (RG) transformation for period-doubling. We prove the existence of the corresponding renormalisation two-cycle in a Banach space of analytic maps and gain rigorous bounds on the corresponding universal state space scaling constants. This result provides a further step in proving a series of outstanding conjectures concerning distinct universality classes for period-doubling. It extends the recent results for unidirectionally-coupled maps (the FS-type) to bidirectionally-coupled maps, and generalises the framework from fixed points to periodic orbits of the corresponding renormalisation operators. It also provides a further step in establishing the conjectured picture that the C-type universality class is born from the FS-type class via a period-doubling bifurcation in the dynamics of the RG transformation itself. The proof relies on rigorous computations to establish that a variant of Newton's method for the two-cycle is a contraction map. The C-type scaling regularity is known to occur in a number of dynamical systems of interest, perhaps most notably in biologically-plausible models of nephron blood pressure autoregulation.

papers.title: Analogues of the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function and related problems
papers.abstract: Upper bounds for the Riemann zeta function $ζ(s)$ as $\Im(s)\to\infty$ have been extensively studied in connection with the Lindelöf Hypothesis. In particular, the Lindelöf Hypothesis is one of the most important open problems in analytic number theory. It is also known to be equivalent to certain mean value estimates, which provide a fundamental connection between pointwise upper bounds and integral mean values of zeta-functions. In this paper, we consider an analogue of the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function $ζ_r (s,a,(w_1,\dots,w_r)) = \sum_{m_1=0}^\infty \cdots \sum_{m_r=0}^\infty (a+m_1 w_1+\cdots+m_r w_r)^{-s} $ for $\Re(s)>r$, with $a,w_1,\dots,w_r>0$, and establish equivalent conditions in terms of integral mean values. We treat the rank-one case and, under a polynomial growth assumption on the derivative, the general-rank case. The $\Q$-rank of $\langle w_1,\dots,w_r\rangle$ specifies the region considered in our statements; the equivalence argument itself does not establish that its left boundary is a critical line.

papers.title: On Santaló's Problem
papers.abstract: This paper investigates an isoperimetric-type problem posed by L. A. Santaló, concerning convex surfaces in hyperbolic 3-space that minimize total mean curvature among all convex surfaces with fixed surface area. This problem asks for a characterization of the minimizers and for the optimal form of a Minkowski-type inequality in hyperbolic 3-space. In this work, we propose a conjectural description of the minimizers under certain regularity assumptions. We also construct a new family of convex surfaces as as potential minimizer candidates and establish a property of the singular points of any minimizer.

papers.title: On the Variety of Hyperspace Selections
papers.abstract: If $f$ is a continuous selection for the Vietoris hyperspace $\mathcal{F}(X)$ of the nonempty closed subsets of a space $X$, then the point $p=f(X)\in X$ is not as arbitrary as it might seem at first glance. In fact, the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ of all these points reveals certain information about the variety of Vietoris continuous selections for $\mathcal{F}(X)$. Thus, for a connected space $X$, we will show that every point $p\in \mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is not only noncut, but also an endpoint of $X$. Another result of this paper is that in an arbitrary topological space $X$, the closure of the set $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is always a totally disconnected subset. Furthermore, we will also show that $\mathcal{O}_{cs}(X)$ is a closed subset of every first countable totally disconnected space $X$.

papers.title: Residual-Weighted Randomized Jacobi: Sharpened Bounds via Residual Concentration and Asynchronous Extension
papers.abstract: We study randomized stationary methods for symmetric positive definite linear systems in which component $j$ is selected with probability proportional to $|r_j|^\ell$. This family interpolates between uniform sampling on the nonzero residual components ($\ell \to 0^+$) and Gauss--Southwell relaxation ($\ell \to \infty$). For $\ell = 2$ we sharpen the one-step analysis using the inverse participation ratio (IPR) of the residual, $ν^2(r) = n\|r\|_4^4/\|r\|_2^4$, which is $1$ for a uniform residual and approaches $n$ as it concentrates. The resulting bound multiplies the guaranteed expected-progress coefficient of uniform sampling by the IPR (and the expected progress, for constant-diagonal $A$). We extend the analysis to asynchronous execution via the Avron--Druinsky--Gupta (ADG) framework, obtaining, under an a priori envelope on the IPR, an epoch-based reduction bound in which the IPR controls both the progress coefficient and the certified delay window. Synchronous runs on three structured problems and eight Matrix Market matrices support the sharpened bound, and shared-memory experiments show an IPR trajectory nearly insensitive to concurrency. There, committing a buffered residual value (consistent reads, the easier case for ADG) led to divergence at high concurrency on every problem, while re-reading the component at update time (inconsistent reads) diverged in a minority of runs on one problem. We conjecture a feedback-damping mechanism, test its predictions, and find that sufficiently small fixed steps and an adaptive IPR-driven step-size rule removed the instability in every run, at a cost in speed.

papers.title: Propagation of Regularity for Schroedinger Equations with Time Dependent Potentials
papers.abstract: The dynamics of Schrödinger equation with time dependent potentials of general time dependence is considered. It is shown that for localized in space potentials, there is propagation of regularity which is uniformly bounded in higher Sobolev norms. Unlike the cases where the solution scatter, and then propagation is proved via a standard bootstrap argument, the solutions considered here have a part that does not scatter, as expected in general. For this we introduce propagation estimates that work directly in (e.g.) $H^2(\mathcal{R}^3).$

papers.title: Mechanisms and Pathways of Extreme Events in Partially Observed Stochastic Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Extreme events occur across the natural, engineering, and socioeconomic sciences, where rare but high-impact episodes can lead to disproportionate consequences and pose challenges for prediction and risk management. Existing studies have mainly focused on the statistics, sampling, forecasting, and attribution of extremes from observable variables. We develop a mathematical framework for studying the mechanisms and pathways of extreme events in partially observed stochastic dynamical systems with hidden variables. By integrating data assimilation with information-theoretic and trajectory-based diagnostics, we infer latent precursor dynamics, quantify their uncertainty, and determine how their influence propagates toward an observed extreme event. Conditional Gaussian models provide a tractable analytical setting for closed-form diagnostics, while the framework extends more broadly through numerical methods. From a trajectory-wise viewpoint, we compare filtering and smoothing distributions to identify the onset of hidden precursors and quantify their temporal influence range. From a statistical viewpoint, we construct event-conditioned hidden-state distributions to identify sensitive triggering directions, representative latent pathways, and distinct candidate pathway classes through clustering. Three case studies illustrate the methodology. In an intermittent stochastic model, hidden damping dynamics emerge before observed bursts, and filter-smoother discrepancies provide an onset diagnostic. In a stochastic model with damping and forcing, separate damping-induced, forcing-driven, and mixed pathways to extremes are identified. In a nonlinear topographic-flow model, distinct mechanisms and pathways for blocking and unblocking patterns associated with observed extreme events are revealed.

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a normed space
papers.abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of every real or complex normed space $X$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $X$.

papers.title: Self-similar dendrites with finite boundary and P-sprouts
papers.abstract: Each self-similar dendrite K with a finite self-similar boundary defines a finite acyclic edge-labeled bipartite graph G, called the sprout of K. The paper shows that the sprout G determines the combinatorial properties of the dendrite K and its topological structure.

papers.title: The Geometric Wall: Manifold Structure Predicts Layerwise Sparse Autoencoder Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: SAEs operationalise the linear representation hypothesis: they reconstruct model activations as sparse linear combinations of dictionary atoms hypothesised to represent meaningful linear directions. Their reconstruction error varies sharply across layers in ways that existing scaling laws, fitted at a single layer, do not explain. We contend that this variation is the empirical trace of the changing geometric structure of activation manifolds across depth: as their intrinsic dimension and curvature vary from layer to layer, so does the difficulty of approximating them with sparse linear dictionaries, and SAE width-sparsity scaling becomes a layer-dependent function of manifold structure rather than a single universal law. We conduct the first cross-layer SAE scaling study, fitting per-layer scaling-law surfaces to 844 residual-stream Gemma Scope SAE checkpoints spanning all 68 layers of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, and relating the fitted scaling parameters to four geometric summaries of the activation manifold. We find that manifold geometry predicts the per-layer width-scaling exponent in both models, explaining variation that cannot be reliably captured by layer depth alone. A controlled experiment on 150 synthetic manifolds, where intrinsic dimension and curvature vary independently, further reveals two distinct geometric contributions: intrinsic dimension governs the rate at which reconstruction improves with dictionary width, while curvature governs the residual error at the largest trained width. At the six Gemma showcase layers where richer width grids permit identification of an asymptotic floor, the fitted floors follow the same geometric ordering, consistent with the second-order residual that sparse linear approximations of curved manifolds can leave behind. SAEs thus encounter not merely a finite-resource ceiling but a geometric wall set by the manifold they are trying to reconstruct.

papers.title: Factorization and monotonicity methods for reconstructing an impenetrable obstacle in inverse biharmonic scattering
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of an impenetrable obstacle with a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition from far-field measurements. The associated data-to-pattern operators are noninjective, because the biharmonic scattered fields can be decomposed into propagative and evanescent components. We derive new symmetric factorizations of the far-field operator and analyzie the middle operators on the closures of the ranges of the adjoint data-to-pattern operators to establish range identities. These identities yield factorization criteria for the support of the obstacle when the wavenumber is not an associated transmission eigenvalue. Furthermore, we derive monotonicity criteria without excluding transmission eigenvalues. Numerical experiments for Dirichlet obstacles illustrate the reconstruction methods and show their performance with noisy data and for wavenumbers near a clamped transmission eigenvalue.

papers.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.

papers.title: Deep Learning of Solver-Aware Turbulence Closures from Nudged LES Dynamics
papers.abstract: The differentiable physics paradigm may be leveraged as an a-posteriori approach for discovering turbulence closure models by embedding a neural network parameterization directly inside the solver and optimizing it given potentially sparse target data. This addresses a key limitation of a-priori learning where direct numerical simulation (DNS) data is used to approximate the subgrid stress with the assumption of a low-pass filter. Closures trained in this a-priori manner frequently lead to unstable deployments due to the mismatch between the assumed filter and the effect of numerical discretizations and coarse-graining. In comparison, while typically stable during deployment, a-posteriori learning incurs high computational costs due to the need to backpropagate through a large eddy simulation (LES) solver. Furthermore, a-posteriori methods are challenging to apply broadly since they require significant modification of existing solvers. Finally, both approaches are limited when generalization is desired across different numerical schemes with their implicit filtering characteristics. In this work, we present a deep-learning approach for turbulence closure modeling built on the continuous data assimilation framework. Our approach enables the a-priori training of closures using DNS data observed only at coarse-grid points without modifying or differentiating through the LES solver, while preserving stability during deployment for the recovery of long-term statistics. We focus on the model's ability to adapt to different discretizations by explicitly conditioning it on the numerical scheme. We use two- and three-dimensional canonical cases to test our framework and show that the learned correction systematically tracks the discretization error of the coarse solver.

papers.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
papers.abstract: We address short-wave asymptotics for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization and blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

papers.title: The Dedekind completion of an Archimedean ordered vector space as a reflector
papers.abstract: We consider the category $\mathbf{AOVS}$ of Archimedean ordered vector spaces with linear maps which preserve all existing nonempty suprema, and its full subcategories $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$, consisting of directed spaces, Dedekind complete vector lattices and universally complete vector lattices, respectively. We deduce from some results in the literature that $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$ are reflective subcategories of $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, with the usual Dedekind completion being the reflector in $\mathbf{DVL}$. In contrast to these facts, we show that a non-directed Archimedean ordered vector space of dimension greater than $1$ has no reflector in either $\mathbf{DVL}$ or $\mathbf{UVL}$. In particular, there are no free Dedekind complete vector lattices over a set with more than one element. We also use the occasion to show that a free vector lattice with $α$ generators embeds into a free vector lattice with $β$ generators if and only if $α\leβ$, and explore the concept of the free completion of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong unit.

papers.title: The Schwarzian Derivative for Convex Holomorphic Mappings in Several Complex Variables
papers.abstract: We study the two components of Oda's Schwarzian derivative, the tensor $S_f$ and the quadratic form $S^0_f$, for convex holomorphic mappings of the polydisk and for Roper--Suffridge extensions of convex functions to the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with norms taken in the Bergman metric. For the polydisk we obtain the sharp bound $\|S_f\|\leγ_n$, where $γ_n$ is the maximum of an explicit quartic form on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with $γ_2=2$ and $γ_n\to2\sqrt2$, and the sharp bound $\|S^0_f\|\le 4/(n+1)$, $n\ge2$, in both cases the extremal mappings are products of half-plane mappings. For Roper--Suffridge extensions both norms are computed exactly in terms of the Schwarzian derivative of the one-variable function. In particular $S^0_f$ reduces to the classical Schwarzian derivative, and the theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood yields the sharp bounds $\|S_f\|\le1/\sqrt{n+1}$ and $\|S^0_f\|\le 1/(n+1)$, with equality for the parallel strip.

papers.title: Spectral Dehn Functions: Hyperbolicity, Filling Geometry and Diffusion
papers.abstract: We show that Dirichlet eigenvalues of van Kampen diagrams can distinguish groups whose Dehn functions have the same order. The Dehn function bounds the least filling area in terms of word length. We use the random walk on the faces, stopped at the exterior. For each null word we take the infimum, over its fillings, of the reciprocal of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, then maximize over words of length at most $n$. We call this the spectral Dehn function. Its coarse growth is a quasi-isometry invariant for presentations whose generators form a word ball and whose relators are all null words of length at most three. In such a presentation of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the boundary word of a square can have a filling with more faces and a larger first eigenvalue than any of its least-area fillings. For two groups with quartic Dehn functions, it is at most $Cn^4$ for one and at least $cn^6/(\log n)^2$ for the other. The spectral Dehn function is bounded exactly for word-hyperbolic groups. For other finitely presented groups it grows at least as fast as $n^2/(\log n)^2$. In these presentations the bound is sharp for non-hyperbolic automatic groups and for non-hyperbolic groups acting properly and cocompactly by isometries on proper geodesic Lipschitz $1$-connected spaces. For the face walk we maximize the expected absorption time over starting faces. In these classes its supremum over least-area fillings of cyclically reduced null words of length at most $n$ has order $n^2$. Taking the infimum over all fillings of each null word before maximizing over words of length at most $n$ gives order $n^2/\log n$ in these presentations. Under a quadratic isoperimetric inequality, every non-hyperbolic group has, for each sufficiently large $n$, a null word of length at most $n$ whose least-area fillings have, for the face and vertex walks, $j$th Dirichlet eigenvalue of order $j/n^2$ for $1\le j\le cn^2$.

papers.title: A family of groups extending McLain's
papers.abstract: Given a strict partial order $Δ$ on a set $Λ$ and an arbitrary ring $R$ with $1\neq 0$, the corresponding McLain group $M(Δ)$ has been studied in depth. We construct a larger family of McLain groups $G(Δ)$, where $Δ$ need be neither asymmetric nor transitive, while satisfying two weaker axioms. Structural properties common to all members~$G(Δ)$ of this new family are investigated, including a group presentation, a description of the factors of its descending central series, a canonical form for its elements relative to any total order on~$Δ$, and a recursive determination of its upper central series. In addition, we prove the natural isomorphism $G(Δ)/G(Γ)\cong G(Δ\setminusΓ)$, where $Γ$ is a normal subset of $Δ$, and $G(Γ)$ and $G(Δ\setminusΓ)$ are extended McLain groups on their own right. This result has no parallel in the classical context.

papers.title: 2D inviscid Boussinesq equations and 3D axisymmetric Euler equations: (1) A unification ($Em$), (2) Finite-time blow-up of unified $(1+1)$D models on the horizontal ray ($Rm$) and on the vertical ray ($Zm$)
papers.abstract: This revision corrects the axis reduction of earlier versions and replaces the $(1+1)$-dimensional systems studied there. We unify the 2D inviscid Boussinesq ($m=1$) and 3D axisymmetric Euler ($m=2$) equations in Hou--Li type variables into one system $(Em)$ and restrict it to the horizontal ray, $(Rm)$, and the vertical ray, $(Zm)$, of the meridian plane. On the axes the angular pressure terms produce $P_{θθ}$, which we close by $x^{-2}P_{θθ}=-f\,P_{xx}$; consistency at the apex $x=0$ forces $f(t,0)\in\{0,2\}$, and we take $f\equiv2$. Then $(Rm)$ and $(Zm)$ are nonlocal transport systems with an explicit one-sided Hardy-type operator of order $k$. The apex values satisfy one closed ODE system, common to both rays, which we classify completely; for $λ=m^2(q+1)$, $b/a=m^2(mq+2)/(m^2q-2)$ it becomes a Constantin--Lax--Majda type equation, explicitly solvable in the CLM-2 case. We prove local well-posedness, show that smoothness is lost no later than the apex blow-up time $T_{\rm apex}$, construct exact cores around the apex, and show that the energy $E_m$ is finite if and only if $k>(m+3)/2$ or a flux at infinity vanishes. Hence, in explicit parameter windows, smooth compactly supported finite-energy data lose smoothness no later than $T_{\rm apex}$ while $E_m$ stays finite. A self-similar analysis describes the inner layer at the apex; for $(R2)$ in its window, computations show blow-up at the apex at $T_{\rm apex}$ with bounded energy, and the residual gap is explained by a short-wave instability seeded by rounding errors. No ratio $b/a$ gives both rays generically finite energy. Finally, with two closure functions the reduction is exact, the apex dynamics contains one free function, the anisotropy of the pressure Hessian at the origin, and we prove that keeping it in an explicit window forces finite-time blow-up of $(E1)$ and $(E2)$ themselves.

papers.title: On CR manifolds of CR dimension 1
papers.abstract: We classify all maximal symmetry models of CR dimension 1, depending on their Bloom-Graham and Tanaka types, give coordinate realization to some of those models and prove a general extension principle.

papers.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.

papers.title: On Big-M Reformulations of Bilevel Linear Programs: Hardness of A Posteriori Verification
papers.abstract: A standard approach to solving optimistic bilevel linear programs (BLPs) is to replace the lower-level problem with its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality conditions and reformulate the resulting complementarity constraints using auxiliary binary variables. This yields a single-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model involving big-$M$ parameters. While sufficiently large big-$M$s that preserve at least one bilevel-optimal solution can be computed in polynomial time, verifying a priori that given big-$M$s do not cut off any feasible or optimal lower-level solutions is known to be computationally difficult. In this paper, we establish two complementary hardness results. First, we show that, even with a single potentially incorrect big-$M$ parameter, it is coNP-complete to verify a posteriori whether a given optimal solution of the resulting MILP model is bilevel optimal. In particular, this negative result persists for min-max problems without coupling constraints and applies to strong-duality-based reformulations of mixed-integer BLPs. Second, we show that verifying global big-$M$ correctness remains computationally difficult a posteriori, even when an optimal solution of the MILP model is available.

papers.title: Quantile-Based Skewness for Fuzzy Numbers With Probabilistic Foundations: An Application in Portfolio Optimization
papers.abstract: This article quantifies asymmetry under imprecision by introducing a probabilistic interpretation for fuzzy numbers and a non-moment based skewness coefficient derived from it. The coefficient adapts classical quantile-based skewness measures (Bowley, Kelley, and Groeneveld-Meeden) to the $α$-cut representation of fuzzy numbers.
