For each $0<\varepsilon\leqslant 1$ we also construct a cover by half-spaces of measure at most $(1+\varepsilon)t$, with cardinality bounded by $$B_n\varepsilon^{-(n-1)/2}\frac{w_μ(t)-w_μ(a_nt)}{t}.$$ The exponent $(n-1)/2$ is optimal for $n\geqslant 2$, as shown by the Gaussian example. We further establish containment coverings for half-spaces in every dimension: there is a family of $O_n(w_μ(t)/t)$ Borel covering sets, each of $μ$-measure $O_n(t)$, such that every half-space of measure at most $t$ is contained in one covering set. We also obtain a relative wet-part estimate with sharp exponent $2/(n+1)$ and a reverse doubling inequality.

papers.title: Spin-geodesic systems
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability hypotheses, to ordinary rolling on a Euclidean hypersurface. Our second main result is a Liouville theorem: for an arbitrary symmetric spin-coupling field B, the spin-geodesic flow preserves the canonical Liouville volume on its mechanical phase space. This holds even though the flow is not symplectic unless $B$ is identically zero.

papers.title: The coordinate dependence of numerical rank: charts adapted to level sets
papers.abstract: Sampling a smooth field on a grid can give an array of high numerical rank even when the field is simple. A Gaussian ridge rotated off the grid axes is the standard example: in coordinates which follow the ridge, the same field has rank one. The rank therefore depends on the chart, that is, on the coordinates in which the field is sampled. We ask which properties of a chart control this rank. For a field which depends on position only through a function $φ$, a chart whose coordinate lines follow the level sets of $φ$ gives rank one. Building on this, we show four things. First, mesh quality does not control rank: a chart whose cells have perfect size and shape can still give infinite rank. Second, when a chart follows the level sets of an estimate of $φ$, the extra rank depends on a single quantity, the defect, which measures how much the true field varies along each coordinate line. Its size matters only logarithmically, its complexity through a count which cannot be improved in general, and when the defect is simple across the level sets the cost stays small. Third, whether the defect is simple can be checked by differentiating the true level function along the flow which builds the chart. Fourth, rank and invertibility fail differently. When the curve behind an offset chart is perturbed, the rank grows slowly, but the chart stops being invertible abruptly, once the offset exceeds the distance at which neighboring normals of the curve first cross. A chart built from the level sets of a field estimate stays invertible when the gradient of the estimate does not vanish on the band and the coordinate lines along each level set do not cross themselves. Pre-registered experiments in two dimensions show how far the bounds are from the observed ranks, and suggest when each kind of chart is preferable; two choices in the last comparison were made after the experiments.

papers.title: A Principled Framework for PDE-Based Shock Capturing in High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
papers.abstract: PDE-based artificial viscosity (AV) captures shocks in high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods by solving an auxiliary PDE for a smooth viscosity field. The behavior of that field is set by how the terms of the AV PDE scale with the element size $h$ and polynomial degree $p$, and by how its coefficients are parametrized. This work derives both choices from analysis and studies the impact these choices have on the implicit steady-state solver. First, an $L^2$-projection analysis shows that the thinnest shock a polynomial space can represent monotonically scales with the resolution length $\bar h = h/p$, and a scaling analysis of the AV PDE gives concrete conditions on its diffusion and source terms for the solution to be self-similar in $\bar h$. Prior formulations satisfy them only under $h$-refinement at fixed $p$; the AV PDE is scaled so that they hold under $hp$-refinement, and the captured shock thins accordingly. Second, a Green's-function analysis of the steady AV PDE gives closed-form expressions for the width and magnitude of the AV. In the standard parametrization the two are coupled: raising the diffusion coefficient widens the AV but lowers its peak. An alternative parametrization of the decay coefficient removes the coupling in the Green's-function response and inverts it in the coupled state-AV problem, so that widening the AV raises its peak instead of lowering it. Third, a parameter study on a Mach 5 viscous flow over a half-cylinder characterizes how the choice of solution variables and the AV PDE's time, width, and magnitude coefficients affect the robustness and cost of the implicit solve. The choice of variables dominates robustness, with entropy variables converging over the largest region of the width-magnitude parameter space. Together, the three contributions make PDE-based AV more predictable to tune and its implicit solve more robust.

papers.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
papers.abstract: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.

papers.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

papers.title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
papers.abstract: Let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $ρ$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $ρ$ on the $Π$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $ρ$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $ρ$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\barρ$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.

papers.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
papers.abstract: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

papers.title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $Ω$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $Ω$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$ in previous results with an explicit polynomial power of $\log\log\log x$.

papers.title: Limit theorems for almost conditionally identically distributed random variables
papers.abstract: $ξ$-Almost Conditional Identically Distributed ($ξ$-a.c.i.d.) random variables are generalizations of conditional identically distributed (c.i.d.) and exchangeable ones. $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in applications in statistics, such as in recursive algorithms and heteroskedastic observations, and are parametrized by a sequence $ξ=(ξ_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ that quantifies departure from the c.i.d. property. In this work, we extend limit theorems for exchangeable and c.i.d. random variables to the more general setting of $ξ$-a.c.i.d. random variables. After proving a Strong Law of Large Numbers, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic directing measure of the sequence to be absolutely continuous with respect to a given $σ$-finite measure. Then, under regularity assumptions on the parameter $ξ$, three different Central Limit Theorems for $ξ$-a.c.i.d. sequences are derived, involving the predictive, empirical and asymptotic directing distributions. These theorems have several statistical applications, including the construction of asymptotic credible intervals in Bayesian predictive inference.

papers.title: Exotic Universal Covers and Free Cyclic Actions from the Cartwright-Steger Surface
papers.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we construct a closed minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $35$, and signature $1$. The construction is a genus-five symplectic sum of a blowup of the regular fourfold Cartwright-Steger cover and a cyclic Akhmedov-Park manifold. The gluing identifies the homomorphisms from the two surface groups to $\Z/m$. The universal cover is minimal symplectic and is homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $(18m-1)\CP\#(17m-1)\CPb$. It admits a free symplectic action of $\Z/m$. Intermediate quotients give examples with fundamental group $\Z/n$ and characteristic numbers $(e,σ)=(35k,k)$ for every $n\geq2$ and $k\geq1$. Using the same Cartwright-Steger summand, we also construct, for every $m\geq2$, a minimal symplectic four-manifold with fundamental group $\Z/m$, Euler characteristic $31$, and signature $1$, whose minimal symplectic universal cover is an exotic copy of $(16m-1)\CP\#(15m-1)\CPb$ with a free symplectic $\Z/m$-action.

papers.title: The Z[tau]-foam: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam as arithmetic in the icosahedral module
papers.abstract: Goodman-Strauss's Dodecafoam is a substitution that fills the regular dodecahedron with dodecahedral bubbles of sizes tau^{-k}, tau=(1+sqrt(5))/2, using the seven kinds of cells into which the twelve planes of its stellation cut it. We rewrite it as exact arithmetic in one Z[tau]-module of rank three, the span M of the six five-fold axes, on which the icosahedral group acts by 120 matrices in GL(3,Z[tau]). A placed inflated copy of a cell is a union of cells iff its facet levels lie in {+-1,+-tau^3} and it lies in the dodecahedron. Solving this finite linear system for all scales at once gives exactly the 22 rules known from a geometric search; no rule exists at any scale other than 1,tau,tau^2,tau^3. The substitution becomes integer arithmetic on six-tuples and reproduces the bubbles of the geometric foam exactly. Whether a point of M is the centre of a bubble of size tau^{-k} is decided by at most k+3 exact sign vectors (its address), without building the foam, and all bubbles of one size are obtained by sieving the points of M whose Galois conjugate satisfies |x^*|<=2 tau^k, a bound we prove with computer assistance. The number of bubbles of size tau^{-k} is A beta^k+O(|beta'|^k) with beta=(1+sqrt(29))/2. Hence the closure of the rescaled conjugates of the bubble centres has box dimension at most log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3, and the bubbles are not selected by any cut-and-project window with interior. The other foams of the 1999 article are sub-foams of this one. The 50400 substitutions allowed by the rule list give 18899 bubble sets, and the Dodecafoam is a product set of 13440 of them, to the depth tested. In four dimensions the same linear system, for the star cut of the 120-cell, reproduces the 718 clusters of a geometric search and adds the scale sqrt(5) tau^2.

papers.title: Nonparametric estimation of a common marginal hazard function under censoring and spatio-temporal dependence
papers.abstract: This article investigates the nonparametric estimation of a common pooled marginal hazard function from right-censored durations exhibiting spatio-temporal dependence. We propose two estimators based respectively on the Nadaraya-Watson method and the (k)-nearest neighbors (k)-NN) approach. Under assumptions of stationarity, regularity, non-informative censoring, and weak spatio-temporal dependence, we establish their pointwise and uniform convergence rates as well as their optimal asymptotic order. A simulation study compares their finite-sample performance. Two real-data applications with right censoring are considered: a multicenter clinical trial with 53.8 percent censoring and 1,746 geolocated and time-stamped requests submitted to New York City's 311 municipal service, of which 35.5 percent are censored. The empirical results illustrate the relevance of the proposed methods in the presence of spatial and temporal dependence.

papers.title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
papers.abstract: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $λ^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper. The main new ingredient is a rigidity phenomenon: a pair as above, of size $n\ge2$, whose characteristic polynomial is congruent to $λ^n$ modulo $4$ is necessarily a fold of a smaller pair. It follows that such a pair is nilpotent as soon as its characteristic polynomial is congruent to $λ^n$ modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$. Finally we show that the eigenvalue zero of an $m\times m$ matrix in Corless's skew-symmetric family has multiplicity at most $2^{v_2(m+1)}-1$, with equality attained. The classification, the rigidity statement, the cardinality of the sets $\cN_n$ and the criterion modulo $2^{1+\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces revisited
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $Δ_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincaré inequality uniform in $s$, and the $Γ$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.

papers.title: Homological Properties of $L\otimes_{\Bbbk} N$
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian algebras over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ such that $A\otimes_\Bbbk B$ is Noetherian. Let $I$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$ and $B$, respectively, and let $L$ and $N$ be nonzero finitely generated modules over $A$ and $B$, respectively. In \cite{R4}, the author investigates the relationships between certain algebraic properties of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ and the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$, and vice versa. In the present paper, we characterize the Gorensteinness, approximate Cohen--Macaulayness, and maximal depth property of $L\otimes_\Bbbk N$ with respect to $\mathcal{I}=I\otimes_\Bbbk B+A\otimes_\Bbbk J$ in terms of the corresponding properties of $L$ and $N$ with respect to $I$ and $J$, respectively. In particular, when $A$ and $B$ are local rings, we describe these properties of $L \otimes_{\Bbbk} N$ as a module over the local ring $A \otimes_\Bbbk B$.

papers.title: Independent and end-faithful spanning trees in infinite graphs
papers.abstract: Spanning trees rooted at the same vertex are independent if, for each vertex other than the root, the paths from the root to that vertex are pairwise distinct and internally vertex-disjoint. Zehavi and Itai conjectured that, for every positive integer $k$, every finite $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. We show that every $2$-connected graph, finite or infinite, has two independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex. For locally finite $2$-connected graphs, both trees can be chosen end-faithful. We also prove that every locally finite $3$-connected chordal graph has three independent end-faithful spanning trees. Counterexamples show that local finiteness is essential for the version with independent end-faithful spanning trees. We further show that every $3$-connected graph with a universal vertex or a finite vertex cover has three independent spanning trees rooted at any prescribed vertex.

papers.title: Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
papers.abstract: We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. For a fixed geometry, latent responses and a Lipschitz bound are estimated jointly through a convex optimisation problem with constraints imposed on selected trajectory pairs. We show that the choice of fidelity loss leads to different structural behaviour: Huber regularisation strictly reduces the pair-restricted Lipschitz seminorm whenever the exact interpolant has a finite positive seminorm, whereas $L^1$ fidelity can preserve exact interpolation below a data-dependent threshold. For grouped observations, global and local Lipschitz structures are combined while keeping group identity outside the trajectory geometry. The global component draws on observations from other groups, while the local component uses each group's history to account for group-specific behaviour. We also characterise when group-specific observations can be fitted exactly under a shared Lipschitz bound and establish a regularity bound for the combined predictor. We describe a computational implementation based on constraint generation and illustrate the framework through an application to longitudinal sow-production data.

papers.title: Invariant subspace problem for trace-class perturbations of subnormal operators
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a subnormal operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $K$ be a trace class operator. In the present paper, we prove that $S+K$ has a nontrivial invariant subspace. Furthermore, for a normal operator $S$, we prove that if the Hausdorff dimension of $σ(S)$ is greater than $1$, then $S+K$ has a hyperinvariant half-space.

papers.title: Weak-Weak Stability for Multi-Species Nonlocal Cross-Diffusion Systems with Endpoint Lorentz Kernels
papers.abstract: The quantitative weak-weak stability for multi-species nonlocal cross-diffusion systems on the torus is established. The interactions of the species are described by a symmetric, positive semidefinite matrix-valued kernel whose gradient belongs to the endpoint Lorentz space $L^{d,\infty}$, where $d\ge 2$ is the space dimension. The central estimate, formulated in terms of a modulated Hellinger distance-interaction energy, yields uniqueness of solutions with finite Boltzmann entropy and Fisher information. The proof relies on a two-level endpoint mechanism: The Boltzmann entropy controls the interaction energy, while the Fisher information controls the associated force field. Further results are the immediate $L^2$ regularization and the exponential decay to the homogeneous equilibrium. As a particular application, uniqueness and stability for the two-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with periodic Coulomb kernels are obtained.

papers.title: Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk
papers.abstract: A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$. We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces. Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.

papers.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
papers.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradient-based inverse learning enables single- and multi-parameter identification, including simultaneous recovery of mode-resolved phonon relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates in steady-state and transient problems. GPU performance and scalability are evaluated with respect to spatial resolution, angular discretization, and phonon bands, including comparisons with an MPI-based BTE solver. JAX-Nano provides a unified computational framework for three-dimensional phonon transport, automatic differentiation, and inverse parameter identification, enabling sensitivity analysis and optimization of nanoscale thermal systems.

papers.title: Filters as a localization of nets
papers.abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.

papers.title: Uniform dominance of Golod local rings
papers.abstract: We prove that every Golod local ring $R$ is uniformly dominant. More precisely, we show that its dominant index is at most the embedding dimension of $R$. The proof is based on a numerical criterion for formality of bounded complexes whose homology is annihilated by the maximal ideal.

papers.title: A Class of Monotone Quasi-Newtonian Flows Coupled to Nonlinear Equations: Analysis and Finite Element Approximation
papers.abstract: We analyze a monotone quasi-Newtonian flow coupled with nonlinear heat and concentration equations. In the model, the viscosity depends on the temperature, the concentration, and the velocity gradient, and the diffusivities depend on the temperature and the concentration. We show the existence of weak solutions without smallness assumptions on the data, and their uniqueness under suitable smallness and regularity assumptions. For the numerical approximation, we consider the Taylor--Hood and mini elements. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to a subsequence, to a weak solution, and we derive a quasi-best approximation result and convergence rates. We present numerical experiments in two and three dimensions that illustrate the theory.

papers.title: $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over commutative Noetherian rings
papers.abstract: We prove $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over every commutative Noetherian ring.

papers.title: Questions, Explanation and Synthesis in Service Mathematics: Course Design with Didactic Units and Hybrid Teaching
papers.abstract: Students may have access to a convincing mathematical explanation without being able to reconstruct or adapt it. A course must provide opportunities to develop that understanding while keeping the work sustainable for students and teachers. This article develops a methodology for service mathematics in which a question ledger guides both course authoring and classroom decisions. Course-relative didactic units organise explanatory purposes, prerequisites and connections, initially calibrated by a five-to-seven-minute expert account. Teaching combines preparation, student exposition and supported repair with substantial teacher exposition and synthesis. Their allocation changes with the topic, audience and conditions of teaching. Compression and recovery explain how developed constructions become reusable while their grounds remain accessible. Three analyses from mathematics for computing-full Sudoku encoding, grayscale projection and a software failure contract-show how contrasting cases guide explanation and revision. The practice-informed contribution connects coherent course design with adaptable teaching and manageable preparation, and identifies questions for evaluating learning, participation and sustained teacher effort.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Payoff-Gradient Learning in Möbius Pricing Games
papers.abstract: We prove global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in every typewise Riemannian metric, which for scalar actions is the same as typewise mirror descent, with explicit rates, in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games that includes first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The result holds for symmetric self-play: all players use a common strategy and apply the same payoff-gradient update at each type. Convergence is from every continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy, including pooling, and does not rely on the monotonicity or Minty conditions that underlie existing guarantees in other games. Instead, the class is characterized by two structural properties: a direct payoff effect that is independent of the action, and a payoff difference at the allocation threshold that is affine in the action. These properties reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping equation for the common strategy, which, under the stated coefficient and metric assumptions, admits a unique viscosity solution. Comparison barriers make the uniform distance to the unique rest point a strict Lyapunov functional and yield convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents. In allocation games, the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under the stated tie-breaking conditions, and a positive lower slope bound converts strategy-error bounds into explicit approximate-equilibrium guarantees. A projected grid scheme with a slope floor makes the approximation constructive, with error bounds under deterministic perturbations and almost-sure convergence on a fixed grid under martingale gradient noise.

papers.title: An Efficient Long-Time Stable Second-Order Ensemble Method for the Parameterized Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: Ensemble simulations for uncertainty quantification, ensemble forecasting, and long-time statistics require stability over arbitrarily long horizons without time-step restrictions. We develop a second-order ensemble method for parameterized incompressible Navier--Stokes equations that uses a common, time-independent Brinkman (shifted Stokes) operator for all members. The scheme combines BDF2, a mean-reverting scalar auxiliary variable (mr-SAV) treatment of convection, and viscosity splitting with a shared viscosity $\barν$ treated implicitly and memberwise deviations explicitly. For constant viscosities satisfying $0<ν_j<4\barν/3$, we establish unconditional, uniform-in-time dissipativity under uniformly bounded forcing, including an absorbing bound independent of initial data and time-step size. We show that the upper viscosity threshold is sharp for fixed $\barν$. For spatially varying random viscosities, unconditional long-time stability holds under a signed pointwise condition that confines $ν_j$ to $(\barν/3,4\barν/3)$ uniformly away from the endpoints; for proportional spatial profiles, it holds over the full range $0<ν_j<4\barν/3$. Under the full-range constant-viscosity condition and sufficient regularity in two dimensions, we prove second-order temporal error bounds for velocity, the auxiliary variable, and the discrete time primitive of the pressure error. Numerical tests corroborate long-time stability at large time steps and the sharpness of the viscosity threshold, demonstrate accurate individual solutions and ensemble statistics, and show that mean reversion prevents long-time drift. Reusing the shared operator reduces computing time by about half relative to member-by-member solves.

papers.title: Multipliers and integration operators on Hardy--Bloch type tent spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the boundedness of integration operators $J_g$ and $I_g$ and pointwise multipliers $M_g$ on Hardy--Bloch type tent spaces $\mathcal{BT}^p$. The main difficulty is that these spaces are defined through a non-tangential maximal function of the radial derivative, which places the problem at the interface of holomorphic function theory and harmonic analysis. We completely characterize the boundedness of $I_g:\mathcal{BT}^p\to\mathcal{BT}^q$ for all $0<p,q<\infty$, and obtain a complete characterization for $J_g$ and $M_g$ when $p<q$. For $p\geq q$, we establish separate necessary and sufficient conditions. The proofs in the case $p\leq q$ are mainly based on some fractional maximal function estimates, whereas those in the case $p>q$ are mainly based on a synthesis lemma. We also give examples showing that several converse implications in the range $p\geq q$ fail.

papers.title: Mean First Passage Times for Loop-Erased Random Walks and Erased-Loop Size Distributions on Graphs
papers.abstract: Loop-erased random walks provide a natural way to extract self-avoiding trajectories from ordinary random walks by chronologically removing loops. They are deeply connected with uniform spanning trees: the loop-erased path between two vertices has the same distribution law as the unique path connecting these vertices in a random spanning tree. In this work, we use this connection as a computational framework for finite graphs. First, using the classical transfer-current theorem, we obtain an explicit formula for the mean first passage time of loop-erased random walks. The resulting expression returns the expected length of the loop-erased path as a weighted sum over simple paths, where the weights are exact determinantal probabilities obtained from the spanning-tree kernel. Second, we express the distribution of erased loop sizes in the same framework. This distribution measures the scale of the redundant excursions removed during loop erasure and provides information that is complementary to effective path length. The approach is applied to arbitrary finite graphs and then specialized to complete graphs, cycle graphs, and motif-based networks, where explicit formulas and asymptotic behaviors are obtained. Numerical experiments show strong agreement between the theoretical predictions and Monte Carlo simulations. The results provide a unified method for quantifying both the effective paths kept by loop erasure and the loops removed during random exploration of networks.

papers.title: A feasible point method for derivative-free linearly constrained optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework for linearly constrained derivative-free optimization (DFO) in which the original objective function is evaluated only at feasible points. The method first analyzes the linear constraint system using certificates of infeasibility and implied activity to detect infeasibility or a singleton feasible set, or, when the feasible set has positive dimension, to identify the affine subspace spanned by the feasible set and obtain an equivalent reduced representation with a strictly feasible base point. It then transforms the resulting reduced problem into an unconstrained optimization problem by means of a pointed feasible retraction and an exact penalty function. The retraction maps arbitrary trial points to feasible points by an explicit scaling in the reduced coordinates, so that no constrained optimization or projection subproblem is required during objective evaluations. This construction permits a broad range of unconstrained DFO methods to be used as inner solvers while preserving feasibility of the original objective evaluations. Numerical experiments compare several such variants on linearly constrained test problems of different dimensions. The results show that the choice of inner solver affects robustness, the number of problems solved, function-evaluation efficiency, and computational time, and that relative performance changes with problem dimension.

papers.title: Three almost symmetric metatiles generate the Spectre tiling
papers.abstract: We present a system of three `metatiles' for the Spectre aperiodic monotiling, named `D23'. These are similar in concept to the {\HTPF} system for the hat tiling: the metatiles have their own substitution system which can be iterated as many times as desired, and then the lowest-order metatiles can be converted into Spectre tiles. One of the three metatiles has order-2 rotational symmetry, and the other two are `almost symmetric' with orders 2 and 3 respectively, in the sense that although the region covered by the tile's $n$-times deflation is not exactly identical to its rotation, within their intersection, the proportion of non-matching tiles tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$. This near-symmetry corresponds to cases of near-symmetry in the Spectre tiling itself. A curious property of this system is that one of the three metatiles disappears completely in the conversion to Spectres!

papers.title: On Partially Totally Real Riemannian Maps and Their Sharp Curvature Inequalities
papers.abstract: We introduce partially totally real Riemannian maps into Kähler manifolds and examine the geometry of their associated distributions. For complex space forms, we obtain a Chen-type curvature inequality retaining the contributions of the mixed second fundamental form and O'Neill's tensor, together with an arbitrary-codimension estimate involving partial mean curvatures. We characterize equality in the principal inequality and give an example attaining the bound when $\dim\mathcal D\geq4$, including a case with nonintegrable horizontal distribution.

papers.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$. We also show that finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group of rank three are, up to isomorphism, precisely the products of finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona groups of ranks one and two. Four further groups can act faithfully on rationally connected threefolds. For each of these groups, the faithful action is unique up to birational conjugacy and automorphism of the acting group.

papers.title: Improved Singular Adams-type inequalities and the existence of extremals in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $H_0^2(Ω)$ denote the Sobolev space on $Ω$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain containing the origin, and let $λ(Ω)$ denote the first eigenvalue of the bi-Laplacian $Δ^2$ on $Ω$ subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish the following singular Adams inequality of Adimurthi-Druet type: for $0<β<4$ and $0\leqα<λ(Ω)$, \[ \sup\limits_{u\in H_0^2(Ω),\|Δu\|_2^2=1}\int_Ω\frac{e^{32π^2(1-\fracβ{4}) u^2(1+α\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^β}dx < +\infty. \] Moreover, this supremum is infinite for $α>λ_1(Ω)$. Furthermore, we show the existence of extremal functions, that is, for sufficiently small $α>0$, there exists $u^*\in H_0^2(Ω)\cap C_{\mathrm{loc}}^4(Ω\setminus{0})$ with $\|Δu^*\|_2^2=1$ such that \[ \int_Ω\frac{e^{32π^2(1-\fracβ{4}) {|u^*|}^2(1+α\|u^*\|_2^2)}}{|x|^β}dx=\sup\limits_{u\in H_0^2(Ω),\|Δu\|_2^2=1}\int_Ω\frac{e^{32π^2(1-\fracβ{4}) u^2(1+α\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^β}dx. \] These results can be regarded as a further development, in the singular setting, of the theory on the existence of extremals established by Lu and Yang [Adv. Math. (2009)]. Our proof relies on the blow-up analysis of the subcritical maximizers, combined with biharmonic truncation adapted to the singular weight, capacity-type estimates on annular regions and a test function argument. A key novelty of our approach lies in carrying out the blow-up analysis without relying on an explicit expression for the limiting profile near the blow-up point, which is unavailable in the present setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform such a blow-up analysis without the explicit form of the limiting profile.

papers.title: Learning the Boltzmann Collision Operator with Structural Constraints for Fast Kinetic Simulation
papers.abstract: The high-dimensional integration in the Boltzmann collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in deterministic kinetic simulations. We develop a structure-preserving neural operator that provides an efficient approximation of this nonlinear collision mapping. The operator maintains the gain-loss structure of the original Boltzmann collision operator, and, by construction, is proportional to the square of the gas density. Conservative moment projection and entropy correction enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as entropy dissipation. By construction, the collision term also vanishes at all Maxwellians. In the numerical scheme for simulations of gas dynamics, we establish nonnegativity of the distribution function with the learned collision operator and prove exponential relaxation to the moment-matched equilibrium when a positive spectral gap is imposed. Numerical experiments for a constant collision kernel demonstrate a favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff relative to Fourier spectral evaluations. Although trained on smooth distributions, the same operator handles discontinuous distribution functions and is embedded without retraining in steady Couette flow, normal-shock, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity solvers. These results demonstrate a reusable approximation for repeated collision evaluations that retains kinetic structure and supports accurate deterministic simulation.

papers.title: Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
papers.abstract: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers. Introducing auxiliary variables eliminates higher-order derivatives from the PDE residuals, while separate random feature bases in the unknowns provide flexibility in approximating fields with different scales and regularity. For the CH equation, we scale the chemical potential to address the disparity between its magnitude and that of the phase field. We compare the first-order and corresponding higher-order formulations and systematically examine the effects of initialization distributions, the random feature range $R_ξ$, seven activation functions, and dense versus separable space-time bases. We also evaluate gradient-based adaptive sampling, residual reweighting, and mild spatial derivative-penalty regularization. Across the reported benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces relative $L^2$ and absolute $L^\infty$ errors by nearly one to three orders of magnitude compared with the various PINN baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of first-order RPNNs for accurate approximation of phase-field dynamics with sharp transition layers.

papers.title: Torrelli's Question for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Torrelli asked whether the class $[1/f]$ belongs to the intersection homology $\mathcal{D}$-module of a hypersurface if and only if $-1$ is a simple root of its local Bernstein-Sato polynomial. We prove this equivalence for isolated hypersurface germs with $2\le n\le 4$ variables, and we construct isolated counterexamples with $n$ variables for every $n\ge 5$. In fact a counterexample with $[1/f]\in\mathrm{IC}_D$ and $\mathrm{mult}_{s=-1}b_f(s)=r\ge 2$ always needs at least $r+3$ variables. The counterexamples modify a three-variable example of Saito and adjoin suitable pure powers in the new variables. We also show that a counterexample polynomial in $n$ variables needs at least $n+1$ monomials, and we record further cases in which the equivalence holds.

papers.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.

papers.title: The Dynamical Manin-Mumford Conjecture for automorphisms of Hénon type
papers.abstract: We prove the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture for polynomial automorphisms of the complex affine plane of dynamical degree $>1$ proposed by Dujardin and Favre. More precisely, we prove that an irreducible algebraic curve contains infinitely many periodic points of such an automorphism if and only if it is the fixed locus of a polynomial involution conjugating some iterate of the automorphism to its inverse.

papers.title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
papers.abstract: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$. More precisely, we show that the quotient of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ by the relevant power of $2$ is odd exactly when $n$ is an odd square, or $2$, $3$ or $6$ times an odd square, depending on $k$. As a consequence, we obtain several new infinite families of congruences modulo arbitrary powers of $2$, such as \[ \text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(3n+2)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+4}}, \] and \[\text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(6n+5)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+5}}. \] We also obtain an analogous improvement of a result of Li and Tang (2026) modulo powers of $3$, and an infinite family of internal congruences modulo powers of $2$.

papers.title: Censored Regression Models with Endogeneity: A Survey
papers.abstract: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of methodologies developed to handle endogeneity in censored regression models. We emphasize their theoretical basis, and estimating methodologies. The paper summarizes the benefits and drawbacks of each technique and addresses expansions to nonlinear, panel, and high-dimensional settings, offering researchers practical assistance and identifying options for future methodological improvement in censored models with endogenous regressors.

papers.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
papers.abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and Röhrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.

papers.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
papers.abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.

papers.title: Polynomial identities of the two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra
papers.abstract: We describe a basis for the polynomial identities satisfied by the unique two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra $B$ over a field of characteristic zero. Modulo the right-symmetric identity, this basis consists of two irreducible identities of degree three. We construct linear bases for the multilinear components of the relatively free algebra of the variety $\mathcal V=\operatorname{var}(B)$ and determine their decompositions into Specht modules. Using the resulting $S_n$-module decompositions, we prove that the commutator subspace is right nilpotent in every proper subvariety of $\mathcal V$. Moreover, in any proper subvariety satisfying a nontrivial identity of degree $n\ge2$, the index of right nilpotence of the commutator subspace is at most $2n$.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_β$-Gradient Flow in a Kähler Surface
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_β$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact Kähler surface, with $β> 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

papers.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

papers.title: Profinite groups with coprime automorphisms whose orbits generate nilpotent subgroups
papers.abstract: Suppose that a profinite group $G$ admits a finite group of coprime automorphisms $A$ such that for any $\varphi\in A$ every subgroup $\langle x^{\langle\varphi\rangle}\rangle$ generated by the $\langle\varphi\rangle$-orbit of an element $x\in G$ is nilpotent. It is proved that $[G,A]$ is pronilpotent, and if $A$ is soluble and the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(A)$ is locally nilpotent, then $G$ is locally nilpotent.

papers.title: Worst case tractability of weighted linear tensor product problems under the absolute error criterion
papers.abstract: This paper studies weighted linear tensor product problems in the worst case setting. We consider algorithms that use finitely many evaluations of arbitrary continuous linear functionals. We investigate algebraic and exponential tractability under the absolute error criterion in the case $λ_1>1$, where $λ_1$ is the square of the univariate maximal singular value. We obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for various notions of algebraic and exponential tractability on weights and univariate singular values. Our approach is to convert algebraic tractability of the problems for the absolute error criterion with $λ_1 > 1$ to exponential tractability of the normalized problems. Specifically, we solve Open Problem 27 as posed by Novak and Woźniakowski (2008).

papers.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
papers.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.

papers.title: Normal Homogeneous Counterexamples to Wolf's Homogeneity Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct free Clifford--Wolf subgroups of order two whose quotients of compact, connected, simply connected normal homogeneous manifolds are not homogeneous. The universal covers are the oriented real flag manifolds $M_{d}=SO(N)/\prod_{i=1}^{q}SO(d_{i})$, equipped with the metric induced by the negative Killing form, where $N\geq4$ and $q\geq3$ is odd. We determine its full connected centralizer, the effective connected isometry group of the quotient, and the corresponding orbit space. These calculations prove nonhomogeneity and give explicit formulas for the cohomogeneity, fundamental group, and Euler characteristic. These examples are found by ChatGPT 6 Astra.

papers.title: Exact-Order Mellin Transfer and Prime-Support Filtrations
papers.abstract: We establish a unified exact-order Mellin transfer principle that converts the multiplicity of a critical Mellin pole into arithmetic prime-support depth. For an exact-order Möbius transform in lattice dimension $\ell$, a base pole of order $r$ at $s=\ell/2$ satisfies \[ \ord_{s=\ell/2}\widehat{\mathscr P_{N,\ell}H}=ω(N)-r. \] The complete Jordan--Mellin jet is explicit, and its first surviving coefficient selects the canonical weight $W(N)=\prod_{p\mid N}\log p$. After the corresponding jet normalization, this weight governs a kernel-independent moving-support law and a mod-Poisson regime. With simultaneous splitting marks in finite Galois extensions, the same weight yields a multivariate polynomial whose mixed coefficients are reciprocal compositum degrees; it recovers pairwise intersection degrees and, under a full-rank hypothesis, also governs the coupled saddle and large-deviation geometry. In spectral geometry, a two-variable family attached to any positive self-adjoint elliptic operator has a transverse normal crossing whose parameter jets generate every higher critical pole order; exact-order dilation therefore realizes every positive prime-support depth. An explicit Bernoulli--Barnes/Barnes--Epstein model shows how a pole collision shifts the finite critical layer from one-prime to two-prime support. Thus arithmetic support, Galois compositum data, and spectral pole geometry arise from one exact-order Mellin mechanism.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
papers.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: An Algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay
papers.abstract: A 4-dimensional algebra with straightening laws which is an integral domain and which is not Cohen--Macaulay over an arbitrary field is constructed. Furthermore, it is shown that every three-dimensional graded ASL domain is Cohen--Macaulay.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Two-Dimensional Poiseuille Flow via a Dilation Multiplier
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear stability of the Poiseuille flow for 2D incompressible Navier Stokes equations.The key observation is that, after Fourier transformation, the Poiseuille flow and its curvature give rise to a kinetic operator and a potential whose commutators with the same bounded dilation multiplier are both nonnegative.To close the nonlinear estimates, we incorporate the zero mode of the initial velocity into the background shear flow, thereby further improving the threshold.

papers.title: On a simple family of Ricci-flows of O(3)-hypersurfaces: Counterexamples to the theorem on the preservation of positive definite Ricci curvature everywhere
papers.abstract: This note provides a concise derivation of the equation of Ricci áows on O(n)-rotational hypersurfaces in En+1 which consists of a pair of parabolic equations (cf. Lemma 2 of ß4) via simple applications of classical theorems of rotational surfaces in E3, governing the Ricci-evolution of their generating plane curves. Furthermore, the second equation can be transformed to that of the evolution equation of their "curvature proÖles" (cf. Lemmas 3 and 3íof ß4). In ß5, we consider a speciÖc family of initial generating curves of "curvature proÖles" that are only tiny modiÖcations of the constant function K= 1 R ;R 1, in a very small vicinity of the symmetric middle point as indicated in Fig. 2. Note that the short-time unique existence of analytic solutions of such a simple system of parabolic equations follows simply via Nash-Moser Theory. The simple estimate of ß5 shows the curvature k1( t(0)) is already becoming negative at a very short time (cf. ß5.3).

papers.title: Integral abelianizations of higher spin Torelli subgroups
papers.abstract: We determine the integral abelianizations of the Torelli subgroups preserving an $r$-spin structure for $r\geqslant2$ and genus $g\geqslant5$. Set $n=r/\gcd(r,2)$. For a surface with one boundary component, the free rank agrees with that of the Torelli group, and the torsion subgroup is the direct sum of the usual Birman--Craggs--Johnson $2$-torsion and $\mathbb{Z}/n^2\mathbb{Z}$. For a closed surface, an $r$-spin structure exists precisely when $n\mid g-1$, and the same description holds with the additional cyclic factor replaced by $\mathbb{Z}/\gcd(n^2,g-1)\mathbb{Z}$. The additional cyclic torsion is determined by the Casson--Morita homomorphism.

papers.title: The inverse Erdős--Fuchs problem for $k$-fold sums
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $k\ge 3$, we construct an infinite set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{h\le n}r_{kA}(h)=Γ(1+1/k)^k n+O_k(n^{(1-1/k)^2})$, where $r_{kA}(h)$ counts ordered representations of $h$ as a sum of $k$ elements of $A$, with repetitions allowed. This improves Dai and Pan's bound for a linear main term. In the paired random model used here, fluctuations of the stated order occur infinitely often almost surely.

papers.title: Differentiability of the solution to an SPDE with respect to the model for the associated regularity structure
papers.abstract: Given a stochastic partial differential equation that falls within the scope of the theory of regularity structures, we show that its solution is, in a suitable sense, a smooth function of the underlying model. This allows one to infer the regularity of the solution with respect to any perturbation of the noise from that of the model. As an application of our results, we provide an elementary proof of the Malliavin differentiability of solutions to a wide class of equations driven by Gaussian noises.

papers.title: Coordinate Ordering and Non-collinear Central Configurations
papers.abstract: We establish a mass-independent criterion for N-body central configurations based on a special coordinate ordering of the bodies. Moreover, we identify a region in the plane that contains no non-collinear central configurations. This provides a way to exclude non-collinear central configurations that are nearly collinear.

papers.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
papers.abstract: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

papers.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
papers.abstract: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor

papers.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
papers.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

papers.title: Tuning the false discovery rate in the closed eBH procedure
papers.abstract: The closed eBH procedure controls the false discovery rate under arbitrary dependence between the input e-values. It takes the target false discovery rate $α$ as its input and outputs a rejection set $R$, the usual goal being to maximize its size $\left|R\right|$. This note discusses a modification of the closed eBH procedure that allows choosing the target false discovery rate post hoc: the rejection set and its level $α$ can be chosen after seeing the data, and the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to $α$ is at most 1. We adapt Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to computing, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations $(\left|R\right|,α)$ of the size of a rejection set $R$ and its level $α$. The frontier allows us to compute an optimal rejection set in view of a given utility function $F$, $F(\left|R\right|,α)\to\max$, striking a balance between the goals of reducing $α$ and increasing $\left|R\right|$.

papers.title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove an Erdős-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.

papers.title: Weak-type bow shocks
papers.abstract: An existence proof is given for bow shocks ahead of blunt convex wedges that are transonic and of weak type at infinity, including cases for arbitrarily small shock strength. It is also proven that any such flow is necessarily univalent, meaning the position-to-velocity map is injective.

papers.title: Pre-d-algebras, pre-f-algebras and their completions
papers.abstract: We define pre-d- and pre-f-algebras on Archimedean pre-Riesz spaces by conditions on the order and the multiplication only, and show that a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if its multiplication extends to an f-algebra multiplication on its Riesz completion. On order dense subspaces of C(K), K a compact Hausdorff space, in which disjoint positive elements separate the points of K, a pre-Riesz algebra is a pre-f-algebra if and only if multiplication by every positive element is band preserving

papers.title: An extension of Janowski functions with applications
papers.abstract: Janowski functions are regular functions of the form $p(z)=1+p_1z+\cdots$, which are subordinate to $L_0(a,b:z)=(1+az)/(1+bz)$ for real numbers $a,b$ such that $-1\leq b<a\leq 1$. In this paper, we expand the space of the constants, $a$ and $b$, of the superordinate function, $L_0(a,b:z)$, to a larger set of complex numbers and provide some applications.

papers.title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
papers.abstract: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. If the positive perturbation is summable at the normalized scale, the normalized process converges to a finite non-negative limit; strict positivity is then equivalent to absolute summability of the relative perturbation. We also give criteria for divergence of the contraction-adjusted state, first-order comparisons, and counterexamples illustrating the role of the hypotheses. Harmonic step sizes yield exact power laws with strictly positive random coefficients. Applications include learning automata, urns with signed sampling bias, response-adaptive reinforcement, generalized Simon models with signed updates, branching processes in varying environments, and linear stochastic approximation with multiplicative noise.

papers.title: Structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations with gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a structure-preserving active flux method for the compressible Euler equations under gravitational fields, ensuring exactness for the generalized hydrostatic equilibrium state and the preservation of positivity for both density and pressure. This approach entails the update of the cell average and the point values simultaneously. To obtain the equilibrium preservation of the scheme for the cell average, the strategy pursued is to reformulate the gravitational term using the steady state solution, followed by the application of a decomposition algorithm. For the point values, we introduce minor adjustments to the Lax-Friedrichs flux vector splitting, coupled with the same finite difference operator performed on the flux and source term to restore the well-balancedness. Furthermore, a posteriori Multi-dimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) paradigm is adopted for achieving positivity preservation and oscillation control near strong discontinuities. A series of numerical experiments are performed to verify the high-order accuracy of our proposed method, along with its exact equilibrium and positivity preservation, and its ability to capture small perturbations at or close to steady flow without spurious oscillations.

papers.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of Böhning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

papers.title: The Space of $k$-Positive Potentials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study weak geodesics in the space of $k$-positive potentials on a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that any two smooth strictly $k$-positive potentials can be joined by a weak geodesic of class $C^{1,1}$. As an application, we prove that the pair $(\mathcal H_k,d_2)$ is a metric space.

papers.title: Well-balanced nodal finite volume WENO scheme with flux localization for hyperbolic balance laws
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general framework for constructing arbitrarily high-order well-balanced ``nodal" finite volume weighted essentially non-oscillatory (WENO) schemes, specifically tailored for hyperbolic balance laws. To handle complex systems involving nonconservative products and steady-state solutions with global integral quantities, we introduce a flux localization technique. This technique defines the numerical fluxes, incorporating the entire source term and nonconservative products, locally within each computational cell. By exactly preserving the nodal equilibrium state and conservatively updating the cell averages within a finite volume framework, the method avoids both reference-state reconstruction and the use of ODE solvers. The well-balanced property is achieved by performing high-order WENO reconstruction and employing a linear segment path in terms of equilibrium variables, rather than conservative ones. A rigorous theoretical analysis confirms that the scheme exactly preserves all the targeted stationary solutions. The effectiveness and versatility of the proposed method are demonstrated through a series of numerical experiments on various systems of hyperbolic balance laws.

papers.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

papers.title: Interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control for partitioned multiphysics systems
papers.abstract: We develop an interface-aware dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) formulation for multiphysics systems, within an optimization-based partitioned coupling framework. The finite-element interface-input operator is projected onto the reduced space and kept fixed during identification, while the unknown state-dependent local dynamics are learned from trajectory data. The common interface control is recomputed online by minimizing the mismatch between the reconstructed physical interface quantities. The formulation accommodates local subproblems governed by ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and differential--algebraic equations (DAEs). For a DAE subproblem, tangent projection identifies the state dynamics, whereas a residualized normal regression identifies the pressure balance and provides an algebraic pressure reconstruction. We further propose regularized quadratic correction DMDc to enrich the tangent dynamics and, for DAEs, the normal pressure balance through jointly fitted linear and compact quadratic operators. Feature normalization and block-dependent regularization control the enlarged regression while retaining the prescribed interface operators and identified DAE geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on problems involving both ODE--ODE and DAE--ODE couplings. The numerical results demonstrate accurate predictions and stable long-time behavior.

papers.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
papers.abstract: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Spherical Brownian Motion collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the quantitative convergence of the spherical Brownian motion (SBM) collisional particle system for the Maxwellian Landau equation via Wasserstein distances. When used as numerical method, it enjoys linear complexity $O(N)$ in particle number $N$, and conserves the momentum and energy almost surely. Moreover, only random grouping and sampling are needed for simulations without further numerical discretization. In the first part, we identify the large particle mean field limit of the system, and the Wasserstein convergence to the limit is justified through a coupling similar to the recent work for the Nanbu type Monte Carlo method \cite{BorghiPareschi2025}. The key difference is that the particles in our coupled shadow system are not i.i.d. due to the perfect matching. In the second part, the convergence of the mean field dynamics to the Landau solution is justified by the relative entropy with a bound $O(τ^2)$, being $τ$ the stepsize. This results in an $O(τ)$ bound for the Wasserstein distance error. A crucial technical tool in the convergence in relative entropy is to provide suitable bounds on the derivatives of the logarithmic density or score function in the mean field dynamics. The combination of these estimates leads to the full convergence of the squared Wasserstein distance with order $O(N^{-1/2}+τ^2)$ for the numerical scheme in $d=3$.

papers.title: A $C_2$-cofinite non-rational principal $W$-algebra of type $D_4$
papers.abstract: We show that a simple principal $W$-algebra can be $C_2$-cofinite and non-rational. For $\mathcal W=\mathcal W_{-38/7}(D_4,f_{\mathrm{reg}})$ of central charge $-50$, D. Xie predicted seventeen irreducible modules and a logarithmic module of lowest conformal weight $-2$. We determine the Zhu algebra $A(\mathcal W)$ and the Poisson algebra $R_{\mathcal W}=\mathcal W/C_2(\mathcal W)$. Both have dimension $18$, and $A(\mathcal W)\cong\mathbb{C}^{16}\times\mathbb{C}[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$. We construct all seventeen irreducible $\mathcal W$-modules using the realization of $\mathcal W$ as a diagonal coset in $L_{-14/3}(D_4)\otimes L_1(D_4)$ and our previous classification of irreducible $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-modules in the category $\mathcal O$. We also construct an indecomposable $L_{-14/3}(D_4)$-module and use the coset realization to obtain an indecomposable logarithmic $\mathcal W$-module. Its lowest generalized $L(0)$-eigenspace is two-dimensional, and $L(0)$ acts on this space by a nontrivial Jordan block with eigenvalue $-2$.

papers.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$.
