Each bipartite graph has this property. We unravel the structure of the family MACL(G) of all maximum anticliques (independent sets) of a König-Egarváry graph G. This enables us to enumerate $MACL(G)$ not only in output polynomial time, but also in a compressed format (using wildcards). All of this can be viewed as an instance where ALL minimum solutions of a submodular function can be enumerated efficiently.

papers.title: Isolation in Random Graphs
papers.abstract: We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $γ(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $ι(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$. We also identify a transition in the gap $γ(G)-ι(G)$ when $\log(1/p)=o(\log n)$. This gap tends to infinity in probability when $p$ is well below $(\log\log n/\log n)^2$ and is at most one with high probability when $p$ is well above this scale. Finally, for every fixed graph $F$, we show that the classical minimum degree bound for domination is asymptotically sharp for $F$-isolation, even for regular host graphs.

papers.title: Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
papers.abstract: The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order Hölder source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius larger than the circumradius. For a simply connected obstacle with analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and conformal center inside the obstacle, a Faber--Vekua normal form gives the sharp spectral law in terms of logarithmic capacity, with the same leading constant as for the disc. This class includes every convex analytic obstacle. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral transition and illustrate its use in choosing the regularization level. The analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction.

papers.title: A rigorous Abel-summed Hardy-type identity for $p$-circle domains via regularized Poisson summation
papers.abstract: In our previous work, a generalized Hardy-type identity (GHI) for astroid-type $p$-circle domains was formally derived in terms of generalized $p$-Bessel functions. However, the direct application of the Poisson summation formula to the indicator functions of these domains leaves the convergence and rigorous justification of the resulting oscillatory series unresolved. In the present paper, we address this difficulty by introducing an anisotropic regularization based on convolution kernels with Fourier multipliers $e^{-t(|ξ_{1}|^p+|ξ_{2}|^{p})}$. We establish the corresponding regularized Poisson summation identity and rigorously justify the limiting process through uniform estimates for lattice-point sums. A key feature of our analysis is the determination of boundary contributions: smooth boundary points carry weight $1/2$, whereas the contributions from axial cusps vanish for $0<p<1$. These results lead to an Abel-summed GHI, expressed in terms of the distorted-angle-dependent $p$-Bessel functions introduced in our previous work, with explicit boundary corrections. In particular, for $p=2$, the identity recovers the Abel-summed form of the classical Hardy--Voronoï Bessel series. Our result provides a rigorous regularized counterpart of the previously proposed identity, while the convergence of the corresponding unregularized series remains a separate problem.

papers.title: Avoiding squares over words with lists of size three
papers.abstract: We prove that every sequence of lists of size three admits an infinite square-free word, establishing that the Thue choice number of the path is three. More precisely, the number of compatible square-free words of length $n$ is at least $c(5/4)^n$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. The proof combines a computer-assisted construction of weights with the weighted counting method previously introduced by the author. We first consider words avoiding only squares of bounded period and use a finite state model to certify a uniform lower bound on their growth. The counting argument then controls the loss caused by excluding longer squares. The main new ingredient is a coarser description of the states, which makes the computation feasible without restricting the union of the lists. The same computation yields a deterministic polynomial-time strategy for constructing an infinite square-free word when each list is chosen adversarially after the preceding letters have been fixed.

papers.title: An Optimal Liouville Theorem for the Fully Fractional Heat Equation
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonnegative entire classical solution of the fully fractional heat equation $(\partial_t-Δ)^s u=u^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero for $n\geq2$, $0<s<1$, and $1<p<(n+2s)/(n-2s)$. No global boundedness, decay, or symmetry assumptions are required for the solutions. The exponent range is sharp, since the critical equation admits positive stationary solutions. Our result provides a fractional counterpart of Quittner's optimal Liouville theorem for the classical semilinear heat equation, while our proof follows a new and simpler approach. For bounded solutions, we combine elliptic nonexistence and compactness to control superlevel set measures by the local energy dissipation of the weighted extension. A local energy inequality then gives nonexistence by iteration. Doubling, local regularity, and a nonlocal convergence theorem yield a universal pointwise bound in terms of the parabolic distance to the boundary, which implies our Liouville theorem for general solutions.

papers.title: A reciprocal-matrix proof of Sendov's theorem and applications to control theory
papers.abstract: This proof grew out of the author's research on interpreting mathematical statements from the viewpoint of control theory. Its value lies both in the understanding it brings and in the applications that arise from the argument. Let $a$ be a simple zero of a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points, counted with multiplicity, then the reciprocals $1/(a-c_j)$ are the eigenvalues of an explicit matrix built from the other zeros. A failure of Sendov's bound at $a$ would therefore make the associated discrete-time system asymptotically stable. This observation leads to an alternative proof of the quadratic inequality of Tang and Zhang, including its equality case. Building on the reflection and centering arguments of Mazur, Tao and Zhang, we estimate the change in the integral of the derivative product when all the reciprocal displacements are replaced by their mean $s$. An exact pairwise cancellation bounds the difference in terms of the variance. For an interior zero rotated to $0<a<1$, the normalized trace $s$ determines a contour through $\overline{s}/a$. If the mean squared reciprocal distance is at most one, integration along this contour gives $(n-1)(2a\Re(s)-a^2)<20$. A uniform phase estimate and reflection at $1/a$ then rule out this possibility in every degree $n\ge 257$. A fourth-moment estimate treats degrees two through five. For degrees five through 256, three bounds derived from one polynomial moment identity exclude the full range of the two remaining real parameters by exact integer arithmetic. As an application, Sendov's theorem illustrates how differentiating the denominator of a closed-loop transfer function can increase robustness in discrete-time systems and decrease it in continuous-time systems. The proofs have been formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Pathwise Factorization and Uncertainty Quantification for Impedance Obstacles with Random Boundaries
papers.abstract: We develop a factorization method with finite-sample statistical guarantees for two-dimensional acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles whose boundary is random and whose data are finitely many noisy multistatic measurements. In the two-dimensional far-field normalization, the symmetrization must act on a phase-rotated far-field operator; we prove the optical and range identities for every realization of a compact family of uniformly bi-Lipschitz domains, with jointly measurable regularized indicators. A quadrature-weighted finite-sample analysis separates angular approximation, measurement noise, test-vector error, and regularization, and yields a consistency theorem for empirical means and variances, joint in all data parameters. Bounded indicators admit simultaneous confidence bands, a diagonal threshold recovers the probability that a sampling point lies in the random obstacle, and a nested design yields unbiased variance components. Computations use a combined-field integral equation proved invertible at all frequencies, and the finite-grid guarantees are examined in a coverage study against a high-accuracy Monte Carlo reference.

papers.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
papers.abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $ξ$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

papers.title: Generalized anti-Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: The anti-Ramsey number was introduced by Erdős, Simonovits, and Sós and is defined to be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color the edges of a graph to avoid a rainbow copy of some graph. One can generalize this by, instead of forbidding a rainbow copy of a graph, putting a cap on the number of colors that appear on any copy of that graph. To be precise, let $\AR(G,H,q)$ be the maximum number of colors that can be used to color $E(G)$ so that every copy of $H$ sees at most $q$ colors. One can see that $\AR(G,H,q)$ is nondecreasing in $q$. In this paper, we investigate the linear and quadratic thresholds of $\AR(G,H,q)$ when $G=K_n$ and $H$ is connected.

papers.title: Cohomology of twisted tensor products over commutative rings
papers.abstract: Over a commutative ground ring, cohomology of a twisted tensor product of two rings mixes their cohomology via the twisting. We focus on bicharacter twistings and give explicit descriptions when the ground ring is itself a module. We state our main results for ground rings that are hereditary and contain roots of unity corresponding to finite grading groups. As a class of examples, we compute cohomology rings of Taft orders over cyclotomic integers.

papers.title: Connected Cayley Approximation of Power Graphs of Finite Groups
papers.abstract: For a nontrivial finite group \(G\), we define its connected intersection density as the maximum, over all connected Cayley graphs on \(G\), of the proportion of edges that also belong to the undirected power graph of \(G\). We show that this density is \(1\) if and only if \(G\) is cyclic, and that it is \(1/4\), \(1/6\), and \(1/12\) for \(A_4\), \(S_4\), and \(A_5\), respectively. For the dihedral group of order \(2n\), with \(n\geq 3\), we give a general formula and show that the connected intersection density equals \((\binom{n}{2}+1)/n^2\) if and only if \(n\) is a prime power. We also give a formula for the connected intersection density of dicyclic groups. For generalized quaternion groups of order \(2N\), where \(N=2^{m-1}\geq 4\), the density is \(\frac{N^2+8}{2N(N+1)}\). For the elementary abelian group \(C_p^r\), where \(p\) is prime and \(r\geq 1\), the density is \(p^{1-r}\).

papers.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
papers.abstract: Let $Φ(P)=|P|μ_1(P)$, where $μ_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $Φ$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $Φ(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szegő--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.

papers.title: Dynabase: A Database of Extreme Examples in Arithmetic Dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce Dynabase, a database cataloging extreme examples in arithmetic dynamics related to several major open conjectures: the Morton--Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture and the dynamical analogue of Lang's conjecture on canonical heights, as well as data on postcritically finite maps and maps with nontrivial automorphisms. This database collects the known examples of extreme behavior for these problems and tracks the current status of subproblems based on degree and field of definition.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial Approximants vanishing arbitrarily close to the origin
papers.abstract: This work concerns a sequence of stable polynomials on the bidisk whose affine optimal polynomial approximants in the Hardy space of the bidisk have zero varieties that come arbitrarily close to the origin.

papers.title: Partial sums of Rogers-Ramanujan functions
papers.abstract: Explicit positive multisums on base q^5 for the Rogers-Ramanujan sum function and its partial sum are given. 32 combinatorial interpretations for these identities are given. The classical mod 5 Rogers-Ramanujan identities are recovered as a limiting case. These results are equivalent to a quintic basic hypergeometric identity.

papers.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose window is a line segment is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice: if $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3$ is a plane which is not spanned by vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^3$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$, and $σ$ is a segment of any length which is transverse to $V$, then the set of points $v\in V$ with $v+x\inσ+\mathbb{Z}^3$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}^2$. For planes of Diophantine slope this is a theorem of Burago and Kleiner, and the point of the present paper is that no Diophantine condition on the plane is needed. We also show that the same conclusion holds when the window is a finite union of intervals. Together with the author's construction of a cut-and-project set in a plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window of countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to any lattice, this shows that for planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ the answer to the bi-Lipschitz question depends on the shape of the window rather than on the Diophantine properties of the plane.

papers.title: Arinkin's sheaf and Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract: Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincaré bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincaré kernel for an elliptic surface. As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both. We also construct an explicit deformation that connects Markman's construction of a projectively hyperholomorphic bundle on products of hyper-Kähler manifolds of K3${}^{[g]}$-type to that of Hartlieb and Shah. This answers a question of Hartlieb and Shah.

papers.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
papers.abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.

papers.title: A posteriori estimates for inverse evolutionary problems
papers.abstract: The paper is focused on a posteriori error analysis of evolutionary problems, which are ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. They may have no solutions and respective approximations may be highly unstable. For these problems, the a posteriori error estimation concept applicable to well-posed problems is not valid and requires a significant reformulation. A posteriori estimates of the functional type provide the basis for addressing this issue. They generate computable quantities that estimate the distance between a function (approximate solution to the inverse problem) and exact solution of a "close" well-posed initial boundary value problem associated with the same differential equation. The solution of this close problem exactly satisfies one part of the imposed conditions and the others are satisfied approximately with the accuracy $\eps$. This idea is elaborated for several evolutionary problems generated by the reaction-convection-diffusion equation: backward parabolic problem, problem with non-local time conditions, Cauchy parabolic problem, and parameter(s) identification problem. The estimates derived not only control the accuracy of approximate solutions, but also suggest a unified approach to calculating them numerically.

papers.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
papers.abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.

papers.title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
papers.abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.

papers.title: On the number of edge-disjoint $K_r$ in $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gy\H ori and Keszegh [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{37} (2017), 1113--1124] proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. We extend this result to cliques of arbitrary fixed order. Specifically, we prove that for every fixed integer $r\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_{r+1}$-free graph on $n$ vertices with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges contains at least $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$, where $t_{r-1}(n)$ denotes the number of edges in the Turán graph $T_{r-1}(n)$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G$ is obtained from $T_{r-1}(n)$ by adding edges within one of its parts, with the added edges forming a triangle-free graph.

papers.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $γ\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $γN$, and that near each threshold $γk$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-Δ_V^{(k)}=-Δ_V\otimes 1_{μ_k}-dΓ_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-Δ_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $γ^{-1}$ below $γk$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-cγ})$ for every $c<2δ_V$. Here $δ_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

papers.title: Möbius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $λ\in F^\times$, \[ \card{A+λA^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a Möbius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
papers.abstract: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

papers.title: Additive Fréchet Regression for Random Objects
papers.abstract: Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fréchet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fréchet regression, while more flexible than global Fréchet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fréchet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
papers.abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

papers.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
papers.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

papers.title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
papers.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

papers.title: Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure
papers.abstract: Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $κ^{-1/2}$, where $κ$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $κ$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.

papers.title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
papers.abstract: AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.

papers.title: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
papers.abstract: We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.

papers.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
papers.abstract: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit. We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k<N$. We deduce that these probabilities are rational functions of $N$ and, by taking the limit $N\to\infty$, that the corresponding half-plane probabilities remain rational. This establishes key aspects of Romik's conjectures. Our proof uses identities of Fonseca and Zinn-Justin, derived through the qKZ formalism, which express these probabilities as ratios of enumeration numbers for totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions (TSSCPPs). These plane partitions admit a dimer representation, allowing us to apply Kasteleyn theory. We evaluate the resulting hypergeometric sum using Zeilberger's and Gosper's algorithms and then take the half-plane limit $N\to\infty$. Along the way, we derive a somewhat simplified expression for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix entries (encoding correlations in TSSCPPs) of Ayyer and Chhita, which might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
papers.abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.

papers.title: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
papers.abstract: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

papers.title: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
papers.abstract: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

papers.title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
papers.abstract: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

papers.title: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient
papers.abstract: For every $γ\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $γ$-Hölder under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $γ=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

papers.title: Minimization of free energy in a Poisson--Boltzmann problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a mathematical model in which an ionic solution composed of several types of spherical ions is confined between two uniformly charged parallel planes. The ion concentrations at equilibrium, determined by the interplay between thermal and electrostatic effects, are obtained by minimizing the free energy of the system. The resulting minimization problem is infinite-dimensional, and we prove the existence and uniqueness of its solution by means of a norm-convergence direct method based on the Banach--Saks property of the space in which the problem is posed. The existence proof is technically challenging because the functional to be minimized is not coercive in general. Three illustrative problems are considered and solved numerically.

papers.title: Large $k$-cross-free families
papers.abstract: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

papers.title: Anytime-valid inference for time series via self-normalization
papers.abstract: We develop a self-normalized approach to constructing asymptotic confidence sequences for a broad class of parameters of stationary time series under weak dependence. Our theory covers nonlinear marginal parameters, including quantiles, expectiles and expected shortfall, as well as autoregressive coefficients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of self-normalization to construct asymptotic confidence sequences for time series. A key advantage is that the construction avoids direct estimation of the long-run variance, which can be particularly challenging for nonlinear parameters under serial dependence. Following an initial burn-in period of length $m$, confidence intervals are released sequentially, with simultaneous coverage over all subsequent times converging to $1-α$ as $m\to\infty$. We propose two sequential self-normalizers with complementary statistical and computational advantages. The forward construction uses only the history of sequential parameter estimates, leading to minimal computational overhead. The three-block construction typically yields narrower confidence sequences and is compatible with the optimal law-of-the-iterated-logarithm width rate. Together, these constructions extend the benefits of self-normalization to sequential inference under dependence. We investigate their finite-sample performance through simulations and illustrate their use in Markov chain Monte Carlo output analysis in the supplementary appendix.

papers.title: Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma
papers.abstract: This remark offers an expository reconstruction of OpenAI's proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact Kähler manifolds, together with new results. We extract a volume Schwarz lemma for extremal discs and derive a pointwise volume comparison: the volume form of a Kähler metric with $\mathrm{Ric}(ω)\ge-ω$ is bounded below by an intrinsic volume form built from the Kähler--Einstein metrics of pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix. As a consequence, if a compact Kähler manifold $X$ has nef canonical bundle and its Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix is bounded at some point, then $X$ is of general type.

papers.title: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity
papers.abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs). Yet, it is unknown whether its simplest differentially private Noisy SGD counterpart fulfills similar favorable guarantees even on strongly convex losses. We resolve this question affirmatively. We upper bound the parameter estimation error for a single pass of Noisy SGD with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes on smooth and strongly convex Lipschitz losses over a compact convex domain under Renyi DP. Specialized to strongly convex GLMs, our error bounds match minimax lower bounds we derive based on the Score Attack framework. In particular, this provides the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression, avoiding poly-logarithmic terms present in existing results. Our analysis is versatile as it relies on standard convex analysis and establishes the same rates in expectation and with high probability.

papers.title: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
papers.abstract: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary. Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
papers.abstract: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.

papers.title: Nondefective lifts of stationary discs and the 2-jet determination problem
papers.abstract: We introduce a natural notion of defect for lifts of stationary discs attached to a CR nondegenerate submanifold $M \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ of codimension $d$. We prove that the existence of a nondefective lift of a stationary disc implies that germs of CR automorphisms of $M$ are uniquely determined by their $2$-jet. We emphasize that, in particular, this unifies all previously known results on this question.

papers.title: Local Clustering Tests and Botnet Localization in Sparse Random Geometric Networks
papers.abstract: We use local clustering to test for botnets in sparse random geometric networks. Under the null hypothesis, the vertices are independent uniform points on a fixed-dimensional torus, with edges determined by a distance threshold. Under the alternative, an unknown set of vertices ignores the geometry and connects independently with the same marginal edge probability. Every prescribed vertex has the same marginal binomial degree law under both hypotheses, so its degree alone carries no information. Triangle closure, however, distinguishes the two models. Under the null, conditional on a degree of at least two, the local clustering coefficient has exact mean $C_d>0$, a known constant that depends only on the dimension. Under the alternative, the corresponding mean is $p_n$ for a bot. For a non-bot, the corresponding mixture mean converges to $C_d$ when the botnet size is $o(n)$. We prove non-asymptotic concentration bounds, an exponential bound on the worst-case risk of a scan test, and exact-support recovery. For every deterministic sequence $1\leq k_n=o(n)$, if $μ_n=(n-1)p_n$ satisfies $μ_n/\log n\to\infty$, the local rule recovers the botnet with probability tending to one, uniformly over all label sets of size $k_n$. The proof combines geometric U-statistics, bounded differences on random neighborhoods, and a stability bound showing that genuine vertices retain their geometric clustering when bots form only a vanishing fraction of their neighbors. The test does not use the latent positions. The theorem assumes that the model parameters are known, although $C_d$ can instead be estimated consistently. In the high-expected-degree regime, the rule also works for a single bot.

papers.title: Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.

papers.title: Spectral asymptotics for vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We consider vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators $-Δ_{a} +V$ with magnetic potential ${a}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and electric potential $V$ given by a symmetric and positive semidefinite $m\times m$ matrix-valued function whose entries belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Assuming that $\|\operatorname{curl} {a}(\cdot)\|\operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb{R}^m} + V$ belongs to a certain matrix reverse Hölder class, we characterize necessary and sufficient conditions under which the spectrum of $-Δ_{a} +V$ is discrete, and study the eigenvalue asymptotics and exponential decay of eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Nonlinear Fourier series
papers.abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

papers.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
papers.abstract: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.

papers.title: Preventing cycles in Lotka--Volterra systems
papers.abstract: We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria. For the broader class of Volterra--Lyapunov stable matrices, we show that two equilibria are joined by a heteroclinic connection exactly when the species that enter have positive invasion rates at the source and the species that leave have nonpositive invasion rates at the target. We show by examples that the three graphs can differ, that the dominance threshold is sharp, and that generalized dominance is not necessary for acyclicity. We also give a quantitative criterion for cycle exclusion in terms of the symmetric and skew parts of a weighted interaction matrix.

papers.title: Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
papers.abstract: We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.

papers.title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

papers.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.

papers.title: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

papers.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
papers.abstract: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an application, we prove a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK-percolation.

papers.title: Comprehensive Gröbner Bases in Macaulay2
papers.abstract: Studying parameter-dependent polynomial systems often requires stratifying parameter space according to the algebraic or geometric properties of the specialised systems. Comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, which provide Gröbner bases valid under every specialisation, either uniformly or on specified regions of parameter space, are classical tools for studying polynomial ideals under specialisation. We introduce ComprehensiveGBs, a Macaulay2 package for computing comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, either over the full parameter space or under specified parameter conditions. We describe its use and implementation, with examples involving Weierstrass cubics and graphs.

papers.title: Profile-Anchored Control: Velocity Shaping with Exact Disturbance Rejection and Transient-Free Replanning
papers.abstract: In many motion-control problems, how a target is approached matters as much as whether it is reached: speed and deceleration must stay within actuator, safety or comfort limits despite unknown loads and disturbances. Position-dependent velocity profiles provide a natural way to describe such requirements. We show that the square of such a profile can be used both to plan the motion and to construct the controller that executes it. Our main result, profile-anchored control with exact rejection (PACER), recovers the nominal motion after a finite time under an unknown gain and load, and then allows the profile to be replaced mid-motion without a transient. It combines a static law for scalar second-order systems with a dynamic law for first-order ones, used for disturbance rejection. The static law guarantees uniform global asymptotic stability under an unknown input gain with a known lower bound, and finite-time stability under local homogeneity, while the first-order law gives analogous guarantees under disturbances of bounded rate and provides the exact rejection in PACER. Replanning of a profile under speed, acceleration and jerk limits can be formulated as a convex program. The approach is illustrated on a simulated elevator.

papers.title: Rigidity of Complete Self-shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension
papers.abstract: We prove that a connected complete immersed self-shrinker in Euclidean space whose second fundamental form $h$ satisfies $|h|^2\le1$ is either a linear plane or a complete Riemannian covering of a generalized round cylinder. Neither properness nor polynomial volume growth is assumed. This proves the pinching classification conjectured by Cao and Li %[Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{46} (2013)] in arbitrary codimension. The proof combines a localized maximum principle, a pointwise lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci tensor, a weak Harnack inequality, and the convexity of the shrinker potential at the endpoint.

papers.title: Degree Lower Bounds for Symmetric Boolean Functions: Breaking the Prime-Gap Barrier
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonconstant symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables has exact real polynomial degree at least $n-O(n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3})$. This makes progress toward the conjecture of von zur Gathen and Roche that the degree is always at least $n-3$. The original prime-gap argument of von zur Gathen and Roche yields a degree deficit of $O(n^{0.525})$ using the theorem of Baker, Harman, and Pintz, or $O(n^{0.52})$ using an estimate claimed in a recent preprint. Our $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/3})$ bound on the degree deficit improves upon the $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ bound obtainable from the prime-gap approach, even assuming the Riemann hypothesis or Legendre's conjecture. Notably, our proof avoids prime-gap estimates entirely. The proof combines vanishing binomial moments with the arithmetic of linear recurrences. A quantitative form of the integer Hankel determinant method in the Pólya--Carlson theorem forces the function's values on a central interval of Hamming weights to satisfy a short rational recurrence. A second determinant argument bounds the number of characteristic roots near $-1$. Through the binomial transform, these roots can then be cancelled by a polynomial test of degree below the deficit. An integer annihilator and contour estimates make the test isolate the first failure of the recurrence, yielding a contradiction with the vanishing-moment conditions. If the recurrence agrees with the function on a sufficiently long interval, arithmetic height bounds instead force a bounded period, which is ruled out by a separate polynomial test. Every numbered result in the paper has been formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
papers.abstract: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

papers.title: An operator $b$-positivity conjecture for Jack characters
papers.abstract: Goulden and Jackson defined a Jack deformation $a_{μν}^λ(α)$ of the connection coefficients of the symmetric group and conjectured that these were polynomials in $b=α-1$ with nonnegative interger coefficients. This conjecture was extended to the structure constants of (stable) Jack characters by Śniady. We formulate a stronger operator conjecture: the differential operators $Δ_μ(α)$ that multiply by stable Jack characters should have coefficients in ${\mathbb N}[b]$ in the normally ordered Heisenberg basis $p_ID_J$. We provide numerical evidence, as well as theoretical consequences of the conjecture which can be rigorously proved. Namely, we exhibit two families of $α$-shifted symmetric functions whose associated differential operators are ${\mathbb N}[b]$ positive simultaneously on the bases $p_ID_J$ and $Δ_μ(α)$. These operators correspond to the Boolean cumulants of the Jack transition measure and to the Cartan generators of the affine Yangian $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak gl}_1)$.

papers.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We show that for every field $K$ of positive characteristic there exists an algebraic matroid $M$ over $K$ such that the dual matroid $M^*$ is not algebraic over any field. Our conceptual proof relies on the theory of matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups. As an application, we deduce that the classes of supports of realizable volume polynomials and of realizable covolume polynomials differ in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schrödinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlocal Schrödinger equation driven by a fractional Laplacian of order~$2s$, with~$s$ close to~$1$. Differently from the existing literature, which focused on either global problems in the whole of~$\R^n$ or Dirichlet conditions, we study here the case of nonlocal Neumann conditions in the halfspace. Moreover, we prove that ground states are nondegenerate, i.e. the only solutions of the linearized equation are linear combinations of the tangential derivatives of the ground state. Consequently, the ground state is unique, up to tangential translations and a change of sign.

papers.title: Semi-global Convergence and Finite-Sample Error Bounds for Model Predictive Path Integral Control
papers.abstract: We investigate the global optimisation behaviour of Model Predictive Path Integral Control (MPPI) in the low-temperature setting. For objective functions with a unique global minimum and under weak additional assumptions, allowing non-convexity and non-smoothness, we establish semi-global convergence of the mean-field or population level MPPI iteration to this global optimum. We also establish finite-sample results that show that with high probability the MPPI iteration comes close to the global optimum and provide sample complexity results. Under slightly stronger assumptions, we make these results more quantitative and provide concrete bounds on the inverse temperature and number of samples. Finally, we illustrate the results on the classic LQR problem.

papers.title: First Neumann eigenfunctions on piecewise smooth Jordan domains with convex corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every nonzero eigenfunction of the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded planar Jordan domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth arcs meeting at interior angles strictly between $0$ and $π$ has nonvanishing gradient in the interior; hence its extrema are attained only on the boundary. The eigenvalue may be multiple and the domain need not be convex; every convex polygon is included. The method adapts a recent Green-kernel approach for smooth domains.

papers.title: Harish-Chandra isomorphism over arbitrary base rings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $R$ be any commutative ring. We prove that Harish-Chandra projection induces a natural, strict filtered isomorphism $U_R(\mathfrak{g}_R)^{G_R} \simeq \operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathfrak{h}_R)^{W,\bullet}$, whereas the corresponding Chevalley restriction need not be surjective even over a field.

papers.title: Hook histories and a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for dual canonical Grothendieck functions
papers.abstract: We establish a two-parameter Murnaghan--Nakayama rule for power-sum multiplication in the dual canonical stable Grothendieck basis. The coefficients admit a closed boundary product formula and a signed combinatorial description by hook histories. We determine their exact support and prove an exact divisibility law for off-diagonal coefficients governed by the edge-connected components of the indexing skew diagram. We also obtain a hook expansion of power sums, an explicit binomial reduction to the dual stable rule, and a Grassmannian $K$-homological interpretation of the one-parameter specialization. Finally, we deduce complementary rules for power-sum multiplication in the canonical basis and the corresponding lowering operation in the dual canonical basis.

papers.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
papers.abstract: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

papers.title: When Suspicion Adds Up: A Stochastic Framework for Optimizing Honeypot-Based Insider-Threat Detection
papers.abstract: Insider threats pose security risks when employees or other trusted users misuse their access to organizational systems. Detecting these threats is difficult because harmful activity can resemble routine behavior. Honeypots, or decoy resources monitored for suspicious interactions, can provide evidence of potentially malicious activity. We develop a decision framework that models evidence accumulation through honeypot interactions using a continuous-time Markov chain and jointly selects honeypot counts and monitoring horizons to minimize expected losses from malicious activity and false detections. For thresholds of two and three interactions, we derive closed-form true- and false-detection probabilities and expected detection times conditional on detection within the monitoring horizon. We characterize boundary cases and establish stochastic-ordering results. Our numerical results highlight the value of the proposed framework across different settings.

papers.title: Analyticity of $\operatorname{Sine}_β$ pair correlations
papers.abstract: We prove that the pair correlation function of $\operatorname{Sine}_β$ extends holomorphically in $β$ to $\Reβ>0$ at every fixed nonzero separation. Our proof combines a random walk representation of the stochastic sine phase moments, stretched-exponential Fourier decay obtained by coupling, and weighted energy estimates for complex $β$.

papers.title: How Should Candidates Be Weighted under Open-List Proportional Representation? Harmonic Weights and Dirichlet Order Statistics
papers.abstract: Candidates in open-list proportional representation systems are not equally prominent, and measurements that involve aggregation over candidates therefore require some form of weighting. We address the question of how those weights should be chosen. Since weights based on realized preference votes are unavailable in advance and endogenous to the electoral outcome, we seek a priori weights that depend on list position alone, and derive them as expected ordered vote shares under a probabilistic model of the division of the list vote among candidates. The natural starting point -- the uniform distribution on the simplex -- is unrealistic, as it prescribes the same degree of concentration of the vote for every list, and under it the leading candidates become more alike as lists lengthen. The other members of the symmetric Dirichlet family require a concentration parameter, which is unknown and which there is no reason to expect to be constant across countries, parties, and elections. Accordingly, we treat that parameter as random. We prove that under a scale-invariant prior restricted to lists with at least two effective candidates, the expected share of the $k$-th candidate decays as $1/k$, and we show that over the leading positions of a long list, up to one hundred of them, the resulting weights are within 1.4 to 3.4 percent, in total variation, of the harmonic weights $(k H_n)^{-1}$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. No fixed value of the parameter yields similar weights. Moreover, under the uniform distribution itself, harmonic weights are exactly the normalized expected margins between consecutive candidates.

papers.title: Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
papers.abstract: We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-λa^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.

papers.title: Equality in the clique bound for critical graphs
papers.abstract: A graph is $k$-critical if its chromatic number is $k$ and every proper subgraph is $(k-1)$-colorable. Gao and Ma (2023) proved that every $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph with $n > k \ge 4$ contains at most $n - k + 3$ cliques of size $k - 1$, and asked which graphs attain this bound. We answer this question by showing that equality holds if and only if $n - k + 3$ is odd and the graph is isomorphic to the join of a complete graph on $k - 3$ vertices and a cycle of length $n - k + 3$. More generally, for $n>k\ge3$, we determine when the size of a nonempty family of distinct $(k-1)$-cliques in an $n$-vertex $k$-critical graph attains the upper bound $s-k+3$, where $s$ is the number of vertices covered by the family. Equality holds if and only if the graph is such a join (with the complete part empty when $k = 3$) and the family consists of all its $(k-1)$-cliques.

papers.title: The distortion of finitely generated subgroups in hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We show that the range of distortion functions of finitely generated subgroups of hyperbolic groups is essentially as broad as the range of time-complexity functions $T(n)$ of Turing machines. More precisely, we show that for each such $T(n) \geq n$ for which $T(n)^3$ is superadditive, there is a hyperbolic group $G$ with a finitely generated normal subgroup $N$ such that $\text{Dist}_N^G(n) \simeq 2^{T(n)^3}$. Our approach is to estimate the distortion of the kernels in Wise's HNN version of the Rips construction, and then to look at what these estimates yield when the $S$-machine groups of Sapir, Birget, and Rips are the inputs to the construction.
